title: fix first-page header layout and tiff header images
author: Sirsyorrz
body:
Opening a .docx with a different first-page header (`titlePg`) containing a TIFF logo showed three problems:

- The body started below the *default* header's height, so a taller first-page header overlapped the first table.
- TIFF pictures weren't decoded (`image` built without the `tiff` feature), so the logo showed as a grey box.
- Once the logo decoded, the app crashed on open: headers are drawn dimmed, and `vello_cpu` 0.2 panics on image paints with sampler alpha below 1 (`not implemented: Applying opacity to image commands`). Images are now faded through an opacity layer instead.

Tests: `tall_first_page_header_pushes_body_down` (layout) and `dimmed_header_image_renders` (render, reproduces the panic without the fix). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: truncate style gallery labels and keep hanging previews in view
author: Sirsyorrz
body:
Two Styles gallery issues seen with documents that have long custom style names:

- Labels were painted at full width and ran into neighbouring tiles. They're now truncated with an ellipsis to the tile width (full name stays in the hover tooltip).
- Styles with a hanging indent larger than their left indent previewed with the first line off the tile's left edge. The preview now sets the left indent to the hanging amount, so bullets stay visible and the first line starts at the edge.

Checked visually with `ui_shot`; `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Fix font dropdown hang caused by nested egui context lock
author: DWAA1660
body:
Opening the Home font dropdown hangs the portable app while rendering its first uncached font preview. The preview-budget callback holds egui's context write lock and then calls `ui.input`, which attempts to acquire the same lock again.

Read the frame time before entering `Context::data_mut`. Keep preview caching and the 12-preview frame budget intact. Add a regression test with a bounded wait that exercises rendering an uncached preview, deferring an over-budget preview to the next frame, and reusing cached textures.

Closes #5.

Validation:
- Regression test passes with the fix; restoring the original nested access makes it fail after egui's 10-second deadlock timeout.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 250 tests passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, asset attribution, dependency layering, and `cargo xtask wasm`: passed.
- Headless Windows UI screenshots verified entering text in a blank document, opening the font menu, selecting Amiri, and inserting more text.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops at a pre-existing Windows-only `clippy::useless_format` error in `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:805`. The remaining gates were run separately. Focused UI Clippy passes with that existing lint allowed: `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::useless_format`.

Developed in a separate checkout and branch to avoid interfering with concurrent repository work.

title: Windows MSI: give WordCraft its own UpgradeCode (fixes #4)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #4.

`packaging/windows/wordcraft.wxs` shipped with DesignCraft's MSI `UpgradeCode` (`49E87D30-…`) and DesignCraft's app component GUID. Windows Installer treats every package with the same UpgradeCode as versions of one product. With DesignCraft 0.2.1 installed, the WordCraft 0.1.0 MSI therefore looked like a downgrade and stopped with "A newer version of WordCraft is already installed", even though WordCraft had never been installed. The reverse would also go wrong: installing DesignCraft after WordCraft would have silently removed WordCraft.

Changes:
- New UpgradeCode and app component GUID that belong to WordCraft only. The header comment, copied from PhotoCraft (`.pcraft`, PSD/PSB), now explains why these GUIDs must stay unique.
- `packaging-lint.yml` fails if the `.wxs` reuses an UpgradeCode or component GUID from a sibling Craft app's installer, or repeats a GUID within the file.

Note: anyone who already installed WordCraft 0.1.0 under the shared code has an entry Windows can't tell apart from DesignCraft. The next WordCraft MSI installs over the same Program Files folder, but the old Apps & Features entry stays until they uninstall it. A clean install is unaffected.

Validation:
- Compared the UpgradeCode and component GUIDs of all eight Craft installers. Only WordCraft and DesignCraft matched, and DesignCraft's version (0.2.1) is above WordCraft's (0.1.0), which reproduces the reported message.
- `xmllint --noout` passes on the new `.wxs`, and `actionlint` passes on the workflow.
- Ran the new lint step locally: it passes on this branch and fails on `main` with the DesignCraft GUID.
- I couldn't build the MSI on Linux; the Windows release job does that.

title: LaTeX (.tex) import and export (#7)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #7.

WordCraft now opens and saves LaTeX (`.tex`, also `.latex`/`.ltx`), alongside Markdown, HTML, RTF and ODT. It appears in the Open dialog filter, File ▸ Export ("LaTeX (*.tex)"), Save As, the web app, `wordcraft-cli convert`, and MCP `open_document`/`save_document`.

**Export** writes a standalone `article` that compiles with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX, using only standard packages, each loaded only when needed (`fontenc`, `ulem`, `xcolor`, `multirow`, `amsmath`, `hyperref`):
- Headings become `\section*` … `\subparagraph*` (Word headings aren't numbered). The title paragraph becomes `\title` + `\maketitle`, and metadata goes to `\hypersetup`.
- Bulleted and numbered lists (nested) become `itemize`/`enumerate`. Also covered: `quote`, `center`/`flushright`, `verbatim` for code, horizontal rules and page breaks.
- Tables become `tabular` with the document's column widths, `\multicolumn`, `\multirow` and cell shading.
- Bold, italic, underline, strike, code, super/subscript, colour, size, links and bookmarks are kept, and all special characters are escaped.
- Equations are written as `$…$` / `\[…\]`, converted from WordCraft's linear format (`(a)/(b)` → `\frac`, `√(…)`, scripts, Greek and operator symbols).
- Pictures can't live inside one `.tex` file, so each becomes its alternative text.

**Import** reads the everyday subset of LaTeX (it isn't a TeX engine, so macros aren't expanded):
- Preamble `\title`/`\author`, sectioning (`\part`/`\chapter` shift levels down), paragraphs, `\\`, and page breaks.
- `itemize`/`enumerate`/`description` (with `\item[label]`), `quote`/`quotation`/`abstract`, `center`/`flushleft`/`flushright`, and `verbatim`/`lstlisting`/`minted`/`\verb`.
- `tabular`/`tabularx`/`longtable` with `\multicolumn`, `\multirow`, `\cellcolor`, booktabs rules and `p{}` widths. Floats and captions are also handled.
- Inline and display math (`$`, `$$`, `\(`, `\[`, `equation`, `align`…) becomes WordCraft equations.
- Text formatting commands and dec…

title: Interface languages: follow the system language, or pick one (#8)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #8.

WordCraft's interface can now be shown in **简体中文**, **繁體中文** and **日本語** as well as English, and by default it **follows the system language**.

- New `language` setting, `auto` by default. In auto mode the UI uses the first of the operating system's preferred languages that has a catalog (Windows display language, macOS preferred languages, `LANG`/`LC_*` on Linux/BSD, read via the small `sys-locale` crate), and English otherwise. Chinese locales resolve by script, then region: `zh-TW`/`HK`/`MO` → Traditional, `zh`/`zh-CN`/`SG` → Simplified. `WORDCRAFT_LANGUAGE=ja` overrides the system.
- **File ▸ Options ▸ Interface language** offers "Automatic (system language)" plus each language. The choice persists with the other UI preferences in `ui.json`.
- The `ui.language` command (`{"value": "auto"|"en"|"zh-hans"|"zh-hant"|"ja"}`) sets the language from scripts and agents. Without a value it reports the setting, the effective language and what's available.

How it works:
- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n` is the PdfCraft/PhotoCraft system (same TSV catalog format, parser and locale matching), trimmed to plain entries. English strings in the code stay the keys, and a missing entry shows in English.
- Translation happens at draw time inside the shared ribbon helpers (`group`, `big`, `small`, `split`, `menu_button`, menu items, tooltips including ribbon locations). The same goes for tabs, Backstage, Options, dialogs, panes, status bar, context menu and command search, which matches both English and translated names.
- Command ids, documents, file names, the CLI, MCP and the control channel never see translated text.
- Each catalog has about 780 entries, covering every ribbon tab, group, button, menu item and tooltip, every registered command's label and ribbon location, plus dialogs and Backstage. They were written clean-room from the plain meaning of the English labels, without consulting any Word localisation.
- Fonts: CJK glyphs come from the craft-fonts faces that re…

title: Apply heading/Title clears a paragraph's list numbering
author: justinjohn0306
body:
### Problem
Applying **Heading 1/2/3** or **Title** to a numbered or bulleted paragraph left the list numbering in place. Only **Normal** removed it.

### Cause
`apply_style`'s guard ended with a redundant `&& id == "Normal"`:

```rust
if (id.starts_with("Heading") || id == "Title" || id == "Normal")
    && p.numbering.is_some_and(|n| n.num != 0)
    && id == "Normal"   // <- makes the Heading/Title terms dead
```

So the `Heading*` / `Title` branches never ran, contradicting the comment directly above (`// Applying a heading or Normal removes direct list numbering`). Clippy also flagged this as an `overly_complex_bool_expr` error, which was failing `cargo xtask ci`.

### Fix
Drop the dead `&& id == "Normal"` term so headings and Title clear direct list numbering as intended, and add a regression test covering `para.heading1/2/3` and `para.normal`.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine` — 35/35 pass (incl. the new `applying_a_heading_clears_list_numbering`).
- Resolves the clippy error that blocked `cargo xtask ci`.

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger (only the web build does), and it has no panic hook, so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` is discarded and start-up problems only reach `eprintln!`. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/wordcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/wordcraft.log` next to `ui.json` (Linux `~/.config/wordcraft/logs/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/WordCraft/logs/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\WordCraft\logs\`).
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `wordcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512); without a file the buffer is released.
- **Levels:** `info` for `wordcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **`WORDCRAFT_NO_PREFS`:** such runs log to standard error only, so test and agent runs don't rotate away the user's logs.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first, then a panic hook that reports through `log::error!` (falling back to `eprintln!` when errors are filtered out), so panics caught by the `Session::run` guard reach the file too. Because std quotes string contents in some panic messages (a failed string slice), and that text can come from the user's document, the hook redacts anything between …

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![WordCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/wordcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the WordCraft colour field, WordCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small WordCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 23 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, WordCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.
- `package.sh` copies the TIFF and the layout into the staging folder. The image is still built with `hdiutil makehybrid`, and nothing extra runs in the signing job.

## One behaviour change: the volume name drops the version

`.DS_Store` points at the background through an alias that includes the volume name. With `WordCraft <version>` Finder kept the window and icon positions but lost the background (tested). So the mounted volume is now called `WordCraft`; the DMG file name still carries t…

title: macOS: open files from Finder and `open -a` via application:openURLs: (#27)
author: smkly
body:
Fixes #27

## Problem
On macOS, Finder "Open With" and double-click on a `.docx` show "WordCraft cannot open files in the … format". `open -a WordCraft file.docx` also opens nothing. File > Open and drag-and-drop work.

## Cause
WordCraft reads files to open only from argv. Finder and `open` send files through the `application:openURLs:` Apple Event on the NSApplicationDelegate. Nothing handled that method.

## Approach
- New crate `crates/macos-open` (`wordcraft-macos-open`). It adds `application:openURLs:` to the class of winit's own delegate with `class_addMethod`. It does this at `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunchingNotification`: the delegate exists, and AppKit has not yet delivered the launch documents.
- Why not a replacement delegate: winit 0.30.13 registers its own delegate in `EventLoop::new` and panics if it is replaced: `tried to get a delegate that was not the one Winit has registered`. Its doc comment that says otherwise is stale.
- `apps/wordcraft` installs the handler before `eframe::run_native`. The handler queues the paths and requests a repaint. `raw_input_hook` drains the queue through `file.open`, the same path as argv and drag-and-drop.
- No new external crates. `objc2`, `block2`, `objc2-foundation` and `objc2-app-kit` were already in `Cargo.lock`. The lockfile diff adds only the new workspace package and one dependency edge.
- `xtask/src/layers.rs` classifies `macos-open` as L6.

## Testing
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo build --release -p wordcraft`: pass.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets and layers pass. The wasm step did not run locally (no `wasm32` target installed). The new crate has only macOS-target dependencies and is not a wasm crate.
- Cold open: with the app not running, `open -a` on a `.docx` launched the app with that document open. Confirmed through the JSON control channel.
- Warm open: with the app running, `open -a` on a second file op…

title: Options: remember the user name between runs (#32)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #32.

A user name set in File > Options went back to "WordCraft User" (initials "WU") after a restart. Other options, such as dark mode, were kept.

The name lives in the engine Session, but the desktop app only saved the UI state to ui.json. UiState now has an `author` field. `WordApp::prefs()` fills it from the session when saving, and `WordApp::apply_prefs()` puts it back into the session at startup. An empty name keeps the default. The desktop app's save_prefs/load_prefs now use these two methods. The control channel's `ui.inspect` shows the current name in `ui.author`.

Tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`:
- A name set with `file.setAuthor` survives a save and reload, and a later rename is what gets saved next.
- Prefs without a name keep the default name, and the other settings still load.

title: Ctrl+-, Ctrl+= and Ctrl+0 no longer zoom the whole window (#14)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #14.

What you saw: Ctrl++ zoomed the whole window in. Ctrl+- then "zoomed out", but it also deleted the selected text, and each press needed its own undo. Ctrl+-, Ctrl+= and Ctrl+0 are Word shortcuts here (optional hyphen, subscript, paragraph spacing). egui's built-in keyboard zoom also reacted to them, so one key did two things: it scaled the window and it typed an optional hyphen over the selection.

What changed: WordApp turns off egui's keyboard zoom once at startup, in the same place that installs the UI fonts. This covers the desktop app, the web app and the ui_shot example. These keys now do only what they do in Word. Document zoom is under View > Zoom and in the status bar.

Tests: `word_shortcuts_do_not_zoom_the_window` in crates/ui-egui runs egui frames with Ctrl+Minus pressed twice and checks that the window zoom factor stays 1.0. Without the fix it drops to 0.8.

title: draw Symbol and Wingdings bullets as Unicode when the font is missing (#29)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #29.

Word's default bullet is U+F0B7 in the Symbol font. Where Symbol isn't installed (common on Linux), the substitute font drew whatever it has at that private-use code, so the bullet came out as a wrong glyph instead of a round dot. This affected the app, `render` and `convert`.

List labels in Symbol or Wingdings now use the standard Unicode character for Word's private-use codes when the font is substituted or has no glyph there. For example, U+F0B7 becomes • and Wingdings U+F0A7 becomes ▪. The table is `wordcraft_fonts::word::symbol_font_char`.

Tests: a unit test for the mapping table, and a layout test that puts a Symbol U+F0B7 bullet on a list and checks the label text and glyph.

title: Desktop: remember the window size and position (#23)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #23.

WordCraft always opened at the default size and place. Window size, position and the maximized state were not saved.

What changed:
- The main window's geometry (content size, top-left position, maximized, size of the monitor it was on) is now saved in `ui.json` next to the other UI preferences. It is set on the viewport builder before the window opens.
- While the window is maximized, minimized or full screen, the last normal size and position are kept. Un-maximizing after the next launch returns the window to them. On macOS, egui reads the zoomed state only when the window opens, so there the zoomed frame is saved as a normal size.
- Saved values are checked on load. A size that is not finite or not positive is dropped. Sizes are clamped to the minimum window size and to 16384. Positions and monitor sizes that cannot be real are dropped.
- If the window opens on a monitor of a different size than the one it was saved on (for example, an external monitor was unplugged), it is centred on the screen so it does not open off screen.
- Old `ui.json` files without the new field still load.

Tests: the new unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/window_geometry.rs` cover saving and restoring, keeping the normal size while maximized/minimized/full screen, Wayland (no position), clamping and dropping bad values, moving a window whose monitor is gone, and the `UiState` JSON round trip, including old prefs files.

title: UI: keytips, mini-toolbar, ribbon overflow, macOS typography
author: chiranjeevi-max
body: ## What UI polish for the egui front end. - **Keytips (Alt-key ribbon navigation).** Alt badges the tabs, a second letter drills into that tab's buttons. Suppressed while a text field, the canvas, or a modal dialog has focus, so typing never gets swallowed. On macOS Alt does not arm them at all, because Option is how you type accented characters there; F10 works on every platform. - **Selection mini-toolbar.** Floats above a text selection with font, size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, highlight, colour, alignment. Reuses the ribbon's own widgets so it matches the ribbon. Hides on caret collapse, mid-drag, while a dialog or the context menu is open, and takes no keyboard focus. - **Ribbon overflow ».** Narrow windows reveal hidden groups instead of clipping them. The button appears from the measured content width rather than a stored flag, so widening the window removes it immediately. - **Font dialog preview pane.** Live sample of the chosen font, size and effects. - **macOS typography.** A `TypeRung` ramp (size + weight + size-specific letter-spacing) wired through the title/status bars, per HIG. ## Screenshots Before frames are rendered from a clean build of the base commit. ### Font dialog: live preview added **Before:** **After:** ### Ribbon overflow » (narrow window) **Before:** **After:** ### Keytips (Alt): tab badges, then Home-tab buttons

title: Text boxes and floating objects: editing, drag/resize, wrapping, overflow, footnotes
author: WeebLabs
body:
Text boxes could be inserted but not used. The caret always landed outside the box, so it was not possible to enter text.  This is a set of commits that fixes the text boxes while implementing a shared drag/resize system comparable to that of Word and fixing the text wrapping.

Below is the robutt's summary of the work.

## What changes

**Editing text boxes**
- Insert › Text Box puts the caret in the new box; click into a box to edit it, click outside or press Esc to leave (Esc lands just after the box). Double-click selects a word inside the box. No text box inside a text box, as in Word.
- Copy/paste gives the pasted box its own copy of the text (it used to share the original's story, or point at an unrelated part when pasted into another document; Insert › Text from File too).
- Deleting or cutting a box removes its text from the document; undo and cut/paste still bring it back.
- Text that doesn't fit is hidden, as in Word (the first line always shows).

**Selecting, moving and resizing (pictures, shapes, text boxes)**
- Click an object (a text box by its border) for a frame with eight handles; drag to move, drag a handle to resize (pictures keep proportions from a corner, Shift toggles), arrows nudge a floating one, Esc cancels a drag.
- A dropped object anchors to the paragraph under it, relative to that paragraph, so the text it lands on wraps and it moves with that text.

title: Default Windows startup to DirectX 12
author: DWAA1660
body:
No WordCraft issue reports this yet. This is a preventive fix for the same Windows startup crash.

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to WordCraft. FilmCraft has the same change for storytold/filmcraft#179.

## Problem

WordCraft's desktop app uses eframe's default wgpu instance, which enables `PRIMARY | GL` on Windows. Creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. The app then flashes in Task Manager and exits with no window and no error (storytold/designcraft#167, storytold/filmcraft#179, storytold/filmcraft#268). `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` was the verified workaround.

## Change

- New `apps/wordcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and the web build are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p wordcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux): clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo check -p wordcraft --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`: clean, so the Windows-only call site compiles. (Windows-target clippy stops on an existing `useless_format` lint in `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:805`, which this change does not touch.)
- Limitation: no Windows/AMD hardware here, so the driver crash itself was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the designcraft report.

title: M6: footnotes no longer cite themselves in saved .docx files
author: goldsbd
body:
Any document with a footnote added in WordCraft failed to open in LibreOffice ("source file could not be loaded").

title: Add a Chat add-in: invite local AI agents to edit the document with you
author: lpgn
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a **Chat** pane to WordCraft. You can invite local AI agents (for example Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or pi) into the pane. An agent joins with a one-time invite code and a name, for example `@claude`. Then the agent can read the document, talk with you in the chat, and edit the document.

WordCraft records each text change that an agent makes as a **tracked change under the name of the agent**. You accept or reject the changes, as you do with a human reviewer.

The PR also adds a **key to the control port**. Before this PR, when you started WordCraft with `--control`, any local process could send commands to the port. Now each window writes a random key to a file that only your user can read (mode 0600). Each request must contain a key.

## Why

Many people now write documents together with an AI agent. Today, the agent must edit a copy of the file, and you must compare the versions. With this add-in, the agent works in the document that you have open, and you see each change at once. Track Changes keeps you in control: an agent cannot change text without a mark.

## How to try it

1. Start WordCraft with the control port: `wordcraft --control 7981`.
2. Open a document. Open **Review › Chat** or **Share › Invite an agent…**.
3. Type your name in **You:**. Type an agent name, for example `@claude`. Click **Invite**, then **Copy**.
4. Paste the line into the session of the agent. The line is: `wordcraft-chat join <window>:<code> --as @claude`.
5. Write in the chat. With one agent, each line is for that agent. With two or more agents, mention the agent (`@claude`) or use `@all`.

The agent uses the `wordcraft-chat` client (`tools/wordcraft-chat/`, Python standard library only). When the agent joins, the client prints a short briefing one time. The agent does not have to read other instructions.

- write and delete text in the body, tables, headers, footers and notes (always as tracked c…

title: fix(ui): prevent font preview context deadlock
author: Cyberverse-cent0
body:
Problem: Opening the font picker renders each font entry through a preview callback. That callback called ui.input(...) from inside ui.ctx().data_mut(...). Both operations access egui’s shared context lock, so the nested access blocked until egui’s 10-second timeout and triggered the RwLock deadlock panic.

The fix is in previews.rs. All five wordcraft-ui-egui tests passed, and the native app launch check showed no panic. Commit 9950525 was created; the subsequent git push exited successful

title: Ruler: dragging an indent marker is one undo step (#57)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #57.

What you saw: after dragging an indent marker on the ruler, Ctrl+Z moved the marker back one small step at a time instead of returning it to where the drag started.

Cause: while a marker is dragged, the ruler runs `para.indents` on every frame, and `Session::run` takes an undo checkpoint for every mutating command. A single drag left one undo step per frame.

What changed:
- `Session` gets `join_next_undo()`. It is a one-shot flag: the next `run` adds its change to the previous undo step instead of starting a new one. `run` always clears the flag, so nothing else is affected. If the history is empty it still takes a checkpoint.
- The left, first-line and right indent markers call it on every drag frame except the first. The first frame takes the checkpoint, so one Ctrl+Z goes back to the indents from before the drag, as in Word. Redo puts the whole drag back. The indent still updates live while you drag.

The issue also asks for the L-, J- and T-shaped markers that Word has on its ruler. That is a separate feature and is not in this PR.

Tests: `joined_commands_are_one_undo_step` in crates/engine/src/tests.rs sets one indent, then simulates a three-frame drag (the first frame normal, the next two joined), and checks that one undo goes back to the indent from before the drag, a second undo removes the first indent, and redo restores everything. Without the change in `run`, the first undo only undoes the last frame.

title: Layout: first-page header test no longer depends on installed fonts
author: dkhlapov
body:
## Problem
`tall_first_page_header_pushes_body_down` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`) fails on Linux machines that don't have Carlito installed, so `cargo xtask ci` fails on a fresh checkout:

panicked at crates/layout/src/tests.rs:170:5:
Caret { page: 4, x: 72.0, top: 597.11035, height: 15.868652 }

title: Web: embed in a host page (?host open/save bridge, ?accent colour); word-level compare; real dates on the web
author: vanamagautam24
body:
We want to use WordCraft in the browser as our lab's paper editor: papers live on our server, and the web app embedded in an iframe opens and saves them. This PR adds what that needs, without changing behaviour for anyone who doesn't opt in.

## Host mode (`?host`)
With `?host` on the iframe `src`, the embedding page drives the editor through `postMessage`:
- **From the host page:** `open` (a document's bytes), `run` (any command) and `save`.
- **From WordCraft:** `ready`, `result`, `saved` (the `.docx` bytes) and `dirty`.

In host mode, Save sends the document back to the page instead of downloading it.

**Message trust:** messages are accepted only from the parent window at the host's origin, which is the page's own origin or `?host=<origin>`.

**Ordering:** an `open` is handled in order with later messages, so a `run` sent right after an `open` applies to the opened document. Details and an example are in `packaging/web/README.md`.

## Host colour (`?accent=RRGGBB`)
`theme::set_app_color` lets an embedding app use its own colour for the accent, checked buttons and selection, in both light and dark themes. Dialog headers and Backstage use the same colour. The web build reads the colour from `?accent=`.

## Compare
- **Revised document as bytes:** `review.compare` / `review.combine` take the revised document as base64 `data` (with an optional `name`), for hosts without a file system.
- **Word diffs for edited blocks:** a block of edited paragraphs between unchanged ones is now paired up and diffed word by word. Previously only a deletion directly followed by an insertion was diffed, so editing two neighbouring paragraphs showed both as wholly deleted and re-inserted.
- **Formatting kept:** diffed words keep their own formatting.
- **Inline objects kept:** paragraphs containing pictures, fields or equations stay whole, because a text diff would drop those objects.

author: dkhlapov
body:

The per-launch auth token (suggested fix 1) changes the control protocol, and `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect` and the screenshot tooling would all need to pass it. ## Control server (`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs`)
Before, a line that wasn't JSON got a `bad JSON` reply and the server kept reading. So an HTTP request to the port, such as a web page's `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:<port>/", {method: "POST", mode: "no-cors", body})`, could carry a command such as `file.saveAs` in its body. `serve` now hands its reading and writing to `serve_lines`, which takes any reader and writer, so the behaviour can be tested without a socket.

Ctrl/⌘+click on a document hyperlink handed any URL to the system. Now it follows only `http`, `https` and `mailto` links. Anything else (`file:` URLs, bare paths, `javascript:`, custom schemes like `ms-msdt:`, a leading space) shows a status bar message instead. The message is translated through `tl!`, with entries added to the zh-hans, zh-hant and ja catalogs. In-document `#bookmark` links still work as before.

title: Desktop: keep the off-screen check until the monitor size is known (#23)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Follow-up to #38, as suggested in review: the restored window geometry was taken on the first frame even when `ViewportInfo::monitor_size` was not known yet, so the off-screen rescue never ran if the monitor size arrived a frame later.

- New `window_geometry::take_rescue(&mut Option<WindowGeometry>, &ViewportInfo)`: while the monitor size is missing (or not finite and positive), the pending geometry stays in place. When the size is known, it takes the geometry and asks `rescue_position`, which is unchanged.

title: Page break (Ctrl+Enter) survives ODT/TXT/Markdown/HTML export and no longer glues words (#84)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #84

Ctrl+Enter inserts a page break character (U+000C) into the paragraph text. The DOCX writer handles that character itself, but the ODT, HTML, RTF, TXT and Markdown exporters all go through the shared flow model in `model.rs`, and `flow_para` dropped the character there. So the break was lost and the text on both sides of it ended up in one paragraph ("num twoPage two").

`flow_para` is now `flow_paras` and returns a `Vec<Para>`. A page break character ends the current paragraph, and the text after it starts a new paragraph with `page_break` set. The exporters already know what to do with that flag: ODT writes `fo:break-before="page"`, HTML writes a page-break style and RTF writes `\pagebb`. TXT and Markdown have no way to mark a page break, so there the two parts are now separate paragraphs. A break at the start of a paragraph does not leave an empty paragraph behind; it moves the break and the list numbering to the paragraph that follows. Breaks in hidden or deleted text are still skipped.

Test: `page_break_char_splits_paragraph` builds a paragraph `"num two\u{c}Page two"` and checks that the flow model gives two paragraphs, the second one with `page_break`. It also checks that the TXT export does not contain "twoPage" and that an ODT export and re-import keeps the break on "Page two". Before this change the flow model gave a single paragraph, so the test fails.

Only paragraphs that contain U+000C are affected. Text after a break in a list item becomes an unnumbered paragraph.

title: Lists: a numbered list after a bulleted list keeps its numbering in ODT, RTF and Markdown (#83)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #83.

A numbered list right after a bulleted list was written as part of the bulleted list. ODT and RTF exported it as bullets, and Markdown kept counting, so it came out as "3., 4." instead of "1., 2.".

The ODT and RTF writers group consecutive list paragraphs into one list and take the kind of each level from the first item at that level. Now a top-level item of the other kind (bulleted or numbered) ends the group and starts a new list. The Markdown writer resets its counters on the same condition.

Nested items are not changed. A sub-list of the other kind under an item still belongs to its parent list.

Test: `numbered_list_after_bullets_keeps_its_kind` exports two bullets followed by two numbered items. It round-trips them through ODT and RTF and checks that the numbered items stay numbered. It also checks that Markdown writes `1.` and `2.`. Without the fix, ODT and RTF read the numbered items back as bullets, and Markdown writes `3.` and `4.`.

title: Find and Replace: Replace All now respects Track Changes (#88)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #88.

With Track Changes on, **Replace All** edited the text directly: no tracked insertions or deletions were recorded, so the replacements could not be reviewed or rejected. A single **Replace** was already tracked, because it goes through the normal typing path (`type_text`) on the selected match.

`edit.replaceAll` now does the same when Track Changes is on: for each match, starting from the last one, it selects the match and calls `type_text`. The old text stays in the document as a tracked deletion and the new text is a tracked insertion. Going from the last match to the first keeps the earlier positions valid, because a tracked deletion leaves the text in place and only the text after the current match changes. With Track Changes off, Replace All works as before. The whole command is still one undo step, because the session sets one undo checkpoint per command.

Test: `replace_all_is_tracked` turns on tracking, replaces "towards" with "toward" in "We walked towards the light, then towards home.", checks that tracked revisions exist, then rejects all changes and checks that the original text comes back. The test fails without this fix (no revisions are recorded).

title: DOCX: keep a line break written directly in a paragraph (#96)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #96.

Some document-assembly tools write `<w:br/>` (or `<w:cr/>`) directly inside `<w:p>` instead of inside a `<w:r>`. LibreOffice shows these as line breaks, but WordCraft dropped them, so the text on both sides ran together and the break was lost on save.

`read_inline` now handles a bare `w:br` / `w:cr` by passing it to `read_run_child` with the paragraph's default run properties. Page and column breaks (`w:type="page"` / `"column"`) are read the same way as inside a run. Breaks inside runs are not changed.

Test: `bare_break_directly_in_paragraph` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs` reads a paragraph with a bare `w:br`, `w:cr` and page break between runs, checks the text, and checks it again after a write/read round trip.

title: HTML import: tables without borders stay borderless in .docx (#99)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #99.

HTML tables have no borders unless they ask for them, but every imported table got the `TableGrid` style, so court captions and signature blocks came out with every cell boxed.

The HTML importer now records whether a table asks for borders: a `border` attribute on `<table>` that is empty or greater than 0, or a CSS `border` / `border-top|right|bottom|left` declaration on the table or on any of its cells whose value is not `none`, `hidden` or `0`. `FTable` carries a new `borderless` flag. When it is set, the converted table gets no table style, so Word draws no grid.

- Bordered HTML tables (`<table border="1">`, `style="border:1px solid ..."` on the table or a cell) keep `TableGrid`.
- ODT, RTF, and tables that come from an existing document set `borderless: false`, so they work as before.

Test: `html::tests::borderless_tables_get_no_grid_style` checks three borderless forms (no attribute, `border:none`/`border:0`, `border=0` with `border: 0px none`) and three bordered forms. Without the fix, the borderless cases get `TableGrid` and the test fails.

title: Issue #174: Footnotes and endnotes from Word files show their number
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #174.

Every note Word writes starts with a `w:footnoteRef` / `w:endnoteRef` mark, which is the note's own number. The reader skipped it, so imported notes read " First footnote text." with no number.

Notes made by `references.footnote` already start with a `NoteRef` to themselves. Layout numbers it (including the footnotePr/endnotePr number format), and the writer turns it back into the mark (#53). #53 notes that notes read from Word files never contain one; now they do.

- `read_notes` reserves the note's part id first, and the mark reads as a `NoteRef` to that note, keeping the mark run's formatting. A mark outside a note, or of the other kind, is ignored.
- The writer still writes the mark exactly once per note. When the first paragraph holds the note's reference to itself, the mark goes there with that reference's formatting, so `rStyle FootnoteReference` survives a save. Before, it became a plain superscript run.
- Not covered: `numStart`/`numRestart`, which WordCraft doesn't support yet.

### Tests
- `note_marks_reference_their_own_note` (reader): footnotes and endnotes, a stray mark of the wrong kind, and a mark in the body.
- `word_note_mark_round_trips_once`: two save/read passes, checking exactly one mark, `rStyle` kept, and no self-citation.
- The reader test fails on `main`.

### Verified (macOS arm64)
- `cargo xtask ci` passes, and so does the craft-fonts `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast` (FreeBSD workflow step).
- In the app, synthetic decimal and lowerLetter/upperRoman documents now show ¹ ² ³ and ᵃ ᵇ ᶜ / ⁱ ⁱⁱ. A saved copy reopens pixel-identical, with `footnotes.xml` in Word's structure.

Note: if #104 lands first, `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs` has a trivial conflict (both PRs add a test in the same place); keep both.

title: Issue #175: Tables: cell text takes its table style's formatting; derived table styles keep their base
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #175.

Word's Table Grid sets `<w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="240" w:lineRule="auto"/>`. Cell text ignored it and used the document defaults (8 pt after, 1.08 lines), so rows came out about 60% taller than in Word, and an 80-row table took 3 pages instead of 2. A table style based on Table Grid that adds red bold text showed no red, no bold and no borders.

- Style resolution gets a table-style level (`resolve_para_in`, `resolve_char_in`) in ECMA-376 §17.7.2 order: document defaults → table style → paragraph style chain → character style → direct formatting. Anything the paragraph style chain sets, Normal included, beats the table style, so a document whose Normal sets its own spacing keeps tall rows, as in Word.
- `StyleSheet::table_style` merges the basedOn chain: pPr, rPr, conditional parts, and borders edge by edge. Before, layout took the first style in the chain that had table parts and dropped the rest.
- Each cell paragraph gets the table style's paragraph and run formatting, with header row / total row / first column formatting on top. Conditional run formatting now sits under the paragraph style rather than over it.
- DOCX: `wholeTable` pPr/rPr and cell shading are now read, as are a table style's `tblPr` shading and `tblCellMar`. All of them are written back.

**Behaviour change:** new tables use Table Grid, so tables made in WordCraft get compact rows too.

**Not covered yet:** pPr in conditional regions, band columns, last column and corner cells, `wholeTable` cell borders, bold/italic toggling across style levels (§17.7.3), and applying the document's default table style to tables that name none.

### Tests
- doc: one test per hierarchy level, and one for the basedOn chain merge (including a loop).
- layout: three tests that fail on `main`.
- docx: the `wholeTable` / shading / margins reader, and a round trip.

title: macOS: open documents from Finder (double click, Open With, Dock)
author: ssamstudio
body:
## What

Double clicking a .docx in Finder, using Open With, or dropping a file on the Dock icon now opens it in WordCraft. Before, macOS showed "WordCraft cannot open files in the Word Document format", even though the app declares those types in its Info.plist and reads them fine from File > Open.

## Why it happened

Finder hands documents to an app with an `odoc` Apple Event, not command line arguments. winit's application delegate doesn't answer that event, so AppKit's default handler reports the error.

## How

- New crate `wordcraft-macos-open`. Before the event loop starts it registers for `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunchingNotification`; when that fires it installs an `odoc` handler. That timing is after AppKit installs its defaults (so ours isn't replaced) and before the files the app was launched with are delivered (so they aren't missed).
- The handler queues the file paths. The app drains the queue every frame and runs `file.open`; a waker requests a repaint if the UI is idle.
- On other platforms the three public functions are no-ops.

## The `unsafe` question

Sending Objective-C messages needs `unsafe`, and the workspace forbids it. I kept it as contained as I could:
- the crate's lints are the workspace's, except `unsafe_code = "deny"` instead of `"forbid"`
- only its macOS-only `imp` module has `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`
- every call is a documented Foundation API, nil-checked, with a SAFETY comment
- it's registered as a `Standalone` crate in `xtask layers`: no workspace dependencies and no UI toolkit

If you'd rather not take `unsafe` at all, another route is waiting for winit to support open-file events on macOS. I'm happy to change direction.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the queue and waker; `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers) passes.
- On macOS with an installed build:
  - [x] Open With > WordCraft while the app is running opens the file
  - [x] Open With > WordCraft while the app is closed launches it with the file open
  - [ ] …

title: Layout: space paragraphs like Word (overlapping spacing, border room, line spacing below text)
author: ssamstudio
body:
## What

Vertical spacing now matches Word. On a one-page test document, text had drifted by 8 pt from Word's positions by the end of the first page; it's now within Word's own on-screen pixel rounding.

## Three rules, measured

I measured these against Word for Mac with synthetic documents, black box, per the clean-room rules (no Word files committed):

1. **Space after and space before overlap.** The gap between paragraphs is the *larger* of the previous paragraph's space after and this one's space before, not their sum. I tested 10/4, 4/4, 6/12 and 5/5 pt with the same style, different styles, and compatibility mode 14 and 15: always the larger. They only add up when the document sets `w:doNotUseHTMLParagraphAutoSpacing`, which is now read, kept in `Settings::add_paragraph_spacing`, and written back.
   This reverses the comment in `layout_box` that said "no collapsing". I'd be glad to share the probe documents if you want to re-measure.
2. **Paragraph borders take room.** A top or bottom border adds its distance from the text plus its width (a heading with a rule pushed the next paragraph down in Word, but not here). A run of paragraphs with the same borders is one box, so there's no room between them.
3. **"Multiple" line spacing puts its extra room below the text.** Word puts the extra of 1.08, 1.5 or double spacing under each line, so a paragraph's first line starts where a single-spaced one would. WordCraft put it above.

Line heights themselves already matched (Arial and Times New Roman 11 pt, single and 1.08).

## Testing

- Layout tests for each rule: the larger spacing wins in both directions, the additive option, border room (and none for invisible borders), one box for identical borders, and the extra line spacing sitting below the text.
- docx round trip for the new setting; the full test suite and clippy pass.
- On that document: maximum line position difference from Word went from 8.6 pt to 2.9 pt. The rest is Word's display rounding (it snaps each…

title: Layout: shrink spaces in justified lines like Word 2013+ (compatibility mode 15)
author: ssamstudio
body:
## What

Justified paragraphs now break lines where Word does. Word 2013 and later (compatibility mode 15) fit more text on a justified line by shrinking its spaces by up to 20% of their width. WordCraft didn't, so long justified paragraphs wrapped differently: a one-page test document's summary took 8 lines instead of Word's 7, and everything below moved down.

## How

- In `break_lines`, a justified line may run past the right edge by up to 20% of the width of the spaces on it so far; the overflow is then taken out of the inner spaces, in proportion to their widths (`shrink_line_spaces`). Trailing spaces still hang.
- The last line of a paragraph is shrunk too if it only fits that way. Lines with tabs never shrink.
- This depends on the compatibility mode, which WordCraft didn't track. It's now read from `settings.xml` (`w:compatSetting compatibilityMode`), kept in `Settings::compat_mode`, and written back. So saving an older file no longer silently upgrades it to mode 15, which changes how Word lays it out. A .docx that names no mode is treated as Word 2007 (12); new documents are 15.

## Sources

The behaviour is documented from the interoperability side by LibreOffice's "smart justify" work (no code used; behaviour only):
- https://numbertext.org/typography/ (measurements: up to about 20% of space width; last line shrunk if needed; not in tabulated lines)
- https://bugs.libreoffice.org/show_bug.cgi?id=119908

## Testing

- Layout tests: mode 15 fits more per line than 14; no line ends past the margin; justified lines still reach it; left, center and right alignment are unaffected; lines with tabs never shrink.
- docx tests: mode read (15, 14, missing, junk, out of range, other vendors' URIs), and round trip for 11, 12, 14 and 15.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except the wasm step, which I couldn't run (no wasm32 target in my environment; the change is plain Rust in layout/doc/docx).
- Checked against Word for Mac on a one-page justified document: line breaks now ma…

title: Render: draw on-screen text like macOS, on whole pixels
author: ssamstudio
body:
## What

On macOS, pages in the editor looked lighter and thinner than the same document in Word or other Mac apps. Two causes, two fixes:

1. **macOS thickens glyphs on screen** (font smoothing). WordCraft drew exact outlines, so the same font and colour looked weaker. New `RenderOptions::text_darkening` strokes each outline by the amount macOS uses. The values come from Pathfinder (MIT/Apache-2.0), which measured them against macOS: 1.21% of the pixel size horizontally, 1.25 times that vertically, each capped at 0.3 px, and none past 72 px per em. A stroke grows the outline evenly, so I use the mean of the two. It's skipped for translucent text (the stroke over the fill would show as a darker rim).
2. **Page textures were drawn at fractional positions after scrolling**, so every glyph was resampled and blurred. `pixel_aligned` puts a screen-resolution texture on whole device pixels at its own size.

The editor turns darkening on for on-screen pages on macOS only (canvas, style gallery, template thumbnails). PDF and PNG exports, and other platforms, are unchanged.

## Testing

- Tests: `stem_darkening` follows the curve (proportional, capped, off past 72 ppem, safe for 0/NaN/negative); darkening adds a bounded amount of ink and is off by default; page textures land on whole pixels and textures that aren't screen resolution are left alone.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (wasm step not run, as above).
- Compared side by side with Word for Mac on a Retina display: text weight and greys are much closer.

---

title: DOCX: a style's East Asian / complex-script font no longer replaces the Latin font (#93)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #93.

`rpr` in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` used `w:cs` / `w:eastAsia` as the run font whenever an `rFonts` had no `w:ascii` / `w:hAnsi`. Word-made files often give the Normal style `<w:rFonts w:eastAsia="Times New Roman" w:cs="Times New Roman"/>`, so Normal ended up with `font = "Times New Roman"` and overrode the `docDefaults` font for all Latin text.

**Change:** those attributes now stand in for the Latin font only when the run is hinted as that script (`w:hint="eastAsia"` / `w:hint="cs"`). Otherwise the font is left unset and inherited, as Word does (ECMA-376 §17.3.2.26: each `rFonts` attribute is inherited separately).

**Tests**
- `docx/tests/fixtures.rs::style_rfonts_without_ascii_inherits_doc_defaults_font`: the styles from the issue resolve plain text to Calibri, and a run with `w:hint="eastAsia" w:eastAsia="SimSun"` still gets SimSun. Fails on `main` (`Some("Times New Roman")`), passes with the change.
- The issue's repro (docDefaults Calibri, Normal with only `eastAsia`/`cs`; one plain and one bold 24pt paragraph) through `wordcraft-cli convert`: `pdffonts` listed LiberationSerif / LiberationSerif-Bold before, and Carlito / Carlito-Bold (the Calibri substitute) after.
- Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass. **Not run locally:** the wasm step of `cargo xtask ci` (my toolchain lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target); this PR's CI covers it.

**How this was made:** this fix was written with Claude Code (AI coding assistant) at my direction and tested as described above. The commit carries a Co-Authored-By trailer.

title: PDF: field results, note numbers and equations export as their text, not U+FFFC (#97)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #97.

The display list (`crates/layout/src/display.rs`) took each glyph run's Unicode text from `p.text[c.start..c.end]`. For an inline object that slice is just the U+FFFC placeholder, so anything an object draws as text (REF and other field results, footnote/endnote reference numbers, equations) mapped to U+FFFC in exported PDFs: drawn correctly but extracted, searched and copied as U+FFFC.

**Change:** `Builder::shape_atomic` records the text an object cluster shows (`ParaLayout::object_text`, by byte start), and `ParaLayout::cluster_text` returns it for those clusters; the display list uses it. Ordinary text clusters are unchanged.

**Tests**
- `pdf/src/tests.rs::field_results_are_extractable_text`: a paragraph with a REF field exports with no U+FFFC and extracts as "See Section 3.01 for details.". Fails on `main`, passes with the change.
- The issue's `cross-reference.docx` (built by hand from its python-docx script): `pdftotext` gave `See` / U+FFFC / ` for details.` before, and `See Section 3.01 for details.` after.
- Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass. **Not run locally:** the wasm step of `cargo xtask ci` (my toolchain lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target); this PR's CI covers it.

**Not addressed:** the "[ . . . Unresolved cross-reference . . . ]" text from the larger document. WordCraft never produces that string, so it's most likely the field's cached result in that file. With this change the PDF shows whatever cached result the field holds.

**How this was made:** this fix was written with Claude Code (AI coding assistant) at my direction and tested as described above. The commit carries a Co-Authored-By trailer.

title: HTML import: pictures referenced by a relative path are embedded (#98)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #98.

The HTML importer loaded `img` only from `data:` URIs; any other `src` fell back to the alt text.

**Change**
- `formats::html::import_with` / `parse_with` take an `ImageLoader` (`&dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`) for sources that aren't `data:` URIs. `import` / `parse` keep their behaviour (no loader), so the formats crate stays free of file access and wasm-safe.
- `engine::io::open_path` (desktop app, CLI, `file.open` with a path) passes a loader that reads relative paths from the HTML file's folder. It percent-decodes the path (`my%20logo.png`) and drops `?query` / `#fragment`. It doesn't follow URLs (`http:`, `file:`, `//host`) or absolute paths, and skips files over 256 MB. Bytes that aren't a picture are ignored, because `make_img` sniffs the format, so the alt text is kept.

**Tests**
- `formats/src/tests.rs::html_img_sources_go_through_the_loader`: relative sources go through the loader; a missing one keeps its alt text; without a loader nothing loads.
- `engine/src/tests.rs::html_pictures_load_relative_to_the_file`: a temp folder with `page.html` and `img/my logo.png`. The picture is embedded, while a `.txt` file and an `http:` URL keep their alt text. Fails on `main`, passes with the change.
- The issue's repro: `wordcraft-cli convert image.html out.docx` now writes `word/media/image1.png`, both from the HTML file's folder and from another working directory.
- Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass. **Not run locally:** the wasm step of `cargo xtask ci` (my toolchain lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target); this PR's CI covers it.
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` pass.

title: Control port: require a per-window key (split from #54)
author: lpgn
body:
## Summary

Today, when you start WordCraft with `--control`, any local process can send commands to the app. This PR adds a key:

- Each window writes a random 256-bit key to `<config>/wordcraft/control-key.<instance>` (mode 0600 on Unix) after the port opens. It removes the file on a clean exit. `<instance>` is the Flatpak instance id, else `local-<port>`.
- Each request must contain the key (top-level `"key"`), or the connection sends `{"method":"auth","key":…}` one time. The app checks the key on every request. An unknown key gets `unauthorized`, and the connection closes.
- A line over 1 MiB gets an error, and the connection closes. A connection that sends no authorised request in 30 s closes.
- The MCP bridge reads the key from `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_KEY` or from the key file. As you asked in #54, it sends the key only when the `--connect` address is loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, `localhost`). For other addresses it does not send the key, and it tells you to use a tunnel.
- Docs: `docs/control-protocol.md` (Keys). The agent guides show the key in their examples.

## Tests

- `cargo test --workspace`: 317 passed (20 new). `cargo xtask wasm`, `layers`, `assets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Clippy with `-D warnings` is clean on the crates that this PR changes. (Workspace clippy fails on current `main` with rustc 1.95, in code that this PR does not touch: `layout/hit.rs`, `engine/tests.rs`, `formats/odt.rs`, `formats/rtf.rs`, `xtask/layers.rs`.)
- Live test on Linux: the key file has mode 0600; a request without the key or with a wrong key is refused; `auth` works; the 1 MiB and 30 s limits work; the MCP bridge works over `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` and sends no key to a LAN address; the key file is removed on quit; without `--control` there is no key file and no open port.

title: Track changes: keep other authors' deletions, credit paragraph splits, exact edit snapshots (split from #54)
author: lpgn
body:
## Summary

The engine fixes from #54, with tests:

- **A tracked delete keeps the deletions of other authors.** Before this PR, when you deleted a range with Track Changes on and another author had already deleted part of it, the engine signed that part as your deletion. Now the earlier deletion keeps its author, as in Word.
- **A tracked paragraph split gives the new paragraph mark to the author of the split.** Note: nothing outside the engine shows this mark yet. `review.changes`, `document.inspect` and the DOCX writer do not include paragraph-mark revisions. This was so before this PR.
- **Edit snapshots** (`edit_snapshot` / `restore`): a caller can run a command and take it back exactly: the document, the selection and the undo stack, also at the 500-step undo limit. This is the base for a check that must refuse a command without leaving an undo step. `edit.undo`, `file.new` and `file.open` between the snapshot and the restore are outside the contract (the method documents this).
- `hostile_params_never_panic` skips `review.readAloud`, because that test made the computer speak during `cargo test`.

## Tests

- `cargo test --workspace`: 302 passed (5 new; each new test failed before its fix). `cargo xtask wasm`, `layers`, `assets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- Live test on Linux, through the control port: author A deletes "charlie", then author B deletes "bravo charlie delta". `review.changes` and the saved DOCX keep A's `w:del` around "charlie". Undo and redo of these steps work in order.

title: ci: Add RISC-V Linux build with deb, rpm, and tar.gz packaging
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Adds cross-compiled RISC-V (`riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu`) Linux builds to the release workflow using Ubuntu 26.04, packaging native `.deb` and `.rpm` files alongside standalone `.tar.gz`, with `qemu-user-static` smoke testing. Also upgrades `flatpak` runners to `ubuntu-26.04`.

### Changes

- **CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**:
  - Upgraded `flatpak` runner matrix to `ubuntu-26.04` and `ubuntu-26.04-arm`.
  - Added `linux-riscv64` cross-compilation job running on `ubuntu-26.04`.
  - Added `nfpm` to generate `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.tar.gz` packages for `riscv64`.
  - Smoke-tests `wordcraft-cli --version` under `qemu-riscv64-static`.
  - Uploads all assets via `dist/release/*`.
- **Packaging (`packaging/linux/package.sh`)**:
  - Added `CROSS_ARCH`, `CROSS_TARGET`, `CROSS_COMPILE`, and `EMULATOR` support.
  - Added `riscv64` to `DEB_ARCH` mapping.
- **Documentation (`docs/releasing.md`)**:
  - Documented `riscv64` `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.tar.gz` release assets.

### Note on AppImage and Flatpak for riscv64

AppImage and Flatpak remain unavailable for `riscv64`:
- **AppImage**: Upstream `appimagetool` continuous releases only produce runtimes for `x86_64`, `aarch64`, `i686`, and `armhf`. There is currently no official RISC-V runtime in AppImageKit.
- **Flatpak**: Flathub does not provide or host `riscv64` platform runtimes (`org.freedesktop.Platform/riscv64`).

title: PDF: draw fonts krilla can't subset as outlines instead of failing
author: naxvog
body:
krilla subsets fonts only when the document is finished, so one font its subsetter rejects ("failed to subset font: malformed font") failed the whole PDF export. On Linux this happens with Caladea Italic and Caladea Bold Italic from `ttf-caladea`, which we use for Cambria, so any Cambria italic text could stop a PDF export.

When finishing fails on a font, the exporter finds the face krilla names, logs a warning, and writes the document again with that face drawn as filled glyph outlines. Every other font is still embedded as selectable text. It gives up after 32 such faces.

`kurbo` moves from dev-dependencies to dependencies of `wordcraft-pdf`; it was already in the workspace.

**Effect:** two documents in docxide-pdf's Word reference corpus that failed to export now export. Nothing else changes.

**Test:** a copy of the bundled Source Sans 3 with one glyph turned into a truncated composite glyph. The old code fails with exactly the corpus error; now the export succeeds, with no text from that font and its glyphs drawn as paths.

title: PDF: put the shown text of fields and note numbers in the text layer
author: naxvog
body:
Fields, note references and equations are laid out as one cluster standing for the object's placeholder character (U+FFFC). The display list took each glyph run's text from the paragraph, so a footer's "Page 1 of 5" reached the PDF text layer as "Page ￼ of ￼". Copy, search and screen readers got the placeholder.

`ParaLayout::shown` now keeps the text each such cluster draws, and the display list uses it. The drawing doesn't change.

**Effect:** 76 of 365 PDFs written from docxide-pdf's corpus had the placeholder in their text; now none do. Line-break agreement with Word rises from 62.9% to 63.4%, because the scorer reads the text layer. The visual scores don't move.

**Test:** a footer with PAGE and NUMPAGES fields exports as "Page 1 of 2" and "Page 2 of 2" (was "Page ￼ of ￼").

title: Lists: honour a list's own level definitions (w:lvlOverride/w:lvl)
author: naxvog
body:
A `w:num` can replace any level of its abstract list with a full `w:lvl` inside `w:lvlOverride`. We kept only the start value from it and numbered with the abstract list's levels, so documents that rely on it show wrong labels. A construction specification (SpecLink) read "A. PART 1 GENERAL" and "I. SECTION INCLUDES" where Word shows "PART 1 GENERAL" and "1.01 SECTION INCLUDES". Saving the document also dropped the overrides, so after a round trip Word showed the wrong labels too.

- `Num::level_overrides` keeps them.
- `Numbering::level` and the list counters prefer them over the abstract list.
- The .docx reader parses them with the same code as abstract levels, and the writer writes them back next to any `startOverride`. Writing a level moved into `write_level`, shared with abstract lists.

**Effect:** 6 of 382 documents in docxide-pdf's corpus use full level overrides. The specification's SSIM goes from 13% to 41%; the other five restate their abstract lists and don't change.

**Tests:** the counters use a list's own levels ("" and "%2.%3" in decimalZero give 1.01, 1.02, 2.01) and fall back to the abstract list for other levels. Level overrides survive a .docx round trip next to start overrides.

title: Layout: put the extra space of multiple line spacing below the text
author: naxvog
body:
With "multiple" line spacing (Word's defaults are 1.08 to 1.16), Word keeps each line's baseline one ascent below the line's top and puts the extra space below the text. We put it above, so all text sat lower by (m − 1) × the natural line height: 2.3pt for Aptos 12 at 1.16, 2.4pt for a Calibri 14 heading at 1.15.

The fix is a few lines in `layout/src/para.rs`. Spacing below single, and the at-least and exact rules, are unchanged.

**Effect** (Measured with docxide-pdf's scorer (`page-metrics`, 150 dpi) against the 365 Word-exported reference PDFs in its test corpus. Both runs use the same open substitute fonts (Carlito, Caladea, Liberation), so the absolute scores are low; compare the before and after numbers, not the levels.)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| first text line within 0.5pt of Word | 127 of 332 | 247 of 332 |
| first text line within 1pt of Word | 167 | 285 |
| mean ink overlap | 19.5% | 21.9% |
| mean SSIM | 39.3% | 40.0% |

68 documents score better and 32 worse. In the ones that score worse, the first line is now where Word puts it; the old offset had been cancelling another error.

**Test:** a paragraph at 1.5 spacing keeps its first baseline where single spacing puts it, and only the line pitch grows.

title: Layout: place floating pictures and shapes the way Word does
author: naxvog
body:
Pictures and shapes anchored in a .docx often landed in the wrong place:

- The reader folded every margin-relative position into "margin", ignored `wp:align`, and kept only `distL` as the distance from text.
- Floats in headers, footers and table cells weren't drawn at all.

**Model and .docx:** `Anchor` gains the left, right, top, bottom, inside and outside margin areas, plus the anchor character and line. `Float` gains alignments (`h_align`, `v_align`, which win over the offsets) and separate top and bottom distances. Reader and writer carry `wp:align`, every `relativeFrom` value and all four `dist*` attributes.

**Layout:**
- `float_rect` places against each reference area, by offset or alignment.
- Floats in headers, footers, cells and text boxes are placed, drawn (behind-text ones under the text) and wrapped around. Headers and footers get a page frame, so page-relative floats land in page coordinates.
- A first line pushed below a top-and-bottom float is drawn and hit-tested where it was laid out.
- Floats follow their paragraph to a new column or page, at the paragraph's actual top. A list item laid out again for this is counted once (`Ctx::next_label`, `Ctx::para_labelled`); before, lists counted 1, 3, 5.
- Wrap areas use each distance as given. The old 9pt minimum is gone, so a float with distance 0 touches its text, as in Word.

**Engine:** switching an inline object to a wrapping style gives it Word's default 9pt side distance. The position presets clear any alignment.

**Not done:** inside and outside margins and alignments ignore mirrored margins (they're treated as left and right). Character- and line-relative positions fall back to the column and the paragraph top.

**Tests:**
- docx fixture and round trip for alignments, reference areas and distances
- layout: alignment in each area, the pushed-down first line, a float moving to page two with space before, floats in a header and in a cell, header floats not changing the body top, hostile distances
-…

title: Tables: Word 2013 table edge, and floating tables (w:tblpPr)
author: naxvog
body:
**Builds on #136:** its commit is the first one here. Please review the last four commits, or merge #136 first and this diff shrinks to them.

**Table edge by compatibility mode**
- Word 2013 and later (`compatibilityMode` 15) put a left-aligned table's border at the margin plus its indent, moved in by half the first cell's left border.
- Earlier modes line the first cell's text up with the margin, with the border one cell margin further out.
- We always did the latter, so in Word 2013+ documents (43% of docxide-pdf's corpus) every table sat a cell margin (usually 5.4pt) too far left.
- `Settings::compat_mode` is now read from `w:compat`: 12 when a document doesn't state one, as Word treats it, and 15 for new documents. It's written back instead of a fixed 15.

**Floating tables** (`w:tblpPr`)
- They were laid out as ordinary tables in the text flow. 71 of 382 corpus documents have them, mostly forms.
- `TableProps::float` keeps the anchors, offsets or alignments, the distances from text and `w:tblOverlap`, and reader and writer carry them.
- A top-level floating table now stands at its position without taking room in the flow, and the text after it wraps around it.
- A table that may not overlap moves below the floating tables in its way.
- A floating table taller than a page runs across pages like a normal table, from its own left edge. Before, its lower rows were lost: one document came out as 3 pages instead of 6.

**Tidy-up commit:** no change in behaviour. It shares the alignment mapping (`FloatAlign::from_ooxml`/`ooxml`) and the placement helper (`align_in`) with floating pictures, and names the steps in the placement code.

**Not done:** floating tables nested in table cells, and in headers, are still laid out in their flow. Word's results there didn't fit any rule I could test.

**Effect** (Measured with docxide-pdf's scorer, `page-metrics` at 150 dpi, against the 365 Word-exported reference PDFs in its test corpus. Both runs use the same open substitute fo…

title: Layout: picture line heights, body top below the header, table row heights
author: naxvog
body:
Two fixes for where the body starts under a header, found with docxide-pdf's header fixtures, plus a note on a rule that is still approximate.

**Picture lines, header gap, effect extents** (first commit)
- A line holding only a picture was exactly as tall as the picture. Word keeps the run's font ascent and descent, with the picture on the baseline.
- Multiple line spacing scaled pictures too. A 144pt picture at 1.15 made a 165.6pt line; Word's is about 146pt, because only the font's line height is scaled.
- The body started 6pt below a header that reaches past the top margin. Word starts it right where the header ends.
- `wp:effectExtent` (room Word keeps around a picture for its shadow) was dropped. It's now read, written back, and reserved in the picture's line.
- `w:lineRule` and `w:hRule` are read case-insensitively, as Word does: `atleast` was read as multiple spacing.

**Table rows** (second commit)
- Word adds the cells' top and bottom margins and the border widths on top of an at-least row height: a 30pt row with 5pt margins and 0.5pt borders steps 40.5pt.
- Word starts cell text below the top border.
- We took the at-least height as the whole row, and drew text at the margin. Rows came out short, and a header built from tables ended 6pt early.

**Note** (third commit): what Word leaves below a line of only pictures is less than a full descent (0.5 to 1.9pt in the fixtures, against a 3.3pt descent). Two other rules each fixed some documents and broke others, so a `shortcut:` comment records the measured cases.

**Effect** (Measured with docxide-pdf's scorer (`page-metrics`, 150 dpi) against the 365 Word-exported reference PDFs in its test corpus. Both runs use the same open substitute fonts (Carlito, Caladea, Liberation), so the absolute scores are low; compare the before and after numbers, not the levels.)
