title: Improve Arabic and RTL layout, conversion, fonts, and interface support
author: kirolos-esmat
body:
Ready for review at `cf05bd0`. Rebased and reconciled directly on latest upstream `main` (`fd0bb2f`) as a single clean commit. Mergeable with 0 conflicts.

**Validation**:
- Workspace tests passed across all modified crates, zero failures.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- All 16 WASM crates compiled (`cargo xtask wasm`).
- All 55 assets attributed in `ATTRIBUTION.md` (`cargo xtask assets`).
- Dependency layers verified clean across 20 crates (`cargo xtask layers`).
- Verified locally on macOS arm64 release build (`WordCraft (Developer).app`).

---

### Scope & Architectural Distinction

As outlined in community tracking **#66 §18** (*"Arabic support must be architectural, not cosmetic"*), complete Arabic/RTL support requires deep integration into document models, layout progression, and file serialization—not just interface translation.

Several open PRs touch Arabic support; it is important to distinguish the two distinct layers:
- **UI Shell & Localization (#1195, #737, #1042, #1032)**: Focuses strictly on translating UI menus (`ar.tsv`) and egui window chrome mirroring (`rtl.rs`) in `crates/ui-egui`. As PR #1195 explicitly notes, these PRs intentionally leave the document canvas, layout engine, and document model untouched.
- **Document & Engine Architecture (PR #398)**: Focuses directly on the core layout engine, document model, formatting converters, numbering, typography, and proofing called for in #66 §18.

These two tracks are **complementary**: PR #398 provides the document engine architecture and can seamlessly defer full UI translation / chrome mirroring to the dedicated work in #1195.

---

### Key Changes

- **RTL Tables**: `w:bidiVisual` round-trip serialization; mirrored column visual layout with logical cell storage; physical outer border preservation; leading-edge indentation; unified under upstream `bidi_visual` / `table.rtl` conventions.
- **RTL Sections**: Column progression, gutter placement, headers/footers, line numbers, and footnote separators …

title: Track Changes: formatting revisions (w:rPrChange/w:pPrChange) (#41)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

Formatting changes become tracked revisions, like insertions and deletions.

- **Model** (`crates/doc`): `PropChange<T>` (revision + properties before the change) on runs and paragraph marks (`CharProps::fmt_change`), paragraphs (`ParaProps::fmt_change`, plus `num_change` for `w:numberingChange`), tables, rows, cells and sections.
- **DOCX** (ECMA-376 §17.13.5): `w:rPrChange` (runs and paragraph-mark `w:rPr`), `w:pPrChange`, `w:numberingChange`, `w:tblPrChange`, `w:trPrChange`, `w:tcPrChange`, `w:sectPrChange` are read and written back, each as the last child of its parent. A change nested inside a change is ignored; `w:id`s are renumbered as for `w:ins`/`w:del`. Fixes the data loss reported in the issue (plain open + save dropped every `w:rPrChange`).
- **Recording**: with Track Changes and Track Formatting on, `Session::run` compares the paragraphs a command changed against the document before the command (paragraphs with the same text, Arc-shared ones skipped). So every formatting command (bold/italic/font/size/colour/highlight/styles/alignment/indents/spacing/lists/clear formatting…) records without per-command code. Same as Word: an author's later changes keep the formatting from before their first change, formatting set back to the original stops being a change, and formatting your own tracked insertion just changes the insertion. Accept/reject, compare, undo/redo and `file.*` don't record. Typed and pasted text doesn't carry a format change.
- **Accept/Reject**: at the caret (run, paragraph mark, paragraph, table cell), on a selection, and Accept All/Reject All. Accept keeps the new formatting and drops the record; reject puts back the old properties (links and ins/del marks stay, and so do cell merges and section headers/footers).
- **Review list**: Next/Previous Change and `review.changes` include format changes (`kind: "format"`, `description: "Formatted: Bold, Size: 14"` in our own wording, and `props` = the properties set). Neighbouring runs cha…

title: Document grid: lines per page and characters per line (#391)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

Layout › Page Setup › Document Grid (`w:docGrid`, ECMA-376 §17.6.5).

- **Model + DOCX**: `SectionProps::doc_grid` (type `default|lines|linesAndChars|snapToChars`, line pitch, `w:charSpace`) and paragraph `w:snapToGrid`, read and written (`w:docGrid` written after `w:bidi` in `sectPr`; Word's no-grid `<w:docGrid w:linePitch="360"/>` survives a round trip).
- **Layout**:
  - Line grid: in paragraphs that snap (the default; `w:snapToGrid w:val="0"` turns it off), each line's height rounds up to whole line pitches with the text centred in them. Multiple spacing is a multiple of the snapped height; Exactly isn't snapped. Headers and footers don't snap.
  - Character grid: `linesAndChars` gives East Asian characters (CJK ideographs, kana, Hangul, CJK punctuation, full-width forms) whole cells of the character pitch, glyph centred. The pitch is the Normal font size plus charSpace/4096 pt. A larger character takes `round(size / default size)` cells. Latin text keeps its own widths. With `snapToChars`, all text snaps to whole cells.
  - Hostile values (pitch 0, negative, NaN, huge; extreme charSpace) are clamped to 1–1584 pt.
  - The grid is part of the paragraph-layout cache key.
- **Command** `layout.documentGrid {"type"?, "linesPerPage"?, "charsPerLine"?, "linePitch"?, "charSpace"?}`: section scope like the other page-setup commands, one undo step, returns lines per page and characters per line. New catalog row: Layout › Page Setup › Document Grid (403/435).
- **UI**: the Page Setup dialog has a Document Grid section (no grid / lines only / lines and characters / text snaps to characters, characters per line, lines per page). When the section has a grid, View › Gridlines draws it instead of the drawing grid. New strings are in all 9 catalogs (including et, sr and sr-latn).
- The Asian Typography paragraph options (kinsoku, word wrap…) and kinsoku in layout were already on main. This PR doesn't change them.
- Docs: layout-parity, file-format-parity, target-app-pa…

title: Track Changes: moves (w:moveFrom/w:moveTo) (#400)
author: vangel76
body:
Builds on #399 (now merged; rebased onto main).

Fixes #400

## What
Moved text is tracked as a move, not as a deletion plus an insertion (rest of gap #5's revision part).

- **Model:** `Revision::move_name` links a move's source (a deletion revision, `w:moveFrom`) and destination (an insertion revision, `w:moveTo`). Runs and paragraph marks keep their `ins`/`del` fields, so layout, PDF and the other formats keep treating moved-away text like a deletion (export shows the result).
- **DOCX** (ECMA-376 §17.13.5.21–28): `w:moveFrom`/`w:moveTo` inside `w:moveFromRangeStart/End` / `w:moveToRangeStart/End` are read as linked moves, moved paragraph marks included (their range starts in the paragraph content, so the mark is resolved after it). On save, the ranges are written around each moved stretch with name, author and date (ids renumbered, start/end ids matching), and moved-away text stays in `w:t`. Hostile input degrades: a move missing either end, a range that never ends, or a `w:moveFrom`/`w:moveTo` outside any range opens as a plain deletion/insertion. Open ranges and names are capped.
- **Recording:** with Track Changes on, `edit.cut` of a whole paragraph or at least a sentence gets a deletion revision of its own and is remembered; the `edit.paste` (or Paste Special › Formatted) right after it, by the same author with the same text, turns both into a move. Any other edit in between, undo or redo forgets it. A tracked paste now also marks the paragraph marks it adds as inserted.
- **Accept / Reject** at either end (caret or selection) resolves both ends: accept removes the source, reject removes the destination and restores the original position.
- **Reviewing Pane** (`review.changes`): kinds `moveFrom` / `moveTo`, with `move` (the name) and "Moved from" / "Moved to" descriptions.
- **Markup:** moves in green with double strikethrough (source) / double underline (destination), moved paragraph marks green; "Moved from" / "Moved to" balloons in the markup area (new st…

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
## Summary

This adds an **opt-in embedding bridge** to WordCraft's web shell, so a page that hosts WordCraft in an `<iframe>` can open a document in it and store what the user saves, instead of Save and Export becoming browser downloads.

I built it to run WordCraft inside **Nextcloud** as a cloud word processor: a Nextcloud app adds "Edit in WordCraft" to the Files menu for Word, ODT and RTF files, opens the document in WordCraft, and writes Save back to the user's Nextcloud (as a new file version). Save As and Export ask for a name and folder in Nextcloud. Nothing in the bridge is Nextcloud-specific; any same-origin host can use it.

Without `?host=parent`, nothing changes: Save and Export download, and the leave-page guard works as today.

The same team's PdfCraft has the equivalent proposal in storytold/pdfcraft#842.

## What changes (2 files, all in `apps/wordcraft-web`)

No changes to `ui-egui` or the engine. The bridge plugs into the hooks `WordApp` already has:

- **`Services::download`** → posts `wordcraft:save` `{ name, bytes }` to the parent. `name` is the document's file name for Save, or the path the parent picked for Save As and Export.
- **`Services::file_dialog`** → for `FileDialogRequest::Save`, posts `wordcraft:pick-save` `{ id, name }` and answers the returned `Receiver` when the parent replies `wordcraft:picked` `{ id, path }` (no path cancels). This is the same asynchronous path the desktop app uses for its non-blocking dialogs (#94), so Save As and Export ask the host where to save instead of downloading under the suggested name. `Open` requests never reach it (the web shell keeps `open_async`), so they're cancelled.
- **`Services::on_dirty`** → posts `wordcraft:dirty` `{ dirty }` when the value changes. In host mode the shell doesn't install its own `beforeunload` guard; the host guards leaving (otherwise the user would get two prompts).
- **Opening** → `wordcraft:open` `{ name, bytes }` from the parent goes into the existing `Inbox`, exactly…

title: Draw: Lasso Select, Add Pen, Ink to Shape and Ink Replay (#395)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #395

## What
- **Lasso Select** (`draw.lasso`): no points picks up the lasso; `{"page", "points"}` selects the strokes mostly (≥60% of sampled points) inside the loop and the drawings whose centre is inside. `draw.lassoMove {dx, dy}`, `draw.lassoColor {color}` and `draw.lassoDelete` act on the selection, one undo step each. The selection lasts until the document changes some other way. In the app you drag a loop and get a dashed frame around the selection. Dragging the frame moves the selection, Delete/Backspace deletes it, the Color menu recolours it, and Esc lets it go.
- **Add Pen** (`draw.addPen {kind, color, width}`, `draw.removePen {index}`): a pen gallery after the built-in pens. Pens are validated and capped at 24. The gallery is saved in `ui.json` (`inkPens`), and on reading, entries that aren't pens are dropped without losing the other settings. Each gallery pen shows its kind's icon over a bar of its colour and width. Clicking a pen picks it up, and right-clicking it gives **Remove Pen**. When a gallery pen is in use, the Color and Thickness menus update it.
- **Ink to Shape** (`draw.inkToShape`): toggles the mode, or `{"value": bool}` sets it. While it is on, a pen or pencil stroke that looks like a shape is replaced by that shape in the same undo step, keeping its colour and width:
  - a line
  - a rectangle or square (upright `Rectangle`)
  - an ellipse or circle (`Ellipse`)
  - a triangle or a polygon of up to 8 corners (a closed non-ink freeform)

  Other strokes stay ink. With ink lasso-selected, the button converts the selection instead (`draw.convertInk`). The recogniser is our own code in `crates/engine/src/cmd/ink_shape.rs`:
  - chord deviation test for lines
  - closure test
  - axis-aligned ellipse fit by RMS of the normalised radius

title: Hyperlinks cover only their own text (#413)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause
Hyperlinks are stored as `CharProps.link` on runs. Two places put the link on a **paragraph mark** as well:

1. `Document::format_range` formats the mark of a fully selected paragraph (right for bold etc.), so selecting a whole paragraph (e.g. `hello`) and inserting a link linked the mark too.
2. `Paragraph::split_off` (Enter) gives the new paragraph's mark the formatting to the left of the split, so Enter at the end of a link carried the link into the next paragraph even when the mark was clean.

Every paragraph Enter then made from that mark, above or below, was born linked, so everything typed there became the link (the video in #413). And because the link hover/Ctrl+click looked up the character at the *nearest* caret position, hovering anywhere right of or below the text hit the linked mark and showed the link tooltip. On top of that, typing right after a link (caret placed at its end) extended it, unlike Word.

## Fix
- **doc**: a paragraph mark never takes a hyperlink: `format_range` keeps the link (and the Hyperlink style that came with it) off the mark; `split_off` gives the new mark the unlinked formatting (`CharProps::unlinked`).
- **engine**: `Session::typing_props` — text typed at either end of a link isn't linked; typing inside it still extends it (Word behaviour).
- **ui-egui**: the hover tooltip and Ctrl/⌘+click follow a link only when the pointer is on the linked character itself (`link_under`, using the layout's selection rects), not beside, above or below it.

## Tests
`crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs`:
- `a_link_covers_only_its_own_text` — the issue's steps: `hi`, `hello`, link `hello`, Enter at its end and type, Enter at its start and type above: only `hello` is linked, no mark is.
- `typing_at_either_end_of_a_link_is_not_linked` — Ctrl+K link, typing after it, at its end later, at its start, inside it, and after Enter at its end.

`docs/typing-parity.md` updated (behaviour row + revision history). `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc -p…

title: Groups keep rotated members' orientation; group resize; ink erase after rotation (#441, #442, #443, #445)
author: vangel76
body:
Four object/ink bugs reported by @coygeek, each fixed in the public command path with a regression test built from the issue's reproduction steps.

## #441: Group discards a rotated shape's orientation
**Root cause:** `group()` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`) reset every member's `Float` to the default, which also cleared its `rot`/`flipH`/`flipV`. The group took over the *first* member's float, rotation included.
**Fix:** each member now keeps its turn (`f.set_spin(spin)` after the reset). When a group is merged into the new group, its own turn is folded into its members' turns. The group box covers the members' turned bounds, and the new group starts unturned.
**Test:** `group_keeps_a_rotated_members_orientation`. It uses the rectangle plus 90° arrow fixture and the 0° control. The page render matches before and after Group, and after a DOCX save and reopen. Members stay two shapes with rotation 0 and 90, and Undo restores the two objects.

## #442: Size leaves a selected group's dimensions unchanged
**Root cause:** `size()` only wrote `w`/`h` for Image, Graphic and Shape. A Group fell through the catch-all arm, so the command succeeded but changed nothing.
**Fix:** it now uses `InlineObject::set_size`, which covers groups. Members scale through the group's `chExt` child space (ECMA-376 §20.1.7.5), as with Move or Resize.
**Test:** `size_resizes_a_group`. After Size the Selection Pane reports `[400.0,200.0]`. The resulting group equals the one `arrange.bounds` produces, members and all, and the members are scaled.

## #443: Ungroup changes the arrangement of rotated group members
**Root cause:** `ungroup()` placed members at their unturned positions in the group's child space and gave each the group's `rot`. It never moved their centres about the group's centre, so a 90° group became a side-by-side row.
**Fix:** a new `shown_members()` helper splits a group into its members as they appear on the page. Each member's centre is turned about the group's centre, a…

author: vangel76
body:
Five editing bugs reported by @coygeek, each with a regression test built from the issue's repro (all five fail on main, pass here).

## #418 Center changes the paragraph beyond the selection endpoint
**Root cause:** `Document::format_paragraphs` used `paths_between`, which includes the end paragraph even when a non-empty range ends at its offset 0, which is exactly where Select Paragraph ends (to include the paragraph mark).
**Fix:** new `Document::para_paths_in(a, b)` drops that last paragraph for a non-empty range ending at a paragraph start (a caret still formats its own paragraph). Used by `format_paragraphs` (alignment, spacing, styles, Clear Formatting…), Increase/Decrease Indent and the list toggle check; the alignment toggle state (`cur`) reads the last covered paragraph instead of the excluded one.
**Test:** `tests::center_after_select_paragraph_leaves_the_next_paragraph_alone` covers Select Paragraph, a reversed range, a range into Beta (centres both) and a caret at Beta's start (centres Beta).

## #419 Selection replacement also undoes the preceding typing
**Root cause:** `Session::run` closed the typing group only for `caret.*` commands; `select.*` (pure) kept it open, so typing, Select Text, typing coalesced into one undo step.
**Fix:** any non-mutating command that changes the selection closes the typing group. Read-only commands (`document.inspect`) still keep it.
**Test:** `tests_typing::typing_then_selecting_then_typing_are_two_undo_steps` (first Undo restores `alpha` with `ph` selected, second removes the typing; uninterrupted typing around an inspect stays one step).

**Root cause:** Change Case replaced text whose UTF-8 length changed (İ → i̇, ı → I) but left the selection's byte offsets alone, so it then cut off converted text or took in text after it.
**Fix:** the selection ends on each converted paragraph are mapped through the replaced stretches to the new offsets.

title: Mail merge: SKIPIF, NEXT, IF in preview, header/footer fields (#427, #428, #429, #430)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes four mail merge rule bugs reported by @coygeek. All changes are in the merge evaluation code in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs`; the recipient data-source code is unchanged, so this doesn't conflict with #341. Fields are now evaluated **in document order with a record cursor**. Preview Results and Finish & Merge share that evaluator (`act` + `condition`), following ECMA-376 §17.16.5.

### #427: SKIPIF kept recipients that match the exclusion condition
- **Root cause:** `eval` replaced `SKIPIF` with empty text, and `finish` emitted one copy for every row without ever deciding whether to exclude it.
- **Fix:** `SKIPIF` now evaluates its condition. When the condition holds, the current merged copy is dropped and the merge continues with the next record. Conditions support `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`, comparing as numbers when both sides are numeric and as text otherwise. Quoted field names such as `"Last Name"` no longer get confused with the comparison value.
- **Test:** `skipif_drops_matching_records` covers the cases from the issue:
  - value `yes` gives `Beta`
  - value `no` gives `Alpha`
  - `absent` and the no-rule control both give `Alpha\nBeta`
  - when both rows match, the result is empty

### #428: Next Record left later merge fields on the same recipient
- **Root cause:** `NEXT` evaluated to empty text, and each copy evaluated every field with one fixed row.
- **Fix:** `NEXT` (and a true `NEXTIF`) advances the cursor for the fields that follow it, and the next merged copy starts after the last record used. The cursor is clamped: records past the last one (or past `to`) merge as blank, never as an out-of-range index. Preview applies the same cursor.

body:

**Cause:** `paste::insert` marked the pasted runs as inserted, but not the paragraph marks the multi-paragraph fragment adds, so Reject All removed the text and left the split (a paste of just `\n` produced no change at all).

author: vangel76
body:
Eight import/export bugs reported by @coygeek, each turned into a regression test from the issue's reproduction (all eight tests fail on `main` and pass here).

## #433 TXT: Windows-1252 and unmarked UTF-16 misdecoded
**Root cause:** `engine::io::open_bytes` handled `.txt` itself with `decode_text`, which only knew BOMs and fell back to Latin-1, instead of using `wordcraft_formats::txt`, which already sniffs unmarked UTF-16 and falls back to Windows-1252.
**Fix:** `.txt`/`.text`/extension-less files open through `wordcraft_formats::txt::import`; `decode_text` (also used for mail-merge CSV) delegates to `wordcraft_formats::txt::decode`.
**Test:** `engine::tests::txt_open_decodes_windows_1252_and_unmarked_utf16` (`0x80` → `€`, `A\0B\0` / `\0A\0B` → `AB`, BOM and UTF-8 controls, odd byte count).

## #434 TXT: list labels dropped on export
**Root cause:** the engine saved `.txt` as body plain text; the formats writer that prefixes list labels plus a tab was never reached.
**Fix:** `.txt` saves through `wordcraft_formats::txt::export`.
**Test:** `engine::tests::txt_save_writes_list_labels` — the issue's Markdown gives exactly `•\talpha\r\n•\tbeta\r\n1.\tfirst\r\n2.\tsecond`; plain paragraphs stay `alpha\r\nbeta`.

## #435 RTF: Unicode in metadata, bookmark names and link targets
**Root cause:** `Reader::word` returned early for the `Info`, `FldInst` and `Bookmark` destinations before `\u`/`\uc` were handled, so only the `\ucN` fallback character arrived; fallback skipping of control words was body-only.
**Fix:** `\u` and `\uc` are processed in those text destinations (with fallback skipping), matching the body.
**Test:** `rtf::tests::unicode_in_info_bookmarks_and_field_instructions` (title/author `Café`, bookmark `café`, link `https://example.test/café`, body `Café`).

title: Fixes: footnotes in table cells, NUMPAGES, bookmark link pages, bookmark around final table, INCLUDEPICTURE results
author: vangel76
body:

Five bug fixes from @coygeek's reports, each with a regression test that fails without the fix. (#425, the TOC depth, is fixed by the switch parsing in #410 and is left out here; #410 now says `Fixes #425`.)

### #450: table-cell footnotes missing from PDF
- **Cause:** `place_para` collects the footnotes referenced on each placed line and gives them the page bottom. `place_table` placed rows without doing that, so a note referenced in a cell was never placed.
- **Fix:** `table_notes` reads the note references in the cell lines of each placed row (or row part) and adds them to the page's note area. The usual rules then apply: the bottom shrinks, and a note that doesn't fit is split or continued. Repeated header rows don't add their notes again.
- **Test:** `layout::tests::table_cell_footnotes_are_placed`

### #451: NUMPAGES/SECTIONPAGES in the body show 1
- **Cause:** the body was laid out with `pages = section_pages = 1`, and the real totals were known only for headers and footers, which are laid out after the body.
- **Fix:** `layout` is now a loop over `layout_pass`. A pass whose body (or its notes) shows a total, and whose page totals turn out different from the ones it assumed, is run again with the totals it found. There are at most three extra passes, in case the digits change the page count. Documents without totals in the body still take one pass, and paragraphs without page fields come from the cache. `SECTION` in the body now counts sections too.
- **Test:** `layout::tests::body_page_totals_count_every_page` (three pages: body and footer show 3 even though the cached result is 9; a single page shows 1)

- **Fix:** the destination is the caret of the bookmark's position: the page and line its start lands on, with the x of the paragraph's piece on that page. If …

title: .doc import fixes: piece bold, section kinds, orientation, list overrides, style inheritance, alternate font names (#458–#463)
author: vangel76
body:
Six Word 97-2003 `.doc` import bugs reported by @coygeek, fixed against the public [MS-DOC] specification. Each fix has one regression test in `crates/docbin/src/tests.rs`. The tests build their fixtures in code, and every one of them fails without its fix.

### #458: piece PRM bold settings ignored
- **Root cause:** `PieceTable::piece_prm` used bit 15 as the Prm0/Prm1 discriminator, read `isprm` from bits 0-6 and read the Prc index from bits 0-14. Per §2.9.215/§2.9.216, bit 0 is `fComplex`. A Prm0 keeps `isprm` in bits 1-7 and its operand in bits 8-15. A Prm1 keeps a zero-based Prc index in bits 1-15.
- **Fix:** decode the Prm by that layout. Piece properties still apply after the CHPX, so a Prm0 that turns bold off overrides a CHPX that turns it on.
- **Test:** `piece_prm_character_formatting_applied` covers Prm0 0x01AA, Prm1 0x0001 and 0x0003 (two different Prcs), and Prm0 0x00AA over a bold CHPX. The controls are an unformatted piece and CHPX-only bold.

### #459: explicit section-break kinds remapped
- **Root cause:** `sprmSBkc` mapped 1→even, 2→odd and 3/4→new page.
- **Fix:** map by SBkcOperand: 0 continuous, 1 new column, 2 new page, 3 even page, 4 odd page. Any other value falls back to new page.
- **Test:** `section_break_kinds_imported` checks all five operands.

### #460: explicit orientation imported with the opposite flag
- **Root cause:** `sprmSBOrientation` treated operand 1 as landscape. Per §2.9.236, 1 means portrait and 2 means landscape.
- **Fix:** 1 sets portrait and 2 sets landscape. Only these two values count as explicit. Without one, the orientation is still inferred from the page shape.
- **Test:** `explicit_section_orientation_imported` covers explicit portrait and explicit landscape (both keep their dimensions) and the two inferred controls.

### #461: negative list references import as unnumbered
- **Root cause:** the `sprmPIlfo` operand is sign-extended from i16, but `num_of` matched 0xF802..=0xFFFF as positive values, so a negative ref…

title: Equation fixes: numbering removal, control colour, undo for navigation edits, LaTeX text spaces (#444, #446, #447, #448)
author: vangel76
body:
Four equation bugs reported by @coygeek, each with a regression test in `crates/engine/src/cmd/equation.rs` that drives the public command API. I checked that every test fails on `main` and passes with this change.

### #444: removing equation numbers deleted later rows
**Root cause:** `equation.number {"value": false}` noticed a number in any row of the equation array, but then rebuilt the equation from the first row only.
**Fix:** every row now goes through `without_number`, which drops everything from the non-literal `#` onwards. A single row is unwrapped as before. Two or more rows stay an `EqArr`.
**Test:** `removing_numbers_keeps_every_row` covers `█(a#(1)@b#(2))` and `█(a@b#(2))`. Both turn into `█(a@b)`, still read `█(a@b)` after a DOCX save and reopen, and get their numbers back on Undo. It also checks that the single-row `a#(1)` still becomes `a`.

### #446: caret navigation dropped an imported fraction's control colour
**Root cause:** `equation.move` always ran its AutoCorrect/build-up step through `with_eq`. That function clears the retained source OMML even when nothing changes, so the writer regenerated `m:fPr` and the `m:ctrlPr` colour was lost.
**Fix:** AutoCorrect and build-up now run on a copy of the nodes. The equation is only written back when the nodes actually changed.
**Test:** `navigation_keeps_imported_omml` imports the red `m:f` from the issue, moves left, and checks that the saved `document.xml` still has `w:val="FF0000"`. The genuine-edit control still applies: typing `x` saves `a/bx`.

### #447: building a fraction during navigation left the document clean and couldn't be undone
**Root cause:** `equation.move` is a pure command, so `Session::run` neither checkpoints it nor marks the document dirty. The build-up it performed was invisible to Undo and to the dirty flag.
**Fix:** when navigation does change the equation, the command records the change itself. It takes `s.checkpoint("Build Up")` before writing and calls `s.touch()` afterward…

title: Accessibility: the document canvas exposes its text to screen readers (#488)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

The document canvas was one opaque widget to assistive technology. It now describes the document through AccessKit (`crates/ui-egui/src/a11y.rs`), the way a browser describes a page:

- The canvas widget is the **Document** node, named after the document (`title_stem`, no new UI strings). It holds the caret and selection as an AccessKit `TextSelection` pointing into the text runs, so a screen reader can follow the caret by character, word and line.
- Each body paragraph is a **Paragraph**, a **Heading** (`level` = outline level + 1) or a **ListItem** (`level` = list level + 1). Consecutive list paragraphs are grouped in a **List**, and the list number or bullet is a **ListMarker** (Symbol-font private-use bullets are reported as `•`).
- Each laid-out line is a **TextRun** with its text, `character_lengths`, `word_starts`, screen bounds, and `character_positions`/`character_widths` for plain left-to-right horizontal lines. A run is split at hyperlinks, inline pictures and AccessKit's 255-character limit, with `next_on_line`/`previous_on_line` links between the pieces. The paragraph mark ends the last run as `\n`, which is how AccessKit finds paragraph ends.
- Tables are **Table → Row → Cell**, with row and column counts and indexes, including nested tables. A repeated header row is described once.
- Pictures and charts are **Image** nodes named by their alt text, with bounds (floating ones use their placed frame). Hyperlinks are **Link** nodes with `url`, wrapped around their runs.
- Size is bounded: only the pages on screen and one page either side are described, capped at 6,000 nodes. Paths from files are depth-limited, and all indexing uses `get`.
- Cost: nothing is built unless AccessKit is active (egui only enables it when a screen reader asks). The tree is cached in `CanvasState` and rebuilt only when the layout `Arc`, the selection, the described pages or their screen rects change.

title: Layout fixes: mirrored margins, tall headers/footers push the body, endnote continuation, footnote caret on continuation pages (#452, #453, #454, #456, #457)
author: vangel76
body:
Five page-layout fixes in `crates/layout`, each with a regression test in the new `crates/layout/src/tests_pages.rs`. The tests check relations between positions (body bottom ≤ footer top, and so on) rather than exact coordinates, so they don't depend on which fonts are installed. All five failed before the fix.

### #452 Mirrored margins keep even-page text at the inside margin
- **Root cause:** nothing in layout read `settings.mirror_margins`. Every page placed text at `margin_left + gutter`.
- **Fix:** a new `mirror_even_pages` pass runs after headers and footers are placed. On pages with an even number it shifts the body, notes, header, footer and `page.body` by `margin_right - margin_left - gutter`, so the inside margin and gutter end up on the right. Page borders are measured from the page edge, so they don't move. Known limit: page-relative floats move with the text.
- **Test:** `mirrored_margins_put_the_inside_margin_toward_the_binding`. Inside 108 + gutter 10, outside 36: odd pages start at x=118, even pages at x=36, and the text width is unchanged. With mirroring off, both start at 118.

### #453 Eight-line footer overlaps body text
- **Root cause:** the body bottom was always `page_h - margin_bottom`, and the footer's height was only measured when it was drawn, after pagination.
- **Fix:** `foot_top_for` measures the footer the same way `headers_footers` places it. `PageBuilder.foot_top` then caps the body bottom (and the column-separator length) at the footer top, keeping at least 36pt of body.
- **Test:** `a_tall_footer_pushes_the_body_up`. On every page the body ends at or above the footer top, and every paragraph is still placed exactly once. A one-line footer leaves the body at the full 720pt bottom.

- **Root cause:** the body top was measured from the section's own `headers.default`. A section that inherits its header through link-to-previous had `None` there and started at the top m…

title: Chinese interface: keep a system CJK fallback after the bundled face; find PingFang on macOS 12 (#486)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause

**Confirmed (from the screenshots):** the characters that show as `□` / `?` are exactly the CJK characters of the zh-hans / zh-hant catalogs that **BIZ UDPGothic**, the embedded Japanese interface face, has no glyph for — and nothing else. I ran the screenshot strings through that font's cmap:

- Simplified: `□□ 常□ 界面□言 □体中文 用□名 自□保存已保存□的文档 在□□□中□示社区按□ … □存□ □出` (选项 规 语 简 户 动 过 标题栏 钮 显 另 为 导 …) — identical to the screenshot.
- Traditional: `開□ □存新檔 文件□容不會改變 □動 應用程式以開□` (啟 另 內) — identical too, which is why Traditional shows fewer boxes.

`?` versus `□` is only egui's replacement glyph: the Inter-based `medium`/`semibold` families (headings, sidebar) have no U+25FB, so egui draws `?`; the proportional family has it (through egui's default fonts) and draws `□`. The catalogs themselves are clean (no literal `?`, no U+FFFD).

A chain with BIZ UDPGothic as the only CJK face and no installed-font fallback is the font setup of **v0.4.0 and earlier** (craft-fonts pin `abb8331`, Japanese faces only; the system fallback came with #248). v0.5.0 embeds Noto Sans CJK SC (I checked the v0.5.0 macOS dmg: the binary contains `NotoSansCJKsc-Regular`), and that face covers every character of both Chinese catalogs. **Likely** the reporter ran ≤ 0.4.0 (the issue was filed 30 minutes after v0.5.0 was published); v0.5.0 should already render these menus. I could not confirm the version they ran.

**Remaining gaps this PR closes** (found while tracing the macOS path):
1. The installed CJK font was only considered when *no* embedded "Hans" face existed (`ui_needs_system_cjk`). An embedded face that lacks some catalog characters (older or subset craft-fonts file) would never get a fallback.
2. On macOS 10.15+ (incl. 12), `PingFang.ttc` lives in `/System/Library/AssetsV2/com_apple_MobileAsset_Font7/<hash>.asset/AssetData/`. `find_ui_font` joined the candidate name directly onto `…/com_apple_MobileAsset_Font7`, so PingFang was never found there.

author: vangel76
body:
Builds on #380 — merge that first (this branch is stacked on `feat/369-shape-text`; the diff includes #380's commit until it lands).

Fixes #491

## What
- **Model**: `SectionProps.text_direction` (horizontal / `tbRl` / `btLr`), serialized only when turned.
- **DOCX**: `w:textDirection` in `w:sectPr` (ECMA-376 §17.6.20) read and written in `CT_SectPr` order (after `w:titlePg`, before `w:bidi`), also inside `w:sectPrChange`. `tbRlV`/`tbLrV` read as `tbRl`; `lrTbV` and unknown values read as horizontal.

Pictures, shapes and text boxes stay upright (their centres move with the turn, a box's text moves with its box). Headers and footers stay horizontal. A section turning the other way than the previous one starts a new page.

title: Font list: installed Chinese fonts are listed, by their Chinese names in a Chinese interface (#505)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause

- **Confirmed (reproduced on Linux):** the font database read only the English family name of each font (`english_or_first`). With Noto Sans CJK and WenQuanYi Zen Hei installed, every face of the `.ttc` collections was cataloged (Noto Sans CJK SC/TC/JP/KR, all weights; nothing was dropped by size or face index), but only as `WenQuanYi Zen Hei`, never `文泉驿正黑`. A Chinese interface therefore showed no Chinese names in the font box, and a document naming a font by its Chinese name (`宋体`, as Chinese Word writes) didn't find the installed font and fell back to another.
- **Likely for the reporter (Windows, screenshot shows the mini toolbar's font list at S):** SimSun, SimHei, Microsoft YaHei and the others are in the list, but by their English names, sorted among the Latin fonts, so nothing in the list reads as a Chinese font. Word in a Chinese interface lists them as 宋体, 黑体, 微软雅黑.

## Fix

- **fonts:** each face keeps its localized family names (name IDs 16 and 1, all languages; read from the `name` table during the scan without loading the file; capped at 64 names of 128 characters per face). New `FontDb::families_in(lang)` lists them in place of the English names for a matching interface language (Chinese matched by script: zh-hans ↔ zh-CN/zh-SG/zh-Hans, zh-hant ↔ zh-TW/zh-HK/zh-MO/zh-Hant; ja, ko by language). `face`, `has_family` and `styles` accept either name; `english_family` maps 宋体 → SimSun; `FontFace::is_east_asian` (OS/2 CJK code pages, or ideograph coverage without them).
- **ui:** the ribbon and mini-toolbar font boxes show the list and the current font in the interface language and store the English name, so the document reads the same on any system. Typing the English name still applies it.
- **East Asian font (`w:eastAsia`):** `CharProps::font_ea` is new. `format.font` with a Chinese, Japanese or Korean font sets it as well (as Word does; a Latin font leaves East Asian text's font alone). DOCX reads and writes `w:rFonts/@w:eastAsia`, and la…

title: CLI: a closed stdout ends quietly instead of panicking (#508)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause
`wordcraft-cli` wrote its output with `println!`/`print!`, which panic when the write fails. Rust ignores SIGPIPE, so once a reader such as `head` closes the pipe, the next write returns `EPIPE` and `println!` panics with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe` (exit 101). `commands --json` (~96 KB) is larger than a 64 KB pipe buffer, so it always hits this. The `mcp` stdio server already returned the `io::Error`, but the CLI turned it into a failure message and exit 1.

## Fix
- Added a small `Failure` error type to `apps/wordcraft-cli`: `Error(String)` for real errors and `StdoutClosed` for a closed stdout. `From<io::Error>` maps `ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` to `StdoutClosed`.
- All stdout output (`info`, `text`, `inspect`, `render`, `run --print`, `commands`, `parity`, `--version`, help) now goes through `write_stdout`, which writes to a locked `std::io::stdout()` with `writeln!`, flushes, and passes errors up with `?`.
- `mcp` passes `serve`'s `io::Error` through the same mapping, so a client that closes stdout ends the server cleanly.
- `main` exits 0 quietly on `StdoutClosed`, like the sibling CLIs. Real errors still print `wordcraft-cli: …` on stderr and exit 1.
- None of the library crates the CLI uses (`engine`, `mcp`, `zotero`, `doc`, `render`) print to stdout.

## Test
New `apps/wordcraft-cli/tests/closed_stdout.rs` (Unix only) runs the built binary:
- `commands --json`: reads 16 bytes, closes the pipe, then checks for exit 0 and no `panicked` on stderr.
- `mcp`: closes stdout, sends a `ping`, closes stdin, then checks for exit 0 and no `panicked`.

Without the fix both tests fail (exit 101 with the panic, and exit 1 with `Broken pipe`). With it, `cargo test -p wordcraft-cli` and `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, and `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. The repro from the issue now exits 0.

Fixes #508

title: Dialogs: switching tabs keeps the window's top edge in place (#507)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause
`dialogs::show` built every dialog window with `.anchor(Align2::CENTER_CENTER, vec2(0, -40))`. egui re-applies an anchor every frame from the window's current size, so when a tab (Paragraph, Font, Borders and Shading, Table Properties…) changed the dialog's height, half the difference went to the top edge and the title bar and tab strip jumped up or down.

## Fix
One small positioning helper in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`, used by the shared dialog builder, so it covers every dialog:
- On the frame a dialog opens it is centred as before (`CENTER_CENTER`, −40 px).
- After that frame, `remember_dialog_top` stores the top edge that centring the measured size gives, keyed by the dialog's window id (egui temp data).
- From then on, `place_dialog` anchors the window `CENTER_TOP` at that offset, so a height change only moves the bottom edge and the OK/Cancel buttons. egui's `constrain` keeps a window that grows past the bottom on screen.
- The stored top is cleared on any frame with no dialog open, and a different dialog (different id) is centred anew. Dialogs were not movable before and still aren't, so dragging is unaffected.

## Test
`dialogs::tests::switching_paragraph_tabs_keeps_the_top_edge` (egui_kittest): opens the Paragraph dialog, cycles through Indents and Spacing, Line and Page Breaks, Asian Typography and back, checks that the OK button moves (so the tabs really differ in height) and that the tab strip's top y stays within 0.5 px. With the old anchor it fails (`[272.0, 317.0, 281.0, 272.0]`).

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib` pass. `docs/ui-parity.md` has a revision row.

Fixes #507

title: Paragraph dialog: mirror indents, same-style spacing, suppress line numbers, don't hyphenate (#512)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

The Paragraph dialog gains the options Word has and we lacked:

- **Indents and Spacing**: *Mirror indents* (the Left/Right labels become Inside/Outside while it is checked) and *Don't add space between paragraphs of the same style*.
- **Line and Page Breaks › Formatting exceptions**: *Suppress line numbers* and *Don't hyphenate*.

## How

- Model: new `ParaProps::mirror_indents` (`w:mirrorIndents`, ECMA-376 §17.3.1.18), read and written in DOCX (after `w:contextualSpacing`, schema order). `contextualSpacing`, `suppressLineNumbers` and `suppressAutoHyphens` already round-tripped and were already honoured by layout.
- Resolved paragraph now carries `mirror_indents` and `suppress_line_numbers`, so a style that suppresses line numbers works too (layout used to read only the direct property).
- Layout: a paragraph with mirrored indents keeps its line breaks (same width) and moves over by the indents' difference on even (left-hand) pages, so the left indent is the inside one. Shading and borders move with it.
- Dialog: OK adds only the options that changed since it opened to the existing `para.set` call (no new command; agents already set them via `para.set {"props": {"mirrorIndents": true, ...}}`). Contextual-spacing layout is untouched (left to #108).
- New strings (Mirror indents, Inside:, Outside:, Formatting exceptions) in all nine catalogs; Reveal Formatting names `mirrorIndents`.

## Tests

title: Spelling: common words like "desktop" are recognised (#520)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause
English spelling checks words against the public-domain **Moby Hyphenator II** list (`assets/hyphenation/en-us.dic`, ~165k words from the 1990s) plus a small hard-coded `EXTRA` array. The list loads in full (no truncation), but it predates everyday modern vocabulary: a probe of ~400 frequent words flagged 65, including `desktop`, `laptop`, `download`, `upload`, `spreadsheet`, `database`, `screenshot`, `inbox`, `offline`, `homepage`, `workplace`, `healthcare`, `mindset`. ## Fix
- New supplement **`assets/spelling/en-extra.txt`**: ~220 lowercase base forms, sorted, one per line, replacing the `EXTRA` array. - Every stem lookup (inflections, doubled consonant, prefixes) now checks the dictionary and the supplement. Suggestions include supplement words (`dekstop` → `desktop`).
- English path only. The other language PRs (#203, #208/#210, #346) are untouched.

## Word source and licence
The supplement is our own list, written for this repository (no other dictionary copied), MIT OR Apache-2.0, with a row in `ATTRIBUTION.md`. Moby itself is unchanged (public domain).

title: macOS packaging: strip extended attributes before signing and verify the DMG's app strictly (#525)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #525.

## Root cause

Confirmed from the script, not reproduced on macOS here: `package.sh` already ran `codesign --verify --strict --deep` on `WordCraft.app` **before** packaging, and the staging copy (`ditto`), `/Applications` symlink, `.background/` and `.DS_Store` don't touch the bundle. The only step between that passing check and the shipped image is `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs … ` + `hdiutil convert`. `makehybrid -hfs` writes a `com.apple.FinderInfo` (Finder location -1,-1) on every file and folder it puts into the HFS image, which `codesign --strict` rejects as "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed", inside the mounted DMG and on a `ditto` copy of it. This is the same failure and the same script lines PdfCraft fixed in storytold/pdfcraft#823, where it was reproduced (makehybrid with or without `-hfs-openfolder` adds FinderInfo to every file; `hdiutil create -srcfolder` adds none).

The DMG container check (`codesign --verify --strict "$DMG"`) passed, which is why the release job didn't catch it.

## Fix (`packaging/macos/package.sh`)

- **Build the DMG with `hdiutil create -srcfolder "$STAGE" -volname WordCraft -fs HFS+ -format UDZO -imagekey zlib-level=9`** instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while copying, which the old comment called flaky on CI ("Resource busy"), so it runs through `hdiutil_retry` (five tries, pauses of 10/20/30/40 s). Volume name stays `WordCraft`, so the `.DS_Store` alias still finds `.background/background.tiff`.
- **`xattr -cr "$APP"` before signing**, so no attribute from a copied source file (icon, font licences) can end up in the signed bundle.
- **Gate after signing the DMG (before notarizing it, so it fails fast):** mount the finished DMG read-only (`-nobrowse -noautoopen`), run `codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2` on the app inside it, `ditto` it out and run the same check on the copy, and, when notarizing, `spctl --assess --type execute -vvv` on the copy. …

title: AutoCorrect: TWo INitial CApitals, cAPS LOCK and table-cell capitals (#544)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

Three of Word's AutoCorrect capitalisation options, engine side:

- **Correct TWo INitial CApitals**: when a word of three or more letters is finished (space, punctuation or Enter) and it has two leading capitals followed by lowercase letters, the second capital is lowered (`WOrd` → `Word`). This runs before the replacement list, so `TEh` → `Teh` → `The`. Built-in exceptions: `CDs IDs PCs TVs DJs GBs KBs MBs TBs VMs`. Users can add their own with `tools.autocorrect {"addException": "…"}` and remove them with `removeException`.
- **Correct accidental usage of cAPS LOCK**: `wORD` → `Word` (three or more letters). `iOS`, `mRNA`, `tRNA`, `rRNA`, `cDNA`, `eSIM`, `eSATA`, `iSCSI` and `vCPU` are left alone. Word also switches Caps Lock off; there's no portable way to do that, so we only correct the word.
- **Capitalize first letter of table cells**: the first word in a cell's first paragraph is capitalised like a sentence start, under its own option. With the option off, it stays as typed.

## How

- New `Session::autocorrect_caps: AutoCorrectCaps { two_initial_caps, caps_lock, cap_cells, initial_caps_exceptions }`, all on by default as in Word. It's exported from the crate and serde-ready (camelCase) so a front end can keep it.
- `tools.autocorrect` takes `twoInitialCaps`, `capsLock`, `capCells`, `addException` and `removeException`, and reports them. Exception length and count are capped.
- Case changes replace one letter at a time, so each letter keeps its own formatting. All string handling is char-boundary-safe, with no unwrap or panic paths.
- Undo: the fixes run inside the existing AutoCorrect pass, so one Ctrl+Z right after the space undoes just the correction.

**Note on #476:** that PR's AutoCorrect Options dialog (`AutoCorrectPrefs`, which already has `cap_cells`) should expose these three toggles and the INitial CAps exceptions list. Either fold `AutoCorrectCaps` into `AutoCorrectPrefs` when it lands, or add the toggles there in a follow-up.

title: AutoFormat: +---+ tables, arrow bullets, smileys inside words, border-line undo (#546)
author: vangel76
body:
## What
Closes the remaining AutoFormat As You Type gaps from `docs/typing-parity.md`:

- **Tables:** `+---+------+` (plus signs around runs of hyphens, the whole paragraph) + Enter becomes a one-row table across the text width. Each column gets its share of the hyphens, and the caret goes into the first cell. The emptied paragraph stays after the table. This only fires for top-level body paragraphs, and a line with more than 63 columns (`MAX_COLS`) stays as text.
- **Arrow bullets:** `> `, `-> ` and `=> ` at the start of a paragraph start a bulleted list with an arrow bullet (➢ U+27A2, ➔ U+2794, ⇨ U+21E8). These are plain Unicode characters, using the existing symbol-font substitution (DejaVu Sans / Noto Sans Symbols), so nothing proprietary is needed. An arrow list doesn't join a plain • list.
- **Smileys inside words:** `:)` `:-)` `:(` `:-(` `:|` → ☺ ☹ 😐, also straight after a word (`ok:)` → `ok☺`).
- **Undo after a border line:** after `---` (and the other border lines) + Enter, Ctrl+Z restores the typed characters and removes the border, and the Enter stays. The `+---+` table works the same way. The plain Enter is recorded as its own undo step, as AutoFormat already does for lists.

All of these are behind the existing AutoCorrect/AutoFormat switch (`autocorrect_on`).

The behaviour follows Word's documented AutoFormat/AutoCorrect options. It was **not** keystroke-compared with Word, and the rows in `docs/typing-parity.md` are marked that way.

## How tested
New tests in `crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs` (keys go through the same commands as the keyboard):
- `plus_and_hyphen_line_becomes_a_table`: column ratio, caret in the first cell, undo, non-matching text, 64 columns stay as text
- `arrow_bullets`
- `smileys_are_replaced_inside_words_too`

title: Chinese documents: character-unit indents, .doc indents and line spacing, floating tables, blank pages (#534)
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #534

I opened the three files the reporter attached (two .docx, one .doc) only to see how WordCraft handles them: I rendered them to PNG/PDF and read their XML/sprm structure. None of their content is in this PR. The regression tests use hand-written XML or documents built in code.

## What the samples showed

**Form .docx (portrait, two tables).** The second table is a floating table placed on the page (`w:tblpPr w:vertAnchor="page"`, `w:tblOverlap="never"`), and its anchor comes after a first table that fills page 1. WordCraft drew it on page 1 at its page position, on top of the first table. That is the "tables from page 2 overlap page 1" symptom. Word puts it on page 2.

**Landscape .docx (two tables).** Between the tables there is a paragraph that starts with a page break. Page 1 is full, so the line holding only the break no longer fit. WordCraft moved that line to page 2, and the break then started page 3. The result was a blank page between the tables.

**Thesis .doc.**
- Every first-line indent was lost, so the body text had no two-character indent. The cause: `sprmPDxaLeft1` (0x8460) has a two-byte operand, but the reader expected four bytes. The older `sprmPDxaLeft1_80` (0x8411) wasn't read at all.
- Exact line spacing (a negative LSPD `dyaLine`) was decoded from the wrong bits. Exactly 20pt was read as 799pt, so each empty paragraph took a whole page: 49 pages instead of about 27.

**Character-unit indents in general.** Chinese documents set indents in characters: `w:firstLineChars`, `w:hangingChars`, `w:leftChars`, `w:rightChars`, and `sprmPDxc*` in .doc. Word measures them in the paragraph mark's font size, and a non-zero value wins over the points value. WordCraft ignored them. In these samples the stored points agree with the character values, so this isn't what caused the visible misalignment. It does go wrong when the two disagree, for example when a style sets indents only in characters.

## Fixes

- **Model:** `ParaProps` gets `indent_left_…

title: Find and Replace: special characters (^p, ^t, …) and wildcards (#543)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

Word's Find and Replace special characters and "Use wildcards" mode, for the dialog and for agents (`edit.find`, `edit.advancedFind`, `edit.replace`, `edit.replaceAll`).

- **Special codes in Find what:** `^p` `^t` `^?` `^#` `^$` `^^` `^l` `^m` `^n` `^b` `^+` `^=` `^s` `^~` `^-` `^w` `^g` `^%` `^v`, plus character codes `^nnn` / `^unnnn`. An unknown `^x` is read as a literal caret. New param `special: false` turns the codes off and reads the text literally.
- **Replace with:** the same codes, plus `^&` (the found text) and `^c` (the clipboard). With wildcards, `\1` to `\9` insert the groups.
- **Use wildcards** (`wildcards: true`): `?` `*` (shortest match) `[abc]` `[a-z]` `[!x]` `{n}` `{n,}` `{n,m}` `@` `<` `>` `( )`. Like Word, wildcard searches always match case.
- **Paragraph marks:** when the pattern contains `^p` (or `^13`/`^b`), the search reads runs of sibling paragraphs as one text with a mark between them, so matches can cross paragraph ends. A `^p` in the replacement splits the paragraph. Replace All is still one undo step. Tracked-deleted text still breaks matches, as before.
- **Options:** `matchPrefix`, `matchSuffix`, `ignorePunct`, `ignoreSpace`.
- **Dialog:** a "Use wildcards" checkbox (Match case and the word options grey out while it is on). A "Search Options" toggle shows Match prefix/suffix, the two Ignore options, Regular expressions (the old "Wildcards (regex)" checkbox, renamed) and a **Special ▾** menu. The menu inserts the code into whichever field last had focus, and its list changes with wildcards and between Find what and Replace with. The new strings are in all 9 catalogs, and the old "Wildcards (regex)" rows are removed.

## How

A new module, `crates/engine/src/cmd/find_pattern.rs`, translates Word patterns into the `regex-automata` engine we already depend on. That engine runs in linear time, so no pattern can backtrack catastrophically. Find what is capped at 1024 characters and `{n,m}` counts at 1000, the existing NFA size l…

title: Find: each Find Next in the dialog moves one match (#468)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #468.

**Cause.** The Find and Replace dialog ran `edit.find` and then `edit.findNext` on every Find Next click (and on Enter). `edit.find` already selects the first match after the caret, so the step after it moved one further. With `cat cat cat cat` the dialog only ever reached matches 2 and 4; with `cat cat` it stayed on the second.

**Fix.**
- `edit.findNext` and `edit.findPrevious` take the same optional search options as `edit.find` (`text`, `matchCase`, `wholeWord`, `regex`). Without options they behave as before (F3, Mod+G, Mod+Shift+G).
- The dialog sends one `edit.findNext` with its options per click, so a changed query or checkbox still takes effect immediately.

**Test.** `find_next_with_options_visits_every_match` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: four matches visit 0, 1, 2, 3 and wrap to 0; two matches alternate; Find Previous with options steps backwards; a new query given to `edit.findNext` applies at once.

**Checks (Windows 11, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc).** `fmt`, `clippy`, `assets`, `layers`, `wasm` pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes except two `wordcraft-ui-egui` tests that are not touched by this change and also fail without it on Windows:
- `paste_picture::tests::paste_inserts_clipboard_pixels` asserts that `/tmp/b.JPG` is an absolute path, which only holds on Unix.
- `zotero::tests::no_zotero_is_a_clear_error` timed out in one run and passed in another (connect to a closed port is slow on Windows).

The dialog itself was not clicked through in the running app; the change there is the one-line dispatch shown in the diff.

title: .doc import: inline pictures, floating pictures and basic shapes (#551)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

`.doc` (Word 97-2003) files kept their text but dropped every picture and drawing. `crates/docbin` now reads them from the OfficeArt records, written from the public specs [MS-DOC] and [MS-ODRAW]:

- **Inline pictures:** the PICF's `OfficeArtInlineSpContainer` (`MM_SHAPE` / `MM_SHAPEFILE`) plus its FBSE/BLIP. Size comes from `dxaGoal`/`dyaGoal` × `mx`/`my` less the crop, and crop and alt text (`wzDescription`) come from the shape properties. The older raw-image path is still there as a fallback.
- **Floating pictures and shapes:** `PlcSpaMom`/`PlcSpaHdr` anchors (character 0x08) are joined with the shapes of the drawings in `OfficeArtContent` (`fcDggInfo`). Placement comes from the SPA bounds and `bx`/`by`; `posrelh`/`posrelv`/`posh`/`posv` win when present. Wrap comes from `wr` plus `fBelowText` (square, tight, through, top-and-bottom, behind, in front), and wrap distances, rotation (with the turned-bounds swap) and flips are kept. Pictures come from the BLIP store.
- **Shapes:** rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, diamond, triangles, star, block arrows, heart, and lines/connectors, with fill and line colour and line width. Groups are flattened into one group coordinate space. Text boxes are linked to their `PlcftxbxTxt` / `PlcfHdrtxbxTxt` story by spid, and each story becomes a `PartKind::TextBox` part.
- **BLIP formats:** PNG, JPEG and TIFF are kept as they are. DIB gets a BMP header and is converted to PNG with the `image` crate (with size limits). EMF/WMF are inflated (zlib via `miniz_oxide`), and the existing metafile renderer draws them. Macintosh PICT is kept as a placeholder of the right size (grey box) and logged.
- **Hostile input:** record lengths are clamped to their parent, and nesting depth, record and anchor counts are capped. Decompression is size-limited, and the per-document picture byte cap still applies. Pictures referenced more than once are stored once.

title: Open legacy Word documents (.doc, Word 97-2003) and show why a file can't be opened
author: benimaru327
body:
## Problem

Sending a legacy `.doc` to WordCraft opened an empty window. The extension wasn't a known format, and the error (`unsupported format .doc`) only reached the log file.

## What this changes

- **Opens `.doc` (Word 97–2003), import only.** New reader `crates/formats/src/doc.rs`: main text through the piece table, character and paragraph formatting (style sheet included), lists, tables with merged cells, hyperlink fields, page breaks, and page size/margins of the last section. It maps to the existing `model::Flow`.
- **Says why a file can't be opened.** A document the user picked, dropped, chose from the recent list or launched the app with now gets a dialog on failure (`Dialog::Message`, `WordApp::open_document`). Commands run through the control channel/MCP still just return the error and never open a dialog.
- **Clear refusals.** Password-protected files (legacy and OOXML) and Word 6.0/95 files get a specific message.
- **Word extensions open by content.** A `.doc` that is really RTF or a renamed `.docx` opens with the right reader; a compound file named `.docx` no longer reports a zip error.
- **Save on a `.doc`** asks for a new name, since the format can't be written.
- One unrelated one-liner: `clippy::useless_format` in the Windows-only Read Aloud code (`cmd/tools.rs`), which stopped `cargo xtask ci` on Windows with current stable.

The reader is written from Microsoft's published Open Specifications **[MS-DOC]** and **[MS-CFB]**. title: Open and save Word XML Document (Flat OPC); open Word 2003 XML (#548)
author: vangel76
body:
## What
- **Word XML Document (Flat OPC `.xml`)**: opens and saves. Reading unpacks the `pkg:part`s (`pkg:xmlData` inline XML, `pkg:binaryData` base64) into an in-memory package (`Package::from_parts`) and runs the existing DOCX reader (`read_opened`); content types come from the part attributes. Namespaces declared on the package elements are carried onto each inline part. Writing runs the existing DOCX writer (`write_parts`, split out of `write_as`) and lays its parts out in one file (`<?mso-application progid="Word.Document"?>`, XML parts inline, binary parts in base64, 76-character lines). No reader or writer code is duplicated.
- **Word 2003 XML (`w:wordDocument`)**: opens (import only). ECMA-376 kept most of the 2003 vocabulary, so the file is rewritten as the package it corresponds to and read by the DOCX reader: hyphenated names (`w:sz-cs`, `w:first-line`, `w:h-ansi`), `w:fareast`, `w:vmerge`, `w:hlink` → `w:hyperlink` + relationship, `w:listPr` → `w:numPr`, `w:lists` (`w:listDef`/`w:list`, `w:nfc`) → numbering, `w:fonts/w:defaultFonts` → doc defaults, inline `w:hdr`/`w:ftr` → header/footer parts, inline footnotes/endnotes → notes parts, `aml:annotation` bookmarks, comments and tracked insertions/deletions, `w:binData` + `v:imagedata` → media parts, `o:DocumentProperties` → core properties. `wx:sect`/`wx:sub-section` are unwrapped and the last `w:sectPr` goes last.
- **Detection**: `.xml` is told apart by its root element (`sniff_xml`). Other XML gets "not a Word XML document" (new `DocxError::NotWordXml`).
- **UI/apps**: File › Export lists "Word XML Document (*.xml)" (translated in all 9 catalogs). `.xml` counts as a format that keeps everything, so Save/AutoSave work like `.docx`. `.xml` added to the open filters (desktop, web) and to the web MIME map.

title: Numbering: Chinese, Japanese and Korean number formats (一、二、三 …) (#534)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause

The sample in #534 numbers headings with `w:numFmt="chineseCounting"` and `w:lvlText="%1、"`. Two things went wrong:

1. **Unsupported format.** `NumFormat` only knew the Latin formats; `chineseCounting` fell back to decimal, so the label was `2、` instead of `二、`. Saving also wrote `decimal` back, so the format was lost.
2. **Wrong font for part of the label (the "letters").** The label `2、` gets its digit from the Latin face and its comma from a CJK fallback face. Layout split it into font runs but kept only the *last* run's style, and display drew **all** label glyphs with that face. The digit's glyph id was then looked up in the CJK font and showed up as some unrelated character. In the reporter's fonts that came out as letters; locally it rendered as hangul or as the wrong digit (`4、5、6、7` in the PNG, while the PDF text layer still said `2、3、4、5`).

A third problem showed in the same sample: a list level without `w:ind` got a 36pt indent on read. Word puts the label at the paragraph's edge.

## Fix

- `NumFormat` now has every ST_NumberFormat value (ECMA-376 §17.18.59). Every format round-trips, including ones we still draw as decimal (Hebrew, Arabic, Hindi, Thai…). Unknown values and `custom` read as decimal.
- New `doc::cjk_numbers`, written from the rules of each number system (values past a sequence's end fall back to decimal):
  - `chineseCounting` / `taiwaneseCounting`: 一…十, 十一…九十九, then digit by digit (一〇〇)
  - `chineseCountingThousand` / `taiwaneseCountingThousand`: 一百零一, 一千零一十, 一万, 一亿零一; one 零 per gap
  - `chineseLegalSimplified` (壹贰叁…壹拾), `ideographLegalTraditional` (壹貳參…)
  - `japaneseCounting` (十, 百一, 一万), `japaneseLegal` (壱拾, 壱阡), `japaneseDigitalTenThousand` (一万二三四五)
  - `koreanCounting` (십일), `koreanDigital` (일영), `koreanLegal` (하나, 열하나 … 아흔아홉), `koreanDigital2`
  - `ideographDigital` / `taiwaneseDigital` (一〇一), `ideographTraditional` (甲乙丙…), `ideographZodiac` (子丑寅…), `ideographZodiacTraditional` (甲子…癸亥)

title: Styles: Update to Match Selection takes the selection's formatting (#555)
author: vangel76
body:
## Root cause
`styles.updateToMatch` (Styles pane right-click › Update to Match Selection) only copied the **direct** run and paragraph formatting at the caret onto the style. When the selected text gets its look from its own style (Normal, Title, …), that direct formatting is empty, so Heading 2 didn't change. It then cleared the selected paragraph's direct formatting **without applying the style to it**, so the selection lost its look as well.

## Fix
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs`: the style now takes the selection's effective formatting: document defaults, then the paragraph style chain, then the character style chain, then direct formatting, all read at the start of the selection. This is applied as a diff against what the style currently gives. Properties that differ are set on the style. Properties the selection doesn't set at all are dropped, so they inherit again. Outline level, numbering and revisions are kept, so Heading 2 is still a level-2 heading. The selected paragraphs then take the style and drop only the direct formatting the style now carries, so a bold word stays bold. Character styles are updated the same way. Table and numbering styles are refused with an error. It is still one undo step.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/previews.rs`: tiles in the Home › Styles gallery had no right-click menu. They now have Update to Match Selection and Modify… (existing translated strings), like the Styles pane.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: revision row.

`update_heading_to_match_selection_takes_the_selections_formatting` (engine) builds a Heading 2 paragraph and a Normal paragraph with 20 pt, italic, red, centred. It selects the Normal paragraph and runs `styles.updateToMatch {"style":"Heading2"}`, then checks:
- Heading 2 now resolves to 20 pt, italic, red, centred and the Normal body font. The font comes from the selection's style, not from direct formatting, which is the case the old code missed.
- Heading 2 keeps outline level 2.

title: Paragraph dialog: OK keeps Exactly and At Least line spacing (#467)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #467.

**Cause.** The Paragraph dialog only edits line spacing as a multiple. `Dialog::open` reads Exactly and At Least as `1.0`, and `apply_paragraph` always sent `"lineSpacing": {"rule": "multiple", "value": line}`. So OK (and Tabs…) with nothing changed, or with only Keep with next changed, replaced Exactly 24 pt / At Least 24 pt with Multiple 1.0.

**Fix.** `Dialog::Paragraph` gets `line_was` (the value shown on open, `#[serde(skip)]` like `asian_was`). `apply_paragraph` takes `(line, line_was)` and puts `lineSpacing` into the `para.set` call only when the value changed. A changed value still sets a multiple, as before.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the dialog still can't show or set Exactly / At Least itself (no rule drop-down), and a paragraph with a fixed rule shows 1.0. Switching such a paragraph to exactly Multiple 1.0 through this dialog therefore isn't possible; `para.lineSpacing` and the ribbon's line-spacing menu still do it.

**Overlap.** #519 also changes `apply_paragraph`'s signature and the `Dialog::Paragraph` fields (adds `opts`/`opts_was`). Whichever lands second gets a small mechanical conflict; I'm happy to rebase.

**Test.** `dialogs::tests::paragraph_dialog_keeps_fixed_line_spacing`: for Exactly 24 and At Least 24, an unchanged OK and an OK with only Keep with next keep the rule; a changed value sets Multiple 1.5. Fails on the old code (`Multiple(1.0)` vs `Exactly(24.0)`). The existing paragraph dialog tests still pass.

**Checks (Windows 11, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc).** `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `assets`, `layers`, `wasm` pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes except `paste_picture::tests::paste_inserts_clipboard_pixels`, unrelated and failing on Windows on `main` too (asserts `/tmp/b.JPG` is absolute, Unix only; noted in #556).

The dialog was not clicked through in the running app; the test drives `Dialog::open` and `apply_paragraph`, which the OK and Tabs… buttons call.

title: Fix CJK fallback mixing serif/sans faces within one run
author: jeleesky
body:
Per-character fallback picks the first covering face in load order. With craft-fonts the bundled order puts BIZ UDMincho before Noto Sans CJK SC, so a run whose East Asian characters fall back (JIS-covered ideographs → Mincho, simplified-only → SC sans) can mix serif and sans glyphs even inside one word (分⽗类 监督学习 数据驱动).

Pick one face covering all of the run's East Asian characters when available (Word also uses a single font per run), keeping the existing per-character fallback when no single face covers them all.

Regression test: east_asian_run_uses_one_face_covering_the_whole_run in crates/fonts/src/lib.rs.

Note: not compiled or tested locally (no Rust toolchain on this machine) — please let CI run

title: fix(layout): match Word's contextual paragraph spacing
author: OPUZZLES
body:
Same-style paragraphs with contextual spacing only on the first paragraph retain too much space. A 12 pt after / 8 pt before pair leaves 8 pt instead of 0 pt; 10 pt after / 12 pt before leaves 12 pt instead of 2 pt. Box layout also suppresses the wrong side and retains extra gaps from the third paragraph onward.

Track each paragraph's contextual flag and remove its own contribution from the merged gap. Preserve style identity and the actual applied after-space. The current-main reconciliation retains automatic paragraph/list spacing, text frames, page-break handling and tracked-deletion layout. Contextual and automatic suppression remove the same gap at most once.

### Current evidence

The requested four-paragraph body/table regression remains present. title: Caret: glide and fade like Word for Windows; File › Options › Advanced › Animation turns it off
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Word for Windows doesn't move its caret instantly, and its caret doesn't blink by switching on and off. WordCraft's did both. Now it follows Word:

- **Keys and typing glide the caret.** Arrow keys, Home and End, a typed letter or space, Backspace: the caret slides from where it was to its new place in 100 ms, fast at first and settling (`cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1)`). The time is the same for one character and for a whole line.
- **A second key before it arrives** makes the caret snap to where it was heading and set off from there, so a held arrow key or quick typing never lags more than one step behind.
- **Clicks don't glide:** the caret is drawn where you clicked. Moves made by scripts, the control channel or MCP don't either (Word's automation moves jump too).
- **The blink fades.** 530 ms on and 530 ms off as before, but each change is a 100 ms fade. A key or a click turns the caret on the same way, from however visible it was, so a caret that was off fades in while it glides.
- **What never glides** (our choice; Word wasn't measured there): a caret that moved because the view changed (zoom, a resized window, scrolling, another document), one that wasn't drawn the frame before (a selection, the canvas without focus), and moves that start or end off screen.
- **Turning it off:** File › Options › Advanced has a new **Animation** section with "Animate the caret (it glides and fades)", on by default. `ui.caretAnimation {"value": true|false}` does the same for agents (no value reads it). It is kept in `ui.json`. Off, the caret jumps and blinks on and off exactly as before. The three texts are in the eleven catalogs: nine translations are mine and unreviewed, and echelon added the Turkish and Russian ones.
- **Agents and screenshots:** with egui's animations off, which the headless harness does, nothing glides or fades, so `ui_shot` and scripted pictures never catch a caret in flight.

## How Word was measured

title: Paste pictures: the file-path test passes on Windows
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

`paste_picture::tests::paste_inserts_clipboard_pixels` fails on Windows, so `cargo xtask ci` stops at its test step there:

```
assertion failed: names_picture_files("file:///home/me/shot%201.png\n/tmp/b.JPG\n")
```

`names_picture_files` accepts a bare path only when the system calls it absolute, and on Windows that takes a drive or a server: `/tmp/b.JPG` is a path everywhere else and a relative name there. The function is right (that is how a file manager's copied paths look on each system); the test's example was Unix-only.

The test now uses the system's own absolute path. On Windows it also checks the forms seen there: a drive path with forward slashes, a `\\server\share` path and a `file:///C:/…` address are accepted, and prose containing a path, a file that isn't a picture and a relative name are still refused. Only the test changes; the app behaves as before.

## Checks

Run locally on Windows with Rust 1.99, on upstream `1d4f741`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and the crate's tests with `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib` (all 159 pass, where one failed before; the one ignored test is the audit that is ignored by default).

It was the only test in the workspace failing on Windows: with it skipped, the other tests and the assets, layers and wasm steps of `cargo xtask ci` passed on the branch of #570, whose checks mention it.

Not run here: Linux and macOS. There `cfg!(windows)` is false, so the assertion is the original string and the Windows-only block does nothing. Left to CI.
