title: IME composition text uses document fallback fonts instead of boxes (#565)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #565.

While an input method (ibus with Avro Keyboard or Bijoy Bayanno) is composing, the canvas draws the composition text above the caret with the interface font (`theme::regular`). The interface fonts (Inter, Source Sans 3, the CJK faces) have no Bangla glyphs, so the composition showed as empty boxes. The committed text was fine, because the document layout already picks a fallback face for each character.

Now, when the composition holds characters outside the range the interface fonts draw (Latin, below U+0250), the canvas asks the document font database (`FontDb::fallback_for`, the same lookup the document layout uses) for a face that covers each one, and adds those faces as last-resort fallbacks to the interface font families (`theme::install_fonts_extra`). Each face is added once and kept, so the next composition in the same script needs no font reload. Faces over 16 MB (the big system CJK collections) are skipped; CJK keeps its existing interface fallback. When the interface language changes and the fonts are installed again, the added faces stay.

Nothing changes for text the interface fonts already draw: ASCII and characters below U+0250 never trigger a lookup.

Test: `preedit_gets_document_fallback_faces` (in `theme.rs`) checks that Bangla composition text gets one face (not one per character), that a face already added is not added again, that nothing is added when the interface fonts cover the text or for ASCII, and that the face ends up last in the interface's proportional family. It fails without the fix (the helpers do not exist).

title: Web: a CSV picked as recipients no longer turns the next TXT drop into recipients (#472)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #472.

**Cause.** On the web, Mailings > Select Recipients > Use an Existing List sets `recipient_list_pending`, and `drain_inbox` only took that flag when the arriving file was a `.txt`. A picked `.csv`/`.tsv` short-circuited the classification before the flag was read, and `mailings.recipients` keeps it (it is exempt from the reset in `execute`), so the flag outlived the picker. The next `.txt` dropped on the page then loaded as recipients and replaced the list that had just been chosen.

**Fix.** `drain_inbox` now takes the flag for every arriving file and puts it back only when that file did not load as recipients. Any recipient file (CSV, TSV, or a TXT asked for through the picker) ends the request, so later TXT drops open as documents through the usual Save Changes prompt. A `.txt` picked as the list still loads as recipients, and a cancelled picker is still cleared by the next command, as before. Only the web inbox path changes; the desktop picker loads the file directly and never used this flag for routing.

**Test.** `an_existing_list_picked_on_the_web_loads_recipients` now also picks a CSV through the picker, checks nothing is left pending, drops `notes.txt`, and checks it asks Save Changes like any document open; after Don't Save the TXT is the document body and the CSV's `Name, City` headers stay. Without the fix the flag stays set and the TXT replaces the recipients with no prompt.

title: Zotero: a pending citation no longer edits a replacement document (#470)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #470.

A Zotero command now remembers which document it started in (`Session::document_id`, the same check the Save Changes dialog and `file_dialogs` already use to tell an edit from a replacement). If New or Open replaces that document while Zotero is still working, each remaining call from that command gets the error "WordCraft replaced the document this command started in". The call is not applied, so the new document gets no field, no text and no undo step. This includes a `Document_displayAlert`: the app shows no question for a document that is no longer open.

The command still finishes normally from Zotero's side. `busy` clears when the connection ends, so the next command works as usual. Commands that keep the same document behave exactly as before.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs`: `ZoteroLink` stores the document id when a command starts. `poll` refuses calls once the session's document id is different.
- `docs/zotero.md`: one sentence about what happens when the document is replaced during a command.
- Test `a_pending_citation_does_not_insert_into_a_replacement_document`: runs the issue's call sequence (getActiveDocument, insertField, setCode, setText "(Sample, 2020)", complete) after `file.new {"template":"blank"}`. It checks that the new document stays empty and has nothing to undo. Without the fix the citation lands in the new document.

title: Zotero: a note with a picture stays when its citation moves to body text (#469)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #469.

When a citation moves out of a footnote or endnote (switching to an in-text style in Document Preferences, or deleting the field), `remove_empty_note` decided whether the note was empty by looking only at its text. A picture has no text, only an object placeholder, so a note holding the citation plus a picture counted as empty. The note, its body reference and the picture were all deleted.

Now the note is removed only if every object left in it is a zero-width marker (`InlineObject::is_marker`: field start/end, bookmarks, comment ranges) or the note's own reference mark. A picture, shape, chart, equation, field or any other object keeps the note, and the citation goes after the note's reference mark, as it already does for a note with other text.

The check is in `remove_empty_note`, so both callers (`Document_convert`/`Field_convert` and `Field_delete`) get the fix. A note that held only the citation is still removed, as `docs/zotero.md` describes.

Test: `a_note_with_a_picture_stays_when_its_citation_leaves` puts a picture in a citation's note, converts the citation to body text, and checks that the note and picture remain and the citation is in the body. It fails without the fix (the note is removed). It sits next to `a_note_with_other_text_stays_when_its_citation_leaves`, which covers the same case with text.

title: Linux: open/save works without a portal file dialog (#576)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #576

## Root cause (verified in rfd 0.17.2's source)
On Linux/BSD, rfd's default `xdg-portal` backend calls `org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser` over D-Bus (it loads libdbus at runtime). If that call fails, it runs `zenity`. If zenity is missing too, rfd logs an error and returns `None`, which is exactly what it returns when the user presses Cancel. So on labwc with only xdg-desktop-portal-wlr (which has no FileChooser) and no zenity, Open, Save As, Export and Insert Picture did nothing at all. rfd's API gives no way to tell "cancelled" apart from "couldn't show a dialog".

## What changed
- **Host (`apps/wordcraft/src/file_dialogs.rs`)**: before the rfd future is polled, the dialog's background thread checks whether a system dialog can appear: `zenity` on `PATH`, or else `dbus-send … Properties.Get org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser version` on the session bus. If neither is there, it answers `Err(reason)`. If `dbus-send` itself can't run, rfd still gets to try. `WORDCRAFT_FILE_DIALOG=builtin` forces the built-in browser on any platform. The rfd filters now come from a single table (`wordcraft_ui_egui::open_filters`).
- **Protocol**: `Services::file_dialog` now answers `FileDialogAnswer = Result<Option<String>, String>`. `Ok(None)` means cancelled, and `Err` means no system dialog could be shown.
- **Built-in browser (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_browser.rs`, native only, `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`)**: a folder path field with Up and Home folder, the subfolders and the files of the chosen type, a file name field (accepts names, absolute paths and `~/…`), and a type list. Save adds the chosen type's extension and asks before replacing a file. When it opens because the system dialog is missing, it explains how to get the system dialog (install xdg-desktop-portal-gtk or similar, or zenity). The answer goes into the same follow-up as the system dialog's: open, save and continue after "Save changes?", export, picture, recipients. It lists only folders the use…

title: File: recover unsaved work after a crash (#518)
author: OPUZZLES
body:
A desktop crash loses new drafts and unsaved edits. This adds local snapshots and File > Recover. Restore opens a dirty document without a path; Discard asks for confirmation. Recovery never saves over the original file.

A background worker snapshots at a fixed ten-second interval. Native JSON preserves media, opaque package parts and embedded source relationships. Each generation is decoded and compared with the full source model before publication. Failed writes retain the last valid generation, and discovery can fall back after corruption. Password-protected sessions skip plaintext recovery; applying a password first removes current recovery copies or refuses the action if cleanup fails.

### Current evidence

The new automation-root architecture test reproduced a mismatch on the recovery branch. The recovery store is a private, host-enabled profile store rather than document-path I/O. Only its exact storage module is exempted from that structural test. A focused runtime test confines document I/O to a separate folder, refuses absolute/traversal restore and discard IDs, restores a known snapshot into a dirty pathless document, explicitly discards it and verifies an unrelated original's bytes and directory remain unchanged. Commands cannot choose the host profile.

Lifecycle, failed-write, corruption, lock, password-cleanup, delayed-restore and full-model serialization controls pass. The approved Recover page remains alongside upstream's Save As page and current native printing/theme behavior.

title: Ribbon and context-menu Paste insert the system clipboard's text (#584)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #584.

Ctrl+V gets the system clipboard's text from egui's paste event and sends it as `edit.paste`'s `text`. The ribbon's Paste menu and the right-click Paste send `{}`, so the engine only had WordCraft's own copy to paste, and text copied in another program was ignored.

- New `Services::clipboard_text`. The desktop app fills it with arboard's `get_text`, as it already does for `clipboard_picture` (#45).
- `WordApp::run` reads it when a paste command comes without `text`. That covers Paste, Keep Text Only, Merge Formatting and Paste Special in the ribbon menu, plus the context menu's Paste. Commands that already carry `text` (the keyboard) are left as they are.
- The text is read before the clipboard picture, so ribbon Paste chooses what Ctrl+V chooses. Some programs copy text together with a bitmap of it (LibreOffice, spreadsheets), and Ctrl+V pastes the text in that case. A picture is still pasted when the clipboard has no text.
- Pasting something copied inside WordCraft keeps its formatting. Copy also puts the plain text on the system clipboard, and `edit.paste` uses its own rich copy when the text matches.
- Web: no change (`clipboard_text` is not set). The browser only gives clipboard contents to a paste event.

Test: `paste_without_text_reads_the_system_clipboard` (`crates/ui-egui/src/paste_picture.rs`). With text and a picture both on the clipboard, Paste, Keep Text Only and Merge Formatting each paste the text and no picture, and Paste Special offers the text format. Without the fix, Paste inserts the picture and the other commands paste nothing.

title: Render OOXML outline and shadow on glyphs
author: EdwardArvinius
body:
Propagate `CharProps` `outline` / `shadow` through `Draw::Glyphs` so raster paint matches `format.outline` / `format.shadow` (hollow stroked glyphs + offset drop shadow).

- Layout: carry flags on glyph draws; include in style-run bucketing
- Render: hollow white fill + colored stroke for outline; soft grey offset for shadow; keeps stem-darkening / synth-bold path for non-outline text
- PDF: ignore paint flags (fill path unchanged)

title: Tables: resize by dragging column borders, row borders and the corner handle (#217)
author: rabis7575
body:
Drag-to-resize for tables on the page, like Word. Closes #217; it follows the review notes on #49.

## What it does

- **Column border:** the pointer turns into a column-resize arrow. Dragging moves the border, and the column on its right gives or takes the difference, so the table keeps its width. With **Shift**, or on the table's right edge, only the column on the left changes. Columns stay at least 6 pt wide.
- **Row border:** dragging a row's bottom border sets that row's height ("at least").
- **Resize handle:** a small square shows past the table's bottom-right corner while the pointer is over the table. Dragging it scales every column and the rows on that page.
- A dashed guide shows the new border (or outline) while dragging, and **Esc** cancels the drag.

## How it addresses the notes on #49

- **One undo step per drag:** nothing is written while dragging. On release the app runs a single command, `table.resizeDrag`, with page coordinates, like `table.draw` / `table.eraser`. The selection is kept.
- **No stolen clicks:** borders are hit-tested in the existing canvas mouse handler, within 4 px of a border. There is no `ui.interact` per cell, and a merged cell hides the borders it covers. Clicks inside cells still place the caret, and a test checks this.
- **No unrelated changes:** two new files (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table_resize.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/table_resize.rs`) plus 21 added lines elsewhere for wiring and the translated label. No deletions outside the progress docs.
- **Geometry comes from the layout** (`Placed::Cell`), so autofit and percentage widths don't make the result jump. Row heights take off the cell margins and border bands that the layout adds to an "at least" height, so the row is drawn at the dragged height.
- `table.resizeDrag` isn't in `catalog.rs` because it is a mouse interaction, not a ribbon or menu feature. I'm happy to add a row if you'd like one.

## Tests

title: Windows: DX12 starts without shipped DXC DLLs (#603)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #603

## Root cause
wgpu 30's default DirectX 12 shader compiler, `Dx12Compiler::Auto`, uses DXC: it loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` the DLL search path finds first (no static DXC in this build). WordCraft ships neither `dxcompiler.dll` nor `dxil.dll`, so that copy belongs to some other program. Without a matching `dxil.dll` beside it, DXC warns `DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found`. wgpu-hal treats any non-empty DXC error blob as a compile error, so its `indirect_validation` compute pipeline fails. The device is then lost and `eframe::run_native` returns `WGPU error: Parent device is lost` (exit code 1) before the first frame. The reporter's tests match this: a matched DXC pair next to the exe works, a mismatched `dxil.dll` doesn't, and `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` works.

## What changed
- `apps/wordcraft/src/graphics.rs`
  - `dx12_compiler(env)`: returns FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) unless `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` (wgpu's own variable: `fxc`, `dxc`, `auto`, `staticdxc`) names another compiler. Unknown values log a warning and fall back to FXC.
  - `configure_dx12_compiler(options, compiler)`: sets `instance_descriptor.backend_options.dx12.shader_compiler` on eframe's `WgpuSetup::CreateNew`.
  - `configure` (Windows only) applies it first. The short-lived DirectX 12 adapter probe (#316) now gets the same backend options, so it doesn't load a stray `dxcompiler.dll` either.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`: updated a comment.
- New unit test `graphics::tests::dx12_compiles_with_fxc_unless_asked`.
- README: a troubleshooting paragraph in the Windows section. ROADMAP: a progress log row and a revision-history row.

This takes the same approach as storytold/lightcraft#484, written for this codebase. No DLLs are added to the repo or the installers.

## Verification
- `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p wordcraft`: ok (cross-check from Linux)
- `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p wordcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: …

title: Fonts: system fallback reads each font file once (#605)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #605

Thanks @LouisGue for the detailed report: the root cause, the repro script and the `strace` numbers made this quick to pin down. A test build on your machine is very welcome.

## Root cause
`FontDb::system_fallback()` walked the whole system font catalog for every distinct character no loaded font covered: it read and parsed each file under 40 MB, then remembered the miss for that one character only. N distinct uncovered characters meant N full reads of every installed font, on the layout thread.

## What changed (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`)
- **Coverage index.** The new `CoverageIndex` lists the cataloged font files and stores each file's coverage as sorted, disjoint code point ranges (`Box<[(u32, u32)]>`, not a set of characters). A file is read once, the first time a fallback search reaches it. Later searches answer from the ranges and read a file again only to load it, once, when it maps the character. Startup is unchanged: the catalog scan still reads only the `name`/`fvar` tables, and indexing happens lazily in the fallback path, so it stops early when a file is found, as before.
- **Same search order and results.** The preferred families (RTL list, `SYSTEM_FALLBACKS`) come first, then files in path order. On a mixed Tangut / Thai / CJK / Ext‑G sample, the PDF embeds the same fonts before and after.
- **Rescans** (`load_system_fonts`): a catalog generation counter makes the index pick up new files and keep the ranges of files still installed.
- **Safety nets:** each preferred fallback family is tried once, so a family that fails to load isn't re-read for every character. The miss set is capped at 65,536 entries and starts over when full. Indexing a damaged file is bounded: at most 256 faces, a budget of 4×0x110000 cmap mappings per file, at most 131,072 ranges kept, and file size checked again while reading (TOCTOU). No new panics or `unsafe`.
- `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` gating is unchanged for the new state. Web is unaffected.

title: fix: protect original files during native saves
author: OPUZZLES
body:
Native saves use a predictable `<document>.tmp` path. An occupied file is overwritten and removed; a link can redirect the write into the original or a neighbouring file. A failed replacement also leaves a temporary DOCX behind.

Create an exclusively owned sibling temporary file instead, write and synchronize it, close it, then replace the destination. Pre-replacement errors retain the original bytes and attempt to clean up only the owned temporary file. Unix temporary files start at mode `0600`; replacement retains an existing regular file's basic permissions. Serialization and password encryption remain unchanged.

### Evidence and validation

Two fresh synthetic CLI replays reproduced the failures on main `1d4f741`. The fixed CLI passed all seven cases:

| Case | Main | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Existing temporary-name file | Overwritten and removed | Sibling bytes retained; edited DOCX reopens |
| Existing temporary-name directory | Save blocked | Directory retained; save succeeds |
| Temporary-name link to original | Reported success; unreadable self-link | Readable edited destination; link retained |
| Temporary-name link to neighbour | Neighbour overwritten; destination becomes a link | Neighbour unchanged; regular edited destination |
| Missing parent / blocked destination | Original unchanged; blocked replacement leaves a temporary file | Original unchanged; no owned temporary file remains |
| Normal save | Edited DOCX reopens | Edited DOCX reopens |

The immutable synthetic input kept SHA-256 `66cf9fefaac91550f6495525c001c65e7628ab2a6885ebda63767d78ea8e5d0b`. All neighbours kept their hashes in the fixed replay; failed saves kept the original document hash. No Word-operated or company documents were used.

- Eleven focused integration/unit cases cover original/neighbour protection, failed and successful Save As state, encrypted saves, Unix permissions, injected partial/complete preparation errors and overlapping prepared saves.

title: DOCX: theme colours and theme fonts take precedence over the fixed values, as in Word
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## What was wrong

When a run or style property names both a theme value and a fixed value, ECMA-376 says the theme value supersedes the fixed one, and Word renders it that way. The DOCX reader did the opposite:

- **`w:color`** read only `w:val`. A heading written as `<w:color w:val="4472C4" w:themeColor="accent1" w:themeShade="BF"/>` stayed blue even when the document theme's accent1 is green. Word draws it as accent1 darkened 25%.
- **`w:rFonts`** preferred `w:ascii` over `w:asciiTheme` (and `w:hAnsi` over `w:hAnsiTheme`). A heading with `w:ascii="Calibri Light" w:asciiTheme="majorHAnsi"` showed Calibri Light (or a sans fallback) instead of the theme's major font.

## Fix

All changes are in `crates/docx/src/read`:

- `PropCtx` now holds the theme's colour scheme and the `w:clrSchemeMapping` from settings.
- A new `PropCtx::theme_color` resolves `w:themeColor` through that mapping. It handles `text1`/`background1`/`text2`/`background2` (defaults dk1/lt1/dk2/lt2), `dark1`…`light2`, `accent1`–`accent6`, `hyperlink` and `followedHyperlink`. It then applies `w:themeTint` / `w:themeShade` (hex bytes) to the HSL luminance:
  - tint: `L·t + (1 − t)`
  - shade: `L·s`
  
  This reuses the existing DrawingML `adjust_lum` helper.
- The theme colour takes precedence in three places:
  - `w:color`
  - `w:u`'s underline colour
  - `w:shd`'s `w:themeFill` (with `w:themeFillTint` / `w:themeFillShade`) for run, paragraph, table, cell and table-style shading
  
  To support this, `shd_fill` and `tcpr` now go through `PropCtx`.
- If the package has no theme part, the fixed colour is kept, as before.
- Styles are read before `settings.xml`, so the reader now picks up `w:clrSchemeMapping` before the styles.
- `w:rFonts` now uses this order: `asciiTheme`, then `ascii`, then `hAnsiTheme`, then `hAnsi`. An explicit `w:ascii` still beats a theme font that's given only for `hAnsi`.
- The model has no theme-colour reference, so saving writes the resolved colour as `w:val`. Re-reading the f…

title: fix(ui): anchor dialogs from top edge so tab changes do not jump vertically (#507)
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #507.

### Root Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:946`, modal dialogs were anchored to the viewport using `.anchor(egui::Align2::CENTER_CENTER, egui::Vec2::ZERO)`. When switching tabs in multi-tab dialogs like the Paragraph dialog (where the second tab has fewer controls and therefore a smaller vertical height), egui re-calculated `CENTER_CENTER` based on the new smaller height. This caused the dialog window to shift downward and vertically jump the tab strip under the mouse cursor.

### Fix
- Changed the dialog anchor to top-centered `.anchor(egui::Align2::CENTER_TOP, egui::vec2(0.0, 100.0))` in `dialogs.rs`.
- The top edge of the dialog remains stable regardless of differing tab content heights, preventing the tab bar from jumping when toggling tabs.

title: fix(ui): advance find by one occurrence on Find Next (#468)
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #468.

### Root Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:1219-1235`, clicking **Find Next** in the Find & Replace dialog was running `edit.find` unconditionally followed by `edit.findNext`. 
- `edit.find` found the current match and advanced the selection to it.
- `edit.findNext` immediately advanced the selection again to the next match.
This caused the search to skip every alternate match when clicking Find Next.

### Fix
- Track whether the search query and options have changed since the last find.
- On **Find Next**, run initial `edit.find` only if the query or search parameters changed; otherwise, run `edit.findNext` once.
- Subsequent Find Next clicks advance smoothly through every single occurrence in document order.

title: fix(ui): read character spacing and font effects back into Font dialog (#552, #466)
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #552 and fixes #466.

### Root Cause
1. In `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs:488`, `format.state` only serialized basic character formatting (font, size, bold, italic, underline, color, etc.) but omitted `spacing` (character spacing pt), `small_caps`, `caps`, and `hidden` effects (#552).
2. In `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:689-694`, when initializing the Font dialog from current selection formatting (`st`), the character spacing field and effect checkboxes were defaulted to empty/false rather than read back from the engine selection state (#466).

### Fix
- Exposed `spacing`, `smallCaps`, `caps`, and `hidden` in `format.state` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`.
- Read and populated `spacing`, `small_caps`, `caps`, and `hidden` from the state JSON into the dialog state when opening the Font dialog in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`.

title: fix(ui): preserve fixed line spacing when untouched in Paragraph dialog (#467)
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #467.

### Root Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`, the Paragraph dialog has a Line Spacing dropdown (e.g. Single, 1.5, Double, Multiple), but does not support selecting or entering custom fixed spacing like `Exactly` or `AtLeast`. When opening the Paragraph dialog on a paragraph with `Exactly` or `AtLeast` line spacing, the dialog mapped it to `Single` (or multiple = 1.0) and unconditionally submitted `lineSpacing` when clicking OK. This unintentionally overwrote the fixed line spacing even if the user never touched the Line Spacing controls.

### Fix
- Stored the initial `line_was: f32` when opening the Paragraph dialog.
- In `apply_paragraph`, only submit the `lineSpacing` property to the formatting command if the user actually modified the line spacing value in the dialog.
- Paragraphs with existing fixed spacing retain their exact settings when modifying other paragraph properties (e.g., margins, indentation, alignment).

title: fix(table): delete all selected columns in Delete Columns (#431)
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #431.

### Root Cause
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:456`, `table.deleteColumn` only inspected the focus cell position to determine which column index to delete (`let col = c.min(grid.len().saturating_sub(1));`). When the user selected multiple columns across the table (or a rectangular range of cells spanning several columns), Delete Columns deleted only the single column containing the caret/focus cell and ignored all other selected columns.

### Fix
- In `table.deleteColumn`, collected all unique column indices across `s.selected_cells` (or fallen back to the focus cell).
- Deleted the selected columns in reverse index order (from highest to lowest index) so earlier indices remain valid throughout deletion.
- Added engine unit test verifying multi-column deletion across selected cells.

title: fix(paragraph): do not format adjacent paragraph when selection ends at offset 0 (#418)
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #418.

### Root Cause
In `crates/doc/src/edit.rs:299`, `format_paragraphs` iterated over all paragraph paths between selection endpoints `a` and `b` (`doc.paths_between(&a, &b)`). When selecting text to the end of a paragraph, selecting through the paragraph break places endpoint `b` at offset `0` of the subsequent paragraph. Because `paths_between` includes `b.path`, `format_paragraphs` applied paragraph alignment (e.g. Center, Right, Left) to the adjacent unselected paragraph as well.

### Fix
- In `format_paragraphs`, when `a != b`, if the iteration reaches `p == b.path && b.off == 0 && b.path > a.path`, skip `p`.
- Formats only the paragraphs that actually contain selected characters, leaving the next paragraph at offset 0 untouched.
- Added unit tests verifying paragraph formatting ignores endpoint offset 0 of the succeeding paragraph.

title: fix(format): preserve formatting runs and update selection on changeCase
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #420 and fixes #421.

### Root Cause
1. In  ormat.change_case, when changing case where UTF-8 byte length changes (e.g. \ß\ -> \SS\), the code was deleting the entire range and replacing it with a single run formatted as the first character, blowing away subsequent runs' formatting (#421).
2. Selection endpoints (\s.sel.anchor\ and \s.sel.focus\) were never updated to account for the byte length difference \delta\, causing the selection to become desynchronized or point past paragraph bounds and crash (#420).

### Fix
- Perform character-by-character conversion and map converted characters across runs within the affected slice.
- Preserve each run's formatting \props\, adjusting each run's \len\ to match its converted text.
- Re-index selection offsets in the affected paragraph so endpoints accurately reflect the new character boundaries and offsets.
- Added unit tests covering multi-run formatting preservation and selection byte desync.

title: fix(export): preserve active document path and dirty flag on copy export
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
Fixes #168.

### Root Cause
When exporting a document copy in other formats (DOCX, ODT, RTF, etc.), the completed export picker was routing through  ile.saveAs. This:
1. Re-pointed the active desktop document's path (s.path = Some(path)) to the exported copy file.
2. Reset s.dirty = false, discarding the modified indicator and leaving unsaved changes unrepresented in the active document.
3. On web, the successful download callback similarly cleared self.session.dirty because it treated it as a full saveAs.

### Fix
- Introduced a dedicated  ile.export engine command that writes a document copy using save_path_with without modifying s.path or clearing s.dirty.
- Updated AfterPick::Export in crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialogs.rs to dispatch to  ile.export instead of  ile.saveAs.
- Updated web download handler in crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs so that  ile.export streams the copy download without resetting self.session.dirty.
- Added unit tests in both wordcraft_engine and wordcraft_ui_egui to ensure exported copies do not adopt the active document path or reset the dirty state.

title: Tables: select, insert and move with the mouse; double-click a border to AutoFit
author: rabis7575
body:

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across WordCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for WordCraft.

title: Complex scripts: shape Myanmar, Khmer and Indic text; caret and line breaks respect syllables (#604)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Myanmar text didn't shape: the vowel sign ေ (U+1031) wasn't drawn before its consonant and stacked consonants didn't form. The fallback font also drew it in a Black (extra-bold) weight, and long Myanmar paragraphs never wrapped. This PR fixes shaping, caret movement, Backspace and line breaks for Myanmar, and the same changes apply to Khmer and the Indic scripts.

- **Shaping:** text is shaped one script at a time. Before, the whole run was shaped as whatever script its first letter used, so in fonts that also cover Latin (Padauk, Myanmar Text) the Myanmar, Khmer and Indic shapers never ran.
- **Font fallback for complex scripts:**
  - It prefers fonts with OpenType layout tables and each script's own families (Myanmar Text, Noto Sans Myanmar, Padauk…). Apple's AAT-only fonts come last, since the shaper can't use them.
  - It loads the whole family, so text gets the regular weight instead of Black.
- **Caret and clusters:** caret stops and layout clusters never split a syllable. This covers the Myanmar vowel signs ာ and း, stacked consonants and Khmer subscripts.
- **Line breaks:** Myanmar, which has no spaces, now wraps between syllables.
- **Backspace and Delete:** in Brahmic scripts Backspace removes one character (a vowel sign or a stacked consonant), and Delete removes the whole syllable. Latin text is unchanged.

**Tests:**
- `doc::cluster::tests`, `fonts::script::tests`.
- `layout::tests_complex`: the cluster and line-break tests don't need installed fonts and fail without the fix. The shaping tests skip when no Myanmar font is installed.
- `engine::tests_typing::{myanmar_typing_steps_by_syllable_and_backspaces_by_sign, indic_and_khmer_backspace_removes_one_character}`.

`cargo xtask ci` passes after merging `main`.

**Not covered yet:**
- Khmer, Thai and Lao still wrap only at spaces; wrapping them needs a dictionary.
- The macOS AAT-font ordering is untested on a Mac.
- Myanmar caret and Backspace behaviour follows standard Windows/macOS behaviour; I haven'…

title: Print Markup: comments in PDF, print, images and text copies (#589)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Comments were missing from every printed, exported or converted copy. This adds **Print Markup**: a print setting, as in Word, that puts a document's comments into its copies.

- **PDF, print and PNG:** each page gets a markup area on the right. Each comment anchored on the page gets a balloon there, with the author's colour stripe, the author's name, the comment text and its replies, and a leader line from the text it comments on. The page is scaled down to fit the paper. Tracked changes are marked up too.
- **HTML, Markdown and plain text:** the copy ends with a numbered list of the comments, each with its author, the text it comments on, what it says and its replies.
- **How to turn it on:**
  - The UI: a Print Markup checkbox in File › Print.
  - Commands: `file.printMarkup` (no undo step, since it isn't part of the document), or a `markup` param on `file.save`, `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf` and `file.exportPng`.
  - The CLI: `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf --markup`.
- **Hostile documents:** comment, reply and parent-chain counts are capped. Balloons that don't fit are clipped to the page, and comments with no room on a full page are left out.

**Tests:** layout tests for the balloons, a PDF test, engine tests and text-format tests. The new strings are in every interface catalog. `cargo xtask ci` passes after merging `main`.

title: Add fonts at run time: Add Font…, drop a font file, font.add (#582)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Users can now add a font without rebuilding WordCraft.

- **Ways to add one:**
  - **UI:** Home › Font › **Add Font…** at the end of the font list (ribbon and mini toolbar), or drop a font file on the window.
  - **Commands:** `font.add` (`{"path"}` or `{"data": base64, "name"}`), `font.list` and `font.remove`, for agents, the CLI and MCP.
- **Formats:** TTF, OTF, TTC, WOFF and WOFF2. WOFF and WOFF2 are unwrapped with [`wuff`](https://crates.io/crates/wuff), a pure-Rust MIT crate whose brotli and zlib decoders were already in the dependency tree.
- **Kept between runs:**
  - **Desktop:** added fonts are copied into the app's `fonts` folder and load at start-up.
  - **Web:** the browser keeps them (`font_store.rs`).
  - Added fonts appear in the font list at once and render, shape and export to PDF like installed fonts.
- **Checked before anything is added:** files are capped at 50 MB, and every face must parse and map characters. A user font only adds faces; it never replaces a bundled or system face that's already loaded, so documents that don't use it keep their metrics.

**Not in this PR:** adding a font from a link (a Google Fonts `css2` URL or a direct `.ttf` URL). `font.add {"url"}` returns a clear "not available yet" error. That part needs a network fetch, which belongs with the HTTP client that the LanguageTool PR (#575) introduces, so it's a follow-up and this PR leaves #582 open.

**Tests:** `engine::tests_fonts` covers add, list and remove, junk bytes and oversized files being rejected, and an added font being measured, plus tests in `fonts::fontdb::user`. `cargo xtask ci` passes after merging `main`.

title: Table: a vertical merge lays out and hit-tests as one cell (#640)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #640

**Root cause.** `layout_table` pushed one `Placed::Cell` per row for every cell, each only as tall as its own row, continuation cells of a vertical merge included. title: Opt-in LanguageTool spelling and grammar checking, public or self-hosted server (#575)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Adds opt-in spelling and grammar checking by [LanguageTool](https://languagetool.org), using either the public server or a self-hosted one.

- **Settings:** File › Options › Proofing › "Check spelling and grammar with LanguageTool".
  - Off by default, because the text is sent to the server.
  - Server address: the public `https://api.languagetool.org` by default, or your own, e.g. `http://localhost:8081`.
  - Optional username and API key. The key is never logged and never returned.
  - Language: detect automatically, or each paragraph's proofing language.
- **Checking:** paragraphs are checked in the background, debounced and paced to the server's rate limit, so typing never waits. Results appear as the usual spelling and grammar squiggles, with suggestions in the context menu, exactly like the built-in checker.
- **Offsets:** LanguageTool reports offsets in UTF-16 code units. They're mapped to document positions safely, which matters for emoji and CJK; out-of-range offsets are clamped.
- **Errors:** timeouts, server errors and rate limits are handled without disturbing editing.
- **For agents:** `ui.languageTool` reads or changes the settings and reports status (checked, checking, error).
- **New crate `wordcraft-languagetool`:**
  - Request and response handling and a background worker.
  - HTTPS goes through `ureq` (rustls) on desktop only.
  - The browser build has no checker yet and says so.
  - The proofing crate takes results from an external checker (`proof::external`).
  - The new crate's place in the layers is registered in `xtask layers`.
- **Clean room:** it only talks to the server's public HTTP API; no LanguageTool code is included.

**Tests:** `languagetool::tests` (no network) cover response parsing, the UTF-16 offset mapping with emoji and CJK (proptest), request building, settings and mapping results to proofing issues. The 12 new interface strings are in every catalog. `cargo xtask ci` passes after merging `main`.

Fixes #575

title: Large documents: benchmark and incremental pagination (#554)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Large documents had never been measured: only the 188-page sample had a benchmark. This adds a large-document benchmark and makes typing in long documents re-lay out only what changed.

**Benchmark:** `cargo xtask bench [--pages N] [--keys K]` (or the `large_doc_bench` example) builds a synthetic book in code, with long paragraphs, headings, pictures, tables, footnotes and fields. It times what the app does: open, first layout, a keystroke at the start, middle and end, rendering visible pages, save and PDF export.

**Fixes:**
- **Incremental pagination** (`layout::incremental`): page-builder state is saved at each block, so after an edit layout resumes from the edited paragraph and stops once the rest of the document lines up again. It no longer places every block.
- **Caching:** the keep-with-next lookahead and table-cell layout keys are cached, so unchanged content isn't measured again.

**Numbers** (500-page target, which came out at 511 pages, with 200 pictures, 100 tables and 250 footnotes; release build at nice 19):

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| First layout | 333 ms |
| Open .docx | 20 ms |
| Save .docx | 33 ms |
| Keystroke at start / middle / end (command + re-layout) | 2.9 / 3.1 / 2.8 ms |
| …re-laying out | 1–2 paragraphs, placing 7–10 of 2,342 blocks |
| Same re-layout placing every block (the old path) | 14.2 ms |
| Render one page while scrolling | 1.1 ms |
| Render 3 visible pages (warm / cold) | 3.1 / 5.0 ms |
| PDF export (25 MB) | 1.06 s |

These are recorded in `docs/layout-parity.md#performance`. Gap #20 in `docs/gaps.md` is narrowed but stays open: real-world corpus documents and PDF export are still to be profiled.

**Tests:** `engine::tests_perf` checks counters rather than wall-clock time: a keystroke in a big document re-lays out only from the edited paragraph and places only a handful of blocks, and incremental results match a full layout. `cargo xtask ci` passes after merging `main`.

Fixes #554

title: Security: pictures travel in the reply, exported links keep only safe targets (#678, #679)
author: petycomp
body:
Fixes #678 and #679, found in a read-only security review of `main` (dba6e66). No High findings in that review; these were the only two concrete issues.

## #678 — predictable temp files from the control channel and the MCP bridge
- `ui.render` and `ui.screenshot` without a `path` now return the PNG as base64 `png` in the reply (the same shape the headless MCP `ui.render` already used) instead of writing `/tmp/wordcraft-page.png` / `/tmp/wordcraft-screenshot.png`, where another local user could plant a symlink that `std::fs::write` would follow. A given `path` behaves exactly as before.
- The `--connect` bridge's `render_page` and `screenshot` tools use the in-reply PNG and no longer round-trip through `temp_dir()/wordcraft-mcp-*.png`; the headless and app branches of `render_page` collapse into one.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` updated.

## #679 — `javascript:` and other schemes written into exported `href`
- New `wordcraft_doc::link` (L1, so every layer can share it): `is_web_or_mail_link` (exact, for handing a link to the OS; `canvas::is_followable_link` now delegates to it) and `is_safe_href` (web, mail, `#bookmark` or relative path; the scheme is read after dropping ASCII controls and spaces, as browsers do, so `java\nscript:` and `\tjavascript:` count as scripts).
- HTML and Markdown exporters write a link only when `is_safe_href`; otherwise the text is plain. The HTML importer uses the same rule (it previously only dropped literal `javascript:`).

## Tests (written first, watched fail)
- `wordcraft_doc::link::tests` — the two predicates against the canvas test's corpus plus `vbscript:`, `data:`, split/whitespace-prefixed `javascript:`.
- `formats::tests::exported_links_keep_only_safe_targets` — a paragraph with eight links exported to HTML and Markdown: scripts never appear, text is kept, safe links still export as links.
- `mcp::tests::render_and_screenshot_through_the_app_use_no_temp_file` — a fake app backend records the calls: never asked for a `path`, pi…

title: Tables: the right-click menu offers the table's commands
author: rabis7575
body:
Builds on #637 (it uses Select Column and the whole-cell selection), so it's stacked on it until
it merges; after that a rebase leaves only this change.

Right-clicking a table cell offered only Insert, Delete (rows, columns, table) and Merge Cells.
Now its table items follow what is selected, as Word's do (checked against Word 2019 for
Windows), all through commands that already exist:

| Selection | Table items |
|---|---|
| caret in a cell | Insert ▸, Delete Cells, Split Cells, Text Direction, Table Properties… |
| several cells | Insert ▸, Delete Cells, Merge Cells, Text Direction, Table Properties… |
| whole columns | Insert ▸, Delete Columns, Merge Cells, Distribute Rows, Distribute Columns, Text Direction, Table Properties… |
| whole rows | Insert ▸, Delete Rows, Merge Cells, Distribute Rows, Distribute Columns, Text Direction, Table Properties… |
| the whole table | Insert ▸, Delete Table, Distribute Rows, Distribute Columns, AutoFit ▸, Text Direction, Insert Caption…, Table Properties… |

Insert ▸ lists Columns to the Left / Right, then Rows Above / Below, as Word does. Table
Properties… and Insert Caption… open their dialogs, like the ribbon's buttons. Labels reuse the ribbon's, so
they're already translated; the two new ones ("Table Properties…", "Insert Caption…") are in all
fifteen catalogs.

**A right-click beside selected cells moves the caret there**, as in Word (checked). With a
column selected, a right-click on a cell of another column in the rows between its first and last
cell counted as "inside the selection" (it lies between the selection's ends in the text), so the
selection stayed and the menu then acted on the column instead of the cell clicked. A right-click
on a selected cell still keeps the selection, so the menu acts on it. This check is a small block

title: Menu buttons grey out while their command is disabled (#658)
author: dkhlapov

title: Ribbon groups shrink to fit the window (#662)
author: dkhlapov
body:
**Builds on #703 (#654) → #699 (#653) → #698 (#658) → #697 (#659).** Those commits appear here until they merge.

At a 1440 pt wide window the Home tab didn't fit: the last groups were cut off behind a scroll chevron. Groups now shrink to fit, from the right:

1. **Compact:** small buttons drop their labels. The tooltips keep the names.
2. **Collapsed:** the group folds into one drop-down button (the group's icon and name). Its menu holds the whole group as designed.
3. **Given back:** a group that still fits after a wide one shrinks returns to its full layout. Collapsing Styles alone frees enough room, and big-button groups like Voice gain nothing from collapsing.

Scrolling with the chevrons stays as the fallback when even fully collapsed groups don't fit.

**How it works:** new module `ribbon_fit`.
- Each group records its width at each level as it draws. Each tab remembers its group order.
- At the start of every frame, the pure `plan()` picks every group's level from those widths and the available width.
- Widths not measured yet are estimated, and the plan settles within a frame or two.
- It works for every tab, including custom ones.

**Results** (headless screenshots of the Home tab):

| Window width | Result |
|---|---|
| 1440 pt | Everything fits; only Styles is folded |
| 1100 pt | Everything fits; only Styles is folded |
| 800 pt | Font and Styles are folded; every group is still visible, with no scrolling |

**Tests:** `ribbon_fit::tests` covers fitting as designed, shrinking from the right, giving back, estimates and junk numbers (NaN, infinity). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Fixes #662

body:
Closes #700. Builds on #600 (it drags borders the same way), so it's stacked on it until it
merges; after that a rebase leaves only this change. It doesn't depend on #637.

With the caret in a table, the rulers now show the table, as Word's do:

- **Column markers** on the horizontal ruler at the column borders of the caret's row (past the
  table's left edge), and **row markers** on the vertical ruler at the bottom of each of the

  on the ruler or on the page.

  were placed as if the paragraph started at the page's margin, so in any column but the first the
  indent markers sat far from the text.

Layout gains `cell_margins` (a cell's own margins, else the table's, else Word's) so the ruler uses
exactly what the layout does. UI: `crates/ui-egui/src/table_ruler.rs`; `table_resize.rs` starts a
drag from a ruler marker (`grab`) and tells the ruler where a dragged border is (`moved`), sharing

title: Bidi: auto-detect RTL paragraph direction when typing Kurdish, Arabic and Hebrew
author: Hevarh1
body:
### Problem
When writing in Kurdish, Arabic, Hebrew or other right-to-left scripts in a new or default paragraph, the base direction defaulted to Left-to-Right (`bidi: None` resolved to LTR).
Under LTR base direction:
- Characters were pinned to start at the left margin (`x = 72.0`).
- Visual reordering placed each newly typed RTL character at the left edge of the run.
- The caret jumped back to the start of the line (`x = 72.0`) on every keystroke, and jumped to the far right on space keys (due to UAX #9 rule L1).

### Solution
1. **UAX #9 Rule P2/P3 Auto-Detection**: Added `wordcraft_doc::bidi::first_strong_is_rtl` to check whether the paragraph's first strong directional character belongs to an RTL script (Arabic, Kurdish, Hebrew, etc., or RTL mark `\u{200F}`).
2. **Layout Fallback**: In `crates/layout/src/para.rs`, unassigned paragraph direction (`p.props.bidi.is_none()`) resolves to `rp.bidi = true` if the text starts with RTL script.
3. **Typing Promotion**: In `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs` (`type_text`), when typing into an unassigned paragraph, if the text starts with an RTL character, the paragraph is automatically promoted to RTL (`p.props.bidi = Some(true)`), matching Microsoft Word's behavior.
4. **Regression Tests**: Added unit tests in `crates/doc/src/bidi.rs` and an end-to-end typing regression test in `crates/engine/src/tests_bidi.rs` ensuring the caret advances smoothly from right to left without snapping back to the left margin.

### Verification
- Tested interactively on macOS (Apple Silicon M4).
- Headless UI screenshot verified caret placement at the typing edge near the right margin.
- `cargo test --workspace` passed (including all 236 engine tests).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed with 0 warnings.

title: Layout: multiple line spacing adds its leading below the text, like Word
author: naxvog
body:
## Root cause
WordCraft put each line's baseline one descent above the bottom of the line box (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`). All the extra leading from multiple line spacing therefore went **above** the text: 1.8 pt at 1.15-spaced 12 pt, and more at double spacing. Word keeps the text one ascent below the top of the line and adds the extra leading **below** the baseline. Below single spacing, Word shrinks the whole box, ascent included.

A second, smaller offset came from `wordcraft_fonts::word::line_metrics`. It split the hhea line gap half above the ascent and half below the descent. Word counts the whole gap as part of the ascent, so the baseline sat 0.25 pt too high for 12 pt Times New Roman.

## Fix
- `baseline_offset` in `para.rs` places the baseline for multiple spacing at `ascent × min(m, 1)` below the line top. Lines that hold a picture still put the picture on the baseline. Exact and at-least spacing still keep the descent below the baseline, and lines that snap to a document grid (#401) still centre their text in the grid pitches.
- `line_metrics` puts the hhea line gap above the ascent (`hhea_line`). The total line height doesn't change, so line pitch is the same. Every descent is half a line gap smaller, though, so text in exact, at-least and grid-snapped lines sits up to half a line gap lower: 0.25 pt for 12 pt Times New Roman, more for fonts with a large gap. On the suite that brings those lines closer to Word too (exact: 5 fixtures better, 1 worse; at-least: 5 better, none worse).
- Regression tests: `multiple_line_spacing_adds_its_leading_below_the_text` (1.15×, 2×, 0.8× and exact spacing) and `the_line_gap_goes_above_the_ascent`. None of the bundled fonts has a line gap, so that test checks the hhea calculation directly.

## How it was found and measured
I ran WordCraft and [docxide-pdf](https://github.com/sverrejb/docxide-pdf) against docxide-pdf's 390 fixtures. Each fixture is a DOCX plus the PDF that Word exported from it. Both outputs were scor…

Word's border drags that #600 left out:

- **Ctrl** while dragging a column border: the columns right of it share the change in proportion to their widths, so
  the table keeps its width (none gets narrower than the minimum). Ctrl wins over Shift. On the table's right edge it
  behaves like a plain drag (only the last column changes).
- **The table's left edge** can be dragged, from just outside it: the table's indent moves and the first column makes up
  the difference, so the other borders stay. A centred or right-aligned table becomes left-aligned where the edge was
  dropped; a floating table moves its horizontal offset. The horizontal ruler gets a marker on the left edge too.
- **Alt** while dragging a column border: the horizontal ruler shows each column's width (in inches, like the ruler) as it's
  going to be.
- **Selected cells:** when the selection runs across two or more cells, dragging one of their column borders (in one of
  their rows) moves it only in their rows; the other rows keep theirs. The grid gets a line for the new border and the
  cells' spans follow (`regrid`). A border of a cell merged down into rows outside the selection moves in the whole
  column, so a merged cell keeps one width.

Engine: `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_resize.rs` — `Share` (who makes up a column border's move), `Edge::Column(0)`,
`ResizeTarget::limit_to_selection` / `only` / `planned_x`, `Plan::indent_by` / `cells`; `table.resizeDrag` takes

title: Tables: drags and Shift+arrows over cells select whole cells
author: rabis7575
body:
Builds on #637 (whole-cell selections), so it's stacked on it until it merges; after that a
rebase leaves only this change.

Closes the known gap noted in #637: dragging the mouse (or Shift+arrows) across cells of several
rows selected the run of text between the two points, so bold, alignment and Delete also reached
the cells of other columns in between, while table commands (merge, shading, delete columns)
treated the same selection as a rectangle.

Like Word:

- **From one cell into another** of the same table, an ordinary drag, Shift+click or Shift+arrow
  selects the rectangle of whole cells between them (shaded as cells). Bold, alignment, Delete,
  typing and copy act on those cells only, through the whole-cell selection from #637.
- **Between a cell and text outside its table** the selection takes whole rows, from the cell's
  row out to the table's edge facing the text, and the text beyond.
- **Extending again goes on from where the selection really runs**: dragging back into the first
  cell selects its text from where the drag started; Shift+Up after Shift+Down shrinks the
  rectangle; Shift+click after a drag keeps the drag's first cell. Nested tables: from a nested
  table's cell into another cell of the table around it, that table's cells.

Checked against Word (2019, Windows), and the same there: a drag from one cell to another
selects the rectangle of whole cells between them; from a cell into the text below, whole rows
from that cell's down to the end of the table, plus the text; back into the first cell, just its
text; Shift+Down from a cell selects whole cells (B1:B2, then B1:B3) and Shift+Right widens the
rectangle.

`Session::sel_ends` (where a widened selection really starts and ends). Every caret command run
with `extend` (Shift+arrows, Shift+click, the app's drag) goes through it in `column::dispatch`,

title: Proofing: Danish spelling and grammar flags, per-run proofing language
author: Irate4147
body:
## What
Danish proofing, picked per run by Review › Language (`da-DK`). English is unchanged.

- **Spelling** (`crates/proof/src/da.rs`): every form in Retskrivningsordbogen 5.1 (COR₁) and Den Danske Ordbog's lemma list (COR.EXT), Danish place names and common given/family names (Wikidata), and compound analysis (*kaffekop*, *Københavnsområdet*) using COR's compound-first forms.
- **Frequencies**: each form carries a frequency class from word counts over the CC0 subsets of Danish Dynaword. They rank suggestions (aa/æ/ø/å-aware: *paa* → *på*) and reject unseen "compounds" one edit from a common word (*bøgerene*).
- **Grammar flags** (blue):
  - Compounds written apart: *tog station* → *togstation*. Pairs Danish writes apart (*over for*, *lav et*, *selv om*) are listed and left alone.
  - Present tense after *at* or a modal verb: *at bliver* → *blive*, *vil står* → *stå*. Only forms that are never a noun or another word class (*at læser*, *at når* are not flagged).
- **Lexicon format** `DCLEX2`: front-coded, deflated, a flag nibble and a frequency-class nibble per form. `assets/proof/da.lex` is ~672k forms, 1.1 MB.

## Sources and licence
All CC0: COR₁ 1.5.1.0 and COR.EXT 1.0 (Dansk Sprognævn), Dynaword subsets `ft`, `nordjyllandnews`, `nota` (the CC-BY-SA Wikipedia subset is not used), Wikidata labels. title: Mini toolbar: measure its width so no button is clipped (#535)
author: louwers-bot
body:
Part of #535 (item 1: the panel is cut off after Align Left). This overlaps with #540, which also fixes this as part of a larger rework. This PR is the narrow fix: the bar measures its own width, so the width can't drift from the controls again.

## Before
The bar's width was a hand-computed constant (432 pt), and its contents were clipped to it. The formula left out the combos' dropdown arrows, the split buttons' arrow halves and the 1 pt spacing between controls. The real row is 510 pt, so Center, Align Right and Justify were cut off.

![Before: the mini toolbar is cut off after Align Left](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/louwers-bot/wordcraft/screenshots/mini-toolbar-width/before.png)

## After
The bar measures its laid-out controls and remembers the width in egui temp memory. When the measured width differs from the width just drawn, it calls `request_discard`, so egui redoes the pass and a clipped bar is never shown. `BAR_W_ESTIMATE` (518 pt, the measured width) is only the first-frame guess. `anchor_rect` now takes the width as a parameter and falls back to the estimate for non-finite or non-positive widths.

![After: every control fits, ending with Justify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/louwers-bot/wordcraft/screenshots/mini-toolbar-width/after.png)

Both screenshots are from `ui_shot`, with the same script on `main` and on this branch.

- `mini_toolbar::tests::every_control_fits_inside_the_bar_from_the_first_frame` renders the bar headlessly over a real selection. title: Layout: blank pages put sections on the right side, and paragraph spacing is the larger of after and before
author: naxvog
body:
Two Word layout rules that cost WordCraft its page count against Word. Both were found by running docxide-pdf's 390 Word-referenced fixtures (the same benchmark as #719). The two commits are independent of #719.

## 1. Blank pages put sections on the side Word puts them
**Root cause:** WordCraft added a blank page only for odd- and even-page section breaks, and decided by the section's *restart* number. Word also adds one in another case, and decides differently:
- **Next-page breaks with different odd and even headers:** a next-page break that restarts the numbering at an odd (even) number starts on an odd (even) sheet. WordCraft never added this page. In `bush_fires_act_comparison`, Word's blank page 2 was missing, so every later page was one off; three more fixtures had the same problem.
- **Odd- and even-page breaks:** the decision uses the number the section would get by counting on. A section that restarts its numbering gets no blank page unless the document prints both sides (different odd and even headers, or mirror margins). A restart at the wrong parity takes the next number instead.
- **Header on the wrong page:** the blank page was the new section's first page, so it took the title-page header away from the page that should have it. It now ends the previous section, as in Word.

**Fix:** `section_side` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` decides on the blank page and the restart number; the section loop adds the page for the previous section. Test: `sections_land_on_the_side_their_break_and_numbering_ask_for`.

## 2. The space between paragraphs is the larger of after and before
**Root cause:** WordCraft added a paragraph's space after to the next paragraph's space before. Word uses the larger of the two: 6 pt after followed by 6 pt before leaves 6 pt, not 12 pt. In `clean_energy_regulator_guidelines`, the summed spacing pushed a section's last paragraphs onto an extra page.

**Fix:** The rule applies in the body (`place_para`) and in boxes (`layout_box`: tabl…

title: Pictures: WMF drawings fill their frame like Word plays them
author: naxvog
body:
WMF pictures were drawn in the wrong frame. In docxide-pdf's Word-referenced fixtures, a Bulgarian coat of arms came out as a solid black box, a Ukrainian emblem at a fifth of its size, and a plain WMF logo strip shrank to a point. This is the same benchmark as #719 and #733; this PR is independent of both.

## Root cause
Word plays a WMF into the picture's box the way a GDI player does:
- the player sets anisotropic mapping;
- the placeable header's bounds are only the first window, mapped onto a viewport of the picture's size;
- the file's own `SETWINDOWORG`/`SETWINDOWEXT` records then replace that window.

WordCraft instead mapped the header's bounds through the file's *final* mapping and used the result as the frame:
- **`bulgarian_farmland_allocation_order`:** the drawing sits in a window centred on the origin (−1193…1193), nowhere near the header's bounds (238…285). The tiny frame blew the lion up into a black box.
- **`ukrainian_municipal_heating_resolution`:** a portrait window (98×136) replaced the landscape bounds (601×302), so the bitmap filled a fifth of the frame.
- **Plain WMFs:** without a placeable header, an anisotropic file that sets a window but no viewport kept the 1×1 default viewport and shrank to a point.

## Fix (`crates/metafile`)
- **Placeable WMF that never sets a viewport:** `Canvas::play_into` sets up the player's mapping (window = bounds, viewport = picture size), and the frame is the target. Window records in the file replace the window.
- **Plain WMF:** the first window extent the file actually sets is the target, unless the file sets its own viewport.
- **Unchanged:** files that set their own viewport, or that use `MM_TEXT` or the metric map modes, are read exactly as before, so all existing metafile tests pass unchanged.
- **`SETROP2`:** WMF `0x0104` and EMF type 20 are now read. With `R2_NOP`, shapes and paths draw nothing; the coat of arms uses it to draw its bounding rectangle, which showed up as an outline. The mode is saved and…

title: Linux: "Use system setting" follows the desktop's light/dark setting
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Linux the interface theme's "Use system setting" was always light. winit doesn't report a system theme there (`RawInput::system_theme` stays `None`), so `Appearance::System` fell back to light whatever the desktop was set to. macOS, Windows and the web build already get an answer and are unchanged.

The fix is ported from PdfCraft, storytold/pdfcraft#881. I also looked at the other approach in storytold/craft-launcher#120.

- `apps/wordcraft/src/desktop_theme.rs` asks the XDG desktop portal's Settings interface for `color-scheme` on its own thread, so the frame loop never makes a D-Bus call. It reads the first answer straight away and then re-reads every 4 s. It wakes the window when the answer changes, so an idle window picks up a theme switch too.
- It asks the standard `org.freedesktop.appearance` key first (a number: 1 dark, 2 light; GNOME and KDE answer it), then `org.gnome.desktop.interface`, whose string XFCE's portal proxies. pdfcraft's second key, `org.freedesktop.interface.color-scheme`, didn't look like one any portal answers, so I used the standard key instead. Portals without `ReadOne` get the older `Read`.
- The shell's `raw_input_hook` hands the desktop's answer to egui as `system_theme`. That way `Appearance::System` (`ui_is_dark`) and egui's own `ThemePreference::System` follow it exactly as they follow macOS and Windows, and `ui-egui` doesn't change. If there's no session bus, no portal, or the desktop states no preference, the input is left alone.
- `zbus` is pinned to the 5.19.0 that's already in `Cargo.lock` through accesskit, so no new crates. It's only built for `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.

This PR doesn't change the default theme (that's #718), and it doesn't touch the title bar.

Tests: unit tests for parsing the portal's answers (number, string, wrapped in variants, bounded nesting), the watcher keeping its last answer, and the raw-input override. `cargo test -p wordcraft`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft --no-deps --all-targe…

title: Layout: an inline picture wider than the text keeps its size, like Word
author: naxvog
body:
Inline pictures, charts and shapes wider than their line were shrunk to the line's width, and their height with it. Word draws them at their own size: the picture runs past the margin, the page edge clips it, and the line is as tall as the picture. This is the same benchmark as #719, #733 and #739; this PR is independent of them.

## Root cause
`layout_para` scaled every inline drawing wider than the line (`w > maxw`) down to it. In docxide-pdf's Word-referenced fixtures:
- **`case179`:** a 1014 × 100 pt picture became 468 × 46 pt, so everything below it on the page moved up.
- **`alfies_arc_adult_safeguarding_policy`:** a header's 1014 pt-wide logo strip (an OLE metafile) was shrunk to the text width.

## Fix
- **Body, headers, footers and table cells:** inline drawings keep their size. Every page output already clips at the page: the PDF page box, and the page bitmaps that the rasteriser and the editor draw.
- **Text boxes:** they don't clip what runs past their sides yet, so a drawing wider than a text box is still fitted to the box rather than spilling over the page. `ParaEnv::fit_objects` comes from `BoxBudget::inside()` and is part of the paragraph cache key. Clipping text-box content like Word does is a possible follow-up; it needs the index and hit testing to look inside clips.
- **Table auto-fit:** unchanged. Column measuring already used an unbounded width, so auto-fit columns were sized to the picture before this change.

Tests:
- `inline_picture_wider_than_the_text_keeps_its_size`: size and line height.
- `inline_picture_wider_than_a_text_box_is_fitted_to_it`
- `graphic_items_scale_with_their_frame`: replaces `oversized_graphic_draws_shrunk_with_its_items`, which asserted the old shrinking. It now checks what that test protected: a chart's items and strokes scale with its frame.

Two 4000 × 4000 pt pictures (the size cap) lay out as 3 pages in 2 ms.

title: Ink: draw the live pen stroke in the dark-page colour while drawing, not only after lifting the pen (#730)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #730.

On a dark page (View > Switch Modes), saved ink is rendered through `RenderOptions::ink`, which inverts lightness and lifts black to the paper grey. So a black pen stroke shows as white once it is saved. The live stroke in `ink::paint` used the raw pen colour, so it stayed black while you drew and turned white only after you lifted the pen.

Changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/ink.rs`):
- New helper `screen_ink(dark, colour, alpha)`. It applies the same `RenderOptions::ink` mapping as the page renderer, with the default `dark_paper` (`DARK_PAPER`, the same value the canvas uses).
- The live pen/highlighter stroke uses it, so the stroke has its final colour from the start.
- Ink Replay draws the saved strokes itself over pages rendered without ink, and it had the same problem: on a dark page it replayed them in their light-page colours. It now uses the same helper.

Test: `ink::tests::live_ink_follows_the_dark_page`. A black pen stays black on a light page and turns white on a dark page, and alpha is kept.

title: Backspace still erases while Shift is held (#707)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #707.

**Cause:** `keys::dispatch` first looks up the shifted combo (`Shift+Backspace`), which nothing is bound to. When that fails, it falls back to the plain combo only for `caret.*` commands, so they can extend the selection. `text.backspace` was not part of that fallback, so Shift+Backspace did nothing.

**Fix:** a small `shift_variant_params` helper says how a plain-key command runs when Shift is also held and nothing is bound to the shifted combo:
- caret moves keep `{"extend": true}`, as before;
- `text.backspace` runs normally, as in Word and the other editors.

Everything else still falls through, as before. Shift+Delete is left alone, because in Word on Windows that key means Cut. Custom keys still come first: if the user binds Shift+Backspace in Customize Keyboard, that binding wins. If they remove plain Backspace, the fallback finds nothing. The equation editor already ignored Shift for Backspace, so it needs no change.

**Test:** `keys::tests::shift_backspace_still_erases` checks the helper for `text.backspace`, a caret move and `text.delete`. It does not compile or pass without the fix.

title: Let dialogs be dragged by their title bar instead of pinning them to the screen centre (#732)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #732.

**Cause:** `place_dialog` anchored every dialog on every frame: `CENTER_CENTER` on the first frame, then `CENTER_TOP` with the remembered top offset (the #507 fix). egui makes an anchored window immovable (`Window::anchor` sets `movable(false)`), so the Symbol dialog, and every other dialog shown through `dialogs::show`, could not be dragged by its title bar.

**Fix:** the dialog stays anchored and centred for its first two frames only. The first frame measures it and the second centres it at that size. After that it has no anchor, so egui's normal title-bar drag works. All frames use `pivot(CENTER_TOP)`, so egui stores the window's position as its top-centre point. As a result:
- a taller or shorter tab (Paragraph, Font, Borders and Shading…) still moves only the bottom edge, so the #507 behaviour is kept and `switching_paragraph_tabs_keeps_the_top_edge` still covers it;
- the dialog still opens centred, 40 px above the middle, as before.

The pivot has to be the same on every frame. In title-bar drag mode (the desktop default), egui 0.36 takes the stored pivot position and ignores `current_pos`. If it read a top-left point as a top-centre point, the dialog would jump left by half its width.

Each time a dialog opens it is centred again, as before. This PR does not add a remembered dialog position.

**Test:** `dragging_a_dialog_title_bar_moves_it` opens the Paragraph dialog in a kittest harness and checks that it opens horizontally centred. It then presses on the title bar, drags 200 px left and 120 px down, and checks that the window moved by that amount. On `main` the window does not move, so the test fails.

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

title: Ruler: the horizontal scale mirrors for right-to-left paragraphs (#692)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #692

## Summary
When the caret is in a right-to-left paragraph, the horizontal ruler now mirrors like Word's: the scale runs from the right edge, tick numbers increase right-to-left, and the indent/tab markers sit exactly on the flipped ticks.

## Root cause
`rulers()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` anchored the bar's tick loop at the page's left margin and converted ticks straight to screen x, regardless of paragraph direction. The indent/tab markers already had RTL-aware `sx()`/`s_at()` mirroring, which produced exactly the reported mismatch: markers flipped to the right while the scale kept running left-to-right.

## Fix
The RTL decision (`resolve_para(..).bidi` at the selection focus) is hoisted above the bar drawing, and all horizontal-ruler geometry is expressed as "distance along the reading direction from the page's start edge" through new mirror/inverse helpers `ruler_x()` / `ruler_d()`. Because the drag hit-mapping reads the pointer through the same mirrored transform, dragging the (now right-side) start indent handle still edits the same `para.indents` fields. Section margins and the white text-area rectangle stay physical, as in Word — only the numeric scale mirrors.

## Tests
- `the_ruler_scale_mirrors_for_right_to_left` — pure geometry: 0 lands on the right page edge (including asymmetric margins), `ruler_d(ruler_x(d)) == d` for both directions, tick/margin-mark policy, and strictly descending mirrored screen positions.
- `setting_a_paragraph_rtl_mirrors_the_ruler_numbers` — end-to-end frame test that runs the real `para.rtl` command and asserts the painted "1"/"2" labels mirror about the page centre; verified to fail with mirroring disabled.

title: Save As: a bare filename typed in the dialog now saves correctly (#689)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #689

## Summary
Save As now saves under the filename typed in the dialog. Previously, typing a new bare name ("chapter two") produced a file the engine could not write, while changing only the folder worked — the reported asymmetry.

## Root cause
The desktop Save dialog (`apps/wordcraft/src/file_dialogs.rs`, `FileDialogRequest::Save`) called `set_file_name(name).save_file()` with **no filter**. rfd 0.17's Windows backend only calls `IFileDialog::SetDefaultExtension` for a filter's extension, so with no filters the dialog had no default extension: a user replacing the pre-selected seeded name with a bare name got back an extension-less path (`chapter two`). The engine picks the serializer by extension (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`), so `file.save` failed with "can't save as `.chapter two`" and the UI only flashed a transient status message — "does not work". Keeping the seeded name (`.docx` included) and changing the folder kept the extension, which is why that direction worked.

## Fix
Save dialogs now get a "Documents" filter listing every format in `wordcraft_engine::io::SAVE_EXTS`, with the suggested name's own extension hoisted first so rfd's `SetDefaultExtension` appends the document's format to a bare typed name (falls back to `docx`). This also fixes bare names in Export As and gives macOS/Linux panels the same behaviour. Async plumbing, `AfterSave` continuations, password handling, and engine-side `s.path`/dirty/autosave retargeting are untouched. The engine still (correctly) refuses explicit extension-less paths from scripts/agents.

## Tests
- `save_dialog_defaults_to_the_suggested_format` (app crate): the default extension is the suggested name's format (docx/odt/pdf), unknown extensions fall back to docx, every savable format offered exactly once.
- `save_as_with_a_new_filename_saves_under_it` (ui-egui): open `one.docx` → Save As pick `sub\two.docx` → saved under the new name, `session.path` updated, and the F12 funnel re-seeds the dialog with the n…

title: Selection: dragging past the viewport edge auto-scrolls (#688)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #688

## Summary
Dragging a text selection near the top or bottom edge of the document viewport now auto-scrolls, Word-style, so you can select beyond the visible page with the mouse.

## Root cause
Mouse-drag selection was handled entirely by the canvas widget (`Sense::click_and_drag` on the content rect), which consumes the drag — so egui's ScrollArea drag-to-scroll never engaged, despite the comment claiming it did. Nothing scrolled while dragging.

## Fix
While a drag selection (or Alt column drag) is active, each frame computes an edge-scroll delta with a new pure helper `edge_scroll(p, lo, hi, dt)`: zero while the pointer is ≥ 32 pt inside the viewport, then a linear ramp from 45 pt/s at the margin boundary to 720 pt/s at the hard edge, scaled by `stable_dt` (clamped to 0.1 s so a stalled frame can't jump the page). The delta goes through the same `clamped_scroll` the manual wheel uses, so it persists and stops at the document's ends. The drag pointer is clamped into the viewport before `layout.hit`, so with the pointer parked at an edge the selection end keeps walking as content scrolls under it — Word's behaviour. Non-drag wheel scrolling and caret scroll-into-view are untouched.

## Tests
- `edge_auto_scroll_ramps_from_the_margins_and_clamps` — pure helpers: zero mid-viewport, correct direction at both edges, strictly monotonic ramp, full speed capped past the edge, dt stall clamp, NaN/infinity/inverted-band safety, and no scroll when the document fits the viewport.
- `dragging_a_selection_past_the_viewport_edge_auto_scrolls` — driven frames: holding the pointer 40 px past the bottom edge advances the scroll offset, grows the selection while stationary, and mouse-up leaves a non-collapsed selection.

Tunables are named constants at the top of `canvas.rs` next to `GAP`/`RULER` (`EDGE_MARGIN`, `EDGE_SPEED_MIN`, `EDGE_SPEED_MAX`, `EDGE_MAX_DT`).

`cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Layout: a page total in the footer no longer lays the body out twice (#771)
author: dkhlapov
body:
A page total in the footer ("Page X of Y") made every layout lay the whole body out twice.
