title: Affix engine: FLAG UTF-8, 128 flag bits, continuation classes, FORBIDDENWORD (#100)
author: edurbs
body:
Related to #100 (multilingual spell check). Makes the #346 Hunspell-subset engine load real-world dictionaries that declare `FLAG UTF-8` — verified end to end with the system-installed VERO pt_BR.

**Stacked on #346**: this branch is based on its head (`polish-interface-and-proofing`); `crates/proof/src/affix.rs` itself comes from there. Merge after #346, or take these commits along with it — happy to rebase either way.

## What

`crates/proof/src/affix.rs` only. No new dependencies, no unsafe, wasm-safe.

- **`FLAG UTF-8` / `FLAG DEFAULT` accepted** (`long`/`num` still error). Per-character flags are what the reader already parses — the directive check was the only blocker. Real dictionaries declare it (VERO pt_BR: `FLAG UTF-8`, 106 flags).
- **Flag masks widened `u64` → `u128`.** VERO needs 106 distinct flags; the cap was 64. WCAFF1 is unchanged — it stores flag characters and re-derives the masks on load.
- **Continuation classes** (`SFX A 0 able/B`): the derived form carries flag B, licensing a further suffix (`workable → workables`) that the bare stem cannot take. `form_has_flag` walks the chain depth-bounded (`MAX_CHAIN = 3`), `forms()` enumerates the same chains, and with no continuations declared everything degenerates to the previous behavior — existing dictionaries are unaffected.
- **`FORBIDDENWORD`** — was a hard error. Stems carrying the forbidden flag are listed but never correct and never inflect.
- **UTF-8 BOM** stripped from `.aff`/`.dic` input: VERO glues one to the count line, which parsed as a stem.

## Measured (local, installed VERO 3.2)

- Before: `FLAG UTF-8 is not supported` (line 2), then `continuation classes are not supported` (26 rules), then `106 distinct flags; at most 64 are supported`.
- After: loads as-is — 312,295 stems, 25,829 rules — and agrees with the system `hunspell -d pt_BR` on a probe set: the same 8 misspellings flagged, the same acceptances.

## Tests

- 7 new tests in `affix.rs`, all synthetic (no system dictionary neede…

title: Portuguese proofing: pt-BR spelling, suggestions, grammar and hyphenation (#100)
author: edurbs
body:
Related to #100 (multilingual spell check). Portuguese proofing — pt-BR spelling, suggestions, grammar and hyphenation — as a third language in the per-run framework, following the Polish module (`crates/proof/src/pl/`) as its template.

**Stacked on #346 → #782**: the branch carries their commits; the Portuguese work is the last 10 (`2551b7d` up). Merge after those, or take the commits along — happy to rebase either way. Everything below needs the affix engine from #782 (VERO declares `FLAG UTF-8`, uses 106 flags, 26 continuation rules and `FORBIDDENWORD`).

## What

- **`crates/proof/src/pt/`** — spelling against the Hunspell `pt_BR` dictionary installed on the system (VERO and its derivatives; read at runtime through `crate::hunspell`, never bundled — LGPL/MPL), names capitalized, compounds checked part by part (`guarda-roupa`, `ex-marido`), user dictionary applies. Without a dictionary installed, Portuguese text gets no marks, like Word without the language's tools.
- **Suggestions** (`pt/suggest.rs`), the Polish rounds retuned: missing accents from the dictionary's `MAP` groups first (`coraçao` → `coração`, `saude` → `saúde`), the `REP` confusions (`seje` → `seja`, `excessão` → `exceção`), a missing space after a short function word (`nãoé` → `não é`), one typo over `TRY`, then an accent-folding stem scan. Ties break toward the change nearest the word's start (`saúde` before `saudê`, both words). Bounded input and rounds.
- **Grammar** (`pt/grammar.rs`): conservative rules with Portuguese messages — repeated words (the emphatic doubles Portuguese allows stay), space before punctuation, double spaces, sentence capitals (Portuguese abbreviations, ordinals, dialogue dashes), doubled punctuation. No comma rule: `que` opens a clause only sometimes, so a wrong flag would cost more than a missed one.
- **Hyphenation**: hyph-utf8's `hyph-pt.tex` bundled unmodified — BSD 3-clause (licence header in the file), ATTRIBUTION.md row with source and SHA-256, 426 Liang pattern…

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root (#769)
author: isaac-levine
body:
`wordcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. VectorCraft already has two flags for this, so this adds the same ones here with the same names and behaviour, and one client config works across the apps:

    wordcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

Every file a command reads has to be inside the read root and every file it writes inside the write root. A root left out grants none of its access, so the read root alone makes the server read-only. Paths are made absolute, symlinks followed (for a file that doesn't exist yet, the nearest existing folder is resolved and the rest must be plain names), then compared with the root by whole path components, so `/work2` is not inside `/work`. On Windows case is ignored and device names like `CON` and `NUL` are refused. Refusals come back as normal tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

**Where the checks live**

All path-based access in the engine already went through `io::open_path_with` and `io::save_path_with`, apart from four commands that called `std::fs` directly (`insert.picture`, `picture.change`, `mailings.recipients`, `file.exportPng`). Those now go through two small helpers, `io::read_file` and `io::write_file`, and the checks sit in those four functions. A new test fails if a command module starts touching the file system on its own again. `Headless::with_automation_roots` in the mcp crate runs each call inside the confinement, and the CLI gets the flag parsing (`--flag DIR` or `--flag=DIR`, a flag given twice or a missing folder is an error, `--connect` together with the flags is an error). `docs/mcp.md` gets a "Confining file access" section.

Covered reads: `open_document`, `file.open`, `file.newFromTemplate`, `insert.textFromFile`, `insert.object`, `insert.picture`, `picture.change`, `mailings.recipients`, `review…

title: CI: run cargo xtask ci on pull requests and pushes to main (#754)
author: isaac-levine
body:
Nothing runs `cargo xtask ci` on pull requests or on main right now. The workflows on main build for FreeBSD and Windows ARM64, lint packaging and cut releases, but fmt, clippy and the test suite only run on each contributor's machine against whatever main they branched from. Once a few PRs merge, the combination can be red and nobody notices until the next person's local run fails on code they didn't touch (the fmt and test examples in #754).

This adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with one Ubuntu job that runs `cargo xtask ci` on `pull_request`, on pushes to `main`, and on `workflow_dispatch`. It is the same shape as GridCraft's and DeckCraft's `ci.yml`: same permissions, same concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, same apt packages for winit/wgpu/rfd, a rustup install that includes the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target for the wasm step, and `Swatinem/rust-cache` saved only on main. Like DeckCraft's workflow it also checks out `storytold/craft-fonts` at the commit `release.yml` and `freebsd.yml` pin and sets `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, so the layout tests see the fonts a release embeds. That step is optional (`crates/fonts/build.rs` builds without it) and can be dropped if you'd rather keep the job minimal.

The `clippy::large_enum_variant` warning mentioned in the issue is already fixed on main (`Obj(Box<InlineObject>)`), and clippy is clean on rustc 1.99, so there is no code change here. I didn't add a `rust-toolchain.toml` since neither sibling repo has one.

Testing: `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (all 6 steps: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm). I also ran the workflow itself on GitHub Actions in my fork before opening this, and it passed in 20 minutes: https://github.com/isaac-levine/wordcraft/actions/runs/38197991982

Fixes #754

title: fix(engine): use unique temporary path for atomic save
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
### Summary

In `crates/engine/src/io.rs`, `save_path_with` writes atomically by saving into a temporary path next to the destination before renaming it to the final destination:
```rust
let tmp = path.with_extension(format!("{}.tmp", ext_of(&path.to_string_lossy())));
```
Because this temporary path was completely static and predictable (e.g., `document.docx.tmp`), concurrent saves in the same directory could collide and race on writes. Furthermore, in shared directory environments, a predictable filename allows symlink pre-creation attacks.

### Changes
- Replace static `{path}.tmp` with `unique_tmp_path(path)`, appending the process ID and a monotonic atomic counter: `.{stem}.{pid}.{n}.tmp`.
- Add a unit test `atomic_save_unique_temp_path` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` verifying that consecutive invocations yield distinct paths containing the process ID.

title: fix(styles): prevent circular style inheritance in document stylesheets and commands
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
### Summary

In `crates/doc/src/styles.rs` and `crates/engine/src/cmd/para.rs` / `table_style.rs`, style inheritance chains did not proactively check for circular `basedOn` dependencies when creating or modifying paragraph or table styles.

While `StyleSheet::chain` caps traversal at 32 items to avoid unbounded recursion, establishing cycles (such as `A -> B -> A`) leads to incorrect property resolution and corrupt inheritance structures.

### Changes
- In `StyleSheet`:
  - Added `causes_cycle(&self, id: &str, based_on: &str) -> bool` to determine whether basing `id` on `based_on` forms a cycle.
  - In `upsert`, break circular `based_on` assignments if detected by clearing `based_on`.
- In `cmd/para.rs`:
  - Validate `basedOn` in `para.createStyle` and `para.modifyStyle`, returning `CmdError::Params("circular style inheritance (basedOn cycle)")` if a cycle is attempted.
- In `cmd/table_style.rs`:
  - Check for cycles in `table.newStyle` (`build_new`), matching existing cycle rejection in `table.modifyStyle`.
- Added unit tests in `crates/doc/src/styles.rs` (`style_cycle_prevention`) and `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` (`style_inheritance_cycle_rejected`).

title: fix(doc): remove fully covered tables in cross-container delete_range
author: AnandkumarMall
body:
### Summary

In `crates/doc/src/edit.rs`, when `delete_range` spans across containers (such as from a paragraph before a table to a paragraph after a table), it previously cleared text in paragraphs inside the table cells, but only removed tables if they were top-level and strictly between `a` and `b` where `a.path.depth() == 0 && b.path.depth() > 0`.

If the range completely encompassed a table across boundaries (e.g. from paragraph `0` before the table to paragraph `2` after the table), the table cells were emptied of text but the table skeleton itself remained as an empty, orphaned table structure.

### Changes
- In `delete_range`:
  - Track paragraphs that were fully selected and cleared (`from == 0 && to == len`).
  - Collect candidate tables along paths between `a` and `b` (including top-level blocks between `a` and `b`).
  - If every non-empty paragraph in candidate tables is covered by the deletion range, remove the entire table block from the document.
  - Call `ensure_nonempty()` and safely clamp return position if `a` was removed.
- Added a unit test `delete_fully_covered_table_across_containers` verifying that selecting and deleting across a table completely removes the table skeleton.

title: layout: make Myanmar fallback tests deterministic
author: echelon
body:
## Problem
`tests_complex::myanmar_syllables_are_single_clusters` and `tests_complex::myanmar_in_a_latin_font_falls_back_to_a_regular_myanmar_face` (from #652) passed alone but failed in about 1 of 4 full `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` runs (3 of 12 here). The failures were `left: [0, 3, 6, 12, 18] right: [0, 6, 12, 18]` and `one face for the word`.

## Root cause
The bug is a race in `FontDb`'s system font fallback, not in the tests. The tests share `FontDb::global()`, and layout asks for a fallback face per character from several threads.

- `system_fallback` marks a preferred family ("Padauk" for Myanmar) as *tried* before it loads it. A second search that ran at the same time skipped that family as already tried. It then fell through to the coverage index and loaded the first cataloged file in path order that maps the character. That file was `Padauk-Bold.ttf`, on its own.
- So characters of one syllable fell back to different faces (Padauk Bold and Padauk Regular). The shaper split the syllable at the face change (`[0, 3, …]`), and the word no longer had one face.
- Separately, `cached_fallback` cached a search's answer under the face count read *after* the search. An answer chosen before another thread's load could therefore be cached as current.

## Fix (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`)
- System fallback searches run one at a time, under a new `searching` lock. A search that waited checks the loaded faces again first, so it uses the family the earlier search loaded instead of loading another file.
- `loaded_fallback` / `search_fallback` return the face count the answer was chosen from. `cached_fallback` doesn't cache an answer if more faces have loaded since then.

The test assertions are unchanged, and there are no sleeps or retries. Wasm is unaffected: there is no system fallback there.

## Verification
- Before: full layout suite failed 3 of 12 runs.
- After: test binary 20/20 passing, then `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` 15/15 in a row (197 tests).

title: fix: preserve external file changes on save
author: OPUZZLES
body:
Save can overwrite changes made by another application after a document is opened. This checks the destination against the bytes opened or last saved and refuses a conflict while retaining local edits. The dialog offers Keep editing or Save copy; idle AutoSave pauses after refusal.

The check runs after an exclusively owned sibling temporary has been prepared and synchronized, immediately before replacement. Identical-byte replacements remain valid. Save As aliases are guarded, and a separate destination preserves both versions. Failed saves restore core properties and leave the candidate password uncommitted. Native I/O retains automation root checks, and password-save conflict checks precede recovery cleanup.

### Refresh and review fixes

Integrated main `4a251d4b9c724a5bd3dd75f7c91c6aae77c6650e` while preserving the published history and maintainer fix `a66b28f3`. All upstream catalog rows and the five conflict strings remain in all 22 catalogs; conflict strings now sit near the headers to avoid shared append locations. Documentation retains both main's updates and the save contract.

Reduced failures also showed alias and Rename bypasses: an externally replaced symlink, retargeted logical path, replacement hard link, or replacement after Rename could lose external changes. The guard now follows both tracked spellings and current entry identities. Rename changes the tracked paths while retaining the original content fingerprint. Lossy saves through aliases retain the logical path used by the open session. Relative destinations are normalized before checking missing aliases. Case aliases are remembered while the file exists; canonically equivalent Unicode names remain conservatively reserved after deletion. Distinct filenames remain available for copies.

A FIFO substituted for a tracked entry could block identity checks. Unix opens are now nonblocking and entry types are checked before and after opening. A bounded regression protects against that hang without to…

title: In-app AI assistant with a Claude-Code-style harness (#25)
author: PabloRaka
body:
Closes part of gap #25 (in-app AI assistant).

## What

An **Assistant** pane (Home › Assistant) that edits the open document through the same tools as the MCP server, with a harness modelled on Claude Code's so the model's behaviour is enforced in code, not only in the prompt.

- **Providers:** Claude (Anthropic Messages API) and every OpenAI-compatible API — Gemini (`/v1beta/openai`), OpenAI, Nvidia NIM, Fireworks, DeepSeek, Grok — plus a custom base URL (Ollama, vLLM…). Two wire formats, not seven: each provider is a preset row. The model list is fetched from the provider (`GET /models`), with a filterable dropdown; any name can still be typed.
- **Edits are tracked changes** by "AI (model)", and one request is one Undo step. The user's own author name and tracking setting are put back afterwards.

## Harness (`crates/assistant/src/guard.rs`)

| Rule | How it's enforced |
|---|---|
| Read before edit | Commands that change the document are refused until the model has read it in this request |
| Plan | `plan` tool; the pane shows a checklist |
| Ask when ambiguous | `ask_user` tool pauses the loop; the pane shows the question with option buttons |
| No deletion without permission | Each command is measured on the accepted text; removing original text over a threshold (or a paragraph, or a picture) is rolled back and the pane asks Allow once / Allow for this request / Deny |
| No style changes unless asked | Font, size, colour, highlight, theme commands ask the same way; bold/italic/headings/lists don't |
| Stay in the selection | Edits outside the selected paragraphs are rolled back and refused |
| Verify | Finishing after an edit without reading back gets one reminder |
| Context | Old tool output is elided; at most 25 rounds per request |
| No file access | `file.*`, undo/redo, turning tracking off and macros are blocked and hidden from `list_commands` |

## Architecture

title: Ctrl/⌘+F focuses the Find box, so typing searches (#772)
author: Yasas-Sri
body:
Closes #772

## What
Pressing Ctrl/⌘+F opened the Find window, but the focus stayed on the document, so typing went into the text instead of the search box.

Now the **Find what** box takes focus when the Find window opens, so you can press Ctrl/⌘+F and start typing. 

## How
- `Dialog::Find` gets a `focus` flag, set when the window opens.
- On the first frame, Find what requests focus and the flag is cleared, so focus moves only once. 
- Find what gets a fixed id (`find_what`) so the test can check it.

## Test
`find_shortcut_focuses_find_what` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) presses Ctrl/⌘+F as a real key event, then checks that:
- Find what has the focus,
- typed text goes into Find what,
- nothing is typed into the document.

Checked locally: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` (222 passed). Also tried in the app: Ctrl+F, then typing goes straight into the box.

title: i18n: add Bulgarian (bg) interface translation
author: bulgariamitko
body:
WordCraft can now show its interface in Bulgarian. Pick "Български" in File › Options › Interface language, use `ui.language` with `{"value":"bg"}`, or leave the automatic setting to follow a `bg-BG` system locale.

No Microsoft Word (or other product) localisation was consulted, and no other catalog in this repository was used. Bulgarian is translated on its own terms, not adapted from Russian or Serbian.
- **Conventions.**
  - Commands and buttons use verbal nouns (Запазване, Вмъкване на таблица).
  - Instructions use the polite imperative (Въведете, Изберете).

  - Product and format names stay in Latin letters.
- **Style names.** Built-in style names show translated (Нормален, Заглавие 1, Цитат…), like Russian.

### Code
- `i18n/mod.rs`: `bg` registered after `tr`. `bg`, `bg-BG`, `bg_BG.UTF-8` and `bg-Cyrl-BG` resolve to it.
- `i18n/audit.rs`: the "every looked-up string has an entry" check is now shared by Russian and Bulgarian (`has_every_string_the_interface_looked_up`). Russian's behaviour is unchanged.
- Tests (`i18n/tests.rs`):
  - locales and the saved preference, without changing the document;

title: Hyphenation: Bulgarian text follows the Bulgarian syllable rules
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What

Bulgarian text is hyphenated by **Bulgarian syllable rules**, so automatic hyphenation works in Bulgarian documents (Layout › Hyphenation › Automatic, text in `bg-BG`).

Rebuilt on main's per-language proofing (`ProofLang`, #346 and the Polish work), which replaces my earlier `Option<&str>` version:

- **`ProofLang::Bg`** (`bg`, `bg-BG`, `bul`): hyphenation only. `is_proofed()` is false, so, like `Other`, Bulgarian gets no spelling or grammar marks until there is a Bulgarian dictionary.
- **`crates/proof/src/bg.rs`**: the rules, clean-room from the Bulgarian spelling rules. No pattern file or word list, and nothing taken from another language's data.
  - Two vowels may be split: на-у-ка.
  - One consonant between vowels goes to the next syllable: ма-ма.
  - A consonant cluster splits after its first consonant (сес-тра, ком-пю-тър), except that an obstruent before р/л starts the next syllable (до-бре, та-бли-ца).
  - `й` stays with its vowel: строй-ка.
  - `дж`/`дз` are never split: хо-джа.
  - The consonant before `ь` stays with it: шо-фьор.
- **`hyphen.rs`**: `core_breaks` uses the Bulgarian rules for Bulgarian words (`Source::Rules`). Latin-script words in a Bulgarian run (`WordCraft`, `publication`) are hyphenated as English, as in any other language.
- **Layout:** unchanged. It already takes each word's language from its run.

## Tests

- `bg::tests`: the rules (срич-ко-пре-на-ся-не, бъл-га-ри-я before limits, та-бли-ца, от-го-вор …), and that non-Bulgarian letters (including Russian `ё`) are left alone.
- `lang::tests::tags_resolve`: `bg`, `bg-BG`, `BG_bg`, `bg_BG.UTF-8` and `bul` resolve to `Bg`, but not `bgx`; Bulgarian is not "proofed".
- `hyphen::tests::bulgarian_words_follow_the_bulgarian_rules`: the paragraph limits apply (Бъл-га-рия, not …ри-я), as do punctuation and quotes (`„шо-фьор“,`); Latin words in a Bulgarian run match English.
- `layout::tests::bulgarian_text_is_hyphenated_by_its_own_rules`: in a laid-out paragraph, every hyphenated line…

title: fix(ui): equation gallery tiles follow the dark theme (#817)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #817.

In dark mode the Equation tab drew every gallery tile on a hardcoded white background with black equation pictures: the Equation button picture, the structure galleries (Fraction, Script, Radical, ...), the built-in equations menu and the symbol buttons.

- All four tile backgrounds in `equation_tab.rs` now use `Tokens::input`, which is white in the light theme and dark in the dark theme, like the other input-style surfaces.
- `math_image` now turns the rendered equation into an ink mask with the existing `ink_mask` helper, and `paint_math` tints it with `Tokens::text`. The font menu entries already do this (#535). Because `paint_math` is the only way these pictures are drawn, every tile above gets the fix. `math_texture` has no other callers, so equations in the document body are not affected.

Light mode looks the same as before. The only difference is that equation ink now uses the theme's text colour instead of pure black.

Test: `previews::tests::math_pictures_are_ink_masks` renders `x/y` through `math_image` and checks that the paper is transparent and the ink is white with coverage alpha, ready to be tinted. It fails on main, where the paper is opaque white.

title: Comment cards show the time as well as the date (#812)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #812.

Comment cards in the Comments pane sliced the stored ISO timestamp to its first 10 characters, so only the date was shown and the time was lost.

They now show `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (the format suggested in the issue): a small `comment_stamp` helper in `crates/ui-egui/src/panes.rs` keeps the first 16 characters and replaces the `T` separator with a space. Seconds and the zone suffix are dropped to keep the card compact. A date-only or empty value is shown unchanged, as before. The helper works on chars, so a short or non-ASCII value cannot split a character or panic.

Only the comment card label changes; the stored date and the `review.comments` output are not touched.

Test: `comment_stamp_keeps_date_and_time` covers a full timestamp, a date-only value and an empty value.

title: ODT import reads page size, orientation and margins from styles.xml (#810)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #810.

**Cause:** saving to `.odt` already works, and `styles_xml` writes the page width, height, margins and `style:print-orientation` into `styles.xml`. The ODT importer never reads `styles.xml`, though, so on reopen the document fell back to the default page (US Letter, portrait, 1" margins). That is why a changed page size or orientation seemed not to be saved.

**Fix** (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`): `import` now reads `styles.xml` and applies the page layout of the first `style:master-page` (the one the body uses) to the document's section. It takes `fo:page-width` / `fo:page-height` and the four `fo:margin-*` values in any ODF length unit, using the existing `length()` helper. Orientation comes from `style:print-orientation` and falls back to width > height when the attribute is missing. This follows the DOCX reader, which uses `w:orient` and falls back the same way. Missing or invalid values leave the defaults in place.

**Tests:**
- `page_size_orientation_and_margins_round_trip`: export a landscape A4 page with custom margins, import it again, and check that the page setup is the same.
- `page_layout_follows_the_first_master_page`: a hand-written `styles.xml` in the LibreOffice style (two page layouts, units in cm/in, `print-orientation`) resolves through the first master page.

Both tests fail on `main`.

**Docs:** `docs/file-format-parity.md` now lists page size, orientation and margins for ODT, with a new revision-history row.

title: Accept and Reject at the caret cover a tracked change split by a comment (#809)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #809.

`resolve_sel` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs` took only the one run around the caret. Comment anchors (`CommentStart`/`CommentEnd`) split a tracked insertion or deletion into several runs, so Accept or Reject at the caret resolved only part of the change, and the text on the other side of the comment stayed tracked.

Now, when the run at the caret is a tracked insertion or deletion, the range grows over the neighbouring runs that carry the same revision (same `ins`/`del` id), and steps over a comment anchor when the same revision goes on after it. Formatting-only changes at the caret work as before. A selection (not a caret) works as before.

Test: `accept_and_reject_cover_a_change_split_by_a_comment` types a tracked insertion, adds a comment in the middle of it, puts the caret before the comment, and checks that both Accept and Reject resolve the whole insertion. It fails on main (the text after the comment start stays tracked).

title: Keep the font table and embedded fonts when saving a .docx (#770)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #770.

Opening and saving a .docx with embedded fonts dropped `word/fontTable.xml`, `word/_rels/fontTable.xml.rels` and the `word/fonts/*` parts, so the saved file fell back to whatever fonts the next reader had.

WordCraft doesn't render embedded fonts, so, as the issue suggests, the parts are passed through unchanged. This uses the same mechanism that already keeps chart, SmartArt and OLE parts:

- **Reader** (`read/mod.rs`): the part the main document relates with the `fontTable` relationship is kept with `keep_part_tree`, along with every part it reaches (the font files). Its bytes go to `Document::passthrough` and its content types and relationships go to the embedded-parts manifest.
- **Writer** (`write/embed.rs`, `write/mod.rs`): `EmbedWriter::font_table` writes `word/fontTable.xml` and its fonts back with their original relationship ids, content types and bytes, and relates the table from `document.xml.rels` (new `rt::FONT_TABLE`). Obfuscated fonts (`.odttf`) stay valid because the `w:fontKey` in the table is byte-for-byte the same.
- Documents without a font table are unchanged: nothing is kept and nothing is written.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the "Themes, font table" row no longer says embedded fonts are not read.

Test: `embedded_fonts_survive_a_round_trip` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs` builds a package with a font table that embeds two Roboto faces. It checks that the table, its relationships, both font parts and the `document.xml.rels` entry are present after a save, and that the fonts are still there after a second open and save. Without the fix it fails because `word/fontTable.xml` is missing from the output.

title: Zoom after One Page keeps one page per row (#768)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #768.

After **One Page** (or **Page Width**), any percentage zoom (Zoom In/Out, the Zoom dialog's percent, the status bar slider, Ctrl + mouse wheel / pinch) cleared the fit mode, and the canvas then went back to automatic columns, so on a wide screen the pages jumped to side by side. Word keeps one page per row in that case.

**Change**
- New `ViewState::single_column` (`#[serde(default)]`): set when One Page or Page Width is chosen (ribbon, Zoom dialog "Page width" / "Whole page"), cleared by Multiple Pages (ribbon, Zoom dialog "Many pages") and View › Page Movement › Side to Side. A percentage zoom leaves it alone.
- `canvas::geometry` keeps one column while it is set, the same way it already does while the fit is `onePage` / `pageWidth`.
- Every zoom path goes through `view.zoom`, so the ribbon buttons, dialog, slider and Ctrl + wheel are all covered by the one change.
- `docs/ui-parity.md` zoom row updated.

Without One Page / Page Width chosen, zooming out still flows pages side by side as before (#251); Multiple Pages then zooming also keeps the automatic columns.

**Tests**
- `engine::tests::zoom_after_one_page_keeps_single_column`: One Page / Page Width set the flag; Zoom Out and `view.zoom` keep it; Multiple Pages and Side to Side clear it.
- `ui-egui` `zoom_after_one_page_keeps_one_page_per_row`: a 4-page document at 1280 px, One Page then 30% stays at 1 column (was 4); Multiple Pages then 30% still gives 4 columns.

title: Tables: row borders stay apart around a vertical merge (#640)
author: rabis7575
body:
A follow-up to #600 now that #669 is in. Since #669 a vertically merged cell is one `Placed::Cell` as tall as
all its rows (its continuation rows get a `covered` box). The resize geometry from #600 took a row's bottom from
its tallest box, so in a table with a vertical merge the row where the merge starts reached down to the merge's
bottom:

- the border under that row couldn't be grabbed anywhere ("there's no table border or resize handle there");
- dragging the next row's bottom border resized the first row instead, to the merge's height plus the drag;
- the corner handle scaled that row from the merge's height, and the row lookup for column borders treated the
  rows below it as part of it.

Tables without a vertical merge are unchanged.

**Fix** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table_resize.rs` only): a row ends at its shortest box, and no lower than where the
next row starts (for a row whose every cell starts a merge, which has only taller boxes). The heights measured after
a row drag (taking the margins off an "at least" height) now come from the same geometry instead of the tallest box.
This is the same rule #669 uses for the Cell Size boxes in the ribbon ("take the shortest box in this row").

**Test:** `a_vertical_merge_keeps_each_rows_border`: a 3×2 table, the eraser merges the first column's top two
cells; the border under the first row is still found (`Edge::Row(0)`), the merge's bottom is the second row's border
(`Edge::Row(1)`), and dragging the first one 20 pt makes the first row 20 pt taller and leaves the second alone. On `main`
without the fix the test fails at the first lookup: the border under the first row isn't found.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the engine's `table_resize`
tests pass. No new commands, labels or docs changes (a fix to #600's behaviour).

title: Word 365 cover pages: freeforms in groups, text-box margins and Resize to fit (#743)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #743.

A Word 365 cover page lost its look. The missing fills were theme-coloured shapes (scheme colours and `wps:style` fill references), which main already draws since #611; the reporter's 0.5.0 build predates it. This PR fixes the two causes still open on main:

- **A freeform inside a group keeps its outline.** Custom geometry (`a:custGeom`) was read only for standalone shapes, so a freeform in a `wpg` group was drawn as a rectangle.
- **Text boxes keep their own margins and Resize shape to fit text.** `wps:bodyPr` `lIns`/`tIns`/`rIns`/`bIns` and `a:spAutoFit` were ignored, so layout used the default 7.2/3.6 pt margins and cut text that didn't fit; a tight title box lost its second line. Both are read, laid out and written back.

Tests: `cover_page_group_fills_freeforms_and_text_box_margins` (crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs, before and after a save) and `own_margins_and_resize_to_fit_keep_the_text_in_view` (crates/layout/src/tests_textbox.rs). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Note: the file attached to the issue had already been re-saved by WordCraft, so its fills are gone; reopening the original from Word shows them.

Not covered: Resize to fit doesn't grow the shape itself (it uses the size Word stored and stops the text being cut); VML-only text-box margins (`v:textbox inset`) aren't read.

title: Sorting and table numbers follow the text's language (#836, #837)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Sorting and table numbers now follow the text's language (`w:lang`, falling back to the document default).

- **Collation (#837).** Table › Sort, Home › Sort, the index (and its letter headings), the bibliography and the Table of Authorities use the language's alphabet. In Polish, Kraków < Łódź < Zakopane and ćma < dom < zebra. Swedish puts å ä ö after z; German sorts ä with a; Spanish puts ñ after n; Czech, Slovak and Hungarian follow their alphabets. This comes from a small hand-written table in `crates/doc/src/collate.rs` (no ICU). English results don't change.
- **Decimal comma (#836).** Table sort and formulas read numbers with the language's separators (`crates/doc/src/locale_number.rs`): in Polish `1,5` sorts before `2`, `=SUM` of `3,50` and `2,25` writes `5,75`, and `1 250,00` + `100` = `1350`. English still reads `1,250.50`; grouping must be in threes, so `1,5` is never read as 15.
- **Crash fix.** The table and paragraph sort comparisons could disagree with themselves, which Rust's sort may panic on. They now always give a consistent order (numbers first, then text).

Tests: `table_sort_reads_decimal_comma_in_polish`, `table_formula_reads_and_writes_decimal_comma_in_polish`, `table_and_paragraph_sort_use_polish_alphabet`, `index_sorts_polish_entries_and_headings` (crates/engine/src/tests.rs), plus unit tests for every language in both new modules, including junk input. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Not covered: interface lists (styles, fonts, bookmarks) still sort by code point; the bibliography and Table of Authorities sort in the document's default language; no full CLDR collation (French reverse accents, Swedish v/w).

Fixes #836
Fixes #837

title: Tests: linear-time checks measure CPU time, robust under load
author: echelon
body:
## Problem
Tests that assert linear-time behaviour by wall-clock ratios (`unequal_formats_lay_out_in_linear_time`, `hidden_separators_with_automatic_hyphenation_lay_out_in_linear_time`, `many_hidden_float_anchors_lay_out_in_linear_time`, pdf `long_fragmented_hidden_headings_export_in_linear_time`, proof `hyphenating_a_long_word_is_linear`) failed now and then on loaded machines but passed alone.

## Fix (test-only; no production code changes)
A small `cost_ratio(scale, small, big)` helper, used by all five:
- **CPU time, not wall clock**: the test thread's on-CPU time from `/proc/thread-self/schedstat` on Linux (safe file read; wall clock fallback elsewhere), so time spent waiting for a CPU on a busy machine doesn't count.
- **Small input repeated `scale` times** per timing, so both timings are long compared with the clock's resolution.
- **Interleaved rounds** (small, big, x5 after a warm-up), cheapest kept, so a busy spell hits both sizes alike.
- **8x input everywhere**: linear is about 8x, quadratic about 64x, and the limit is 24x. The pdf and hyphenation tests previously used 4x with an 8.0 limit, and hyphenation measured about 7.2 even when linear.

## Verification (machine loaded, load avg 15-35 on 32 cores)
- Each changed test 10x: 30/30 binary runs ok; 60 linear ratios all in **7.7-8.8** (limit 24).
- Full `wordcraft-layout` suite 5x: 199/199 each time. pdf and proof suites pass.
- **Still catches quadratic code**: I put back each old quadratic pattern locally, one at a time, and every affected test failed:
  - uncapped style bucket scan: unequal formats **90-104x**
  - hyphenator rescanning the word per point: hidden separators **36x**, hyphenation **50-65x**
  - anchor run walk restarted per object: float anchors **188x**
  - left-out range scan per char in `text_without`: PDF headings **37x**
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: Undo history list beside the Quick Access Toolbar's Undo (#701)
author: dkhlapov
body: Adds Word's Undo history list. A ▾ next to the Quick Access Toolbar's Undo lists recent steps, newest first. Hovering a row highlights it and every newer one, and the footer says what a click will do ("Undo 1 Action", "Undo 3 Actions", or "Cancel" when nothing is highlighted). A click undoes all of them at once and closes the list. Redo has no list, as in Word for Windows. *The Undo list open from the ▾ beside Undo, after typing, a new paragraph, more typing, then Bold and Italic. Hovering the third row highlights it and the two newer steps, and the footer reads "Undo 3 Actions"; a click undoes all three.* - **Engine:** `Session::undo_history()` (labels newest first, at most `UNDO_LIST_MAX` = 100) and `Session::undo_steps(n)`, which stops before a step that would remove the document's protection. - **Commands:** `edit.undoTo {"count": n}` is disabled with nothing to undo. A missing, zero, negative or non-numeric count is a params error, a count above the depth is clamped, and fractions round down. The read-only `edit.undoHistory` returns `{undo, depth, redo}` for the CLI and MCP. - **Catalog:** new row "Quick Access › Toolbar › Undo List" → `edit.undoTo` (parity 484/499). - **UI** (`chrome.rs`): uses the existing `dropdown` icon and `Tokens` colours. No new assets. - **Strings:** four new strings in every catalog. Russian, Ukrainian, Serbian, Polish and Czech use count-neutral wording. title: New documents follow the system region: A4, centimetres and decimal comma outside the US (#838)
author: dkhlapov
body:
New blank documents follow the system region, as in Word. They start on A4 outside the Letter territories (US, Canada, Mexico, the Philippines, …). Lengths are shown in centimetres outside the US, with the region's decimal separator (`2,54 cm`). Templates keep their own size.

- **Region** (`crates/geom/src/region.rs`): read from a locale tag (`pl-PL`, `de_AT.UTF-8`, `zh-Hans-CN`…; junk falls back to en-US). Paper is Letter in the territories CLDR lists for it and A4 elsewhere. Inches are used in the US (and Liberia and Myanmar), centimetres elsewhere.
- **Engine:** `Session.region` is a plain value, so nothing below the UI depends on sys-locale. Headless sessions and the CLI stay en-US, so output is the same on every machine. `Session::units()` uses an explicit choice if there is one, otherwise the region's unit. A blank `file.new` uses the region's paper with 2.54 cm margins and keeps main's editing language. `file.options` takes `"region": "pl-PL"` and `"units": "auto"`.
- **Where the region comes from:** `WORDCRAFT_REGION`, then `LC_ALL`/`LC_PAPER`/`LC_MEASUREMENT`/`LC_NUMERIC`/`LANG`, then sys-locale (the browser's language on the web). On Windows it is the home location (`GlobalizationPreferences.HomeGeographicRegion`; this adds the `System_UserProfile` feature to `windows`).
- **Fields:** length fields and menus show the region's decimal separator and accept either separator and any unit (`1 in` in a cm field). `Unit::format_with` takes the separator.
- **Saved preference:** `Prefs.units` is now optional and saved under a new key, `measurementUnits`. The old key always stored the inch default, so it can't be told apart from a real choice. **Anyone who picked a unit since #795 will see it reset to the region's default once.**

title: Insert › Picture takes WMF and EMF metafiles (#802)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Insert › Picture takes Windows Metafiles (`.wmf`) and Enhanced Metafiles (`.emf`).

WMF and EMF pictures already drew when they came inside a document (`crates/metafile`, in the renderer and the PDF writer), but inserting one failed with "not a supported image", and the Insert Picture dialog's filter, drag-and-drop and paste left them out.

- `wordcraft_render::metafile_size()` gives a metafile's natural size in points (placeable WMF and EMF frames; very large frames scaled to 22 inches on the longer side, keeping the shape) and its extension.

- `.wmf` and `.emf` are added to the file dialog's picture filter, drag-and-drop, file paste and the web app's picker. The error for an unsupported file now names WMF and EMF too.

Test: `insert_picture_takes_a_windows_metafile` (engine): a placeable 72 × 36 pt WMF is inserted at that size and stored as `.wmf`; a non-picture still fails with the format list. `docs/file-format-parity.md` gets a row for picture formats (SVG, TIFF, ICO and HEIC are still missing). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Font list previews no longer keep every family in memory (#848)
author: dkhlapov
body:
The Font box no longer keeps every font family it shows in memory.

**Cause.** Each Font box entry is drawn in its own font. That went through the full layout and render path (`previews.rs` `font_preview_fn` → `snippet` → `FontDb::face`), which loaded the whole family (every style file) into the global font database, where fonts are never unloaded. Every trip through the list kept another 20–30 families for good, so memory climbed with each font change (1.47 GB after 40 changes in the report).

**Fix.**
- `FontDb::preview_face` (crates/fonts): a family that's already loaded reuses its face; an installed one is read into a face the database doesn't keep, so it is freed when dropped.
- `wordcraft_render::render_text_line` draws that face directly, without the shared outline cache.
- `font_entry_image` (ui-egui `previews.rs`) replaces `snippet` for font list entries; a name the font can't draw, or a font that can't be read, shows in the default font.
- Also: `FontFace::glyph_outline`, `FontDb::loaded_font_bytes` (for measuring), and `is_loaded` made public.

**Measured** (Linux, 745 installed families): previewing 120 families went from +411 MB of resident memory (410 MB of font data held) to +17 MB (none held). A run like the report's (open the list, apply a font, lay out and render, 40 times) held 634 / 788 / 808 / 1013 MB of font data after 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 changes before, and 224 / 354 / 357 / 537 MB after.

**Not covered.** What remains is the families actually applied: each loads once (whole family) and stays. Ordinary fonts cost 0–5 MB, but a large family can be far more (Noto Serif CJK +174 MB here). Switching between fonts already used adds nothing. Loading single style files, or unloading unused families, would be a follow-up.

Tests: `fonts::tests_sysfonts::font_list_previews_load_nothing_for_good` (40 generated families previewed 5 times each: no faces or font data kept) and ui-egui `previews::tests::font_menu_entries_leave_installed_families_unloaded`. `c…

title: Section breaks no longer delete the selected text (#852)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Layout › Breaks deleted the selected text before inserting a section break.

**What happened in #852.** The attached document had been saved by WordCraft, and the word "one" isn't in it at all: the body is an empty paragraph with a next-page section break, an empty paragraph, "two", and a final continuous section. `breaks()` (crates/engine/src/cmd/page.rs) called `delete_selection` before splitting, so with "one" selected (a double-click selects a word), inserting a continuous break removed it. `wordcraft-cli run` with `select.text "one"` then `layout.break continuous` produces XML identical to the attachment. With a plain caret the break was already right, and the DOCX reader and layout handle continuous sections correctly.

**Fix.** A section break now goes just before the selection and keeps it; the selection stays on the same text in the same direction (new `shifted_by_split` helper), the main-text check uses the start of the selection, and the selection is restored if the split fails. This also stops Columns › "This point forward", which inserts a continuous break first, from deleting a selection.

Word's exact behaviour here (keep the selection vs. replace it) wasn't checked against Word; either way, deleting the user's text was wrong.

Test: `cmd::page::tests::section_break_keeps_the_selected_text`: "one" selected then a continuous break gives `["", "one", "two"]` with "one" still selected; a backward selection inside a paragraph keeps its text and direction; the document saved to DOCX and reopened has 2 sections, the last continuous, on 1 page with "one" above "two". `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Fixes #852

title: Wingdings, Webdings and Symbol text draws as Unicode symbols (#776)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Text set in Word's symbol fonts (Wingdings, Wingdings 2, Wingdings 3, Webdings and Symbol) now shows the intended symbols. These fonts are proprietary and never bundled, so before, a substitute font drew letters (or nothing) at their codes.

- **Tables** (`crates/doc/src/symbol_fonts.rs`): every code 0x20–0xFF of the five fonts mapped to Unicode, for both ways Word stores them: the private-use code U+F020–U+F0FF (`w:sym`) and the plain 8-bit code in a run set in that font. Soft hyphens are left alone. Sources (recorded in the module header): Unicode's Adobe `symbol.txt` for Symbol (codes it maps to private use are left out), and "Status of encoding of Wingdings and Webdings Symbols", L2/12-368 (WG2 N4384, 2012) for the other four, checked against UnicodeData names. Wingdings 0xFF (a logo) was never encoded and falls back as before. It lives in `doc` so layout, formats and the engine share it; the old partial `symbol_font_char` in `crates/fonts/src/word.rs` is gone, and that file's symbol substitute list now matches "Wingdings 2"/"Wingdings 3" and includes Noto Sans Symbols 2.
- **Layout** (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`): symbol-font characters are mapped before font fallback and shaping, so normal fallback picks an installed face that has the symbol; clusters still point at the stored text. If the real font is installed, its own glyph is used. A few list bullets fall back to a common look-alike when no installed face has the exact symbol. List labels go the same way. Merged with the numeral display modes (#501): the symbol mapping applies first, then the numeral form.
- **Text output**: PDF text, copy as text and TXT export give the Unicode characters. The stored text never changes, so DOCX round trips keep the original characters.

Tests: doc unit tests (both storage forms agree for every font; known codes per font, e.g. Wingdings ☺ 0x4A, ✓ 0xFC, ◼ 0x6E); a layout test (a Wingdings run draws and reads as ☺✓, stored text unchanged); a DOCX fixture with `w:sym`, a Wing…

title: Click in the left margin selects lines (selection bar) (#856)
author: dkhlapov
body:
A click in the left margin beside the text (Word's selection bar) selects lines, as in Word. Before, it only put the caret at the start of the line.

In the selection bar (left of the body column, between the header and footer areas):
- click selects the line; double-click the paragraph; triple-click or Ctrl/⌘+click the whole document;
- dragging selects whole lines at whatever height the pointer is; Shift+click extends the selection by lines;
- the pointer is an arrow (`CursorIcon::Default`; egui has no right-pointing arrow).

Changes:
- **Layout** (`crates/layout/src/hit.rs`): `selection_bar_at(page, x, y)` (the start of the body line at that height when the point is in the bar; nothing beside table lines or text hanging into the margin), `body_line_at(page, y)` (nearest top-level line, for drags), `line_span(pos, hint)` (the whole visual line, trailing spaces and break included, and whether it's the paragraph's last line).
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/caret.rs`): `select.line` selects the whole line (with the paragraph mark on a paragraph's last line) and takes an optional `{"pos"}`; before it selected start to end like Home/End, and nothing else used it. `select.dragUnit` accepts `"line"` and `"document"`.
- **UI** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): the clicks, drags and cursor above.

Tests: layout `selection_bar_finds_the_line_beside_the_pointer`; engine `selection_bar_selects_and_drags_by_lines` (with junk params); egui_kittest `selection_bar_clicks_select_lines` (click, double-click, triple-click, a three-line drag, Shift+click, the cursor). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Not yet: the right-margin bar for right-to-left paragraphs (they're reachable from the left margin for now), selecting table rows from the margin, a right-pointing cursor; Ctrl/⌘+click in the bar has no test of its own.

Fixes #856

title: styles.modify takes the hex colours format.color takes (#865)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #865: the colour half.

`format.color` takes `RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBB` and `auto`, but `styles.modify` (and `format.set`) deserialize `CharProps` directly. `TextColor`'s derived `Deserialize` only knows `"Auto"` and `{"Rgb": [r, g, b]}`, so `"1B1611"` failed with "unknown variant".

`TextColor` now has a hand-written `Deserialize`:
- a string goes through the new `TextColor::parse`, which is exactly what `format.color` did (that command now calls it too, so there's one parser);
- anything else reads through a private enum shaped like the old derive, so `"Auto"` and `{"Rgb": [...]}` read as before.

`Serialize` is unchanged, so documents written today and those already on disk round-trip identically. An invalid colour (`"1B16"`, `{"Rgb": "1B1611"}`, `7`) is still a parameter error, and the style is left as it was.

Validation:
- `props::tests::text_color_reads_hex_and_keeps_its_serialized_forms` and `tests::modify_style_takes_hex_colours_like_format_color` fail on main and pass here. Turning an invalid string into `Auto`, or dropping the `{"Rgb": ...}` form, fails both.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc -p wordcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Left out to keep this small: `underline_color`, `shading` and border colours (plain `Rgb`, still only `[r, g, b]`), and the issue's second request, documenting the `CharProps` / `ParaProps` shapes in `docs/mcp.md`. So #865 should stay open for the docs part.

title: STYLEREF fields show each page's result in headers and footers (#775)
author: dkhlapov
body:
STYLEREF fields work: in headers and footers each page shows its own result, which is how Word templates put the current chapter title on every page.

- **Field** (`crates/layout/src/styleref.rs`, ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5.59): the code is parsed. The result comes from an index of body paragraphs in document order, with their styles, text, character-style runs and list numbers. In a header/footer it's the page's first paragraph with the style (`\l`: the last), else the nearest one before the page, else the next one after. In the body it searches back from the field, then forward. Accepts a style name or id (any case), a heading level (`STYLEREF 1`) or a character style, and the switches `\n \w \s \t \p` (`\r` works like `\w`). With no match it shows "Error: no paragraph in this style."
- **Per page**: `FieldCtx` carries the STYLEREF index; `headers_footers` gives each page its result, so the screen and PDF export show the live value. The paragraph cache key includes a hash of the index, so editing a heading updates the headers.
- **Body fields** update with the other fields (`update_seq` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs` uses the same module). The old chapter-number behaviour of `\s` (falling back to the heading count) is kept, and the caption tests pass.
- **Insert › Quick Parts › Field** lists STYLEREF, with a style picker and the switch checkboxes. `Counters::values` added in `crates/doc/src/numbering.rs`.
- Double-click to enter and leave headers/footers, also asked for in the issue, already works on main.

title: Fonts: documents use the craft-fonts Simplified Chinese face (fixes FreeBSD CI after #567)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Builds with craft-fonts (releases, and the FreeBSD job) put only craft-fonts' Japanese faces in the document font database; its Noto Sans CJK SC was used by the interface alone. Simplified-only ideographs in a document then had no face unless the system had one, and the run-level CJK pick from #567 found no face covering a mixed run. The FreeBSD job's `east_asian_run_uses_one_face_covering_the_whole_run` fails on main for this reason, and so does every PR that touches `crates/fonts` (e.g. #874).

- `FontDb::with_font_dirs` adds the craft-fonts Simplified Chinese faces after the Japanese ones, so Japanese text still falls back to the Mincho first and simplified Chinese gets the SC face.
- `fallback_reads_each_installed_font_file_once_however_many_characters_miss` used U+30001.. as "characters nothing maps", but Noto Sans CJK SC maps part of CJK Extension G there; it now uses Supplementary Private Use Area-A, which no font here maps.

title: cli: print usage on mcp --help and -h
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
## Summary

Enables `wordcraft-cli mcp --help` and `wordcraft-cli mcp -h` to print subcommand usage and option descriptions rather than exiting with `unknown option --help`.

Relates to #374 (partial improvement for CLI discoverability and options; does not close #374).

## Problem and Root Cause

When invoking `wordcraft-cli mcp --help`, argument validation in `validate_options("mcp", &rest, MCP_OPTIONS)` checked the options list `MCP_OPTIONS`. Because `MCP_OPTIONS` only registered `--connect` and `--author`, `--help` was rejected as an unknown option before any help text could be rendered, outputting:
```
wordcraft-cli: mcp: unknown option --help
```

## Implementation Summary

- Registered `--help` in `MCP_OPTIONS` so `validate_options` recognizes the help flag.
- Defined `MCP_USAGE` documenting the `mcp` subcommand purpose, options (`--connect`, `--author`), and help flags (`-h, --help`).
- Handled `--help` and `-h` in the `mcp` command dispatch using `write_stdout` to output `MCP_USAGE` cleanly (including handling closed pipes gracefully).
- Preserved existing behavior: unknown options (e.g. `--hepl`, `--foobar`) continue to be rejected with exit code 1.

## Regression Tests

- **Unit tests** (`apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs`):
  - Verified `validate_options` accepts `--help`.
  - Verified unknown options (`--hepl`) are rejected before execution.
  - Verified `run(&["mcp", "--help"])` and `run(&["mcp", "-h"])` return `Ok(())` and reference documented flags.
- **Integration tests** (`apps/wordcraft-cli/tests/mcp_help.rs`):
  - Executed compiled binary with `--help` and `-h`.
  - Verified exit code 0, empty stderr, and stdout containing usage and options.

## Verification & CI Results

Verified locally on macOS (Apple Silicon):
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-cli`: all 8 tests passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed (0 warnings).

title: Smooth scrolling through a very large table (#811)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Scrolling through a document with one very large table is smooth again.

**Cause.** Not table layout: `Session::layout()` is cached by revision, so scrolling never re-laid anything out. Two things ran on every frame, even with nothing moving:
- `page_key` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) fingerprinted every item of every page for the page texture cache, building a string for every cell border: 436 ms a frame on the issue's file (1,096 pages, 5,323 rows, 68k cells).
- `markup_width` walked all paragraphs (`has_format_changes` and others), twice a frame (~55 ms).
- Separately, page textures were never dropped, so scrolling through the document kept every page it had shown.

**Fix** (ui-egui only; layout and rendering untouched):
- each page's content fingerprint is computed once per layout, and only for pages on screen or already cached; the view-dependent part of the key is computed once per frame;
- the document checks behind the markup-area width are cached per document id and revision;
- textures for pages more than 3 screens from the view are dropped and re-rendered when they come back.
Merged with Reading Mode (#740), whose own off-screen skip this covers.

**Numbers** (release, headless kittest at 1440×900, loaded machine, so rough):

| | Idle frame | Scroll frame median / max |
|---|---|---|
| Issue's docx, before | ~598 ms | ~591 / 1820 ms |
| Issue's docx, after | 2.35 ms | 4.5 / 13.7 ms (max includes page renders) |
| Synthetic 2000×8 table (137 pages), before | ~45 ms | ~57 / 107 ms |
| Synthetic 2000×8 table, after | 1.3 ms | 3.6 / 7.3 ms |

Tests (`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_perf.rs`): `scrolling_a_big_table_fingerprints_only_pages_coming_into_view` (600×8 table: only on-screen pages are fingerprinted at first, idle frames fingerprint nothing, 60 scroll steps fingerprint only pages coming into view, the layout stays the same object, at most 12 textures are kept); `big_table_scroll_bench` (`#[ignore]`, set `WORDCRAFT_BENCH_DOCX` to time a real file). `cargo…

title: Drawing ink no longer jumps the view back to the caret (#859)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #859.

Every command that isn't `view.*`, `document.*` or `format.state*` sets `scroll_to_caret` in `after_command`, and that included the `draw.*` commands the canvas runs when you lift the pen (`draw.stroke`), erase (`draw.erase`) or use the lasso (`draw.lasso`, `draw.lassoMove`). On the next frame the canvas scrolled back to the caret, which is usually still on page 1, so every stroke drawn further down the document threw the view away. Drawing never moves the caret (the draw commands only shift its offset when they insert or delete the ink's anchor character), so `after_command` now leaves `draw.*` out as well.

Validation:
- New test `drawing_ink_keeps_the_view_where_it_is` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: runs `draw.stroke`, `draw.lasso`, `draw.lassoMove` and `draw.erase` (each asserted to succeed) and checks none of them asks to scroll to the caret, then checks that `text.insert` still does. On main it fails with "draw.stroke scrolled to the caret".
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Other commands that act on objects (`arrange.*`, `shape.*`, `picture.*`) take the same path; I left them alone since I haven't checked they never move the caret.

title: Open RTF in its code page, and Word/RTF files whose extension is wrong
author: xmaks82
body:
Two problems found by opening a private corpus of 251 real Russian Word documents (business letters, contracts, résumés; can't be shared):

**1. 38 of 44 `.doc` files didn't open at all.** They are RTF saved with a `.doc` extension, which hh.ru résumé downloads and many accounting/report generators produce. Word opens them by content; WordCraft dispatched on the extension and failed with `not a Word document (compound file): Invalid CFB file (wrong magic number)`. `open_by_content` (#569) already sniffs signatures, but only for unknown extensions. Now `open_bytes_with` also routes there when a Word/RTF extension contradicts the content: RTF in `.doc`/`.dot`/`.docx`, a `.docx` package renamed `.doc`/`.rtf`, a Word 97-2003 file renamed `.docx`. Matching files take the usual path.

**2. Once open, their Russian text was mojibake.** The RTF reader decoded every `\'hh` and raw 8-bit byte as Windows-1252 (`Ñ÷åò ¹ 12` instead of `Счет № 12`). It now decodes in the current font's code page (`\fcharset`, or an explicit `\cpg`), else the default font's (`\deff`), else the document's (`\ansicpg`), falling back to 1252 as before. `wordcraft_doc::encoding` gains the single-byte Windows code pages 874 and 1250–1258 (tables written from the code page definitions) and the RTF/Word charset → code page map (204 → 1251, 238 → 1250, 161 → 1253…). Double-byte East Asian charsets are left as they were.

Result on the corpus: all 38 open, with correct Cyrillic. The one remaining failure is a `.docx` that is genuinely truncated.

Tests: `documents_open_by_content_when_the_extension_is_wrong` (engine), `code_pages_from_ansicpg_and_font_charsets` (formats: `\ansicpg1251`, font charsets switching Western → Cyrillic → Central European inside one paragraph, default font charset, `\cpg` over `\fcharset`, raw 8-bit text), `single_byte_code_pages` (doc). `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test` for doc/formats/engine/docbin, wasm check for the three crates. `docs/file-format-parity.md` updated.

title: Docs: list the CharProps and ParaProps fields (#865)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:

`docs/mcp.md` gets a "Character and paragraph properties" section listing every field of `CharProps` and `ParaProps` as `format.set`, `para.set`, `styles.modify` and the table style commands take them: the JSON name, its type, and the accepted values for the enums, `lineSpacing`, `numbering`, `tabs` and borders. It also says that an unknown field is ignored rather than refused, which is what makes a misspelt name hard to spot. `docs/control-protocol.md` links to it. The `color` row describes what main accepts today (`"Auto"` or `{"Rgb": [r, g, b]}`); whichever of this and #881 lands second can add the hex form to that line.

title: i18n: French wording fixes after #729
author: tellebma

title: RTF: read page size and margins, lay tables out on their cell edges
author: xmaks82
body:
RTF opened on US Letter with 1" margins whatever the file said, and every table got equal columns and a full grid. Russian accounting/HR exports (A4, 2 cm margins, borderless layout tables whose rows have different `\cellx` edges) came out about twice as long as in Word.

- `\paperw`/`\paperh`/`\margl`…`\margb` (and the `…sxn` section forms), `\headery`, `\footery` and `\landscape` now set the section; out-of-range values keep Word's defaults. Tables size to that page (new `model::to_doc_in`).
- A table's column grid is the union of its rows' `\cellx` edges; each cell spans the grid columns between its left and right edges, as Word lays it out.
- A table with no left/right cell borders is laid out without the grid style (`\clbrdrb` rules alone don't make it ruled; `\brdrnone` is no border).

**Checked** against Word's own page counts (Word COM export) on 44 real RTF documents (most named .doc): total page-count difference 198 → 30, exact matches 3 → 17, no file got worse. `.docx` results unchanged.

Builds on #896 (RTF code pages) — its first commit is that PR's; review the last commit.

Tests: `page_size_and_margins`, `table_grid_from_cell_edges_and_borders`; `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats -p wordcraft-engine` and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: Fonts: treat Windows charset names (Times New Roman Cyr, Arial CE…) as the font itself
author: xmaks82
body:
Old Russian and Central European documents name fonts by their Windows 3.1 charset aliases: `Times New Roman Cyr`, `Arial CYR`, `Courier New CE`, `Arial (Hebrew)`. Windows maps these to the font itself (`HKLM\…\FontSubstitutes`), so Word shows Times New Roman; we treated them as unknown families and fell back to the sans default, which changes the look and the page count.

`resolve()` now tries the base family (not marked as substituted when it is installed), and otherwise substitutes for the base family (`Times New Roman Cyr` → Liberation Serif, like Times New Roman). New `charset_base_family()` with tests in `unknown_family_substitutes`.

Found while comparing WordCraft against Word's own PDF output on a corpus of real Russian business documents. `cargo test -p wordcraft-fonts` and clippy pass.

title: Tables: formulas with cell references, functions, number formats and F9
author: rbr48
body:
Table Layout › Data › Formula was a fixed set of string checks: any unknown function was silently summed, cell references weren't read, and Update Field never recalculated a formula field.

Formulas are now parsed and evaluated (crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs):
- cell references and ranges by grid column (=B2+B3, =SUM(B2:C3)),
  + - * / ^, parentheses and the comparisons = <> < <= > >=
- SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN, PRODUCT, ABS, INT, SIGN, ROUND, MOD, IF (only the branch taken is worked out), AND, OR, NOT, TRUE, FALSE, DEFINED
- ABOVE/LEFT/RIGHT/BELOW sum the first run of numbers next to the cell, as observed in Word; `=SUM()` is a syntax error, as in Word; a bare `=SUM` takes ABOVE or LEFT from the cell
- the \# numeric picture (`#,##0.00`, `0%`, `;` sections)
- an unknown function or a syntax error is an error and inserts nothing; input is bounded (formula length, nesting depth)

Update Field (F9) re-evaluates formula fields from the cells they read.

title: fix(doc): count generated numbered-list labels as words
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
### Summary

In Microsoft Word, automatic numbered-list labels (`1.`, `2.`, etc.) are counted as independent words in document statistics, while bullet markers (`•`, `-`) are omitted. Previously, WordCraft's word counting traversed only plain paragraph run text (`plain_text`), omitting generated list numbers. This caused WordCraft to report 357 words for the sample document (`crates/engine/src/sample.rs`) compared to Word's 361 words (a 4-word discrepancy corresponding to the 4 numbered steps under "Opening the studio").

This PR updates word counting to include generated numbered-list labels across document stories, matching Microsoft Word's word count behavior while strictly preserving character counts and plain text.

Fixes #893

---

### Root Cause & Implementation Details

1. **Root Cause**:
   - In WordCraft, list numbers are generated dynamically from abstract list definitions and counter state (`numbering::Counters::next_label`), rather than being stored in paragraph run text.
   - Counting words using `count_words(&d.plain_text(StoryRef::Body))` only inspected run characters in `Block::Para`, ignoring the prefix numbering labels.

2. **Word Count Implementation**:
   - Added `Document::story_word_count(&self, s: StoryRef) -> usize` and `story_word_count_of(bl, numbering, styles, counters, depth) -> usize` in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`.
   - `story_word_count_of` steps list counters in document order. For paragraphs with numbering, it evaluates the generated label:
     - Formats with `NumFormat::Bullet` or `NumFormat::None` are skipped.
     - Numbered labels (e.g. `1.`, `a)`, `I.`) are counted as words via `count_words(&label)`.
     - The paragraph run text is counted via `count_words(&p.plain_text())`.
   - `Document::word_count()` and `Document::word_count_including_notes()` call `story_word_count`.

3. **LevelSuffix::Nothing & Word Independence**:

title: Track Changes: Accept All keeps the paragraph after a tracked deletion (#864)
author: 2mingho
body:
Fixes #864.

## Problem
With Track Changes on, deleting a range that ends at a paragraph's end (end of "Alpha" to end of "Charlie") and choosing **Accept All** also joined the next paragraph: `AlphaDelta\nEcho` instead of `Alpha\nDelta\nEcho`. Without tracking the result was right, and Reject All was right.

## Cause
`Paragraph::delete` gives an emptied paragraph's mark the properties of the text that went (`para.rs`, "Keep the formatting of what's deleted for the mark when emptying"), revisions included. In `resolve_para`, accepting the fully deleted "Charlie" therefore left its mark carrying the deletion revision, and the same call then removed that mark as an accepted deleted paragraph mark, joining "Delta" into it.

## Fix
`resolve_para` keeps the mark's own revisions (`ins`, `del`, `fmt_change`) across the text deletion.

## Tests
- New `accepting_a_deletion_that_starts_at_a_paragraph_end_keeps_the_next_paragraph` replays the report plus an untracked control. It fails on `main` (`AlphaDelta\nEcho`) and passes with the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm all pass.

## Not covered
I only checked Accept All. Reject All goes through the same code path, but I did not add a test for it.

Also adds my `contributors/people.toml` entry (display name only).

body:

title: Portable mode: a portable.txt beside the exe keeps settings in WordCraftData (#867)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Closes #867.

A file named `portable.txt` next to the executable now keeps WordCraft's settings folder in a `WordCraftData` folder beside it, instead of `%APPDATA%\WordCraft` (or the macOS/Linux equivalents). Everything that already lives in that folder moves with it: `ui.json`, `logs/`, `custom-dictionary.txt`, the user's added `fonts/` and the control-key files. It works the way FilmCraft (#303) and PhotoCraft already do it: the marker has to be a file, and a folder called `portable.txt` is ignored. On macOS the marker goes next to `WordCraft.app`, not inside the bundle, and `WordCraftData` is created there too. The folder name is `WordCraftData`, as the issue asks. The Windows portable zip now ships `portable.txt`. The MSI and the macOS `.app` don't, so installed copies keep their current paths.

The change is in `wordcraft_control_key::settings_dir()`, which every one of those paths already goes through (`prefs_path`, `log_dir`, `user_dict_path`, `load_user_fonts` and the control server in `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`, and the key lookup in `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`). `wordcraft-cli` sits next to `wordcraft.exe` in the zip, so `wordcraft-cli mcp --connect` finds the key in the same folder. Without a marker, `settings_dir()` returns exactly what it returns today. `WORDCRAFT_NO_PREFS` still turns preferences, the dictionary, fonts and the log file off, portable or not.

I kept the FilmCraft model rather than PhotoCraft's writability probe. `settings_dir()` is a plain path lookup that both the app and the MCP bridge call, and the app already copes with a folder it can't write: preferences aren't saved and the log says `no log file`. If you'd rather have the probe and a fallback to `%APPDATA%`, I can add it.

craft-settings (storytold/craft-libs#22) will cover this once it lands; the marker and folder names here are meant to become this app's `PORTABLE_MARKERS` / `PORTABLE_DIR` values there.

Overlap with #586: it adds a `WORDCRAFT_PROFILE_DIR` override at the top…

title: Track Changes: Accept All no longer joins an extra paragraph after a tracked delete from a paragraph end (#864)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #864

## Cause

`Paragraph::delete` (`crates/doc/src/para.rs`) copies the formatting of the text it deletes onto the paragraph mark when the deletion empties the paragraph, so the empty paragraph keeps the look of what was typed in it. That copy included the revision fields (`ins`, `del`, `fmt_change`), which are not formatting.

`review.acceptAll` accepts a tracked deletion by deleting the text. For a paragraph whose whole text was tracked-deleted ("Bravo" and "Charlie" in the issue), the mark therefore turned into a deleted mark as well, and the next step joined the following paragraph into it. In the issue's example the third paragraph ends up with a deleted mark that was never part of the change, so "Delta" is pulled into "Alpha".

Rejecting has the same problem from the other side: Reject All after typing into an empty paragraph removed the typed text, the mark picked up the text's insertion, and the empty paragraph itself was rejected and joined to the next one.

## Fix

When `Paragraph::delete` empties a paragraph, the mark keeps its own `ins`, `del` and `fmt_change`. Only the formatting is taken from the deleted text. One place changes (`crates/doc/src/para.rs`), no change in `review.rs`.

## Verified

Built `wordcraft-cli` from `main` and from this branch and ran the issue's steps (`text.insert` + `text.newParagraph` for the five paragraphs, then `review.trackChanges`, `select.range` end of "Alpha" to end of "Charlie", `text.delete`, `review.acceptAll`, `document.text`):

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Accept All | `AlphaDelta\nEcho` | `Alpha\nDelta\nEcho` |
| Reject All | `Alpha\nBravo\nCharlie\nDelta\nEcho` | unchanged |
| untracked delete | `Alpha\nDelta\nEcho` | unchanged |

Regression tests, each one fails without the fix and passes with it (checked by reverting only the `para.rs` change):

- `tests::accept_all_after_a_tracked_delete_from_a_paragraph_end_keeps_the_next_paragraph` (engine; also checks that Reject All still restores the…

title: DOCX: keep w:dirty on a field begin marker when saving (#877)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #877

## Cause

The reader never looked at `w:dirty` on a field's `w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"` marker, so the model had nowhere to keep it and the writer could not emit it. A plain open-and-save dropped the request that Word rebuild the field on open (generators that can't paginate write a placeholder TOC result and set it). `w:fldLock` takes the same path and already survived.

## Fix

`InlineObject::Field` and `InlineObject::FieldStart` get a `dirty` flag next to `locked`, serialized only when set, so existing documents and JSON are unchanged.

- Reader: `w:dirty` is read from `w:fldChar` begin and from `w:fldSimple` (same on/off parsing as `w:fldLock`) and carried into the objects built for simple fields, range fields (TOCs, `INCLUDEPICTURE`) and the TOC that is turned into a held field (`read/mod.rs`).
- Writer: `field_start` emits `w:dirty="true"` on the begin marker when set, including the held-TOC path that opens the field in the first entry.
- Most of the diff is adding `dirty: false` to existing struct literals (tests and engine commands) and the lines rustfmt re-wrapped because of it.

## Verified

With the issue's `make_min.py` fixture and `wordcraft-cli convert min.docx rt.docx`:

| | begin marker in `rt.docx` |
|---|---|
| `main` | `<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"/>` |
| this branch | `<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin" w:dirty="true"/>` |

New `crates/docx/tests/field_dirty.rs`; the first three fail without the fix and pass with it:

- `a_dirty_toc_field_stays_dirty_through_saves` (two read/write cycles)
- `a_dirty_toc_under_a_heading_with_entries_stays_dirty` (the held-TOC writer path)
- `dirty_survives_on_simple_and_complex_fields_with_a_lock` (`w:fldSimple` and a complex field with `w:fldLock`, lock unaffected)
- `fields_without_the_flag_do_not_gain_it` (control: no flag, `w:dirty="false"` and lock-only fields get no `w:dirty`; passes before and after)

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

## Not changed

title: DOCX: keep w:dirty on fields through open and save (#877)
author: 2mingho
body:
Fixes #877.

## Problem
A field whose `begin` marker carries `w:dirty="true"` lost the attribute after a plain open and save. Generators that can't paginate write a placeholder TOC result and set the flag so Word rebuilds the field on opening; after a WordCraft round trip the placeholder stayed until someone updated fields by hand.

## Change
- `InlineObject::Field` and `FieldStart` get a `dirty` flag (skipped when serialising a clean field, so existing JSON is unchanged).
- Read from `w:dirty` on a complex field's begin marker and on `w:fldSimple`, with `w:fldLock` as the template, including the TOC range path.
- Written next to `w:fldLock` by a new `fld_begin` helper, which replaces two duplicated `if locked` blocks (`field_start`, `enclosure`).
- WordCraft never sets the flag itself.

## Open question for maintainers
Should `references.updateToc` / `updateFields` clear the flag once WordCraft has computed a result? Word does, but our page numbers come from our own layout, so this PR keeps it (the safer side while pagination differs from Word). Clearing it would be a small follow-up.

## Diff size
27 files, but almost all of it is mechanical: every literal `Field`/`FieldStart` gets `dirty: false`, and `rustfmt` re-wraps the lines that got longer. The logic is about 60 lines in `crates/doc/src/para.rs` and `crates/docx/src/{read,write}`. `ROADMAP.md` changes in one table row plus the status line, in case it conflicts with another PR.

## Tests
New `crates/docx/tests/field_dirty.rs` (5 tests, original fixtures): a dirty TOC placeholder, a field whose result spans paragraphs, a `fldSimple`, each field keeping only its own flag, two saves in a row, and negative controls (no flag, or an off value, writes none). With the writer change disabled, 4 of the 5 fail; the negative control keeps passing.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: M1: fields keep w:dirty through saves; computing a result clears it (#877)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #877. Also pins #878 (already fixed on main by #617) with a regression test.

## What was broken

A field begin marker carrying `w:dirty="true"` lost the attribute on a plain open-and-save. Generators that can't paginate (pandoc-style pipelines, python-docx templates) write a placeholder TOC result and set the flag so Word rebuilds the field on open — after a round trip through WordCraft, Word stopped doing that and the placeholder stayed visible.

## The fix

Mirrors `w:fldLock` end to end, exactly as the issue suggested:

- **Model**: `InlineObject::Field` and `FieldStart` gain `#[serde(default)] dirty: bool` (skipped when false, so JSON/docbin stay compatible).
- **Reader**: `w:dirty` read on both `w:fldChar` begin markers and `w:fldSimple`, carried through `FieldState` into buffered fields and range-field starts; the TOC-heading conversion threads it too.
- **Writer**: the begin marker emits `w:dirty="true"` when set — on the buffered path, the `FieldStart` path and the TOC-spanning begin.
- **Lifecycle (the issue's open question)**: computing a result clears the flag — `references.updateFields`/`updateToc` on the fields they compute, like Word's F9. Untouched fields keep it through saves, so a placeholder TOC still refreshes in Word until WordCraft replaces the placeholder. `range_toc_to_field` constructs the engine TOC field already clean.

## Tests

- `field_dirty_flag_round_trips` / `range_toc_dirty_flag_round_trips` (`crates/docx`): the #877 repro shapes — a dirty begin marker injected into a written package survives read→write, and a clean field gains no flag; the range-field test is #878's exact fixture shape (placeholder inside the field).
- `update_fields_clears_dirty` (`crates/engine`): TITLE/NUMWORDS clear the flag when computed; an unknown field keeps it.
- `imported_dirty_toc_updates_in_place_and_clears` (`crates/engine`): pins #878 — the placeholder is replaced in place by the entries, the flag survives plain saves, clears on update, and undo…
