title: fix(ui): draw Arabic and other non-Latin comment text in balloons
author: ms-youssef
body:
## Summary
- **Boxes instead of letters.** Comment balloons and the Comments pane draw comment text and author names with the interface faces, which have no Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and so on. An Arabic comment showed as `□□□□` while the same Arabic in the document body rendered fine. `WordApp::ensure_comment_fonts` now borrows a document fallback face that covers the comment text, the same way the window caption does since #840. It runs once per document revision, and CJK text goes to the CJK UI font instead.
- **Words in the wrong order.** egui lays bidi runs and words out left to right, so once the letters drew, a right-to-left comment read backwards. Read-only balloons now go through `balloon_text`:
  - it wraps by word widths, because egui draws a lam-alef pair as one glyph, so its rows can't be mapped back to characters
  - it puts each row in display order: Unicode bidi runs, words of a right-to-left run reversed (egui already shapes each word right to left), and brackets mirrored
  - it sets right-to-left paragraphs against the right edge
- **No change elsewhere.** Text without right-to-left letters takes the old `painter.layout` path. The editable fields (the selected balloon and the Comments pane `TextEdit`) keep logical order. Reordering editable text would break the caret, and #737's `bidi.rs` is the broader work there.

Related: #63, #211, #215.

## Tests
- `arabic_comment_text_is_drawn_in_the_balloons`: a document with an Arabic comment borrows a covering face, once. It fails without the fix.
- `a_right_to_left_balloon_reads_from_the_right`: measures egui glyph positions. title: fix(references): clear imported TOC field result on update (#878)
author: Totopo27
body:
## Summary

When a DOCX imported from an external producer has a TOC field with an inline placeholder or cached result (e.g. `Placeholder: update fields (F9).`), running `references.updateToc` previously left the field's `result` string intact. As a consequence, `toc_span` in `crates/docx/src/write/story.rs` did not identify the TOC because it expects `result.is_empty()`, causing the DOCX writer to write the field as a self-contained inline field in the first paragraph and write the generated TOC entries as plain paragraphs after the field's `end` marker.

## Fix

In `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs` (`regenerate_toc`), clear `result` on the TOC field in the start paragraph before generating entries. This brings the document model into the shape expected by `toc_span`, allowing the writer to span the TOC field across the entries between its `begin` and `end` markers.

## Verification

- Added regression test `update_toc_clears_stale_field_result_for_docx_span` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` verifying that the placeholder is removed from plain text and that in the exported DOCX XML the entries are contained between `w:fldCharType="begin"` and `w:fldCharType="end"`.
- Ran unit tests across `wordcraft-engine` and `wordcraft-docx`.
- Clean clippy and fmt.

Fixes #878

title: Fix browser font fallback and compatible text box spacing
author: Pav91
body:
DOCX files using Arial can lose a short floating text box caption in the browser when fallback font metrics make the second line exceed the box height. Large text box headings can also overlap nearby objects because DrawingML compatible line spacing is ignored.

This change retains optional metric-compatible document fonts in web builds and registers all optional font scripts in the font database, preserving Japanese fallback ordering. It stores and round-trips `wps:bodyPr/@compatLnSpc` in TextBody and applies font-scene spacing during layout without changing stored paragraph formatting.

Regression coverage checks browser font selection, a 4pt spacer plus 18pt caption inside a 36pt box, compatible large heading spacing, and DOCX save/reopen preservation. No document assets, proprietary fonts, or user documents are included. Arimo used for local verification is an external optional OFL font input; releases must provide a suitable CRAFT_FONTS_DIR to benefit from the substitution.

The reported caption and heading overlap were visually corrected in a locally rebuilt 0.5.0 browser comparison. This PR ports those changes to current main and its newer TextBody model. General pagination parity is outside this change.

Validation on current main: focused font, layout, and DOCX test suites pass with the Arimo optional font input; Clippy for doc/fonts/layout/docx passes with warnings denied; WebAssembly checks for layout and DOCX pass; formatting and whitespace checks pass. The required full `cargo xtask ci` run passed formatting and workspace Clippy but could not complete workspace tests after build artifacts exhausted local disk space. This is a draft pending full CI and maintainer review of compatible spacing semantics.

Updated onto the latest main after opening the PR, preserving newly added upstream layout tests. The complete layout test suite passes after resolving the append-only test conflict.

title: Layout: blank pages put sections on the right side, and paragraph spacing is the larger of after and before (#733, rebased)
author: echelon

Before: the space between two paragraphs was the sum of the first one's space after and the second one's space before, and sections starting on an odd or even page didn't get the blank page that puts them on the right side.

title: Tables: one selected cell's border drags in its row only
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #962. The known gap left in #720 (#711), now that #637's whole-cell selection is in `main`.

title: Tab stops: edit on the ruler (corner selector, click, drag, drag off) and an inline-edit table in the Tabs dialog
author: iot-root
body:
Closes storytold/wordcraft#975.

Editing tab stops meant opening the Tabs dialog from a double-click (#320) — the ruler was read-only, and inside the dialog an alignment change on a selected stop was silently discarded unless Set was pressed first. This makes tab stops directly editable in both places.

## The ruler (Word parity)

- **A selector in the rulers' corner** picks the kind of stop a click sets — Left, Center, Right, Decimal, Bar — cycling on click (right-click cycles back), drawn with the kind's glyph.
- **Clicking an empty stretch of the ruler** sets a stop of that kind, snapped to half a ruler division; **Alt** places freely.
- **Dragging a stop** moves it, with the marker drawn at its landing point, a dashed guide down the page, and a tooltip with the position in the document's unit. **Dragging it off the ruler** (18 pt) clears it; **Escape** cancels, like a table-border drag (#217).
- **Markers draw per kind** (left/right feet, centred tee, decimal dot, bar stem), mirrored for right-to-left paragraphs. Double-clicking one still opens the Tabs dialog.
- Every gesture becomes one `para.tabs` call on release (`set`, `clear`, or `clear`+`set`), so each is **one undo step** and inherited-stop clearing (`TabAlign::Clear`) keeps working. Gestures are primary-button only, a click on an indent marker places nothing, and a drag whose paragraph the caret leaves — or whose release the ruler never saw — is abandoned rather than applied elsewhere (`TabDrag` carries its paragraph).

## The Tabs dialog (beyond parity — flagging for review)

The dialog's staged fields reproduced Word's flow, including its worst trap: select a stop, pick a new alignment, OK — change lost. Rather than patch that, the stop list is now an **inline-edit table**, and the fields it made redundant are gone:

- Each row is **[position] [alignment ▾] [leader ▾] [×]**. The position field is unit-aware (`1.25`, `3 cm`, `18pt`, either decimal separator, via the existing `parse_measure`); rows reso…

title: --help and -h print the usage for the app and every CLI command (#968)
author: Nael-Nathanael

title: fix(cli): reject invalid page and scale arguments
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
Fixes #981

### Problem
In `wordcraft-cli`, `render` and `run --save out.png` accepted invalid or malformed arguments for `--page` and `--scale`:
- Malformed strings (e.g. `--page banana`, `--scale banana`), missing values (e.g. `--page`), and negative page numbers were parsed with `.ok().unwrap_or(...)`, silently falling back to default values (Page 1 and Scale 2.0) with exit code 0.
- Non-positive scales (e.g. `--scale 0` or negative scales) were parsed as floats and passed to `file.exportPng`, which clamped them to `0.1` and silently generated an 80x62 pixel thumbnail without warning.
- Duplicate `--page` or `--scale` options silently took the first occurrence.

### Solution
- Added `find_option_arg`, `parse_page_arg`, and `parse_scale_arg` in `apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs`.
- Validates that `--page` is a positive integer (`>= 1`).
- Validates that `--scale` is a finite, positive number (`> 0.0`).
- Rejects missing operands, malformed inputs, out-of-range values, and duplicate flags with exit code 1 and a clear diagnostic on stderr.
- Validates options before opening files or initializing sessions, preventing unnecessary file access and ensuring no output file is written on failure.
- Preserves documented defaults (Page 1, Scale 2.0) when flags are omitted.
- Normal behavior for valid PNG exports and standard `run --save out.docx` remains completely unaffected.

### Testing
- Added regression tests in `apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs` covering missing operands, non-numeric values, zero/negative/NaN/inf values, duplicate flags, argument ordering, and file non-creation on failure.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-cli`: all 12 unit tests and 2 integration tests passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 gates passed (`fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `assets`, `layers`, `wasm`).

title: Layout: keep with next follows a paragraph moved by widow/orphan control (#966)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #966.

## Problem

A paragraph with keep with next (typically a heading) stayed at the bottom of a page while the
paragraph after it started on the next page. It happened when the page had room for exactly one
line of a next paragraph that has several lines: widow/orphan control moves that first line to
the next page, and the heading was left behind.

## Cause

`next_first_line`, the lookahead `place_para` uses to decide whether a kept paragraph has to
move, asked for room for only the next paragraph's first line. `place_para` then placed that
paragraph under orphan control, which wants two lines at the end of a page, and moved it whole.
The two disagreed by one line.

## Fix

`next_first_line` now asks for the next paragraph's first two lines when it has widow/orphan
control, measured the way `place_para` measures them (top of the first line to the bottom of the
second).

Unchanged:

- a one-line next paragraph still needs one line;
- with widow/orphan control off, the first line is enough;
- a first line that ends in a page or column break still needs one line, because `place_para`
  skips orphan control there;
- a next paragraph that is itself kept with next still moves as a chain (#933).

## Tests

New: `keep_with_next_follows_a_next_paragraph_moved_by_orphan_control` in
`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`. It finds the filler count that leaves one line of room under a kept
heading, then checks the page of the heading and of the next paragraph's first two lines:

| Case | Expected | On `main` |
|---|---|---|
| Room for one line, 4-line next paragraph | heading moves with it | heading stays on page 1 (fails) |
| Room for two lines | both stay | same |
| Room for one line, widow/orphan control off | both stay, paragraph splits after its first line | same |
| Room for one line, one-line next paragraph | both stay | same |

## Checked

title: Native print test: fixed PDF creation date, no flaky byte comparison (#987)
author: dkhlapov
body:
`native_ranges_and_parity_do_not_duplicate_spooler_copies` could fail when a clock second ticked over during the test, as on **Print (macos-latest)** for #882.

**Cause:** the test builds the expected PDF, then submits the job, which builds the PDF again. A document without a creation date gets the current time in `CreationDate`/`ModDate` (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`), so two PDFs built a second apart differ only in those dates.

**Fix:** the test document has a fixed creation date (`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`), so both PDFs carry the same timestamp. The test also asserts that both contain it, so it fails loudly if the date ever stops coming from the document.

`cargo xtask ci` steps pass (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

Fixes #987

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built wordcraft and wordcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#wordcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: Tables: AutoFit in a nested table, whole cells shaded for a selection through a table, Shift+Right at a cell's end
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #971. Three small follow-ups to the table mouse and selection work (#637, #722), one commit each.

**1. AutoFit by double-clicking a nested table's column border** (`table_mouse::fit_column`). The table widens (the columns right of the border keep their widths and move along) only up to the right edge of the text of the cell around it, not up to the page's right margin. Before, a nested table could grow far past its cell; the outer table's AutoFit then widened that column at the expense of the others, or the nested table ran over its cell. A right-to-left outer table uses the cell's start margin on the right. Not observed in Word yet: when the outer table could grow instead, the nested table stays inside its cell here, which is what our layout does with nested tables anyway.

**2. A selection from text into or across a table shades whole cells** (`table_mouse::selection_rects`, used by the canvas). Such a selection already takes whole rows (#722), but only the letters in the cells were highlighted. Now every row it takes from start to end shades all its cells (an empty one too), as selected cells (`CellRange`) do, and the letters in them aren't shaded twice. Only rows of a table the selection runs into or across count: a selection that starts and ends in the same table keeps its text highlight (selecting all the text of a cell must not look like selecting the cell). A nested table in a shaded row shades with it.

**3. Shift+Right at the end of a cell's text selects the cell first** (`table::select_cell_first`, from `column::dispatch`). Before, the first press already selected that cell and the next one. As in Word, the first step out of the cell takes the cell alone (its end-of-cell mark); the next press goes on into the next cell as before. In an empty cell the first press selects it. Shift+Left in right-to-left text does the same (it's the forward step there). Mouse drags are unchanged. Pinned in `tests_typing.rs` and `docs/typing-parity.md` (Editing keys).…

author: y2w8
body:
### Summary
Fixes an issue where deleting a table while **Draw Table** (`table.draw`) or **Eraser** (`table.eraser`) was active left the canvas trapped in tool mode after the contextual Table Layout tab closed.

### Key Changes
- **Tool Reset on Table Delete**: When `table.deleteTable` executes, or when `TableTool::Erase` is active and the selection leaves table cells (e.g. deleting rows/columns until the table is dropped), WordApp::after_command calls `table_pen::stop` to return to the default cursor and caret mode.

title: fix(markdown): preserve table cells containing code spans and pipes
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
Fixes #1008

### Problem & Root Cause
1. **Importer (`split_row`)**: Previously toggled `in_code` on every backtick character (`'`), desynchronizing column splitting on multi-backtick delimiters (e.g. `` `` `|` `` ``) or code spans containing literal backticks (e.g. `` ``a`b\|c`` ``). This caused subsequent column delimiter pipes (`|`) to be skipped and cell contents to be merged into preceding cells, discarding trailing columns.
2. **Exporter (`table_md`)**: Table cell inlines exported code spans directly through `code_span` without escaping literal pipes (`|` -> `\|`), emitting invalid GFM that caused table cell splitting upon re-import.

### Changes
- **`split_row`**:
  - Removed naive `in_code` toggling on backticks.
  - Strictly treats unescaped `|` characters as table column delimiters per GFM §4.10, including when between backticks.
  - Treats escaped pipes (`\|`) as cell content, unescaping them into `|` for subsequent inline parsing.
  - Added backslash-parity checking (`num_bs % 2 == 0`) for trailing delimiter pipes, correctly distinguishing unescaped trailing row delimiters from escaped cell content.
  - Consumes escaped backslash pairs (`\\`) before pipes so `\\|` correctly treats `|` as an unescaped delimiter while preserving `\\`.
- **`inlines_md` / `table_md`**:
  - Added `in_table: bool` context to `inlines_md_impl`.
  - In table cells (`inlines_md_table`), code spans escape literal pipes as `\|` via `text.replace('|', "\\|")` before wrapping in backticks.
  - Standalone code spans outside tables remain unchanged.
  - Avoids double-escaping pipes already handled by normal text escaping.

### Verification
- **Targeted formats suite**: `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats`: 87 passed, 0 failed (8 new regression tests covering single-backtick with `\|`, double-backtick with `\|`, literal backticks with `\|`, 3-column tables, unescaped pipe splitting, and full document-level round trips).

title: Track Changes: rejecting a whole inserted paragraph keeps the next paragraph's style and numbering
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Problem

Reject All on a document where a whole paragraph was inserted with Track Changes (and, symmetrically, Accept All of a whole deleted paragraph) changes the **next** paragraph's formatting: the paragraph after the removed one takes over the removed paragraph's style, numbering and alignment.

In a Word-saved contract this is visible as numbering damage: a tracked, inserted list item (a numbered sub-clause) sits right before a "§ N" heading. After Reject All the text is correct, but the heading becomes the next list item ("4.") of the previous section, and every following § number shifts by one. Word removes the inserted paragraph and leaves the heading untouched.

## Minimal reproduction (in words)

1. Two paragraphs: "Intro" (Normal) and "Heading" (Heading 1).
2. Turn on Track Changes, put the caret at the start of "Heading", type "Inserted" and press Enter.
3. Turn Track Changes off and set the new "Inserted" paragraph to Normal.
4. Review ▸ Reject All.

Expected (Word): "Intro" (Normal), "Heading" (Heading 1).
Actual: "Intro", "Heading" — but "Heading" is now **Normal**.

## Cause

`resolve_para` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs:328`) removes a rejected inserted paragraph mark (or an accepted deleted one) by calling `join_next_para` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:186-189`), which joins the next paragraph into this one and, as documented, "keeps this paragraph's properties". When the paragraph's own content was also inserted (rejected) or deleted (accepted), it is empty at that point, so the join moves the next paragraph's text into an empty paragraph carrying the removed paragraph's properties — the next paragraph's own style and numbering are lost.

## Fix

A new helper `remove_empty_para` removes the paragraph whole when it is empty, carries no section break and is followed by another paragraph in the same container; the next paragraph then keeps its own properties. `resolve_para` tries it before `join_next_para`, so paragraphs that still have conten…

title: Caret: Down and Up from a line start beside a table go into it, not past it
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1007.

**Bug.** Down (and Shift+Down) from the start of the line directly above a table skipped the whole table: the caret landed in the paragraph after it. Up from the start of the paragraph after a table skipped it the same way. From the middle of the line it worked.

**Cause.** `DocLayout::vertical` took the nearest line below (or above) whose horizontal extent covers the caret's x. A line's extent is the room it has, and a cell's lines start a cell margin in from the table's edge. So at the left margin no cell line covers the caret's x, and the next line that does — the paragraph beyond the table — won. The same happened when the x fell in the gap between two cells' text, or left of an indented table, and for an indented paragraph (a list item) under a line start.

**Fix** (`crates/layout/src/hit.rs`). After finding that line, `vertical` looks at the lines that come between the caret's paragraph and it in document order and lie before it on the way. If there are any, the caret goes there instead: into the nearest of them, or a line of another cell in the same table row, choosing the one under the caret's x or else the horizontally nearest. So left of a table it lands in the first cell, right of it in the last. Another cell of the caret's own row (or of the found line's row) never counts as between: in a table, Down still goes to the cell below, even when a cell beside it is taller. When no line covers the x at all, the same row choice replaces "the nearest line": in a row of empty cells the caret now goes to the cell under it rather than the first one found.

**Test.** `tests_typing::down_and_up_from_a_line_start_beside_a_table_go_into_it` checks four moves:
- Down from the start of the line above → the first cell, and then the cell below it.
- Up from the start of the paragraph after the table → the last row's first cell.
- Shift+Down from the line start → the first row only (it used to take the whole table).

title: One Page and the zoom are saved with the document and restored when it is reopened
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #995.

The zoom never left the session: the writer always put `<w:zoom w:percent="100"/>` in settings.xml and the reader ignored `w:zoom`, so every document opened in whatever view was already on screen. Word keeps it in the document, so this does the same: `Settings` gets an optional `zoom` (percent + fit), read from and written to `w:zoom` (One Page = `fullPage`, Page Width = `bestFit`, Text Width = `textFit`; percent clamped to 10-500, `75%` accepted). `stamp_save` copies the current view into it, so both `file.save` and the web download carry it, and `file.open` puts it back on the view. Changing the zoom is still not an edit: the document doesn't become unsaved. 100% with no fit is stored as `None`, so documents that don't care round-trip exactly as before, and opening one leaves the current zoom alone as it does today. Multiple Pages has no `w:val` in Word, so it's saved as its percentage. Happy to switch to an app-level "last view" preference instead if you'd rather not tie it to the file.

Validation:
- `engine::tests::one_page_is_restored_when_the_document_is_reopened`: fails on main (`fit` is `""` after reopening, expected `"onePage"`), passes here
- `docx` `roundtrip::zoom_round_trips`: fails on main (`w:val="fullPage" w:percent="62"` written back as `w:percent="100"`), passes here
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test roundtrip`, `--test word_xml`, `--test fixtures`, `--test malformed`; `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib` filtered on save / open / zoom
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-doc -p wordcraft-docx -p wordcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Fonts: embed Carlito and Caladea for Calibri and Cambria documents
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Problem

Documents set in Calibri or Cambria — Word's default fonts before Aptos, so most existing `.docx` files — paginate differently from Word on macOS and Linux. Neither font is installed there. `crates/fonts/src/word.rs` already lists the open metric-compatible substitutes first (Carlito for Calibri in `SANS`, Caladea for Cambria in `SERIF`), but no build ships them: they are not in `craft-fonts`' `fonts/manifest.txt`, so `has_family("Carlito")` is false and Calibri falls back to Helvetica Neue, whose advance widths differ.

Measured on a 107-page Word document set in Calibri (tables, footnotes, a landscape section), headless `wordcraft-cli info`, macOS arm64:

| font available for Calibri | pages | vs Word |
|---|---|---|
| none (today: Helvetica Neue) | 112 | +4.7% |
| Carlito (this PR) | **106** | −0.9% |

The remaining one-page difference is in line with what I measured on Word documents whose fonts are installed (±1 page on 2–13-page documents).

## Change

`craft-fonts` already carries Carlito and Caladea (OFL-1.1, sourced from google/fonts@7085eb8; their SHA-256 sums match the manifest; `OFL.txt` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` rows included) in its opt-in `fonts/latin-manifest.txt`, added by storytold/craft-fonts#8 (also carried by storytold/craft-fonts#23). Following that repo's `docs/integration.md` recipe, without adding any font file here:

- `crates/fonts/build.rs`: native builds also read `fonts/latin-manifest.txt` when the `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` checkout has one, and embed **only** the `Carlito` and `Caladea` lines (4 styles each, ~3.1 MB). A checkout without that manifest (the current release pin `8dcdacd`), builds without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, and the wasm32 build are unchanged. It registers `rerun-if-changed` on the checkout's `fonts/` directory, so updating the checkout to one with the manifest re-runs the script.
- `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs`: `document_substitute_fonts()` (the embedded Carlito/Caladea faces).

title: macOS: Control-click opens the context menu, with its spelling suggestions
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #996 (the Control-click path; the F7 / Editor path below has no way to pick a correction yet).

On a Mac, Control-click is the usual way to get a right-click, especially on a trackpad. winit reports it as a primary click with Control held, though, so WordCraft just moved the caret: no context menu came up, and the context menu is where the spelling suggestions are. A real right-click or a two-finger click already worked. `raw_input_hook` now turns a Control+primary press into a secondary one on macOS, and its release goes with it even if Control is let go first. Doing it at the input level means every menu works the same way, not just the one on the canvas, the way it does in native Mac apps. Happy to scope it to the canvas instead if you prefer.

Also worth knowing: Spelling & Grammar (F7) and Editor only select the next misspelt word. There's no pane to pick a correction from, so that's another way to end up where the reporter did. I left it out because it needs its own UI.

Validation:
- `canvas::tests::control_click_on_macos_opens_the_context_menu` sends the events winit delivers for a Control-click through `raw_input_hook`, then picks "brown" for "brwn". It fails on main (the menu never opens) and passes here
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib -- control_click_on_macos right_click_on_a_picture shift_f10`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Double-click in the margins edits the header or footer: created on demand, reachable from the body, the clicked page's section
author: iot-root
body:
Closes storytold/wordcraft#1026.

Double-click in a page's margin bands is Word's way into header/footer editing. WordCraft's handler existed but failed twice over: the gate (`header_footer_at`) only recognised the band once the page already had that part, and the transition's first click moved the caret to the nearest body text — whose scroll-to-caret slid the page out from under the second press, leaving the footer unreachable from the body (the header survived only because its nearest text is adjacent).

## What changes

- **`DocLayout::header_footer_band_at(page, x, y)`**: the margin band exists on every page, part or not, and is bounded to the page — the gray beside it and the markup strip are no band. The old `header_footer_at`, gated on an existing story, is deleted (its two callers were the bug).
- **One `hf_click` helper** classifies a click for both the press and release handlers: `Enter(header)` (from the body, another band's part, a footnote — creating the part if the document has none, via the existing `insert.editHeader`/`editFooter`), `Leave` (body double-click while editing), or an ordinary click. It recognises only Header/Footer parts, so footnotes keep ordinary clicking.
- **Transition presses are inert** (Shift excepted), like Word's: the caret stays put, nothing scrolls, and the double-click's second press lands where the user aimed. Double-clicking the other band while editing now switches directly between header and footer.
- **The clicked page's section**: `insert.editHeader`/`editFooter` take an optional `"section"` and the canvas passes the double-clicked page's, so a margin on a section-2 page edits section 2's part. Without it, the caret's section is used — and a caret in another part's story (a header after a band switch, a footnote) falls back to the first section instead of misreading its part path as a body block index.

## Tests

title: European Portuguese: pt-pt interface and pt-PT spelling
author: quebranozes
body:
Adds European Portuguese next to the Brazilian Portuguese that is already there. `docs/gaps.md` and `docs/localization-parity.md` list pt-PT as one of the missing key languages.

### Interface

- New catalog `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/pt-pt.tsv`: the full `pt-br` key set (2,061 entries) in European vocabulary and grammar. 574 entries differ from the Brazilian ones: *Ficheiro / Guardar / Eliminar*, *Tipo de letra*, *Palavra-passe*, *Anular*, *Secção*, *Registar alterações*, *Impressão em série*; no `você`, enclitic pronouns, `a` + infinitive.
- Registered as `pt-pt` ("Português (Portugal)"). It resolves from `pt-PT` and from the regions that write like Portugal (`pt-AO`, `pt-MZ`, `pt-CV`, `pt-GW`, `pt-ST`, `pt-TL`, `pt-MO`, `pt-GQ`). `pt-BR` keeps the Brazilian catalog; a bare `pt` still stays English.
- `pt-PT` added to File › Options › Advanced › Region.

- New `ProofLang::PtPt`, told apart from `ProofLang::Pt` by the run's region. European text is spelled against the Hunspell `pt_PT` dictionary installed on the system (same search places as Polish and pt-BR, LibreOffice's `dict-pt-PT` included). Nothing is bundled: the dictionary is GPL/LGPL/MPL.
- Without a `pt_PT` dictionary, European text falls back to `pt_BR`, which is today's behaviour, so nothing regresses for people who only have VERO.
- Grammar rules and hyphenation patterns are shared between the two spellings; issues carry `pt-PT` as their language.
- `hunspell::decode` also reads ISO 8859-1, which older Portuguese dictionaries use.
- Review › Language offers "Portuguese (Portugal)"; a `pt-pt` interface writes new documents in `pt-PT`.

title: DOCX: keep Office 2016 charts (cx:chart) and their data when saving
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #997.

The reader only understood the `mc:Choice` branches in its known list, so a `cx:chart` choice fell through to `mc:Fallback` and the chart came in as a plain picture. That picture is all that got saved. Now an `mc:AlternateContent` whose choice holds a `cx:chart` is read the same way native ink already is: it becomes a read-only chart graphic drawn from the fallback picture, and `keep_embedded` keeps both branches plus every part they reach (the chartEx part, style, colours, embedded workbook and the picture). On save it's written back as an `mc:AlternateContent` with the original `Requires` value. Both branches get the chart's current frame, so a resized chart and its picture stay the same size. The `cx` and `cx1`..`cx8` namespaces are added to `NAMESPACES` so the `cx:chart` element and the `Requires` prefixes survive parsing and are declared on save. That adds those declarations to every written story root, which Word also does. Happy to switch to declaring them only on the `mc:Choice` if you'd rather keep the root list short.

Validation:
- `office_2016_chart_keeps_its_chart_part_and_fallback_through_saves` (fixtures.rs): fails on main (the chart reads as an `Image`, no `cx:chart` is written), passes here over two saves, both for Word's `Requires="cx1"` and for the `Requires="cx"` form in Apache POI's sample
- `resized_office_2016_chart_resizes_its_fallback_too`: both branches carry the new extent
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test fixtures --test roundtrip --test malformed --test word_xml`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `wordcraft-cli run --file chartex.docx --save out.docx` on POI's `chartex.docx`: chart4/chart6, both workbooks and the AlternateContent are now kept
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: DOCX: a hyperlink with an empty target is no link (#1005)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1005

## Root cause
The DOCX reader took a `w:hyperlink` `r:id` relationship target as the link as-is, so `Target=""` (what LibreOffice writes for the Hyperlink character style without an address) became `Some("")`: every run showed the "Ctrl+Click to follow link" tooltip. The writer already drops empty links, so reader and writer disagreed.

## What changed
- `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`: a blank (empty or whitespace-only) relationship target is no link; the run keeps its Hyperlink style and inherits the enclosing link (normally none). `w:anchor` and real targets are unchanged.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` `link_under`: ignores empty links, so any other path that produces one cannot show the tooltip.
- ROADMAP.md progress log row.

## Tests
- `hyperlink_with_empty_target_is_no_link` (crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs): empty target gives no link, style `Hyperlink` and text kept; `mailto:` and `w:anchor` links still work; round trip keeps only the real links. Verified it fails without the fix.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test fixtures hyperlink_with_empty`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p wordcraft-ui-egui`.

## Not done
- Did not audit the HTML/RTF/ODT readers or `HYPERLINK ""` fields for the same problem.
- No screenshot of the tooltip in the app.

This works with #282, which draws the window controls in WordCraft's own bar on Linux. Once that lands and sets `integrated_titlebar` on Linux, the title comes back in our bar automatically, with no system bar above it.

title: Page background: picture and texture fills are drawn and kept on save (#999)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #999

## Root cause
The reader only looked at `w:background/@w:color`; the `v:background/v:fill` picture (and its image relationship) was never read, so the texture was neither drawn nor kept. The writer then dropped the unreferenced image part on save (data loss).

## What changed
- `doc`: `Settings::page_picture: Option<PagePicture>` (media key, `v:fill` type, `o:title`).
- `docx`: read `v:fill` (`r:id` / `r:embed` / `o:relid`) into the model; write `w:background` with `v:background/v:fill`, the image relationship and part; `w:displayBackgroundShape` also for a picture.
- `render`: the picture is painted behind page content, tiled at 96 dpi for `type="tile"`, else stretched over the page; decoding capped at 64 Mpx, undecodable images leave the paper colour.
- `pdf`: same fill on export (tiles capped at 4096, else stretched).
- `ui-egui`: canvas cache key includes the picture; "print backgrounds" off also omits the picture when printing.
- `design.pageColor` clears the picture (picking a plain colour replaces the fill, as in Word).

## Tests
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test roundtrip page_background`
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-render page_picture`
- also run: engine `hostile`/`page_color`, `wordcraft-pdf`; clippy -D warnings on docx/render/pdf/engine/ui-egui; `cargo fmt --check`; wasm check of ui-egui.

## Not done
- No Fill Effects UI/command for choosing a picture (not required here); gradient/pattern fills of `v:fill` are still not read.
- No separate "show background in Print Layout only" view gate (the colour had none either).

## Unverified
- Appearance against Word (tile scale of 96 dpi is from the spec/observed convention, not side-by-side checked).

title: Ribbon: holding a press no longer scrolls the document (#1019)
author: lasse-tech
body:
Fixes #1019.

## Cause
A double-click is handled on its release. Several double-click paths in `canvas::mouse` (header/footer area: enter or leave it, and others) `return` before the release branch, so `CanvasState::dragging` stays `true`. From then on any held press, on the ribbon too, counts as a drag-select and drives the edge auto-scroll from #688: the pointer is above the viewport, so the document scrolls up until the button is released. A release over the ribbon never reaches `mouse` (no canvas pointer position), so the stale flag survives.

Reproduced headlessly: after a double-click in the header area, a press held on the ribbon for 30 frames scrolled the document by 372 px.

## Fix
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: before the auto-scroll, a drag whose button is neither down nor just released is ended (`dragging`, `column_drag`, `unit_drag`), whichever path skipped the release. The release frame itself still goes through `mouse` as before (format painter etc.).

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs::a_press_on_the_ribbon_after_a_header_double_click_does_not_scroll`: a document with a header, double-click in the header area, then a press held on the ribbon. Fails without the fix (stale drag, document scrolls), passes with it.

Also carries a one-line test fix in `crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs`: a needless `drop(run)` that clippy 1.97 rejects (`drop_non_drop`), which currently fails `cargo xtask ci` on `main`.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Arabic (العربية) UI translation: language switching + font fallback
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
A full `ar.tsv` catalog (2,462 rows: the union of every other language's keys plus the bibliography style rows) for the whole interface — every tab, command, dialog, gallery label and status message — written from the plain meaning of the English with Microsoft Word's Arabic terminology (الصفحة الرئيسية، تخطيط الصفحة، المراجع، تسمية توضيحية، مراسلات، تعقب التغييرات…), count-neutral wording where English pluralizes (`{words} words` → `الكلمات: {words}`). Bibliography style names stay in Latin as the other catalogs keep them, with the parenthetical sort/date notes translated.

- **Registry** — `ar` in `LANGUAGES` (every `ar-*` locale resolves to it); new documents stay in US English (no Arabic proofing yet).
- **Fonts** — the craft-fonts Noto Sans Arabic face added to the UI families, mirroring how the CJK faces load.

No layout mirroring in this PR: egui 0.36 has no global direction switch and no bidi reordering, so the shell still lays out left-to-right and the words of an Arabic label come out in reverse order until a bidi pass (the approach discussed in vectorcraft#1202) lands. I kept this PR to the catalog, the language switch and the fonts rather than pretend at mirroring an API that doesn't exist.

title: Track Changes: deletions inside a field result are tracked, accepted and saved (#1037)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1037

## Root cause
The DOCX reader buffers a complex field's result into a single `InlineObject::Field { result: String }`, whose revision is the object's one `ins`/`del`. A `w:del` / `w:ins` inside the result (between `separate` and `end`) was therefore flattened into plain result text: Accept All kept the deleted characters (`$$140.00`, `5five`) and a save wrote them back without `w:del`.

## What changed
- `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs` (`end_field`): when a buffered result piece carries a different revision than the field itself, the field is kept as a range field (`FieldStart` ... `FieldEnd`, the same path used for fields with embedded pictures), so each piece stays an ordinary run with its own `w:ins`/`w:del`. Accept/Reject All and the writer (`w:del` + `w:delText` between `separate` and `end`) already handle ordinary runs, so they need no change. The split-across-field-end case (`$` inside, `150.00` after the end) works the same way.
- ROADMAP.md progress-log row, docs/file-format-parity.md note.

title: Table eraser: borders beside vertically merged cells merge as in Word (#1039)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1039

## Root cause
`table.eraser` refused every vertical border beside a vertically merged cell, and refused horizontal borders between cells that don't line up.

## What changed (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table_draw.rs`)
- Cells are resolved to their grid rectangle (rows of the vertical merge, grid columns).

title: proof: Czech (cs-CZ) spelling from the installed Hunspell dictionary
author: Losminek
body:
Adds Czech proofing, following the same pattern as Portuguese (#797) and Polish (#346). Today, with the Czech interface, new documents have no language, so Czech text is checked as English and almost every word is underlined.

## What it does

- **`ProofLang::Cs`.** `from_tag` accepts `cs`, `cs-CZ`, `ces` and `cze`. The new module `crates/proof/src/cs/` mirrors `pt/`:
  - the dictionary is looked up as `cs_CZ` / `cs-CZ` / `cs` on the existing Hunspell search paths (`WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES`, `~/.local/share/hunspell`, `/usr/share/hunspell`, LibreOffice extensions);
  - suggestions use the dictionary's own `MAP`/`REP`/`TRY`/`KEY`, read at runtime;
  - grammar stays generic: repeated word and spacing, with digit ratios and scores like `3 : 1` exempt. Messages are in Czech.
- **The dictionary is not bundled.** It comes from the system, e.g. the Debian/Ubuntu package `hunspell-cs` (GPL-2), read at runtime like SJP.PL and VERO. Without it, Czech text gets no marks, as `Other` languages do now. No Czech hyphenation patterns are bundled either: those are GPL-2 too, so Czech keeps the current fallback.
- **The Czech interface** sets `editing_lang: Some("cs-CZ")`, so new documents and opened `.txt`/`.md` are written in Czech. This follows the rule in `i18n/mod.rs` that `editing_lang` is set only for languages `wordcraft-proof` can check. Czech is also added to the ribbon's proofing language menu.

Before this change that line was read as a rule, and flag `y` lost its cross product. Only header candidates are trimmed; rule lines stay literal, even a condition that starts with `#`.

title: Layout: keep with next moves the heading when the next paragraph moves for widow control (#966)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #966.

`next_first_line()` reserved only the next paragraph's first line as the room a kept block needs below it — so a heading with keep with next stayed at the bottom of a page while the paragraph after it moved over whole: with widow/orphan control on, Word does not leave a single line of a paragraph at the bottom of a page, so when only one line would fit the paragraph starts on the next page instead, and the heading has to move with it. LibreOffice moves the heading for the same file (#966).

The room the paragraph after a kept block needs to *start* on the page now follows the same rules Word places it by: its first line plain, its first two lines under widow/orphan control, all of it under keep lines together — and, as before (#933), all of it plus what it keeps with in turn when it is itself kept with the next, so a chain still moves together. A table after a kept block reserves the same placeholder room as before.

Validation:

- Three new tests in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs` pin the behaviour, each self-locating the page edge so they stay valid under future metrics changes: with widow control on, a heading followed by a long paragraph moves over when exactly one line of it would fit, and both stay when two lines fit or the control is off (`keep_with_next_carries_the_heading_when_widow_control_moves_the_next_paragraph`); a kept chain — heading, kept middle, long paragraph — moves over whole when the last paragraph cannot start (`keep_with_next_chain_carries_over_when_the_last_paragraph_cannot_start`); keep lines together on the paragraph after a heading carries the heading over (`keep_with_next_carries_the_heading_when_keep_lines_moves_the_next_paragraph`).
- All three fail on the code before the fix (run with the `lib.rs` change stashed: 1 passed, 3 failed) and pass with it.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` green: 237 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` green: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, asset attribution, layering, wasm build.

title: Comments: a click inside a selected balloon moves the caret in its text (#1013)
author: lasse-tech
body:
Fixes #1013.

## Cause
The comment balloons sit in the markup area beside each page, which is part of the canvas response. egui's `Response::contains_pointer` is true for every widget of the layer under the pointer, even when another widget covers it (see `hit_test.rs`: `contains_pointer` keeps all close widgets whose rect contains the position). So a press inside the selected balloon's text field also counted as a press on the page:

- the check that leaves the selected balloon on a page click ran (`canvas.rs`), so the edit mode ended;
- `mouse()` took it as a document click as well, which would set the document caret and start a drag-select (the same mechanism as #1019).

The first click worked only because nothing was selected yet; the second one left the balloon.

## Fix
`canvas.rs`: a press over a balloon card belongs to the card (`over_balloon`, using `balloon_rects` of the same frame). It applies to both checks: leaving the balloon, and the document click in `mouse()`. A click on the page itself still leaves the balloon.

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs::a_press_inside_the_selected_comment_keeps_it_selected`: a comment's balloon is selected by a click; a press, short drag and release inside its text leave it selected, don't start a drag in the document, and leave the caret and scroll offset alone; a click on the page then leaves it. Red on `main` at the first press. With only the `mouse()` check reverted it fails too, so both checks are covered.

Not in this PR: the request in the issue's second comment (show comments only on click, as a setting and default) is a feature request.

Also carries a one-line test fix in `crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs`: a needless `drop(run)` that clippy 1.97 rejects (`drop_non_drop`), which fails `cargo xtask ci` on `main`. The same change is in #1041.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: DOCX: merge settings.xml into the original instead of regenerating it (#1034)
author: przemek-arch
body:
Part 1 of 2 for #1034 (stage 2 of the proposal there). Part 2, carrying unmodelled package parts and the smaller items, builds on this one and follows as a separate PR.

## Problem

A save regenerated `word/settings.xml` from a fixed list of model settings (`settings_xml`, `crates/docx/src/write/mod.rs`). Every other setting was dropped without a warning. On 18 real-world Word documents (#1034) the losses were:
- compatibility settings in 18/18 files: `overrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification`, `differentiateMultirowTableHeaders`, `useWord2013TrackBottomHyphenation`…;
- `rsids`, `docVars`, `proofState`, `clrSchemeMapping`, `themeFontLang`, `decimalSymbol`/`listSeparator` and `w14`/`w15:docId`;

## Change

The reader keeps the original part when it holds a child the model doesn't own (`has_unowned`), and the writer merges into it (`crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs`):
- **Kept byte for byte:**
  - the original root start tag (namespace declarations, `mc:Ignorable`);
  - every child the model doesn't own.
- **Owned children** (`OWNED`):
  - come from the generated part, or are omitted when the model turned them off (e.g. Track Changes);
  - those the original lacks are inserted at their CT_Settings position;
  - `m:mathPr` and `w:displayBackgroundShape` are only partly modelled, so the original wins (`KEEP_ORIGINAL`).
- **`w:compat`:** only `compatibilityMode` is replaced; it is added if the original lacked it.
- **Dropped:** kept children that point at a relationship (`r:id`, e.g. a `w:mailMerge` data source), since their relationships aren't carried.
- **Fallback:** anything the scanner doesn't expect (undeclared prefix, CDATA, unbalanced tags, non-UTF-8) returns `None`, and the generated part is written as before.
- **Unchanged for WordCraft's own files:** they keep nothing extra, so new documents, second-generation equality and Flat OPC behave as today.

The privacy options `w:removePersonalInformation` / `w:removeDateAndTime` are modelled since #1131, so …

title: Tables: the eraser beside merged cells merges or hides, a drag erases a rectangle, as in Word
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1039.

## What changes

Table Layout › Eraser now behaves as in Word:
- Beside vertically merged cells it merges or hides the border, where it used to fail with
  "erasing a border beside a vertically merged cell isn't supported".
- Dragged, it erases every border inside a rectangle.
- It also takes the table's own edge.

- **Cells merged down the same rows merge.** The border between two cells that are both merged
  down the same rows merges them, row by row, into one cell still merged down those rows
  (`vMerge` restart/continue kept). The text of all of them is kept.
- **Otherwise the border is hidden.** When the two cells can't become one cell, the border is
  hidden on both sides (`nil` cell borders), all along both cells. This covers a one-row cell
  beside a taller merged cell, and a wide cell over two. Like Word, the `nil` goes on every
  row of a merged cell. Clicking a hidden border again reports "that border is already erased"
  and adds no undo step. The hidden line still shows as a gridline. Once both sides span the
  same rows (say, after merging the shorter one down), the border merges them. The merged cell
  keeps the far cell's right edge, so the hidden side doesn't hide it.
- **The table's edge is hidden.** Nothing is beyond it to merge with, so a click on it or a
  rectangle across it hides it (`nil`), in every row of a merged cell.
- **Dragging draws a rectangle.** As in Word, the eraser drags a rectangle from where the
  button went down. On release, every border the rectangle crosses is erased by the rules
  above, in one undo step. Each border is taken whole, even when the rectangle covers only part

title: CLI: render and run reject bad page and scale options instead of silently defaulting (#981)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #981.

`render` and `run --save *.png` parsed `--page` and `--scale` leniently (`arg_value(...).and_then(|p| p.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(default)`): a malformed, missing or out-of-range value silently fell back to page 1 / scale 2.0, `--scale 0` reached the engine and came back clamped to 0.1 as an 80×62 thumbnail, and a repeated flag silently kept the first — all exit 0, all writing a file that is not what was asked for.

Both flags now go through a strict parse at the CLI boundary (`arg_value_once` + `page_scale`), with a clear error and exit 1 when a value is malformed (`--page banana`), missing (`--page` with nothing after it), out of range (`--page 0`, `--page -1`, `--scale 0`, `--scale -2`, `--scale nan`, `--scale inf`), or given twice. Valid invocations behave exactly as before: absent options still fall through to the engine's defaults (`page.unwrap_or(1)`, `scale.unwrap_or(2.0)`), and nothing else about the two commands changed. `--page=2` stays rejected as an unknown option by the existing `validate_options`, which runs before the new check, so there is no second syntax that slips past it. The `run` path shares the same validation, so `run --save out.png --scale 0` fails the same way.

Scope note, deliberate: the engine's own clamp for *accepted* scales (`0.1–8.0`) is untouched, per the issue's frame — `--scale 0.05` still clamps rather than erroring. Tightening that is a separate decision.

Validation:

- Repro matrix, both `render` and `run --save`, against a fresh debug build: every case in the issue exits 1 with `render: --page must be a whole number of at least 1, not `banana``-style errors on stderr and writes no output file; `--page 2 --scale 1` renders byte-for-byte as before (66,956-byte PNG, same as pre-change); no flags still renders page 1 at scale 2.0.
- Five new tests in `apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs`: absent/valid options accepted; ten malformed/out-of-range values rejected (including `nan`, `inf`, `1e-400` underflow to `0.0`); rejecti…

On macOS an app started from Finder or the Dock doesn't inherit shell variables, so `WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES` only works when WordCraft is launched from a terminal. title: .doc: open password-protected Word 97–2003 files (RC4, RC4 CryptoAPI, XOR) (#1079)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1079

## What changed
- `crates/docbin/src/crypt.rs` (new): the three legacy `.doc` schemes, written from the public specs ([MS-DOC] 2.2.6, [MS-OFFCRYPTO] 2.3.5-2.3.7):
  - XOR obfuscation (password verifier method 2 in `FibBase.lKey`, XOR array method 2, tries both Unicode-to-byte conversions)
  - RC4 (header 1.1, MD5 key derivation, 512-byte blocks)
  - RC4 CryptoAPI (header 2/3/4 . 2, SHA-1, 40 to 128 bit keys)
  - own RC4 and MD5 (no new crates; `sha1` is already in the workspace and pure Rust, wasm check passes)
- The password is verified against the stored verifier before anything is decrypted: a wrong password is `WrongPassword`, never a garbled document. WordDocument (past the first 68 bytes), Table (past the header for RC4) and Data streams are decrypted, then the existing parser runs.
- `DocbinError::Encrypted` is replaced by `PasswordRequired`, `WrongPassword` and `Encryption(..)` (AES, external providers and unknown headers give a clear error). New `docbin::is_encrypted` and `read_with_password`.
- Engine: `.doc`/`.dot` (and content-sniffed files) go through `open_bytes_with` with the password and return the same error texts as password-protected `.docx`, so the existing password prompt (and `file.open` with `password`) works unchanged. No new UI strings.
- Docs: `docs/file-format-parity.md` rows, `docs/gaps.md` row 9 (small edit), `ROADMAP.md` progress-log row.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docbin` (77 pass): MD5 RFC 1321 vectors, an RC4 vector, round trips for XOR, RC4 and CryptoAPI (40 and 128 bit, Unicode and Latin-1 passwords), wrong/empty/missing password, tampered verifier, AES/external/unknown-version refusal, truncated and garbled headers (no panic). Fixtures are encrypted in the test with a small encryptor written from the spec.

title: Props colours take RRGGBB too: shading, underlineColor, border colour
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
#881 made `chr.color` take `"RRGGBB"` / `"auto"`, and #899 documented CharProps and ParaProps, but the issue stayed open. The other colours in those objects still only took `[r, g, b]`: `shading` (char and para), `underlineColor` and a border's `color`. So `para.set {"props": {"shading": "C00000"}}` failed with "expected tuple struct Rgb", even though `para.borders` and `table.shading` take hex. `{"color": {"Rgb": "1B1611"}}` from the issue also still failed.

The fix is a hand-written `Deserialize` for `Rgb` that reads a string through the existing `Rgb::parse` (`RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBB`) as well as `[r, g, b]`. Serialization is untouched, so saved documents and settings still write `[r, g, b]`. docbin doesn't go through serde, so nothing non-JSON depends on the derived form. `"auto"` isn't accepted for these fields because a plain `Rgb` has no auto, and it stays a parameter error.

Tests: `props_colours_take_hex_strings` runs `styles.modify` and `para.set` with hex in every one of these fields, checks `[r, g, b]` still works, and checks that bad values are refused without changing anything. A unit test in `props.rs` covers what `Rgb` reads and writes. The #881 tests now expect `{"Rgb": "1B1611"}` to work. docs/mcp.md now describes a "colour" once and uses that in the tables.

`cargo xtask ci` passed fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm. Workspace tests pass except three in wordcraft-layout (`deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`), which fail the same way on unchanged main on my machine. I didn't try it by hand through the CLI or MCP.

Fixes #865

title: Italian proofing: it_IT and it_CH spelling, suggestions, grammar and hyphenation (#951)
author: regalf
body:
Closes #951 (Italian text checked against the US English dictionary). Related to #100 (multilingual spell check).

Italian proofing as a fourth language in the per-run framework, following the Portuguese module (`crates/proof/src/pt/`) as its template.

## What

- **`crates/proof/src/it/`** — spelling against the Hunspell Italian dictionary installed on the system (`it_IT`, else `it_CH` for Swiss users; OS package, Homebrew, LibreOffice; never bundled — the upstream files are GPL-licensed), read at runtime through `crate::hunspell` by the affix engine. Elided forms check the word after the apostrophe (`l'amico`, `un'idea`, `c'è`), hyphenated compounds part by part, user dictionary applies. Without a dictionary installed, Italian text gets no marks, like Word without the language's tools.
- **Suggestions (`it/suggest.rs`)**, same rounds as Portuguese retuned: missing accents first (`caffe` → `caffè`, `perche` → `perché`), the dictionary's `REP` confusions, a missing space (`perme` → `per me`), one typo over `TRY`, then an accent-folding stem scan. Bounded input and rounds.
- **Grammar (`it/grammar.rs`)**: conservative rules with Italian messages — repeated word (emphatic doubles like `piano piano` allowed), space before punctuation, double spaces, sentence capitals (knows `ecc.`, `dott.`, initials, ordinals), doubled punctuation. No comma rule and no English rules on Italian text.
- **`ProofLang::It`** (`it`, `it-IT`, `it-CH`, `ita`) wired through every consumer (`PROOFED`, spelling message "Possibile errore di ortografia", suggestions, grammar); Review › Language menu offers Italian (it was already in the dialog list); the status bar names it; an `it` interface writes new documents in it-IT (`editing_lang`).
- **Hyphenation**: `hyph-utf8`'s `hyph-it.tex` bundled unmodified as `assets/hyphenation/it.pat` (offered under LPPL 1.3+ or MIT; WordCraft uses MIT — header + ATTRIBUTION row + NOTICE entry, like Portuguese): 355 Liang patterns, no exception words.

title: Charts of undrawn types (radar, stock...) show a placeholder
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Radar and stock charts from Word came in as empty space: `chart_items` returned nothing when the plot area had no chart type WordCraft draws, so there was no frame, no title and nothing to say a chart was there.

Now, when the plot area holds only types we don't draw yet, the chart gets a placeholder in its frame. It has the chart area's fill, a light grey border, the chart title if there is one (explicit or Word's automatic one-series title), and a centred line naming the type, e.g. "Radar chart (not supported yet)". Stock, bubble, surface, pie of pie and the 3-D types each get their own name, and anything else is just "Chart". A plot area with a supported type still draws that type, and a supported type with no data still draws nothing, as before. Save is unchanged: these charts keep their original parts.

I didn't do the import note (part 2 of the issue). WordCraft has no import-notes or warnings channel yet. `convert` and `info` print nothing about dropped content, and the docx reader only uses `log::warn!`. Adding one would mean a new reporting path from the reader through the engine to the CLI and the status bar, which felt like its own change. The placeholder at least makes the gap visible on the page and in PDF/PNG export.

Tests: `unsupported_chart_types_draw_nothing` is replaced by `unsupported_chart_types_draw_a_placeholder`. It covers radar with a title, stock without one, an unknown type, and radar next to a line chart, which still draws the line chart. I also rendered Apache POI's chartex.docx with `wordcraft-cli render`: charts 3 and 5 now show the bordered frame with "This is a radar chart" / "This is a stock chart" and the placeholder line. author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1080.

`wordcraft-cli text` printed `Document::plain_text(Body)`, which has no list labels, so bullets and step numbers disappeared. #482 had already fixed the same loss for `convert … .txt` in the engine's TXT export (`wordcraft_engine::io::save_bytes`, "List paragraphs get their label and a tab, as in Word's plain-text save").

`text` now prints the body through that same TXT export, with CRLF turned into `\n` for terminal output. `text file` and `convert file out.txt` now print the same labels:

title: Table selection arrow stays visible on dark paper (#1078)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1078.

Over a table's column and cell selection areas the system pointer is hidden and `table_mouse::arrow` draws a filled selection arrow instead. The fill was always black with a 1px white edge, so on dark paper (`DARK_PAPER = 0x33`) only the thin edge showed and the pointer looked gone. This happened both when scrolling a selection area under the pointer and during a drag from one.

- `arrow` now takes the view's `dark_mode`. On dark paper the column and cell arrows are white with a dark-paper edge. On white paper they are unchanged (black fill, white edge), so the light look stays pixel-identical.
- The hollow row arrow (white fill, black edge) already showed on both papers and is unchanged.
- The colours live in a small `arrow_colors(spot, dark)` helper. A unit test covers every spot on both papers (the test doesn't compile without the fix).

About the drag cause in the issue: with the egui version we use (0.36.2), `PointerState::hover_pos()` returns `latest_pos`, so it is not `None` while a button is down. The drag branch of `paint` already draws the arrow at the pointer, and changing it to `hover.or(latest)` would change nothing. The pointer vanishing during a drag is the same dark-paper contrast problem, and this PR fixes it there too.

title: Mini toolbar no longer covers the ribbon's dropdown lists (#989)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #989.

The floating mini toolbar shown over a text selection was drawn on egui's `Order::Tooltip`, the topmost layer. egui draws menus and combo-box popups (such as the ribbon's font size list) on `Order::Foreground`, which is below `Tooltip`, so opening the size list while text was selected let the toolbar cover it.

The toolbar now uses `Order::Middle` (kept in a `BAR_ORDER` const). Popups and menus draw over it, and it still stays above the document, which egui draws on the background layer. Clicks on the bar still stop there and do not reach the document.

Test: `bar_is_drawn_below_menus_and_dropdown_popups` checks that the bar's layer is below `Order::Foreground`. It fails with the old `Tooltip` layer.

title: Shapes: the drag preview shows the shape alone, not what was behind it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1010.

The drag preview was a cut of the page's cached texture over the object's bounds, so whatever sat behind the shape (text, equations, tables, other shapes) came along with it. The preview is now the object drawn alone: `display::object_display` reuses `object_draws` (the same renderer inline objects use) plus the lines of the text box it shows, and `render::render_items` rasterises those on a transparent background. It is rendered once, when the drag starts moving, and painted at the same place and opacity as before, so dragging still lays out nothing. The page texture accessor it was the only user of goes away.

Validation:
- `objects::tests::a_dragged_shape_leaves_the_text_behind_it` (kittest, real mouse drag, reads the rendered pixels): an unfilled red rectangle in front of black text, dragged into the empty page; fails on main (text pixels inside the preview), passes here
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout -p wordcraft-render -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: DOCX: keep Word ink placed directly in a run when saving (gap #2)
author: rp6186030
body:
## What
Word can store handwritten ink as a `w:contentPart` placed directly inside a run, pointing at an InkML part. WordCraft dropped this form on open, so the ink was lost on save. Ink placed inside a drawing (`w:drawing`) was already kept.

This keeps the direct form through open, edit and save:
- **Read** (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`): a run's `w:contentPart` whose part has the `application/inkml+xml` content type becomes an ink graphic object that carries the original part (relationship, content type and bytes).
- **Write** (`crates/docx/src/write/story.rs`): a directly placed ink part is written back as the same `w:contentPart`, not wrapped in a `w:drawing`. The ink-inside-a-drawing path is unchanged.

Content parts that aren't InkML are still skipped, as before.

## Tests
- `direct_native_ink_content_part_survives_unrelated_edit_and_two_saves` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`): opens a file with direct ink, edits the paragraph text, saves and reopens twice, and checks that the ink, its relationship, content type and bytes are all intact.

## Docs
`docs/gaps.md` (gap #2 and #12), `docs/file-format-parity.md` and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log are updated. Still missing: ink nested in groups or drawing canvases, and drawing Word's ink natively.

title: LaTeX: a "[" after a line break or at the start of a list item stays text
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
A list item whose text starts with "[" (for example "[x] Buy milk") exported as `\item [x] Buy milk`. LaTeX, and WordCraft's own LaTeX import, read "[x]" as the item's label, so the bullet became "x" and the brackets were lost. Text that starts with "[" after a line break exported as `\\` followed by `[1] b`, which LaTeX reads as the line break's optional spacing argument: pdfLaTeX stops with "Illegal unit of measure" ("Missing number" for "[x]") and the bracketed text disappears.

`escape_text` now writes such a bracket as `{[}` when nothing visible comes before it on the line. Brackets after text are unchanged.

`leading_brackets_stay_text` fails on main and passes with the fix. `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass. `cargo xtask ci` stops on three wordcraft-layout tests (`deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`) that fail the same way on unchanged main.

The first commit adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Markdown: list items that start like a block keep their text
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Markdown export wrote a list item's text straight after its marker. Plain paragraphs already go through `escape_line_start`, but list items did not, so an item whose text starts like a block came back as something else:

| Item text | Exported | Imported on `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `---` | `- ---` | a horizontal rule, the item is gone |
| `--` | `- --` | a horizontal rule |
| `1. Intro` | `- 1. Intro` | an empty bullet with a nested numbered item "Intro" |
| `# Agenda` | `- # Agenda` | a heading "Agenda" |
| `+ plus` | `- + plus` | an empty bullet with a nested bullet "plus" |

## Fix

In `write_blocks`, list item text now goes through `escape_line_start`, the same as a paragraph. Bullets need one more check: `--` is not a rule on its own, but `- --` is, so its first hyphen is escaped. An ordered marker can't form a rule. Code items keep their code span.

## Test

`tests::markdown_list_items_that_start_like_blocks_keep_their_text` exports a one-item bullet list for each text and imports it again, and expects one normal bullet with the same text. It fails on `main` (the first case comes back as a rule) and passes with the fix.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats`: 80 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt and clippy pass. In `cargo test --workspace`, 3 tests in `wordcraft-layout` fail, and they fail the same way on `main` without this change: `deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown` and `tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`. Every other test passes. `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass.

title: Expand sample-text formulas on Enter (#1067)
author: lokinmodar
body:
Typing an exact `=rand()` or `=lorem()` paragraph and pressing Enter now replaces it with sample text. Both formulas accept `(p)` and `(p,s)`, default to five paragraphs of three sentences, and restore both defaults if either parameter is invalid or outside 1–200. English sentences are original to WordCraft.

The shared Enter command reuses existing editing primitives, preserving typing and paragraph formatting, Track Changes, and a single undo step. Expansion requires a collapsed caret at the paragraph end and leaves a following empty paragraph. Tests cover both generators, defaults, counts and boundaries, invalid input, exact matching, formatting, undo/redo, and tracked accept/reject. Typing parity and progress documentation are updated; the contributor opted to display their public GitHub profile name.

Validation on native Windows:
- `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo test --workspace -j 2 -- --test-threads=1`: passed, including all 423 engine unit tests and its 19 integration tests.
- `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: passed.
- `cargo build -p wordcraft -j 2`: passed. The Windows app was launched and its control channel confirmed `=rand(2,4)` and `=lorem(2,2)` expansion, one-step undo restoring each formula, and redo; the rendered app window was inspected.
- `cargo xtask ci`: stops at an existing `clippy::drop_non_drop` violation in `crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs:465` (`drop(run)`), unchanged from the base commit.

The 1–200 limits are explicit allocation bounds; exact numerical-limit parity has not been observed in Word.

Closes #1067.

title: Layout: a picture after a content control's start stays on its line (regression from #392)
author: naxvog
body:
A picture that opens a picture content control could disappear: a logo in a fixed-height header text box was drawn in 0.5.0 but no longer in 0.6.1. I bisected it to #392 (content controls are kept), which is the first bad commit; `main` still has the problem.

## Root cause
- **The marker:** since #392, a block content control puts a zero-width `ControlStart` marker at the start of its first paragraph (`read_block_sdt`).
- **The line-breaking rule:** it keeps a line's first item even when it doesn't fit (`if !fits && j > c0`). With the marker in front, the marker became that first item.
- **What happened to the picture:** a picture slightly wider than its line therefore wrapped onto a second line, leaving a line with only the marker above it. In a fixed-height text box the box's text ends at the box, so the picture's line was cut off.

In the real document the picture was 1.5 pt too wide for its box. That's because the box's VML `inset` isn't read yet, which is a separate gap.

## Fix
Markers before an item no longer count as the line's first item. This is the same test the display-equation check a few lines above already uses: `(c0..j).any(|k| … c.kind != ClKind::Marker)`.

Test: `a_picture_too_wide_after_a_content_control_start_stays_on_the_first_line`. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

## Measured
- **docxide-pdf suite (390 Word-referenced documents, `main` 159b84f vs this branch):**
  - `brazilian_logistics_study` SSIM 38.8 → 38.9 %.
  - No other document changes.
- **The real document behind the report (not public):** the logo is drawn again, and page 1 SSIM goes from 71.0 to 72.1 %.

## CI
`cargo xtask ci` steps in a clean Ubuntu 24.04 container (release.yml Linux deps, `craft-fonts` at the pinned ref), on `159b84f`:
- **Passed:** fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, wasm, assets and layers.
- **Tests:** 5 tests fail identically on `main` in that container, because they depend on the installed fonts:
  - fonts: `east_asian_run_uses_o…

title: Files: documents keep their embedded alternative format chunks (w:altChunk), and MHT opens
author: naxvog
body:
Word brings a document's alternative format chunks (`w:altChunk`, ECMA-376 §17.17.2.1) into the document where they stand when it opens the file. WordCraft left them out. Generators and mail-merge tools write whole documents this way, so such a file opened as an empty page. This PR reads them, makes `.mht` files open, and makes web pages open the way Word opens them.

## Root cause
`read_blocks` had no arm for `w:altChunk`. Most chunks are HTML/MHT, RTF or text, and the readers for those live in `wordcraft-formats`, which sits on the same layer as `wordcraft-docx`, so the docx reader can't call them.

## Changes
### docx
- **API:** `read_with(bytes, &ReadOptions { password, chunks })`. `ChunkImporter` is a callback for formats other than WordprocessingML; `read_with_password` now goes through it.
- **Nested Word documents** are read here.
- **Limits per file:** at most 4 levels of nesting, 256 chunks and 512 MB of chunk bytes, the last including unpacked nested packages. The XML depth of a nested document continues from its chunk's depth.
- **Without an importer,** only nested Word documents come in.
- **`w:matchSrc`:** the chunk's content keeps its own formatting. A style whose id the document already has comes along under a new id, and the chunk's document defaults (Word's built-in ones where its file states none) go into its base styles. Unstyled paragraphs use the chunk's own Normal. Without `matchSrc`, the document's styles win.

### doc
- **`Document::adopt`/`adopt_with`/`adopt_blocks`** (moved here from `engine/cmd/paste.rs`) bring another document's media, lists, styles, footnotes, endnotes, comments and revisions along under new ids.
- **Remapping now also covers:** pictures inside groups and charts/SmartArt; the list ids in styles; and table styles together with the revision ids of table/row/cell property changes.
- **Dropped:** a text-box reference that the chunk doesn't bring along.
- **Paste** uses the same code.
- **`Insert › Text from File`** used to …

title: Layout: a centred list heading moves its label with the text
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Problem

A centred (or right-aligned) numbered heading whose label is followed by a space or nothing — a typical contract heading such as "§ 1. Definitions" (`lvlText "§ %1."`, `w:suff="space"`, paragraph `jc="center"`) — is laid out with the label left at the indent and only the text after it centred. Word centres the label and the text together: the line from the indent to the end of the text is shifted as one span.

In a 107-page test contract with 72 such headings, every heading's label sat at the left indent while Word's sits next to the centred title.

## Fix

`crates/layout/src/para.rs`: when the alignment shift applies to the first line and starts at the label (`align_from == c0`) and the label's suffix is `Space` or `Nothing`, the label's `x` moves by the same shift as the text. A tab suffix keeps the old behaviour (the label stays at the indent, as in Word).

## Test

`centred_numbered_heading_centres_label_and_text_together` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): the midpoint of label start and text end is within 1 pt of the line centre, and with a tab suffix the label stays at the indent. It fails without the fix (the label stays at the indent).

## Result

Measured against PDFs exported from Word on the same machine (black-box, not committed): all 72 § headings in the test contract are now within 1.0 pt of Word's position. On a 3-page test document, the share of lines with the same line break as Word went from 90.1 % to 96.7 %.

Checks run locally (macOS arm64):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — OK
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings` — OK
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` — 235 passed
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` — OK
- not run: full `cargo xtask ci` and `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 target here); the change is layout arithmetic only.

title: Export: page images draw headers and footers at full strength
author: przemek-arch
body:

title: Canvas: handle keys before laying out, so a keystroke shows in its own frame
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Problem

`canvas::show` took the layout, painted the pages and only then handled the frame's key events (`keys::canvas_events`). A typed character changed the document after the frame had been painted, so it appeared one frame later — about 17 ms extra at 60 Hz on every keystroke.

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: key events are handled at the start of `canvas::show`, before `session.layout()`, with the canvas focus from the previous frame. The "Save changes?" guard is kept. The same frame then lays out and paints the change.

## Test

`a_keystroke_is_painted_in_its_own_frame` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): after one frame carrying `Event::Text("x")`, the layout the canvas painted (its page-key cache) is the session's latest layout. It fails without the fix (the frame painted the layout from before the keystroke).

## Measurement

Headless, with the `perf_probe` example from #1108, typing into the middle of the longest paragraph of a 106-page document: the layout and page re-render move into the keystroke's frame (median 0.4 → 16.6 ms there, same total over two frames), i.e. one frame less between key and screen. Estimated key-to-screen latency drops from about 50 to about 33 ms.

Checks run locally (macOS arm64):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — OK
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` — OK
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` — 368 passed
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` — OK
- not run: full `cargo xtask ci` and `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: Tools: ui.wheel control method and a headless perf_probe example
author: przemek-arch
body:
## What
