title: Tools: cargo xtask visual-diff compares two PDFs of a document page by page
author: przemek-arch
body:
## What

`cargo xtask visual-diff REF.pdf TEST.pdf OUTDIR [--private] [--dpi N]` compares two PDFs of the same document page by page — typically a reference you exported yourself from another word processor (kept out of the repo, per the clean-room rules) and WordCraft's own export (`wordcraft-cli convert doc.docx out.pdf`).

Per page, in `OUTDIR/result.json`:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ssim` | structural similarity of the greyscale page (8×8 windows) |
| `diff_px` | % of pixels differing by more than 64 levels |
| `lines` | text lines in reference / WordCraft |
| `same_break` | % of the reference's lines found with identical text in WordCraft (same line break) |
| `dy`, `dx` | median vertical / max horizontal offset of the matched lines (pt) |
| `page_start_same` | the page starts with the same line |

plus a summary, the largest horizontal offsets (`dx_diffs`) and the runs of lines that break differently (`break_diffs`). Unless `--private`, it also writes `diff_pNNN.ppm` maps (reference ink red, WordCraft blue, shared black). `--private` writes numbers and short line hashes only, so it can be run on confidential documents.

## Why

"Looks like Word" becomes numbers that layout work can track and compare before and after a change. Example: this is how the centred list-heading fix (#1105) was measured — on a 3-page test document the same-line-break share went from 90.1 % to 96.7 %, page SSIM 0.965; on a 107-page contract it showed that pagination drifts from page 7 on and why (footnote placement).

## How

Std + `serde_json`, like the rest of xtask. poppler does the heavy lifting through `std::process::Command`: `pdftoppm -gray` (read as PGM) and `pdftotext -bbox-layout` (line boxes). Lines are matched by longest common subsequence (equal start/end trimmed first; the table is capped at ~100 M cells). A 107-page pair takes about 2 s.

title: Branding: build-time brand layer for downstream builds (WORDCRAFT_BRAND_DIR)
author: przemek-arch
body:
## Problem

WordCraft's brand terms ask redistributors to drop the ArtCraft name and logo, and community links (Discord) don't fit a downstream product. Today a downstream build has to patch around ten UI files, and those patches conflict with almost every upstream day (`ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, `ribbon.rs`, `dialogs.rs` change many times a day).

## Proposal

Build-time branding from one folder **outside this repository**:

```sh
WORDCRAFT_BRAND_DIR=/path/to/mybrand cargo build --release -p wordcraft
```

`crates/ui-egui/build.rs` turns `mybrand/brand.toml` into constants (`OUT_DIR/brand_gen.rs`, read through the new `ui_egui::brand` module). **Without the variable the generated constants are WordCraft's defaults and every hook falls through to the existing code** — the shipped app is unchanged.

| `brand.toml` | effect |
|---|---|
| `name`, `tagline`, `website` | window title, About, Save Changes title; settings folder (`control-key`) and `docProps/app.xml` Application (`docx`) |
| `[accent] light/dark` | one source for the accent; `Tokens::branded()` derives the text/hover shade and picks the text colour on the accent by WCAG contrast |
| `[hide] discord, artcraft, share, autosave, tabs` | hides the buttons/tabs; the commands stay |
| `[relabel]` | English UI string → replacement, one hook in `i18n::t`/`tc` |
| `[icons] font, glyphs, map` | optional icon font + "WordCraft icon name → glyph" map; `icons::paint` falls back to the built-in icons (and only uses the font once it is loaded) |
| `[[tab]]` | an extra ribbon tab before Help, drawn with the existing custom-group renderer; its commands are registered (`Registry::extend`) and disabled until implemented |
| `[[licence]]` | entries in a Licenses tab of About |

Full reference: `docs/branding.md`.

No asset enters the repo: the brand's fonts, icons and licence files stay in the brand folder, so `ATTRIBUTION.md` / `xtask assets` are untouched.

title: View: Window group commands on the ribbon as entry points (gap #27)
author: rp6186030
body:
Depends on #1098: this branch is based on that commit. Merge that first, or review only the top commit.

## What
Adds the four missing View › Window commands to the command registry, the ribbon and the KeyTips:

| Command | Id | What it does today |
|---|---|---|
| Arrange All | `view.arrangeAll` | Sends an `arrange` UI request; the app shows a status message |
| View Side by Side | `view.sideBySide` | Toggles `ViewState::side_by_side` (the button lights up) |
| Synchronous Scrolling | `view.syncScroll` | Toggles `ViewState::sync_scroll` |
| Switch Windows (Ctrl+F6) | `view.switchWindows` | Opens a menu listing the current document; `{"window": …}` sends a switch request |

**These are entry points only.** WordCraft has no multi-document window management yet, so nothing arranges, tiles or scrolls windows together. Gap #27 stays open in `docs/gaps.md` (3–5 h) for the real behaviour. What this PR does give:
- the commands can be run from the ribbon, the CLI and MCP;
- their state is saved;
- the window behaviour can be built on top later without changing the command ids.

No panic paths. Window commands never edit the document.

## Tests
- `view_window_commands_and_state` (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`) checks that:
  - each command sends its UI request;
  - side by side and synchronous scrolling toggle and accept an explicit `value`;
  - Ctrl+F6 maps to `view.switchWindows`;
  - the document is unchanged.

title: Drawings: VML text boxes keep their margins, fit and alignment; hidden drawings are kept but not shown
author: naxvog
body:
Two gaps in how drawings from older Word files (VML) are shown. Both are measured against Word's own PDF exports.

- **VML text boxes ignored their internal margins.** A `v:textbox` with `inset="0,0,0,0"` (how letterheads and form headers place their address blocks exactly) still had Word's default 7.2 pt / 3.6 pt margins, so its text sat 7.3 pt right of and 3.8 pt below where Word puts it.
- **Hidden drawings were drawn.** VML `visibility:hidden` and DrawingML `wp:docPr/@hidden` were not read, so hidden boxes appeared as empty outlined squares, took room and wrapped text.

## Changes
### VML text boxes (commit 1)
In `read_vml`, a `v:textbox` now fills the same `TextBody` fields DrawingML's `wps:bodyPr` does:
- **`inset="l,t,r,b"`** (ECMA-376 Part 4 §19.1.2.22):
  - a value that's left out (or doesn't parse) keeps Word's default;
  - a bare number is in EMUs;
  - `o:insetmode="auto"` leaves the defaults.
- **`mso-fit-shape-to-text`** becomes `auto_fit`, like `a:spAutoFit`.
- **The shape's `v-text-anchor`** becomes the vertical alignment.
- **In a group,** the `v:textbox` and its `w:txbxContent` are taken together, so a member's margins can't land on another member's text.

The writer already saves these fields as `wps:bodyPr` `lIns`… and `a:spAutoFit`, so they survive a save.

### Hidden drawings (commit 2)
`Float.hidden` is a new flag on the placement data every drawing shares.
- **Reader:** set from VML `visibility:hidden` (floating or inline), DrawingML `wp:docPr/@hidden`, and a group member's `pic:cNvPr`/`wps:cNvPr` `@hidden`.
- **Writer:** written back the same way, so nothing is lost on save.
- **Layout:**
  - `left_out_objects` leaves hidden drawings out whatever is shown: not placed, no wrap area, no hit area, nothing drawn;
  - an inline one gets a zero-size cluster;
  - hidden group members are not drawn and their text boxes are not laid out;
  - the notes of a hidden text box are not placed.
- **Exports** to HTML, Markdown, ODT, RTF, LaTeX and text, and H…

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

title: Canvas: middle-click scrolls the document, like Word
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1065.

Middle-click the document and a marker appears where you clicked; moving the pointer above or below it scrolls, gently near the marker and faster farther away, with a small dead zone around it. Another click (middle, left or right), Escape, any other key, the wheel or leaving the window stops it. Holding the wheel down and dragging scrolls too, and letting go stops it, like Word and Firefox. The new `autoscroll.rs` is pdfcraft's middle-click autoscroll (#111 there) with the same Chromium speed curve, adapted to the canvas: its delta goes through the same path as the wheel and the drag-select edge scroll, and the click that stops it doesn't also move the caret or open the context menu. Read Mode turns columns instead of scrolling, so it's off there and while a dialog is open. WordCraft doesn't paste the primary selection on a middle click, so the button is free on Linux.

It's on for Windows and Linux/BSD and off on macOS (Mac apps don't scroll this way) and on the web (browsers have their own middle-click behaviour). pdfcraft enables it on Linux only; since Word does this on Windows I turned it on there too, happy to switch either way.

title: .doc import: section breaks, huge-PAPX properties, TOC content and leaders, table grids, EMF labels, text frames (#880)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #880.

`.doc` files saved by modern Word import wrong in five visible ways, all verified against a real 285-page 3GPP specification kept locally for testing (never committed; every code change is covered by synthetic-fixture tests in `crates/docbin/src/tests.rs` and `crates/metafile/src/tests.rs`).

## Root causes fixed

| | Symptom | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| A | Row/paragraph properties silently lost | `sprmPHugePapx` (0x6646) ignored — oversized PAPXs live in the Data stream; now resolved (65 537-byte cap, lenient fallback) |
| B | Whole document laid out with the last section's margins (text reflow, +30 pages) | The section-break `0x0C` character was not treated as a paragraph mark, so intermediate sections (and their margins) were dropped |
| C | TOC imports as 679 empty paragraphs | Complex-field results were swallowed into one anchor; TOC fields now keep their cached result as real content (range fields, matching the docx reader) |
| D | Change-history table collapses into 1–2 character columns | Only the first row's `sprmTDefTable` became the grid; now one grid is built from all rows' edges, with per-cell widths, computed spans, cell side margins (`sprmTDxaGapHalf`), fixed table layout, and no phantom cell from the row-end mark |

title: Backstage: add Close to the side menu, after Export
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1124.

The File side menu had no Close. It now sits right after Export and runs `file.close`, the same command as Mod+W, so it gets the existing Save / Don't Save / Cancel prompt for free (Save goes through Save As for a document that was never saved). title: Alt+numpad character codes (#961)
author: dkhlapov
body:
## #961: Alt+numpad character codes

Closes #961. Hold Alt, type a decimal code, release Alt: the character appears at the caret.
- `0xxx` → Windows-1252 (Alt+0233 → é, Alt+0128 → €).
- `1–255` → the OEM code page: cp437 (Alt+233 → Θ, Alt+1 → ☺), or cp850 for Western European locales. The tables are generated from the public Unicode mapping files.
- `>255` → the Unicode character (Alt+8364 → €).
- Not on macOS.

A new command, `text.typeCode {"code", "oem"?}`, does this for agents. It inserts through `text.insert`, so it's one undo step.

**Maintainer call: top-row digits.** egui 0.36 reports keypad and top-row digits as the same key, and eframe doesn't expose raw winit events. So Alt held alone plus top-row digits also composes a code; before, it typed the plain digit on Linux. Ctrl+Alt+digit shortcuts and KeyTips are unchanged. Restricting codes to the keypad would need a patched egui-winit.

**Correction to the issue:** in cp850, 233 (0xE9) is Ú per the Unicode mapping file; é is 130 in both cp437 and cp850.

**Tests:**
- Engine: the mapping and locale cases, and the command (one undo step, bad params).
- ui-egui: Alt held, keypad 0 2 3 3, Alt released gives "é". There's no double-typing if the platform echoes the character, and a bare Alt tap still opens KeyTips.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Not tried on Windows, where the OS composes Alt codes itself. The double-typing guard covers the case where winit passes that character through.

title: Fix blurred text in Web and Draft Layout on long documents
author: ripdog
body:
## Problem
Web and Draft Layout produce one very tall page. The canvas clamps raster scale by the entire page height to fit the GPU's maximum texture dimension (8192px in the reproduction), then enlarges the low-resolution bitmap, severely blurring document text.

## Fix
- Render exceptionally tall pages in stable, full-resolution 1024-device-pixel-high tiles instead of downsampling the whole page.
- Only rasterize tiles that intersect the visible area, reuse cached tiles while scrolling and evict tiles outside the viewport.
- Keep ordinary pages on the existing single-texture path and retain newer cache-key, ink-replay and Hide White Space behavior.
- Add a long-page tiling regression test, and update parity and progress docs.

## Before and after screenshots

title: Zotero: text typed just after a citation goes outside its field
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #898.

A range field's end marker takes no room, so a click just after a citation puts the caret *before* it: whatever you typed there went into the citation's result, Zotero then saw the citation as edited by hand, and asked to replace it when you added another citation or the bibliography (it reported the caret as inside the field). Right after inserting a citation it worked only because the bridge leaves the caret after the marker. Now a collapsed caret sitting on one or more field ends is moved past them (`Document::past_field_ends`) before typing/pasting, before Zotero inserts a field, and when Zotero asks whether the cursor is in a field, which matches Word, where text typed right after a field lands outside it. The arrow-key step over the invisible marker the reporter noticed is unchanged; happy to look at that separately if you'd like.

title: Layout: a list label moves with its text when the paragraph is aligned (#1159)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1159

## Cause

When a line is aligned (centre, or the end edge), `layout_lines` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs` shifts the x of every cluster after the label by the line's slack. The list label of the first line has its own `x`, set from the first-line indent before the alignment is known, and nothing moved it. So with a centred or end-aligned list item the text moved and the bullet or number stayed at the margin. The same happens in right-to-left paragraphs, where `Align::Right` is the left edge, because the label is mirrored after the same shift.

## Fix

The first line's label gets the same shift as its text: `lab.x += shift` where the text is shifted. After a tab stop in the line (`last_tab`) the label stays, as the text before the tab does. The gap from the label to the text (the label's tab or suffix) is unchanged, so label plus text move as one unit, the way Word keeps the bullet attached when a list item is centred or aligned right.

## Verified

Offscreen (`ui_shot`, 900×520, empty document, four bulleted paragraphs: left, centre, right, left again):

| | left | centre | right |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | bullet at the margin | bullet at the margin, text far right of it | bullet at the margin, text at the right edge |
| this branch | bullet at the margin | bullet directly before the text, the pair centred | bullet directly before the text, the pair at the right edge |

New test `crates/layout/src/tests_bidi.rs::list_label_moves_with_its_text_when_the_paragraph_is_aligned`: for left-to-right and right-to-left paragraphs, the distance from the label to the text start is the same for a left, centred, end-aligned and justified paragraph (13.8 pt on `main` for the left one; 201.6 pt for the centred one before the fix), the text really moves (centre, then end), the justified paragraph starts where the left-aligned one does, and every label stays inside the text area. It fails on `main` and passes here. `cargo xtask ci` passes. The layout crate's 235 test…

title: Lists: the bullet or number moves with centred and right-aligned text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1159.

The list label is placed at the first-line indent before the line is broken, and alignment then shifted only the text clusters (`xs`), so with Center or Align Right the bullet stayed at the margin while the text moved. Now the label gets the same shift as the text on its first line, so bullet and text move together as in Word. Numbered and multilevel labels go through the same path, so they're fixed too; right-to-left paragraphs work because the label is shifted before the line is mirrored. When the text itself contains a tab, alignment only applies after the last tab and the label stays put, the same as the text before that tab.

title: Draw: Ink to Math converts simple handwritten symbols into an equation (gap #12)
author: rp6186030
body:
> Depends on #1098: this branch is based on that commit. Merge that first, or review only the top commit.

## What
Adds `draw.inkToMath` (Draw › Convert › Ink to Math). With a lasso selection of pen or pencil strokes, it recognises a small set of line-based symbols and replaces the ink with a native inline equation, the same object Insert › Equation creates:

| Ink | Equation |
|---|---|
| one horizontal stroke | `-` |
| one vertical stroke | `1` |
| one diagonal stroke | `/` |
| two parallel horizontal strokes, stacked and overlapping | `=` |
| a horizontal and a vertical stroke that cross near their middles | `+` |

The command only converts what it recognises:
- Anything it doesn't recognise (curves, rotated or flipped ink, multi-path strokes, highlighter, strokes side by side, an L shape, more than two strokes) is refused with an error, and the ink is left unchanged.
- The conversion is a single undo step. Undo brings back the original strokes.

## How
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`: `ink_to_math` gathers the lassoed strokes in page coordinates (each stroke's placed frame, so ink anchored in different paragraphs compares correctly), classifies each with Ink to Shape's `recognise()`, and maps them to a symbol in `recognized_math`.
  - `equals_geometry` checks that the two strokes are parallel, stacked and overlapping.
  - `plus_geometry` checks that the two strokes actually cross within the central 60% of each.
  - The ink objects are deleted right to left, and the equation goes in at the first anchor.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/equation.rs`: `insert_recognized_linear` inserts a linear-format equation at a position without opening the equation editor.
- "Ink to Math" is translated in all 18 interface languages.

No panic paths: lookups go through `?`/`let … else`, and a failed recognition returns `CmdError::Failed`.

## Tests
- `ink_to_math_replaces_unambiguous_lassoed_strokes_with_an_equation`:
  - `-`, `/`, `1`, `=` and `+` convert;
  - `=` is one undo step, a…

title: Layout: a paragraph ending with a page break leaves its space after on the old page
author: naxvog
body:
A paragraph that ends with a page break kept its mark on the old page (#932), but its **space after** was still added after the break. So the next page started up to a line too low, and the next paragraph didn't get the "no space before after a page-break mark" treatment, because the page no longer counted as "at the top". In `place_para_in_flow`, when the mark stayed with its page break (`after_break_mark`), the paragraph's space after is 0. That 0 is also what `pb.prev` keeps for spacing collapse with the next paragraph.

- **Page break before:** a paragraph with *page break before* right after such a paragraph no longer opens an extra blank page. With 0 pt after, this already worked.
- **Table:** a table that follows the break starts at the top of the page.

title: Layout: paragraph borders take room, picture-only lines keep no descent, line spacing may hang into the bottom margin
author: naxvog
body:
Three Word layout rules that decide where pages break. Each one is measured against Word's reference PDFs, and each needed the others to avoid exposing a wrong page break.

- **Paragraph borders took no room.** Top and bottom borders were drawn, but the text below didn't move. Word puts the border's space plus its width between the text and what follows, so headings with a rule under them sat 1.5–6 pt too high.
- **A line holding only a picture got a font descent below it.** On a paragraph's last line, Word makes such a line exactly as tall as the picture. Multiple spacing adds only its extra leading, so each such paragraph was 2–10 pt too tall.
- **The last line on a page had to fit with its extra leading.** WordCraft also checked the 1.15× or double-spacing leading below the text. Word only needs the text to fit and lets that leading hang into the bottom margin, so WordCraft moved lines (and with widow control, whole paragraphs) to the next page early.

## Changes (`crates/layout`)
### Borders
- **`border_bands`:** gives the top and bottom band, `space + width`, with hostile values clamped.
- **Flow:** the bands are added in the body flow (`place_para_in_flow`), in cells, headers and text boxes (`layout_box`), and in keep-with-next's look-ahead (`next_first_line`).
- **Groups:**
  - consecutive paragraphs with the same borders and indents, list indents included (new `effective_para`), form one group up to a section break;
  - the group has one top rule and one bottom rule;
  - the between border (`w:between`) is drawn above each later member;
  - sides, and shading the members share, run through the spacing between them as one box.
- **Bottom of the page:** a bottom border's band must fit on the page, and a bordered last line doesn't hang.
- **Tall paragraphs:** a bordered paragraph too tall for an empty page overflows there. A local `at_top` counts the paragraph's own top band as still at the top.

### Picture-only lines
`break_lines` notes whether a line holds a…

title: Picture transparency/corrections/color are absolute from the original + transparency slider
author: DevCoderMax
body:
Fixes #1173.

Picture Adjustments used to compound: transparency 80% then 0% stayed faded, brightness +20 then −20 didn't restore, grayscale then vivid couldn't recover colors. `adjust()` always decoded the already-edited bitmap; the `originals` chain existed but only Reset Picture read it. title: Fonts embedded in a .docx lay out and export its text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1171.

Since #831 the reader keeps the font table and its font parts, but only as opaque parts for saving, so layout never saw them and text in a font that isn't installed fell back to another one. A new `wordcraft_docx::embedded_fonts` walks the kept `word/fontTable.xml` (`w:embedRegular/Bold/Italic/BoldItalic`), resolves each `r:id` through the kept relationships and undoes the obfuscation with `w:fontKey` (first 32 bytes XOR the reversed GUID; an all-zero or missing key leaves the file as is). `io::open_bytes_with` passes them through `decode_font_file` and adds them to the font database in memory through a new `FontDb::add_document_fonts`, which also bumps the font generation: `word::resolve` memoises family lookups, so a family looked up while it was missing (an earlier document, or the same one opened before) would otherwise keep resolving to the fallback. Nothing is written to the user font folder, and faces already available are never replaced.

Two choices you may want differently, happy to switch:
- The fonts are added to the process-wide `FontDb` for the rest of the run, not scoped to the one document: per-document fonts would mean threading a font set through layout, render and PDF. Since existing family/style pairs are never replaced, a document that doesn't name the font measures the same.
- OS/2 `fsType` isn't checked. The font is only used to show and export a document that already carries it, but a "restricted licence" font would now be subset into the exported PDF. I can skip those if you prefer.

Validation:
- `tests_fonts::fonts_embedded_in_a_docx_lay_out_its_text` (a renamed JetBrains Mono, embedded as an obfuscated .odttf and as a plain .ttf with the zero key): fails on main (`177.53 vs 288`, the line is measured in the fallback), passes here, also run alone (`--test-threads=1`)

title: Stop Space and Enter from resetting the X11 input context
author: raythurman2386
body:
Fixes #1169.

On Linux with fcitx's XIM server, WordCraft stops accepting keyboard input after a few words. The process stays up. The same key stream types a full sentence when `XMODIFIERS` is unset, and when WordCraft runs as native Wayland (`WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`).

WordCraft forces the X11 backend when `DISPLAY` is set, so a Hyprland session started from the ArtCraft launcher still runs it under XWayland with `XMODIFIERS=@im=fcitx`. The canvas is one click-sensing widget. In egui 0.36, Space and Enter on a focused click-sensing widget set `Response::clicked` (`FAKE_PRIMARY_CLICKED`). The canvas treated that as "take focus" and called `request_focus`. egui's `request_focus` always interrupts IME, even when that widget already has focus. egui-winit turns the interrupt into `set_ime_allowed(false)` then `set_ime_allowed(true)` in the same frame. winit 0.30.13's X11 backend destroys and recreates the XIM input context. fcitx then queues every later key ([fcitx/fcitx5#1641](https://github.com/fcitx/fcitx5/issues/1641)).

On the machine in #1169 the drop lined up with the space after the first word: characters had already landed, then one same-timestamp `set_ime_allowed` false/true pair, and nothing further was inserted. With XIM disconnected, those same pairs kept happening on the spaces between words and the sentence completed.

This patch ignores that keyboard click. A pointer click, an accessibility click, or a drag still requests focus, including a click on a canvas that already has focus, so an in-progress composition still commits. `want_focus` still focuses the canvas when it does not have focus, and no longer re-requests focus when it already does.

This does not unset `XMODIFIERS` (that would break real CJK XIM clients) and does not make native Wayland the default (file drag-and-drop is missing there, which is why `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs` forces X11). The stuck swallow inside fcitx, and winit recreating the context on every IME interrupt, are unchanged. An…

On a long table that meant shaping tens of thousands of paragraphs twice. It now uses `measure_table_columns`, the measurement the AutoFit command already used.
- Every row is still measured. No row cap, so a wide cell in the last row of a long table still widens its column.
- List labels and field results are counted, using cloned numbering counters, so measuring doesn't disturb the real layout or equation numbers.
- The old measurement helpers are deleted.

| Fixture (release, headless) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2,000×8 table, cold layout (137 pages) | 1,223.7 ms | 335.6 ms |

title: Word forms keep their legacy form fields and rows' skipped grid columns when saved
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1174: the save side. Forms opened and saved again keep their legacy form fields and their rows' skipped grid columns.

The reader dropped `w:ffData` when it read a field's `begin`, and `trPr` only knew height, header and cantSplit, so `gridBefore`/`wBefore`/`gridAfter`/`wAfter` went too. `InlineObject::Field` now carries a `form` string with the `w:ffData` as raw OOXML, the way content controls keep their `rpr_xml`. Still open from #1174: drawing `FORMCHECKBOX` as a box (and toggling it), and laying out rows with `gridBefore` from the right grid column. Layout still starts those rows at column 0. The model now has the field for that, but it touches `Table::grid_col`/`cell_at_grid`, the layout passes and hit-testing, so I'd rather do it as a separate PR. Raw XML instead of a typed form field model is a judgement call, happy to switch if you'd rather model the checkbox/text/dropdown parts.

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-fonts is **not** cloned beside the repo, behaviour is unchanged — build.rs warns exactly as it does today.
- The existing `[alias]` entry is untouched.

## Verification

Built with the variable explicitly removed from the environment, so only the config could supply it:

```
env -u CRAFT_FONTS_DIR cargo build --release
```

The crate recompiled and the "no craft-fonts embedded" warning did not appear. Tested on macOS (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, against craft-fonts at its current main.

title: Desktop: a maximized window no longer flashes on and off at start-up on Windows (#23)
author: tlomts-dev
body:
On Windows, a window saved as maximized (#23) flashes on and off several times at start-up before it settles: you see a window appear and disappear within the first second, then the app opens.

## Cause

winit shows a window the moment it creates it maximized, even though eframe starts it hidden until the first frame (the white-flash guard). `WindowGeometry::apply` passed `with_maximized(true)` to the viewport builder, so a maximized window was shown and hidden repeatedly while it was being set up.

## Change

On Windows the window now opens at its normal size and position, still hidden, and the first frame (once the monitor is known, as the off-screen check already waits for) sends `ViewportCommand::Maximized(true)`. Other platforms are unchanged. Un-maximizing still returns to the saved normal size and position.

- `WindowGeometry::maximizes_after_open` / `maximize_after_open`, and `apply` no longer asks for a maximized window where that applies (`crates/ui-egui/src/window_geometry.rs`)
- `App::logic` sends the command on the first frame (`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`)
- New unit test for both platforms' behaviour

## Measured

Polling the process's top-level window every 15 ms on Windows 11 with `"maximized": true` in `ui.json`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| visibility changes before the app is ready | show, hide, show, hide, show (about 4 flashes in 0.2 s) | hidden until the first frame, shown once |
| then | | maximized about 60 ms after it is shown |

Without a saved maximized state the window already behaved correctly (hidden until the first frame, shown once), which is how the cause was isolated.

## Checks

`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib window_geometry` (8 tests) passes on the change. Built and run as a release `.msi`/portable build on Windows x64 to take the measurement above.

title: Tables: Select All then Delete removes a table the document starts with; right-click Delete offers Delete Table again
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1198.

Two separate causes. Ctrl+A in a document that starts with a table puts the selection's start inside the table's first cell, and `delete_range` only dropped covered tables when the range began *outside* a table, so Delete/Backspace emptied the cells and left the table. It now handles the other direction too: a range from the very start of a top-level table to a top-level paragraph removes the covered tables and joins what's left. The right-click part is from #694 (284818b), which replaced the old Delete › Rows / Columns / Table submenu with one item that follows the selection, so with just the caret in a cell the menu only offered Delete Cells and there was no way to delete the table from it. Delete is a submenu again (Cells, Columns, Rows, Table), like the Delete button Word shows on right-click; the rest of #694's selection-dependent items are unchanged. Happy to switch to showing only Delete Table next to the selection's own item if you'd rather keep the menu shorter.

title: docs: clarify external contributor access to shared standards (#1160)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## Problem
The agent instructions require reading `storytold/craftrules`, but external contributors cannot access it. Shared standards, contributor helpers and the release playbook are presented without a clear access boundary.

## Root cause / findings
- The shared repository and referenced paths return HTTP 404 both anonymously and through the authenticated contributor account. A 404 alone does not establish whether a repository is private, moved or deleted.

## Changes
- Direct external contributors to existing public documentation and condition shared/local planning instructions on availability.
- Preserve all existing safety, clean-room, asset, Rust-only, wasm, quality-gate and progress-update requirements.
- Synchronize `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, including the existing contributor-consent rules.
- Make automatic username credits and manual opt-in names explicit; qualify shared helpers and stats refresh as optional or maintainer-only operations requiring access.
- Identify the release playbook and signing reference as internal maintainer resources.

Only the four documentation files are changed. No shared script or private standard is copied, and contributor records, production code and workflow configuration are unchanged.

- Verified new public documen…

## Native-speaker review

I'm a native Swedish speaker. The draft was made with Claude Code, and I reviewed it:

- Before the bulk translation, I approved a glossary of the recurring terms (tabs, common commands, dialog buttons, units). I chose several words myself, for example *Typsnitt*, *Stil*, *Figur*, *Verktygspanel* for the ribbon, *Använd* for Apply and *community* for the Discord texts.

title: Ctrl+Q resets the paragraph without also closing the window
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1218.

The second action came from egui, not from the app's keymap. egui's default `quit_shortcuts` is Command+Q, and egui maps Command to Ctrl outside the Mac. So on Windows and Linux every Ctrl+Q ran `para.reset` and then, at the end of the frame, egui sent `ViewportCommand::Close`. With unsaved changes, that close shows the save prompt. The app now replaces that list with ⌘Q only (`Modifiers::MAC_CMD`, which only the Mac sends), next to where it already turns off egui's keyboard zoom for the same reason. Cmd+Q still quits on macOS, and Ctrl+Q there is still Word for Mac's reset. Windows and Linux are left with Alt+F4 and the close button, as in Word. If you'd rather drop egui's quit shortcut completely and rely on the macOS app menu for ⌘Q, I'm happy to switch.

Validation:
- `ctrl_q_resets_the_paragraph_without_closing_the_window` (ui-egui): fails on main (`Ctrl+Q doesn't close the window`, since egui's output carries `ViewportCommand::Close`), passes here. It also checks that ⌘Q still sends Close.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib ctrl_q_resets_the_paragraph -- --test-threads=1`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Ctrl+Q resets the paragraph without also closing the window (Fixes #1218)
author: Claudio911015
body:
Fixes #1218.

**Problem.** Ctrl+Q is bound to Reset Paragraph Formatting (`para.reset`), as in Word. egui also has its own quit shortcut, `Options::quit_shortcuts` = Cmd/Ctrl+Q, which sends `ViewportCommand::Close`. On Windows and Linux both fire on one key press: the paragraph is reset and the "Do you want to save changes?" dialog opens. On macOS the reset is Ctrl+Q and quitting is Cmd+Q, so they don't clash.

**Fix.** Where the app installs its egui options (next to `zoom_with_keyboard = false`), clear `quit_shortcuts` when not on macOS. Closing the window still works through the window's close button and File › Close.

**Tests.**
- New `ctrl_q_resets_the_paragraph_without_closing_the_window` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` feeds a Ctrl+Q key event and asserts no `ViewportCommand::Close` is sent. It fails without the change and passes with it.

title: Ctrl+wheel zoom keeps the place under the pointer instead of scrolling the page away
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1223 (@nekotxs confirmed it on Linux).

Ctrl+wheel (and pinch) changed the zoom but left the scroll offset in pixels, so whenever you weren't at the very top the page slid away under the pointer while it zoomed. Once the pages reflowed into rows it got worse: the column change set `scroll_to_caret`, and the view glided back to the caret, often pages away. The events egui-winit sends on Linux were fine (Ctrl sets both `ctrl` and `command`, so the canvas already ignores them for scrolling); the scrolling came from the zoom itself, on every platform. Now the canvas notes the page point under the pointer before applying the zoom and scrolls so the same point is under the pointer at the new scale, rows or not, and a pointer zoom no longer triggers the jump to the caret. The zoom buttons and the Zoom dialog are unchanged. Anchoring on the pointer is how browsers and most viewers do it; happy to switch to keeping the top of the view instead if you'd rather follow Word there.

Validation:
- `ctrl_wheel_zoom_keeps_the_place_under_the_pointer` (Linux-style Ctrl+wheel events, several pages down, zooming out through a reflow into rows): fails on main (`frame 0 at 94%: [311.8 488.4] on page 3, was [311.2 311.2]`: the point under the pointer moves 177 pt down the page in the first zoom frame), passes here
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib zoom`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib scroll`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

@nekotxs I could only test this on macOS. If the page still scrolls while you zoom with this, could you say which mouse or touchpad you're using, and whether Ctrl was already held when you started turning the wheel? Thanks!

title: Harden against hostile-document DoS and non-web link export
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Summary

A security pass over the file parsers, layout and exporters found several small, crafted documents that make WordCraft allocate or compute without bound when opened (GUI, `wordcraft-cli`, or the MCP server), plus hyperlink targets written into exported files without the scheme check the HTML/Markdown writers already apply. None of these lets a document run code or read files; they are denial-of-service (lost work in the GUI) and follow-on-click credential exposure. Every fix bounds an attacker-controlled size, matches the existing `MAX_*`/cap style, and lands with a regression test per the never-crash standard.

## Changes

| Area | Problem | Fix | Measured (release CLI, same input) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layout` | A table repeats its header rows on every page it spills onto; many tall header rows paginate to O(headers × pages) placed items | Per-table cap on header-row repeats; pagination still finishes | 2 KB .docx: 1.1 GB → 124 MB |
| `formats` (HTML → model) | Many `<tr>` with large `rowspan` expand to rows × 64 covered cells, and `model::table` pre-allocated a full rows × cols grid only to clear it | Cap rows at `MAX_ROWS` before `insert_covered`, bound its total work, build the grid template with one row | 640 KB .html: >1.5 GB → 215 MB (large plain tables are faster too) |
| `docx` custom geometry | A Bézier segment accepted any number of points, making de Casteljau flattening quadratic | Cap points per segment (conformant segments have ≤3) | 3 KB .docx: 12 s → 0.15 s |
| `docbin` (.doc) | Story tables and the piece table can map the same backing text many times | Hold total materialised characters to 2× the WordDocument stream size — each char costs ≥1 stream byte, so real files never reach it | 45 KB .doc: >1.2 GB → 14 MB |
| `render`, `pdf`, `formats/rtf` | Picture decodes relied on the `image` crate's default limits; the side check in PDF ran only after a full decode | Make the 512 MB allocation cap explicit; apply the existing side limits as …

title: Layout: inside/outside floats swap sides on even pages; Page Setup shows mirror margins (#1181)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #1181.

## Problem
A .docx with mirror margins, and shapes placed in the outside margin of each page, opened with every shape in the right margin. Mirror Margins also looked switched off.

- **Floats:** `w:mirrorMargins` was already read, and the body text already mirrored (#452). But `float_rect` always treated `wp:align` `inside`/`outside` as left/right and `relativeFrom="insideMargin"`/`"outsideMargin"` as the left/right margins, whichever page the float was on.
- **Page-relative floats:** even pages are laid out like odd ones and then shifted by `mirror_even_pages`, so floats placed from the page edge moved with the text. #490 listed this as a known limit.
- **UI:** nothing showed mirror margins. The Margins menu has no check marks, and Page Setup has no option for them.

## Fix
- **Layout** (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`): `PageFrame` now carries the page number and whether even pages are mirrored.
  - Inside/outside alignment and the inside/outside margin areas follow the page side (ECMA-376 `ST_AlignH`, `ST_RelFromH`): on an even page the inside is the right side.
  - Positions are worked out in the frame used before the mirror shift. Floats placed from the page edge now stay put, and the left/right margin areas are each page's own.
  - Floating tables (`w:tblpXSpec`, `tblpPr` relative to page or margin) get the same treatment, in the box and body paths.
- **Engine:** `layout.margins` takes an optional `"mirror": bool`. Presets still pick mirrored or not, and plain numbers alone keep the current setting, as before.
- **UI:** the Margins menu ticks **Mirrored** when the document has mirror margins. Page Setup gets a **Mirror margins** check box under Pages, and the margin labels read Inside/Outside while it's checked. The new string falls back to English in the catalogs; the existing ones are reused.
- **Docs:** `docs/layout-parity.md` row, status line and revision history.

## Tests
- `tests_pages::inside_and_outside_floats_swap_sides_on_even_pages` puts s…

title: Accessibility: Windows Magnifier follows the caret onto a new line (#1119)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1119.

Windows Magnifier now follows the caret onto the new line when you press Enter (or Shift+Enter), instead of staying on the line above until a couple more letters are typed.

## Why it happened

Traced with Windows Magnifier (full screen, following the text cursor) against a local WordCraft build whose AccessKit Windows adapter logged every UI Automation call it answered. On each text-selection change Magnifier:

1. takes the selection (a degenerate range at the caret) and its bounding rectangles; a caret's box has no width, so it moves on;
2. extends the range over the character after the caret and takes that box;
3. if that has no width either, moves the range back over the two characters before the caret and takes theirs.

The canvas described a line's end mark (the paragraph mark, a line break) with no width. On the empty line Enter makes, the character after the caret is the paragraph mark, so step 2 found nothing and step 3 landed on the end of the line above. After one letter, step 3 spans the line above and the new one, so the view still stayed; it moved with the second letter, as the report says.

## Change

- `wordcraft_layout::para::PARA_MARK_WIDTH`: the paragraph mark's box, 5 pt, which `selection_rects` already highlights when a selection runs past a paragraph's end (its three `5.0` literals now use the constant), and `Line::mark_box()`, that box at the line's visual end.
- `a11y.rs`: the paragraph mark and line breaks take that box, so the character after the caret on an empty line has room, on that line, where the caret is drawn.

## Tests

- `a11y::tests::a_magnifier_finds_the_caret_on_an_empty_line`: after Enter, and between two Shift+Enter breaks, the character after the caret is the line's end mark, with a box that has width, starts at the drawn caret and lies on the caret's line. With the paragraph mark's width back at 0 it fails at Enter; with only line breaks' back at 0, at Shift+Enter.
- The #488 test's frame loop moved into a `d…

title: Fonts: the interface CJK fallback skips faces without outlines
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The interface CJK fallback has listed `/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc` as its last macOS candidate since #495. The skrifa crate reads glyph outlines only from the `glyf`, `CFF `, `CFF2` and `VARC` tables. On macOS 27.0.1 the 32 faces in that file have none of them and keep their outlines in Apple's `hvgl` table. `pick_face` counts coverage from each face's cmap alone. The file's first face maps all 1,114 CJK characters of the zh-hans and zh-hant catalogs. When no earlier candidate maps all of them, `find_ui_font` returns that face for a Chinese interface built without craft-fonts, and the interface would draw the characters it takes from that face as blank space.

On this Mac an earlier file maps every needed character: the `PingFang.ttc` asset for a Chinese interface and `ヒラギノ角ゴシック W3.ttc` for a Japanese one.

`pick_face` now skips a face with none of those four tables, and `find_ui_font` goes on to the next candidate. VectorCraft's font scan has the same check (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/781).

**Tests.** `ui_fallback::tests::skips_faces_without_outlines` renames the `glyf` table record of the bundled Source Sans 3 Regular to `hvgl` in memory. It checks that the face still maps `A`, that `pick_face` skips it, and that `find_ui_font` takes the next file. Without the check the test fails at `assert!(pick_face(&hvgl, &['A'], true).is_none())`. No font file is added.

The commands below ran on an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 27.0.1 and rustc 1.99.0. Unless a line says otherwise, `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` points at craft-fonts `8dcdacd`, and `freebsd.yml` pins the same commit.

title: Desktop: a window too big for its screen shrinks to fit when it opens (#1215)
author: rabis7575
body:
The first window could be bigger than the screen, so the end of the vertical scroll bar was out of reach: dragging the scroll bar stopped where the pointer met the screen's edge (#1215).

## Cause

The app asks for a 1440 × 920 pt window. eframe shrinks that start size to the monitor's size, but doesn't count the frame, the title bar or the taskbar, and Windows places a new window down and to the right of the screen's corner. On a laptop screen (1920 × 1080 at 125 % is 1536 × 864 pt) the window's bottom, with the end of the scroll bar and the status bar, was under the taskbar or past the screen's edge. WordCraft saves the window as it was (#23), so it opened that way on every launch.

The scroll bar itself works: in a headless `ui_shot` run on a 334-page document the thumb followed the pointer all the way to both ends, also with the pointer 4000 pt outside the window.

## Change

- `WindowGeometry::fit_on_monitor` (`crates/ui-egui/src/window_geometry.rs`): once the monitor size is known, a window that doesn't fit with 48 pt to spare on each side (for the taskbar, the Dock or a panel; egui reports only the monitor size) gets a smaller size, never below the minimum, and is centred. A window the system placed is on the primary monitor, so its position counts too (one that fits but reaches into the taskbar is only centred); a restored one may be on another monitor, so only its size counts. Maximized, full-screen and minimized windows are left alone.
- `App::logic` (`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`) sends `InnerSize` and `OuterPosition` on the frame that first knows the monitor, just before the existing off-screen check. With nothing restored, the default window (no position) is checked the same way.
- A unit test with real numbers: the laptop screen, Full HD, a large screen, a restored window on a second monitor, a fitted window on its next launch, a tiny screen, and the states that are left alone.
- Docs: `docs/hardware-parity.md` (displays row), `ROADMAP.md` progress log.…

title: Native macOS menu bar (#255)
author: tarpescu
body:
## What

WordCraft's macOS menu bar showed only the app name. This installs the Word-style menus (**WordCraft, File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Tools, Table, Window, Help**) on `NSApp` at start-up, each item running the same command the ribbon does.

- `apps/wordcraft/src/menu.rs` (new): the menu is plain data; `muda` (MIT/Apache-2.0) turns it into AppKit objects. Events are drained each frame and dispatched through `WordApp::run`.
- macOS only (Word on Windows has no system menu; Linux uses the in-window UI), with muda's gtk backend off.
- Items the keyboard already handles (clipboard, undo) carry no key equivalent, so a focused text box keeps Cmd+C, Cmd+V and the like. Quit goes through `file.close` — the save-first close path — not AppKit's immediate `terminate:`.

## Testing

title: Cut copies to the system clipboard from every control
author: tarpescu
body:
Fixes #1265 (audit M18).

## Bug

Cut deleted the selection but, on every path except the raw Cmd/Ctrl+X event, never wrote the system clipboard, so Paste re-inserted the previous copy (data loss). Each UI caller had to publish the clipboard itself, and only some did.

## Fix

Centralise publication in the one sink, `WordApp::run`/`execute`: `edit.copy` and `edit.cut` already return the taken text, so the actor that ran them - keyboard, ribbon, context menu, native macOS menu, command search, CLI/MCP - all reach it. The per-caller `copy_text` calls in `keys.rs`, `ribbon.rs` and `canvas.rs` are removed (headless runs have no `Context`, so nothing is written there).

## Regression (per the audit: one sink, all entry points)

- `cut_and_copy_reach_the_system_clipboard`: the generic dispatch every non-ribbon caller uses.
- `every_cut_entry_point_publishes_to_the_clipboard`: the ribbon button (`run_from_ribbon`) and a real `Event::Cut` through the app's key handling both reach the sink.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` - 363 passed, 2 ignored.

title: fix: remove dead-code unwrap_or magic string in percent_decode
author: ahutsunshin
body:
## Summary

Fix dead code in `percent_decode` by replacing `from_utf8(h).unwrap_or("zz")` with `.ok()` and let-chaining.

## Problem

The `unwrap_or("zz")` fallback in `percent_decode` was unreachable because `h` is always valid UTF-8 — it is sliced from a valid UTF-8 input string. The magic string `"zz"` existed only to let `u8::from_str_radix` fail, but this intent was opaque to readers.

## Solution

Replace the fallback with `let Some(hex) = std::str::from_utf8(h).ok()`, keeping the same let-chain guard style used throughout the rest of the function.

## Changes

- `crates/formats/src/model.rs`: simplify percent-decode hex parsing

title: fix: remove unreachable empty-string branch in open_bytes_with match
author: ahutsunshin
body:
## Summary

Remove an unreachable `| ""` match arm from the file format dispatch in `open_bytes_with`.

## Problem

The `match ext.as_str()` in `open_bytes_with` included `"txt" | "text" | ""`, but `ext.is_empty()` is already guarded above and routes to `open_by_content` before the match runs. The empty-string arm is dead code that misleads readers into thinking empty extensions fall through this path.

## Solution

Drop `| ""` from the match arm. Empty extensions continue to be handled correctly by the earlier guard.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/io.rs`: removed unreachable match alternative

title: security: use explicit u64 literal for 2 GB file size limit
author: ahutsunshin
body:
## Summary

Use an explicit `u64` literal for the 2 GB file size limit in `open_path_with`.

## Problem

The expression `2 << 30` relied on Rust's type inference to produce `u64`, but the naked literal `2` is typed as `i32`. While correct today (compared against `u64 meta.len()`), `2 << 30` sits exactly at `i32::MAX + 1`. If someone ever raised the limit, debug-mode builds would hit an integer overflow panic instead of the graceful error.

## Solution

Write `2u64 << 30` — explicit, self-documenting, and immune to the shift-depth trap.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/io.rs`: explicit `u64` literal for size check

title: refactor: deduplicate ZIP and OLE magic number constants in io.rs
author: ahutsunshin
body:
## Summary

Deduplicate ZIP and OLE magic number constants that were defined locally in two functions.

## Problem

Both `signature_contradicts` and `open_by_content` defined their own identical local `const ZIP` and `const OLE` arrays. Keeping the same bytes in two places creates a maintenance hazard — updating one without the other would silently break format detection.

## Solution

Hoist them to module-level `ZIP_SIG` and `OLE_SIG` with brief doc comments and let both functions reference the same constants.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/io.rs`: two module-level consts replace four local consts

title: perf: lowercase HTML tag names during collection to avoid double String allocation
author: ahutsunshin
body:
## Summary

Inline ASCII-lowercasing into the HTML tokenizer's tag-name iterator chain to eliminate duplicate String allocations.

## Problem

The HTML tokenizer collected tag names as raw-case strings into a `String`, then called `.to_ascii_lowercase()` which allocated a second `String` with a byte-by-byte copy. Every tag processed — both open and close — paid this double-allocation cost.

## Solution

Add `.map(|c| c.to_ascii_lowercase())` to the iterator chain before `.collect()`, then drop the redundant post-collection `.to_ascii_lowercase()`. One allocation per tag instead of two.

## Changes

- `crates/formats/src/html.rs`: close-tag and open-tag name collection

title: feat: add SVG and ICO MIME types to mime_of helper
author: ahutsunshin
body:
## Summary

Add SVG and ICO image extensions to the `mime_of` helper in the formats model.

## Problem

`mime_of` handled png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp but not SVG or ICO — two of the most common image formats for the web. Callers requesting `mime_of("svg")` received `application/octet-stream`, which can cause downstream data-URI or image-handling code to treat SVG as opaque binary.

## Solution

Add `"svg" => "image/svg+xml"` and `"ico" => "image/x-icon"` to the match.

## Changes

- `crates/formats/src/model.rs`: two new match arms

title: Proofing: check spelling off the UI thread and draw squiggles over the pages
author: ripdog
body:
## Summary

Spelling and grammar checks no longer run inside layout. Before this change, layout checked every paragraph while shaping it, and the squiggles were baked into the page display lists and rasters. Proofing settings and `dictionary_generation()` were part of layout's environment hash. So **Add to Dictionary**, **Ignore All** and turning Check Spelling as You Type on or off each cleared the whole layout cache and re-rendered every page on the UI thread. A Hunspell dictionary (Polish, Portuguese) also loaded synchronously the first time layout needed it.

Now:

- **`layout::proofing::check_document`** finds a document's issues (body, headers, footers, notes, text boxes; comments are left out) through a `ProofCache`. It only rechecks a paragraph when its text, run formatting, language, paragraph style, the style sheet's language and no-proof settings, the proofing options or the user dictionary changed.
- **`layout::display::proof_marks`** places issues along the laid-out lines, the way `page_display` draws text (turned table cells included; warped text boxes and turned Drawing Canvases get none). `page_display` no longer draws squiggles. `ParaLayout::issues`, `ParaEnv::proofing`, `LayoutOptions::{proofing, proof}` and the related layout-cache key entries are removed.
- **ui-egui** runs the check on a worker thread and paints the marks over each page, sized like the old 0.8 pt wave and double line and inked for dark pages:
  - Only one check is in flight at a time. While it runs, newer edits wait, and only the latest revision is copied.
  - The worker wakes the UI when it finishes.
  - Each paragraph's result carries a hash of the text it was found in. Marks from an earlier check stay on paragraphs that haven't changed, so typing doesn't blank every squiggle in the document, and they never land on edited text.
  - WASM has no threads, so it runs the same incremental check inside the frame.
- **Context menu:** right-click takes its issue from the background ch…

title: Fix Drop Cap button toggle
author: SyahrulBhudiF
body:
## Summary

The **Insert › Text › Drop Cap** ribbon button could apply a drop cap but could not remove one. A second click kept the paragraph at the default three-line drop cap.

This change makes a parameter-free `insert.dropCap` command behave as a toggle. It removes the drop cap when every selected paragraph already has one. It applies the default three-line drop cap otherwise. Explicit `lines` values remain setters. `lines: 0` removes the property.

- Ran `cargo xtask ci`. Formatting passed. The run stops at an existing unrelated Clippy failure in `crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs:465`, where `drop(run)` triggers `clippy::drop_non_drop`. The task does not touch that code.

title: Table Layout: the Cell Size boxes apply to the whole selection (#1242)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1242

## Cause

`table.rowHeight` and `table.columnWidth` (the Height and Width boxes under Table Layout › Cell Size) took the caret's cell with `cell(s)` and changed only its row / its grid column. With the whole table selected the caret sits in the last cell, so only the last row's height and the last column's width changed, as in the report. Other Table Layout commands already use `selected_cells`, which covers whole-cell selections (a column, a row, the table) and merged cells.

## Fix

Both commands now use `selected_cells(s)`: every row the selection covers gets the height (and rule), and every grid column its cells touch gets the width, in one edit (one Undo). `set_column_widths` clears the table's preferred width once and syncs the cell widths once. Without a selection spanning cells the selection is the caret's cell, so the old behaviour is unchanged. The command parameter text says so.

## Verified

New test `cell_size_boxes_apply_to_the_whole_selection` (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`), a 3×3 table:

| step | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| caret alone, height 20 | row 0 only | row 0 only |
| select table, height 40 | rows `[20, none, 40]` (only the last row changed) | `[40, 40, 40]` |
| select table, width 90 | last column only | `[90, 90, 90]`, every cell's width follows the grid |
| select column, width 70 | first column only | first column only |
| two Undos | | back to the state before the table edits |

It fails on `main` at the second step (`[Some(20.0), None, Some(40.0)]` vs `[Some(40.0); 3]`) and passes here. The existing `cell_size_boxes_set_row_height_and_column_width` still passes. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed

- The up/down arrows next to the Height box that the report also asks for are a UI addition; this PR is the selection bug.
- Table Properties (`table.properties`) still applies its row and column settings to the caret's row and column.

title: Persist Normal defaults and RTF formatting
author: SyahrulBhudiF
body:
Closes #1264

## Story

A new blank document did not have a durable, user-configurable Normal style. Formatting selected in one document was not carried into the next blank document, and RTF files could lose the intended Normal font when the declared default was monospaced. That made common defaults—such as Courier New 10 pt—unreliable across new documents and RTF round trips.

## What this PR solves

- Stores a Normal-style formatting preference in engine preferences: font family, font size, paragraph spacing before/after, and line spacing.
- Applies that preference whenever the desktop app creates a new blank document.
- Adds **File › Options** controls for those values, plus **Use this document’s Normal style** to copy the open document’s Normal style into the saved preference.
- Makes **Design › Set as Default** persist the current document’s Normal style instead of only changing its active design state.
- Ensures the RTF writer declares Normal’s resolved font and size both in the stylesheet and reset paragraphs.
- Stops discarding a monospaced RTF `\deff` font during import, preserving valid defaults such as Courier New.

## How it works

`Prefs` owns the persisted `DefaultFormatting` value. `Session::blank_document()` uses it to construct Normal for new documents. Both Options and Design actions dispatch through `file.options`, keeping the preference update in the engine command path rather than UI-only state.

On RTF export, the writer resolves the document Normal style and emits that font and point size as the default stylesheet style and after each `\pard\plain` reset. On import, the declared RTF default font remains eligible even when it is monospaced.

title: fix(ui): prevent options pane labels from overflowing (#1266)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## Problem

In File > Options, long pane names such as Russian `Специальные возможности` extend past the navigation row and across the divider into the settings column.

## Root cause

The navigation allocates a 170 x 30 point row, but `Painter::text` uses the parent UI's clip rectangle. Allocating a fixed row does not constrain the text's painting bounds.

## Fix

Paint each pane label with `ui.painter().with_clip_rect(r)`. egui intersects this rectangle with the parent painter's clip, so long translations remain within their own rows and retain the surrounding scroll area's clipping.

This follows the existing file-browser and content-control painting pattern. It preserves the 170 x 30 point allocation, fonts, inset, full-row click handling, hover and selected backgrounds, and the complete accessible name supplied by `WidgetInfo::selected`. Short labels remain fully visible. No translations, dependencies, fonts, document-engine code or file-format handling change.

## Regression tests

Two tests use the existing `egui_kittest` harness with the real Options page, English and Russian, 100% / 125% / 150% interface size, and 2x native display scaling:

- Check every navigation label's actual text painting bounds intersected with its renderer clip against its row, including selected and unselected Accessibility. Assert that the Russian galley really exceeds the row width, that General / Display / Save remain fully visible, and that AccessKit exposes full names and selection state.
- Click both ends of Display, Save, Accessibility and General rows; assert hover/selected background rectangles, selected pane state and the corresponding settings content.

title: Restrict Editing: filling in forms opens fillable content controls (#1077)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #1077.

## What

Documents protected with `w:edit="forms"` ("Filling in forms") previously refused **every** edit — a form document could be viewed but never filled in, which is its entire purpose. This PR extends the existing run-then-verify Restrict Editing pipeline with a second kind of editable hole: the interiors of fillable content controls.

- `check_before` gains a `"forms"` arm mirroring `"readOnly"`-with-exceptions: with ≥1 fillable control, commands run and `outside_unchanged` rolls back anything that changes content outside control interiors ("only the editable regions of this protected document can change").
- Fillability = the **innermost** enclosing control's `w:lock` (`Unlocked`/`SdtLocked` fill; `ContentLocked`/`SdtContentLocked` stay frozen). Innermost-wins, so a locked combo inside a fillable block control stays locked.
- Marker pairing is **per block list** (derived from `control_ranges`): orphan/unclosed/past-cap markers are protected content, never holes — malformed or hostile files stay conservative (never panic, never widen holes).
- `developer.properties` changes that alter locking (`lockEdit`/`lockDelete`) are refused while protection is enforced, like Word's "Stop Protection first"; other properties stay editable via CLI/MCP.
- `review.restrict` state reports `"formFields"` (every mode), and Find Next Region I Can Edit jumps between fillable controls; the pane button now shows for forms documents.
- Round-trip: `w:edit="forms"`, the password hash and filled values survive save/reopen; Stop Protection still demands the password; undo can't lift protection.

title: Styles gallery no longer empty for DOCX files without w:qFormat (#1238)
author: alehel
body:
Fixes #1238.

Before: a DOCX saved by LibreOffice opened with an empty Home › Styles gallery. LibreOffice writes `styles.xml` without `w:qFormat` on any style, and the reader took a missing `w:qFormat` as "not in the gallery" for every style.

After: when a styles part marks no style at all, the built-in styles it defines take their usual gallery places and order from WordCraft's built-in style sheet. A file style counts as built-in when it has the same type and the same id, or the same name ignoring case. The name match covers translated ids such as `berschrift2` named "heading 2"; the id match covers the default paragraph style, which the reader already renames to `Normal`. A file's own `w:uiPriority` wins over the built-in order. Custom (`w:customStyle`), unknown (LibreOffice's "Text Body", "Internet Link"…) and hidden styles stay out. Files that use `w:qFormat` anywhere, including `w:val="0"`, are read exactly as before.

The issue's sample now shows Normal, Heading 1, Title, Heading 2, Subtitle and Heading 3, with Title highlighted on the title (checked in a headless `ui_shot` screenshot and in the desktop app). Saving such a file writes `w:qFormat` for those styles, so Word's gallery shows them too.

Test: `styles_without_qformat_fill_the_gallery_from_builtins` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs` (a synthetic styles part, not the issue's file).

Checks run locally: workspace tests, `fmt`, assets, layers, and clippy on `wordcraft-docx`. Workspace clippy fails on main as well on this machine's toolchain (1.95), with `collapsible_match` in `crates/proof/src/affix.rs`. The wasm check didn't run because the target isn't installed here; the change uses only types that already build for wasm.

Not in this PR: the `.doc` reader never marks any style for the gallery, so `.doc` files probably open with an empty gallery too.

title: DOCX: render Word's text watermark from the headers (#1290)
author: tarpescu
body:
Fixes #1290.

## What

Word keeps its text watermark as a VML `v:shape` holding a `v:textpath` inside the headers (id `WaterMark`). WordCraft both dropped that shape on import and never emitted one on export, so `wordcraft-cli convert S08-documento-composto.docx out.pdf` showed no watermark, and saving a watermark to .docx lost it.

**Read:** the reader maps the first such shape in a header to the document's watermark (text from `v:textpath/@string`, font from `font-family`, colour from `fillcolor`, and a non-zero `rotation` means diagonal).

**Write:** the writer emits Word's watermark shape into every header part; a document with no header gets a default one for every section that lacks it. `Check Compatibility` no longer warns that watermarks aren't written.

## Testing

- `word_text_watermark_in_the_header_is_read` (fixtures.rs): text/font/colour/diagonal, a horizontal case, and no-watermark.
- `settings_core_theme_round_trip` (roundtrip.rs): a watermark now survives write + read (previously asserted the opposite).
- End to end: S08 -> PDF page 3 shows the grey diagonal `BOZZA`; S08 opened and saved then reopened still has it; a new document with a watermark saved to .docx and reopened draws it.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx`, `-p wordcraft-engine`, `-p wordcraft-pdf` all green.

title: fix: build with Rust 1.95 (the manifest advertised an impossible MSRV)
author: mute-09
body:
## What

`Cargo.toml` advertised `rust-version = "1.90"`, but the locked egui/eframe `0.36` crates and craft-libs require **Rust 1.95**, so a fresh checkout with an older stable did not build at all.

## Reproduction

```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft
cd wordcraft
cargo check -p wordcraft
```

Before (with rustc 1.93.1):

```
error: rustc 1.93.1 is not supported by the following packages:
  craft-print@0.1.0 requires rustc 1.95
  craft-ui@0.1.0 requires rustc 1.95
  ecolor@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  eframe@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  egui@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  ...
Either upgrade rustc or select compatible dependency versions ...
```

## Fix

- `rust-version = "1.95"` in the workspace manifest.
- Add `rust-toolchain.toml` pinning `1.95.0` with the `clippy` and `rustfmt` components, so `rustup` selects and installs the right toolchain on the first cargo command.
- README quick start notes the pinned toolchain.

## Verified

With the same rustup, after the change:

```sh
cargo check -p wordcraft              # ok
cargo build -p wordcraft              # ok
cargo run -p wordcraft -- --version   # wordcraft 0.6.1
cargo fmt --all -- --check            # clean
```

## Notes

- The exact `1.95.0` pin can be relaxed (for example `channel = "stable"`) if CI prefers; `cargo xtask ci` (clippy/rustfmt) works with the pinned components.
- This PR also adds the contributor entry for `@mute-09` (real name Muthiullah), at their request.

A picture (or shape) with **Wrap Text ▸ Behind Text** could not be dragged where it overlapped text — in the body or in a header/footer. Pressing it did nothing; only the arrow keys moved it, and only after it had been selected another way (for example the Selection Pane). Reported from the field (#82: *Can't move, resize, alter images*).

## Reproduction

1. `cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample`
2. Insert ▸ Header ▸ Blank (or double-click the header area).
3. Insert ▸ Pictures, then Layout ▸ Wrap Text ▸ **Behind Text** (or right-click ▸ Wrap Text ▸ Behind Text).
4. Move it so it overlaps the header text, then press it **where the text covers it** and drag.

**Before:** the picture does not move; only the arrow keys do, once it is selected.
**After:** the picture follows the pointer. A click **without** moving still places the caret in the overlapping text.

The same applies in the body. **In Front of Text** already worked and is covered by the same test.

## Root cause

The hit test deliberately lets body text win over an object behind it (`crates/layout/src/hit.rs`: *"objects behind the text only where there's no text"*), so `objects::pointer` never began a frame drag for a Behind Text object under text.

## Fix

- `grab_at` / `pointer` now treat a Behind Text **picture, shape or group** as a drag candidate even where text covers it, in body and header/footer stories (`behind_drag_at`).
- The press does **not** take the gesture at once: it becomes an object drag only after the pointer passes the drag threshold (`pending_behind`), so a plain click still places the text caret in the overlapping text.
- Text boxes are unchanged: their inside is their text, so only their border grabs them.

## Tests

Three `egui_kittest` UI tests drive real pointer events through the whole app:

- `floating_picture_can_be_dragged_in_front_of_or_behind_text`
- `floating_header_picture_can_be_dragged_in_front_of_or_behind_text`
- `behind_picture_dragged_over_text_witho…

title: Print: pin the native print test document date so the PDF comparison is stable (#987)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #987.

`native_ranges_and_parity_do_not_duplicate_spooler_copies` builds its expected PDF with `session.print_pdf(...)` and then submits the job, which builds the same PDF again. With no `created` core property on the document, `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` stamps each build with the wall clock, so whenever a second ticks over between the two builds the byte comparison fails on `CreationDate`/`ModDate` (and the document ID derived from them) — as seen once on Print (macos-latest) for #882.

The test now pins the document's `core.created` to `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` before printing (the issue's suggested fix, same precedent as `docx/tests/roundtrip.rs`), so both compared artefacts are deterministic. Test-only change: three lines, nothing else touched. No other test in the file shares the pattern — the expected-side `print_pdf` build appears only here; the other tests submit jobs without comparing two builds.

Validation:

- Reproduced the mechanism deterministically: with a forced 2-second gap between the two builds, the artefacts differed exactly as the issue describes (CreationDate/ModDate + derived `/ID` and XMP dates, same length); with the fix in place the same forced gap passes byte-identical. The gap was then removed; the committed diff contains only the fix.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --test native_print` run 10 consecutive times: all green (6 tests each run).
- `cargo fmt -p wordcraft-ui-egui -- --check` clean, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo xtask ci` green: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, assets, layers, wasm.

title: Word's text watermark in DOCX: drawn on screen and in the PDF, and kept on save (#1290)
author: mmazzieri
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @mmazzieri._

Fixes #1290. DOCX files with Word's text watermark (Design › Watermark) now show it on every page, on screen and in the PDF, and keep it when saved back to DOCX.

Word stores the watermark as a VML shape with a `v:textpath` in each header. `read_vml` dropped any `v:shape` without a picture or text box, so the watermark was lost. Headers and footers are now read with a flag on `StoryCtx`. In them, the shape becomes the document's existing watermark (`settings.watermark`), which the PDF and screen renderers already draw:
- text from `string`, capped at 200 characters like `design.watermark`;
- the font from the textpath's `font-family` (quotes stripped);
- the colour from `fillcolor`;
- semitransparent when `v:fill opacity` is below 1 (`.5`, `50%` and `32768f` forms);
- diagonal when the shape is turned.

The first watermark found wins, and the shape is consumed so nothing draws it twice.

Only Word's watermark shape counts: the `PowerPlusWaterMarkObject` id, or text positioned absolutely and centred on both axes. Other VML WordArt stays as before (dropped): a logo in a header, WordArt in the body, a textpath inside a text box, or `on="f"`.

**Writing it back (`crates/docx/src/write/watermark.rs`):**
- Every header part starts its first paragraph with a VML shape (ECMA-376 Part 4) carrying the text, font, fill colour, `v:fill opacity=".5"` when semitransparent and `rotation:315` when diagonal. It is centred on the margins, behind the text, with a `PowerPlusWaterMarkObject<N>` id so the reader takes it back as the watermark. Putting it in the first paragraph means headers gain no line; a header holding only a table takes it in the paragraph that follows the table.
- The shape type is our own geometry: a top and a bottom edge that the text is fitted between. With a single line as the path, Word loads the WordArt but draws nothing (found while checking in Word).
- A section whose pages would show no hea…

title: Insert Hyperlink: Link to › Place in This Document (#1234)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1234

Word's Insert Hyperlink dialog has a "Link to:" column with **Place in This Document**: the top of the document, the headings and the bookmarks. WordCraft's dialog only had an address field, although the document model already stores an internal link (`#bookmark`), Ctrl+click already follows it, and the DOCX reader and writer map it to `w:hyperlink w:anchor`. This adds the missing way to make one.

## What changed

Two commits for the feature plus the docs:

1. **Engine** (`insert.link`, `link.targets`, `edit.goto`)
   - `insert.link` takes `{"bookmark": name}`, `{"heading": block}` or `{"top": true}` besides `{"url"}`. A heading link makes (or reuses) the heading's hidden `_Toc` bookmark, the one Word and the TOC code already use, and links to it; `top` links to `#_top`, Word's built-in name. The text defaults to the bookmark name, the heading's text or "Top of the Document"; `text` overrides it. An unknown bookmark or a block that is not a heading is an error that changes nothing.
   - `link.targets` (read-only, labelled "Link" like `insert.link` so no new translation is needed) lists what a link can point to: `top`, the `headings` (body block, level, text, from the same entries as a table of contents) and the visible `bookmarks` (hidden ones, names starting with `_`, are left out, as in Word).
   - `edit.goto {"bookmark": "_top"}` moves the caret to the start of the document, so following such a link works.
2. **Dialog**: "Link to:" with Existing File or Web Page (the old dialog) and Place in This Document. The second tab reads `link.targets` once and shows "Top of the Document", "Headings" (indented by level) and "Bookmarks"; the text to display follows the choice until it is typed over; OK needs a choice.

## Verified

- New test `links_to_places_in_this_document` (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`): `link.targets` lists the top, both headings with their levels and the one visible bookmark; a bookmark link on a selection; a heading link at a caret inser…
