title: An empty .docx opens as a blank document that saves back to it (#1384)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1384

A zero-byte `.docx`, like the one File Explorer's **New › Microsoft Word Document** makes, couldn't be opened: WordCraft read it as a Word package, failed ("not a valid zip package"), and kept the untitled document it had, so Save asked for a name.

`file.open` now opens an empty file as a new blank document on the Normal template, the same one File › New gives (the region's paper, the editing language), and keeps its path, so Save writes the document back to that file. The same goes for an empty file handed over as bytes (the web's file picker). Files that aren't empty open as before; one that isn't a document still fails.

- `io::is_empty_file`: is the file at a path zero bytes long (inside the read roots; always false on the web, where files come as bytes).
- `cmd/file.rs`: `normal_document`, the Normal-template blank document `file.new` already built, now shared by `file.new` and `file.open`.
- Test `an_empty_file_opens_as_a_blank_document_saved_back_to_it`: opens a zero-byte `.docx` over an untitled draft, checks the path, paper and language, types, saves (no Save As), and reads the text back from that file; then the same file from the picker. Without the change `file.open` fails on the first step.

Every way of opening a file (command line, Open dialog, Recent, drag and drop, macOS open events) goes through `file.open`, so they all get this.

Tested on Linux: `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: feat(print): add orientation support and pass landscape options to spooler
author: emre-clk91
body:
### Summary
This PR adds page orientation support (`Auto`, `Portrait`, `Landscape`) to WordCraft's print interface and passes the corresponding orientation options down to the native spooler (CUPS).

### Motivation / Problem
When printing landscape documents (such as DOCX files configured with `<w:pgSz w:orient="landscape">`), WordCraft exported the document but did not communicate the orientation to the spooler. On CUPS/Linux systems, this resulted in landscape pages being fed as portrait, causing printers to scale/shrink the page into the upper half of the sheet and leaving the bottom half blank. Furthermore, there was no option in the `File > Print` menu to choose or verify page orientation.

### Changes
1. **`crates/ui-egui/src/print_page.rs`**:
   - Added `orientation` field (`auto`, `portrait`, `landscape`) to `PrintSettings`.
   - Added `Orientation` dropdown picker in the `File > Print` sidebar.
2. **`crates/ui-egui/src/printing.rs`**:
   - Updated `Submit` closure type to accept `options: Vec<(String, String)>`.
   - Added auto-orientation detection from layout (`first_page.w > first_page.h`).
   - Pushes `orientation-requested=4` and `landscape=true` for landscape, or `orientation-requested=3` for portrait.
   - Added `orientation` parameter support to `ui.printSubmit`.
3. **`apps/wordcraft/src/print.rs`**:
   - Passes `options` through to `craft_print::Job.options`.
4. **`crates/ui-egui/tests/native_print.rs`**:
   - Added `native_print_passes_orientation_options_to_spooler` unit test validating options for auto, landscape, and portrait modes.

### Verification
- Tested automated test suite (`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --test native_print`): 7/7 tests passed.
- Real-world verification on Linux (CUPS) with physical HP Color LaserJet CP1215 printer: landscape DOCX printed correctly across the full page without scaling issues.

title: Scripts can't close a document with unsaved changes without force (#1268)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1268

A `file.close` sent by a script or agent (control channel or MCP bridge) used to quit WordCraft straight away, losing unsaved edits. Scripts are never shown dialogs, so the app now answers with an error instead:

- On a document with unsaved changes, `file.close` returns an error saying so. Pass `"force": true` to discard the changes and close. Only boolean `true` counts as force; `"yes"` or `1` are refused.
- The check covers every form the control channel accepts: `engine.execute {"command": "file.close"}`, `command {"id": "file.close"}`, and the bare `{"method": "file.close"}`. MCP tools, including `batch`, go through `engine.execute`.
- A clean document closes as before. The user's own close (Cmd/Ctrl+W, the window's close button, Backstage) still shows Save / Don't Save / Cancel. The check sits only in `control::handle`.
- Headless sessions (`wordcraft-cli mcp` without `--connect`) never ask and never error, as before.
- Docs: `docs/control-protocol.md` and the `file.close` params doc describe `force`.

### Tests
- `programmatic_close_keeps_unsaved_work` and `programmatic_close_guard_covers_every_form` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`. Both failed before the change (the app quit) and pass now. `close_asks_before_quitting` stays green.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed on this commit.

### Review notes
An independent review pass caught that the bare `{"method": "file.close"}` form skipped the first version of the check. That is fixed here and re-reviewed.

Left for you to decide:
- `app.quit` (window control) still quits a document with unsaved changes without checking. It's an explicit quit request and outside this issue, so I didn't change it.

Minor follow-ups noted, not done:
- The guard matches the literal id `file.close`, so a future alias for it would need the same check.

title: Ask Agent: hand a selection and an instruction to your own agent over MCP
author: CouchRiv
body:
Select text, click Ask Agent, type what you want: the agent you already run on this machine **edits the document itself**, with WordCraft's own MCP tools (`execute`, `select_text`, `type_text`), and its progress and note show beside the selection.

- Your own agent: WordCraft calls no model, holds no API key, and needs no provider; any MCP client works.
- On the selection: chip floats beside the mini toolbar when an agent is present; disappears when you type or click elsewhere.
- Safe by default: requests require the window key, the port stays on 127.0.0.1, and size caps keep instruction/reply ≤4000 chars and selection ≤100 KB.

3. Select text; open Ask Agent via chip, Help › Agents › Ask Agent, context menu, or Ctrl+Shift+O.
4. Type an instruction (Enter sends, Up recalls the last); follow progress notes; read the answer.
5. Cancel anytime; the agent learns from its next reply ({cancelled: true}).

- Control channel (agent.listen/agent.reply) and MCP (wait_for_request/reply_to_request) run on connection threads, never the UI thread.

title: Styles gallery shows Word's quick styles for DOCX files that mark none, e.g. from LibreOffice (#1238)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1238

DOCX files written by LibreOffice mark no style with `w:qFormat`, and they have no `w:latentStyles`. WordCraft took that literally, so the Home › Styles gallery was empty. Word for Mac 16.113.4 shows its usual quick styles for the issue's sample file (Normal, No Spacing, Heading 1, Heading 2, Title, Subtitle…), and now WordCraft does too:

- When a file marks none of its styles for the gallery, the DOCX reader calls `StyleSheet::add_default_gallery` (`crates/doc/src/styles.rs`). It:
  - marks the file's built-in styles that match one of WordCraft's built-in quick styles (by id or name, case-insensitive) as quick, keeping their own priority when they have one;
  - adds the built-in quick styles the file lacks (No Spacing, Title, Subtitle…).
- It never overwrites a style the file already has by id or name, and never marks a custom style (`w:customStyle="1"`), so a custom "Title" stays out of the gallery and no built-in Title is added over it.
- Files that do mark gallery styles (Word's own) are unchanged.

### Tests
- `styles_without_qformat_get_the_default_gallery` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`) failed before the change (empty gallery) and passes now.
- Also added: `styles_with_qformat_keep_their_gallery`, a custom-"Title" case, and a doc unit test that includes a style matched by name only.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed. The last commit only moves a ROADMAP log row.

### Notes

title: Paragraph dialog: leave mixed formatting alone, apply as one undo step (#1346)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1346

Over several differently formatted paragraphs, the Paragraph dialog showed the caret paragraph's values, and OK gave them to every selected paragraph through `para.rtl`/`para.ltr`, `para.align` and `para.set`: untouched fields normalised, in three undo steps.

## What changes

- **Mixed values.** The dialog reads every selected paragraph (the paragraphs paragraph commands format, so whole-cell column selections too). A field they share shows as before. A field they differ in shows blank: number boxes empty (no unit either), Alignment empty, check boxes neither on nor off (`Mixed` to screen readers), no Direction picked. OK leaves it as each paragraph has it until the user sets it.
- **Only what changed, one undo step.** OK sends the fields that differ from what the dialog opened with, as a single `para.set`: one undo step, and Repeat repeats the whole dialog. The Asian Typography tab goes through the same command.
- **`para.set` takes `"onPage": {"align", "left", "right"}`.** These are the alignment and indents as seen on the page, which each paragraph turns into its own start and end once `props` (a `bidi` in it, say) is applied. A selection of right-to-left and left-to-right paragraphs gets each one's sides right in one command. A new direction alone still keeps the alignment and indents where the dialog shows them. Documented in `docs/mcp.md`.
- **Out-of-range values stay put.** The Spacing and Line spacing boxes no longer pull a value from the document that is outside their range (line spacing 6 in a 0.5–5 box) into range on the first frame. egui reports that as a change, so OK used to write it back.

Not observed in Word yet: here, clicking an in-between check box turns it on for all the selected paragraphs.

title: fix(geom): measurement parser rejects overflow to infinity during unit conversion (#1359)
author: krinry
body:
Fixes #1359

### Summary
`wordcraft_geom::parse_measure()` previously checked `v.is_finite()` on the parsed numerical string, but did not check whether the subsequent unit scaling multiplication (`v * k`, e.g. for inches `k = 72.0`) produced a finite result. For near-maximum finite floats, this multiplication overflows to `f32::INFINITY`, causing `parse_measure` to accept and return an infinite measurement.

### Changes
- In `crates/geom/src/lib.rs`, check that the scaled product `res = v * k` is finite (`res.is_finite()`), returning `None` on overflow.
- Added comprehensive regression tests in `crates/geom/src/lib.rs` covering large overflow values across units (`in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pi`, `li`, default units) and non-finite inputs.

### Quality gates
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-geom` passes (7 tests).
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-geom -- -D warnings` passes with 0 warnings.
- `cargo xtask layers` passes.
- `cargo xtask assets` passes.

title: xtask assets: fail when git ls-files fails, read raw NUL-separated paths (#1364)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1364

`cargo xtask assets` (part of `cargo xtask ci`) spawned `git ls-files` but never looked at its exit status. Outside a usable checkout, or on a git error, the empty output was read as "no files", so the attribution check passed with nothing checked.

- **A failed `git ls-files` is now an error.** A non-zero exit status fails the check, with git's own message.
- **Paths are read NUL-separated (`-z`).** Without `-z`, git quotes a name with non-ASCII letters (`"assets/\303\251.png"`). That name matched no file on disk, so such an asset was silently left out of the check. A newline in a name no longer splits it either.

## Tests

- `assets::tests::a_failed_file_listing_fails_the_check` runs the check in a temporary folder outside any checkout and expects the `git ls-files failed` error. It fails without the status check. If the temporary folder happens to be inside a checkout, the test returns early.
- `assets::tests::reads_raw_nul_separated_paths`: a non-ASCII name with a space, and empty output.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Linux.

title: Mouse wheel keeps scrolling while a text selection is being dragged (#1388)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1388.

Holding the left button to select text and turning the wheel did nothing, so a passage longer than one screen could only be selected by dragging to the window edge or in several steps.

**Cause:** the canvas only takes wheel input while `ui.ctx().dragged_id().is_none()` (`canvas.rs`, the `hovered` flag passed to the wheel and reading-mode handlers). A drag-select on the canvas is itself an egui drag, so the canvas ignored its own wheel input for the whole selection.

**Fix:** a small `wheel_hovered` helper: the pointer must still be over the canvas, and another widget's drag (a scrollbar, a ruler handle...) still owns the wheel, but the canvas's own drag-select (`CanvasState::drag_selecting`) no longer blocks it. The selection already re-hit-tests the pointer every frame while the button is held (the same path the edge auto-scroll from #688 uses), so it keeps growing as the content scrolls under the pointer.

**Tests:**
- `canvas::tests::wheel_scrolls_while_drag_selecting`: the helper's cases (no drag, drag-select, another widget's drag, pointer off the canvas).
- `tests::wheel_scrolls_the_view_while_drag_selecting` (frame-level, modelled on the #688 test): press on the page, drag to the middle of the view, turn the wheel; the view scrolls and the selection grows. Without the fix the view stays at 0.

title: Outline Promote, Demote, Move Up and Move Down add one undo step instead of two (#1363)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1363.

`outline.promote`, `outline.demote`, `outline.moveUp` and `outline.moveDown` run `para.promote` / `para.demote` / `para.moveUp` / `para.moveDown` through `Session::run`. Both the outer and the nested command are mutating, so each pushed its own undo checkpoint: one click added two undo steps, and the first Undo did nothing visible.

The four aliases now call a small `run_joined` helper in `outline.rs` that calls `Session::join_next_undo()` before the nested run, the same mechanism a drag already uses to fold its frames into one undo step. The outer command's checkpoint is the only one, so one action is one Undo. Error rollback is unchanged: `run` still snapshots and restores the whole undo stack around both commands.

The other nested runs in the engine (`draw.eraser`, `draw.inkToShape`, Apply Styles, `review.editor`, `outline.close`) come from pure commands, which add no checkpoint, so they already give one step and are not changed.

Test: `outline_aliases_add_one_undo_step` runs each of the four commands through `Session::run` and checks that the undo depth goes up by exactly one and that one Undo restores the previous document and selection. Without the fix the depth goes up by two.

title: Save preferences through a temporary file and log write failures (#1361)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1361.

`save_prefs` wrote `ui.json` in place with `fs::write` and threw away every error, so an interrupted or failed write could leave a truncated preferences file and nobody would know.

What changes (`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`):

- The new `write_prefs` helper writes to a sibling temporary file (`.ui.json.<pid>.tmp`) and renames it over `ui.json` only after the write succeeds. If anything fails, it removes the temporary file and leaves the old `ui.json` as it was. This is the same pattern `wordcraft_proof::save_user_dictionary` already uses for the custom dictionary.
- A failure to create the settings folder, to serialize, or to write/replace the file is now logged with `log::warn!`, like the other start-up and shutdown messages in `main.rs`, instead of being dropped.

How the issue's points are handled:

- **Non-atomic overwrite:** fixed with the temp file plus rename described above.
- **Discarded write failures:** now reported in the log. They are not shown in the UI. Prefs are saved when the window closes, so there is no window left to show a message in.
- **Several instances writing the same file:** not changed. Each save still replaces the whole file, and the last one to finish wins. The issue asks for a policy here (merge or single owner), and that is a design decision for maintainers, so it is left for a follow-up.

Test: `failed_preferences_write_keeps_the_old_file_and_reports_the_error` puts a directory on the temporary file's name, so the preparation step fails. It checks that `write_prefs` returns an error and that `ui.json` still holds its previous contents. The test also checks that a normal write replaces the file.

title: RTF import decodes Unicode escapes in font names (#1360)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1360.

The font-table branch of the RTF reader handled `\f`, `\fcharset` and `\cpg` and then returned for every other control word, so `\u` and `\uc` never reached the Unicode decoder. A font name written as `Caf\u233? Sans` came in as `Caf? Sans`: the character was lost and its fallback was kept. WordCraft's own RTF export writes non-ASCII font names this way, so its own files hit the bug as well.

The fix is the same one #435 made for metadata, bookmarks and field instructions:
- `\u` and `\uc` in the font table now go through the normal decoder. Decoded characters go to the font name through `ch()`, and the font controls work as before.
- `Dest::FontTbl` is added to the destinations where fallback control words are skipped, so a `\'hh` fallback is dropped too.

Test `unicode_escapes_in_font_names` checks a plain `?` fallback, a `\'e9` hex fallback, `\uc0` and `\uc2`. For each one it checks:
- the default font name,
- a body run set in a second Unicode-named font,
- an import → export → import round trip.

It fails on main.

title: MCP type_text reports a refused paragraph break instead of typing the next line (#1356)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1356.

With `paragraphs: true`, `type_text` stored the result of `text.newParagraph` and then, for a non-empty next line, overwrote it with the result of `text.insert` without looking at it first. When the paragraph break was refused, the next line was typed onto the end of the previous one and the tool reported success.

The loop now stops as soon as `text.newParagraph` fails, so the error is returned and nothing is typed after it. This matches the existing check after `text.insert` in the same loop, and the `execute` batch, which stops at the first failed command unless asked to keep going.

Test: `type_text_stops_at_a_refused_paragraph_break` in `crates/mcp/src/tests.rs` uses a backend that refuses `text.newParagraph` and accepts everything else. It checks that the tool returns `isError` with the backend's message, and that the only commands sent were the first `text.insert` and the refused `text.newParagraph`. Without the fix, the second line is inserted and the call reports success. Successful multiline typing is already covered by `agent_writes_a_formatted_document`.

title: Print to PDF and PNG export replace the file only after it is fully written (#1355)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1355.

`io::write_file` wrote with `std::fs::write`, which truncates the destination before writing. If the write then failed (disk full, interruption), the previous PDF or PNG was gone. Print to PDF (`file.printPdf`) and Export Page as PNG (`file.exportPng`) both write through this function.

`write_file` now calls `safe_save::write`, the function document saves already use through `io::save_path_with`. That function writes the bytes to an owned sibling temporary file, syncs it, and renames it over the destination. When it fails, the original file stays intact and only its own temporary file is removed. An existing destination keeps its permissions. The automation write-root check (`file_access::check_write`) still runs first, as before.

## Tests
- New `write_file_replaces_the_destination_instead_of_truncating_it` in `crates/engine/src/io/safe_save.rs`. It hard-links the destination, calls `io::write_file`, and checks that the destination has the new bytes, the hard link still has the old bytes, and no temporary file is left. Without the fix, `fs::write` truncates the shared inode, so the hard link shows the new bytes and the test fails.
- The failure cases (partial and complete preparation errors keep the original and leave no temporary file) are already covered by `partial_and_complete_preparation_failures_leave_original_and_no_owned_temp` on the same `safe_save` path.

## Docs
`docs/file-format-parity.md`: the "Native save-path guarantees" section now says that `io::write_file` uses the same path. Added a revision-history row.

Scope: only native builds. The wasm `write_file` already returns an error, and browsers save files through their own download path.

title: Restart Numbering keeps the list's own level definitions (#1351)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1351.

`Numbering::restart` built the new list instance from the abstract list only, so a list that defines some of its levels itself (Word's `w:lvlOverride/w:lvl`, e.g. from an imported .docx) lost its own number format, label text and indents on Restart Numbering, and its levels started again at the abstract list's start instead of their own.

- The new instance copies the source instance's `level_overrides`.
- The start overrides that Restart writes now come from each level's effective definition (`Numbering::level`), so a level the list defines itself restarts at its own start. Levels taken from the abstract list restart at the abstract start, as before. The source list's own start overrides are still reset, as before.

Both commands that call `Numbering::restart` (`para.restartNumbering` and `para.setNumberingValue`) now keep the list's own level definitions.

Test: `restart_keeps_the_list_s_own_level_definitions` gives a list its own level 0 (upper Roman, `Part %1`, custom indents, start 5), restarts it and checks the new list keeps that definition and labels its first item `Part V`. It fails on main. Round-trip of `level_overrides` through .docx is already covered by `list_level_overrides_round_trip`.

title: Document::delete_range checks both ends before editing, so an error leaves the document unchanged (#1350)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1350.

`Document::delete_range` trimmed the first paragraph before it looked at the second end. A valid start and a bad end (missing paragraph, offset past the end, offset inside a multi-byte character) returned `Err` with text already removed. A range that enters a table had the same problem the other way round: it cleared the cells first and failed on a bad start offset last.

Now both ends are checked up front: the paragraph must exist (`BadPath`) and the offset must be on a character boundary inside it (`BadOffset`, the same errors `Paragraph::delete` and `para_mut` already return). Nothing is edited until both checks pass. Once both ends are valid, the remaining steps cannot fail on input: the paragraphs in between are cleared over their full length, and markers are re-inserted at the end of the paragraph. The doc comment now says that an error leaves the document unchanged.

`Session::run` already rolls back failed commands, so the editor itself was safe. This change is for direct callers of the model API.

Test `delete_range_with_bad_end_leaves_document_unchanged` calls `delete_range` directly and checks that the text is unchanged after each `Err`:
- missing paragraph as the second end,
- offset past the end of the second paragraph,
- offset inside `é`,
- a range from body text into a table cell with a bad start offset (the cross-container path).

Without the fix, each of these cases leaves text deleted. Valid deletes are still covered by the existing `delete_multi`, `tables_in_paths` and `bad_positions_error` tests.

title: Deleting a comment also removes its header/text-box anchors and replies to replies (#1345)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1345.

`review.deleteComment` left two kinds of dangling data behind:

1. **Anchors outside the body.** `remove_anchors` walked only `StoryRef::Body`, so a comment anchored in a header, footer or text box lost its definition but kept its `CommentStart`/`CommentEnd` objects. It now walks the body and every part (`s.doc.parts`).
2. **Replies to replies.** Only direct replies (`parent == Some(id)`) were collected, while `review.reply` accepts any existing comment as the parent. A reply-to-reply survived with a deleted parent, along with its part. The command now collects the whole reply tree (breadth-first; ids already collected are skipped, so a malformed parent cycle from a loaded file can't loop).

Undo is unchanged: the command still runs as one undo step that snapshots the whole document, so Undo restores the comments, their parts and all anchors.

`all: true` already deleted every comment; it now also clears their non-body anchors.

### Test
`delete_comment_clears_header_anchors_and_nested_replies` (crates/engine/src/tests.rs): anchors a comment in a header, adds a reply and a reply to that reply, deletes the root through `review.deleteComment`, and checks that no comments, comment parts or header anchors are left. It then checks that Undo restores all three comments, the parts and both header anchors. Without the fix the reply-to-reply and the header anchors survive.

title: JSON open repairs hostile run lengths (#1337)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #1337.

- `Paragraph::normalize` sums run lengths with saturation (no overflow panic on `usize::MAX`), moves a run end that falls inside a multibyte character to the next boundary, and makes the runs cover the text exactly.
- `Document::normalize_runs` runs it over every paragraph in every story; `io::open_bytes_with` calls it for `.json`.
- Regression test `json_open_repairs_hostile_run_lengths`: split UTF-8 run, overflowing lengths, short coverage, no runs, surplus length.

Not covered: surplus/missing U+FFFC object markers vs `objects` (lookups already return `None`).

Checks: `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc -p wordcraft-engine`, fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`.

title: DOCX: cap the depth of header/footer parts that reference further headers/footers (#1322)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1322.

A paragraph's `w:sectPr` inside a header or footer can reference another header/footer part. `load_header_footer` reads that part with a fresh `StoryCtx` and `read_blocks(..., 0)`, so the XML depth limit restarts for every part. The `hf_by_path` memo stops cycles, but a chain of distinct parts (`header0 -> header1 -> ... -> headerN`) recursed once per part, bounded only by `MAX_PARTS` (50 000).

The reader now counts the header/footer parts being read (`hf_depth`) and stops following references once it reaches `MAX_HF_DEPTH` (4). A reference past the cap is skipped, the way references past `MAX_PARTS` already are. The rest of the document still loads. Header and footer reads are the only path where one part loads another. Notes, comments and note separators are read in flat loops from the main document, and a header reference inside them goes through the same capped function.

Word does not write section properties inside headers, so real documents never get near this cap.

Test: `malformed.rs::long_header_reference_chain_is_cut_off` builds a 60-part header chain. Without the fix it reads all 60 parts. With the fix it stops after 4, and the test checks for at most 8.

title: Convert Text to Table refuses to drop fields or a table in the selection (#1318)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1318.

`table.fromText` could lose content in two ways:

- **More than 63 fields in a row.** The column count was clamped to 63 and the fields past it were never written into the table, but the paragraph was still removed. The command now returns an error ("a table can have at most 63 columns") before it changes anything.
- **A table (or other non-paragraph block) between the selected paragraphs.** Only paragraphs were read into the new table, but every block in the range was removed, so the table in between disappeared. The command now returns "select only paragraphs to convert" instead. This matches the existing "select paragraphs to convert" error the command already gives for a selection that spans containers.

Both checks run before the first edit, so the document and the undo history stay as they were.

Not changed here: a selection that starts or ends partway through a paragraph still converts the whole paragraph (the same as Word), and inline objects and formatting are still flattened to plain text. Keeping formatting in the cells is a larger change, and I left it out of this fix.

Test: `convert_text_to_table_refuses_to_drop_content` builds a 64-field row and a paragraph, table, paragraph selection. It checks that both return an error and leave the body and undo depth unchanged. Without the fix, both conversions succeed and content is lost.

title: feat(ui): smooth fade and slide transitions when switching ribbon tabs (#1419)
author: Osaym
body:
Closes #1419

### Summary
When switching between ribbon tabs (e.g. Home, Insert, Draw, Layout, References, Review, View, etc.), the switch previously produced an abrupt cut. In Microsoft Word and modern office document editors, switching ribbon tabs features smooth and responsive transitions.

This pull request implements smooth fade and slide transitions when navigating between ribbon tabs, matching Microsoft Word's motion and feel.

### Key Changes
1. **Active Tab Indicator Glide**:
   - The accent-colored indicator bar underneath the active tab button glides smoothly between tabs across the tab strip (interpolating position and width over 160ms) using egui's `animate_value_with_time`.
2. **Directional Content Slide & Fade**:
   - When switching tabs, the ribbon panel content smoothly fades in (opacity 0.2 -> 1.0) with a subtle directional slide (16 pt -> 0 pt) using a cubic ease-out curve.
   - Moving forward (e.g., Home -> Insert) slides in from the right; moving backward (e.g., Insert -> Home) slides in from the left.
3. **Scroll Offset Reset**:
   - On tab switch, the horizontal scroll position resets so the newly activated tab is immediately viewable from its beginning.
4. **Accessibility & Test Support**:
   - Strictly respects `app.animations_on()` and `ui.style().animation_time`. When animations are turned off in settings or in headless test harnesses, switches complete instantaneously with 0 delay.
5. **Quality & Standards**:
   - 100% safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` preserved).
   - Zero panics (`clippy::unwrap_used`, `clippy::expect_used`).
   - Added unit test `ribbon_tab_switch_animation` verifying directional transitions.
   - Full `cargo xtask ci` suite passes all 6 gates (`fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `assets`, `layers`, `wasm`).

title: Layout: formats past 65,536 in one paragraph keep their own style (#1340)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1340

A paragraph's layout gives each distinct format (font, size, link, tracked change…) a `StyleRun`, and every cluster points at one by index. That index was a `u16` clamped to `u16::MAX` while the style was still appended, so from the 65,537th distinct format in a paragraph on, every new format got index 65,535: those runs drew with another run's font, size, link and tracked-change marking.

**Change** (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`): the style index is a `u32`, like the glyph ranges beside it: `Cluster::style`, `Line::hyphen`, `Label::style`, `LabelRun::style`, `RubyLayout::glyphs`, the builder's lookup table, `break_lines` and `hyphen_glyph`. The index is `u32::try_from(styles.len())`; a paragraph can't hold anywhere near `u32::MAX` distinct formats in memory. Every reader already goes through `styles.get(i as usize)` or compares indices with each other, so nothing outside `para.rs` changes.

Memory: `Cluster` grows from 56 to 64 bytes (alignment), about 5 MB more for a 300-page document. Narrowing `ClKind::Object(usize)` to `u32` would win those 8 bytes back; I left it out to keep this change to the index itself.

**Test** `formats_past_65536_in_a_paragraph_keep_their_own_style` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): one paragraph with 65,538 runs, each with its own link, alternating tracked deletion and two font sizes; every cluster's style must carry its own run's link, deletion and size. With the old clamped index it fails at the first run past the limit (run 65,535 drew with run 65,534's link, no deletion and 11 pt instead of 9 pt); it passes here.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (1923 tests).

title: Ribbon: tabs that do not fit go behind a >> menu instead of under the right cluster (#897)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #897.

The tab strip laid its tabs out left to right with nothing handling overflow, while Share, Editing and Comments are drawn right to left over the same row — so in any language whose tab names run longer than English, the last tabs (the contextual Table Design / Table Layout, Picture Format) were drawn underneath those buttons and unreachable: Polish at 1280 pt cut Help to "Pomo" and hid both table tabs (the issue's repro, confirmed here with `ui_shot` before starting).

Tabs that don't fit now go behind a "»" button at the end of the strip, just left of the Share/Editing/Comments cluster, following the issue's first suggestion:

- The right cluster's width is measured with the same formulas that draw it (`icon_text_button_with`'s size calculation, the Share pill's own measure, the same gaps), so the tabs stop exactly short of it — probe-verified pixel-identical in a live frame (measured 274.0/331.7 = drawn 274.0/331.7).
- Two passes: a strip where every tab fits reserves nothing, so English at 1280 keeps today's exact layout, with no "»" button at all. The second pass reserves the button's width only when the first pass overflowed. A tab may run into the cluster's outer button padding (a dead zone where nothing is drawn) without triggering the menu — that hair of slack is what keeps English's strip byte-stable.
- File and the active tab always stay on the strip. An active tab past the break is pinned to the strip's end (as browsers pin the active tab), with the prefix's last tabs moved into the menu to make room; File is never overflowed.
- Menu rows show the translated names, mark the active one, and switching tabs works from the menu; per-tab behaviour on strip tabs (keytips, hover, active underline, double-click collapse, Customize context menu) is unchanged. The overflow rows are mouse-first — no Alt keytips on them; strip keytips are unchanged, and Search Commands reaches every command.

{"id":"para.keepNext","params":"{}"}
{"id":"para.keepLines","params":"{}"}
{"id":"para.pageBreakBefore","params":"{}"}
{"id":"para.widowControl","params":"{}"}

```
{"id":"para.keepNext","params":"{\"value\"?: bool}"}
{"id":"para.keepLines","params":"{\"value\"?: bool}"}
{"id":"para.pageBreakBefore","params":"{\"value\"?: bool}"}
{"id":"para.widowControl","params":"{\"value\"?: bool}"}

title: Free part, list and comment ids after a file's largest ones (#1338)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1338

A document can carry any part, list and comment ids: a `.json` model or a `.docx` (`w:numId`, `w:abstractNumId`) can use `u32::MAX`. New ids were "largest + 1", so adding a comment, note, text box or list to such a document overflowed: a panic in debug builds (`attempt to add with overflow` at `Document::add_part` and `Numbering::add_list`, reproduced on `main`), a wrap to 0 in release, where it could replace part 0. `list.define` used `saturating_add` instead, so its new list took `u32::MAX` again and collided with the existing one, whose definition a paragraph could then pick up.

**Change**
- `wordcraft_doc::free_id(largest, used, min)`: one past the largest id (as before, so ids keep growing and nothing changes for ordinary documents); once that would pass `u32::MAX`, the lowest id from `min` that isn't taken; `None` when every id is taken.
- `Document::try_add_part` and `Numbering::try_add_list` / `try_add_levels` return `DocError::Invalid` when ids run out and add nothing (both list ids are picked before anything is pushed). `Numbering::restart` returns `None` then.
- `add_part` and `add_list` keep their signatures (about 150 callers, importers and tests among them) and use free ids too; if ids ever ran out, which takes more than `u32::MAX` parts or lists, more than memory holds, they add nothing and return 0, an id `free_id` never hands out (0 is "no list" for numbering).
- The commands that add parts and lists use the `try_` versions, so they fail with an error and `Session::run` puts the document back: `insert.textBox`, `insert.wordArt`, `references.footnote`/`endnote`, `review.newComment`, `review.reply`, `para.bullets`/`para.numbering`, list AutoFormat, `para.defineNumber` and `list.define`. Pasting text boxes (`adopt_text_box`) leaves the box without text, as it already does past its depth budget.
- Comment ids (`review.newComment`, `review.reply`) had the same `largest + 1` and use `free_id` too.

Not changed: `templates.rs` already uses `…

title: fix(geom): reject measurements that overflow to infinity in parse_measure (#1359)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #1359.

## Summary

`parse_measure` in `crates/geom/src/lib.rs` validated the parsed `f32` for finiteness but returned `v * k` unchecked, so a finite near-`f32::MAX` input in a scaled unit (inches, centimetres, picas, lines) overflowed to infinity during unit conversion and was accepted as an infinite measurement. The converted result is now checked for finiteness, and overflow is rejected with `None`, matching the existing parse-failure behaviour.

## Changes

- `crates/geom/src/lib.rs` (+31/−1): check the converted value with `is_finite()` before returning it, covering every scaled unit and the bare-number default unit, including negative overflow.
- Same file: new regression test `parse_measure_rejects_overflow_to_infinity` covering overflow in each scaled unit, plus large-but-finite results that must still be accepted.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-geom` — 8 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo check -p wordcraft-geom` — clean
- `cargo fmt -p wordcraft-geom -- --check` — clean

author: Nael-Nathanael

```
error: call to `std::mem::drop` with a value that does not implement `Drop`. Dropping such a type only extends its contained lifetimes
   --> crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs:465:9
    |
465 |         drop(run);
    |         ^^^^^^^^^
    |
note: argument has type `{closure@crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs:446:23: 446:33}`

title: Agents: approve MCP access to an already open document
author: m1ssha
body:
An external MCP client can request access to the document already open in WordCraft, including unsaved work. WordCraft asks **Allow / Deny** before reads or tracked edits. Normal launch needs no control flag or restart.

### User flow

1. Open **File → Options → Agents**, copy the reusable MCP configuration into the external client once, and explicitly enable connection requests. Discovery defaults off; its saved preference is separate from attachment approval. Some clients need a tool reload or new agent session; WordCraft stays open.
2. The agent discovers the intended document and requests attachment. The prompt marks the name as self-reported. Escape denies, pending requests expire without polling extending them, and **Deny and stop requests** disables discovery. A cooldown suppresses repeated prompts across client IDs.
3. Approval grants one client an independent selection and a host-reserved revision author. The agent reads the canonical guide/document, selects a target, edits and verifies; the user reviews and saves. A compact invitation is optional and contains no executable path or duplicated guide.
4. Listening, pending and connected states appear in the status bar. Disconnect/document replacement revokes the old attachment; a new attachment requires approval.

### Review fixes

- Accepted streams explicitly return to blocking mode, including legacy TCP. Authenticated idle connections remain open; partial input stays bounded. Reconnection before transmission is safe, and ambiguous delivery is never replayed.
- Live Windows TCP mutually authenticates app and bridge using HMAC-SHA256, bound to role, session/document and fresh client/server nonces. The raw key is never sent. Four pre-authentication slots with a three-second overall deadline are separate from sixteen authenticated slots. Legacy TCP authentication and private Unix IPC remain compatible.
- Discovery filters canonical JSON descriptors before limiting results and sweeps unchanged records with miss…

title: Page Setup: Justified vertical alignment (#1320)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1320

## What changed
Page Setup › Layout › Vertical alignment gets a **Justified** option. On a justified page the space left over is shared out evenly between the blocks, so the first line sits at the top margin and the last block reaches the bottom margin. This is now in the model, in DOCX (`w:vAlign w:val="both"`, read and written), in the `layout.verticalAlign` command (`justify`), and in the Page Setup dialog.

How Word behaves here was checked by hand in Word for Mac 16.113.4:
- A page that is only partly filled is spread out, and that includes the last page.
- A page that ends in a manual page break is spread out too. The paragraph holding the break counts as the last block. The page after it, holding a single paragraph, stays at the top.
- The last block's Spacing After is kept. With 72 pt after, the last paragraph sits about an inch above the bottom margin, and WordCraft matches that.
- Multi-column pages are not spread out; they stay at the top.

**Also fixed (existed before this PR):** in a document with several sections, the last page of each section was aligned with the *next* section's setting. That affected Center and Bottom as well. Each page now remembers the alignment of the section it started in.

## Tests
- `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`: `section_vertical_alignment_top_center_justify_bottom`, `a_sections_last_page_keeps_its_own_vertical_alignment` (failed before the section fix), `justified_page_keeps_the_last_paragraphs_space_after`, `justified_multi_column_pages_stay_at_the_top`

title: wordcraft --control checks its port (#1426)
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
`wordcraft --control` now checks the value after it. A missing port, a value that isn't a number, or a number outside 1–65535 prints an error that names it, and the app exits with status 2 without opening a window. Before, the value was silently dropped and the app started without the control channel. A bad value also overrode `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`, so the port set there was lost. A flag right after `--control`, such as `--sample` or `--version`, is now read as a flag instead of being taken as the port. Fixes #1426.

After (this branch, no display, `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT=7981` set):

```
$ wordcraft --control abc
wordcraft: --control needs a port number from 1 to 65535, got "abc"
exit 2
$ wordcraft --control 79811
wordcraft: --control needs a port number from 1 to 65535, got "79811"
exit 2
$ wordcraft --control
wordcraft: --control needs a port number from 1 to 65535
exit 2
$ wordcraft --control --sample
wordcraft: --control needs a port number from 1 to 65535
exit 2
$ wordcraft --control --version
wordcraft 0.6.1 (dev)
exit 0
```

Before, each of these went on to start the app. With no display it got as far as opening the window and failed there:

```
Error: WinitEventLoop(Os(OsError { … "neither WAYLAND_DISPLAY nor WAYLAND_SOCKET nor DISPLAY is set." }))
exit 1
```

`--control 0` is now an error as well. Port 0 made the server listen on a random port that nothing reported, so agents couldn't find it. When `--control` appears more than once, any bad one is an error, even if a later one is valid. In Windows release builds the app has no console, so the message isn't shown there, but the exit status is still 2. `--version` has the same limit.

This overlaps with #977: both PRs edit the same argument loop. The changes to `main.rs` merge cleanly; `ROADMAP.md` conflicts on its status line, the usual one-line fix. I merged the two branches locally: `wordcraft --control --help` prints the help and exits 0, and both PRs' tests pass.

Text beside a square-wrapped picture no longer gets split across the narrow strip between the picture and the right margin. title: DOCX: draw VML preset shapes such as Word's right arrow (#1377)
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
Fixes #1377.

Word documents can draw shapes in the older VML format, where a shape points to a numbered preset (`type="#_x0000_t13"` is the right arrow). WordCraft dropped those shapes, so on page 1 of the reporter's file the orange arrow beside "flusso del paziente dal triage al reparto" was missing. They now show with their fill, outline and size, and saving keeps them as regular DrawingML shapes.

Before (upstream/main):

![Page 1 before: only the text](https://github.com/Nael-Nathanael/wordcraft/blob/8663d398fb93533b7eb810434ee35c9e62397e93/before-page1.png?raw=true)

After (this branch):

![Page 1 after: the orange right arrow is drawn](https://github.com/Nael-Nathanael/wordcraft/blob/8663d398fb93533b7eb810434ee35c9e62397e93/after-page1.png?raw=true)

The red box marks the arrow's line. Both images come from `wordcraft-cli convert S03-immagini.docx out.pdf`, then `pdftoppm -r 80 -f 1 -l 1 -png`.

WordCraft draws a VML preset through the same table it uses for the DrawingML preset of the same shape. Rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, diamond, isosceles triangle, five-point star, right arrow, line and straight connector, heart, text box, and the flowchart process, decision and connector shapes come out exactly. Presets WordCraft has no shape for are drawn as the nearest one, as DrawingML presets already are: a left, up or down arrow as the arrow, a right triangle as the triangle, a callout as its box. WordArt text shapes and picture frames without a picture are still left out.

The preset number comes from the shape's `o:spt`, else from its `v:shapetype`, else from Word's shapetype id `_x0000_tNN`. Word writes each shapetype only once, at its first use, so later shapes can only be matched through that id. The numbers are the MSOSPT values in [MS-ODRAW] §2.4.24.

title: A file name that isn't valid Unicode no longer crashes wordcraft-cli or the app (#1440)
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
A file name that isn't valid Unicode, such as a Latin-1 `café.docx` (`caf\xe9.docx`), no longer crashes `wordcraft-cli` or the app. Both read `std::env::args()`, which panics on such an argument before looking at it. Fixes #1440.

The CLI now reads `args_os()`. Commands open their file under its real name: `convert`, `info`, `text`, `inspect` and `render` (first file argument), `zotero` (second) and `run --file`. Saving without a path (`--cmd file.save`) writes back to that file, not to a lossy copy. Any other argument that isn't valid Unicode is an error naming it, with exit 1. That includes output names: `file.save` and `file.exportPng` take their path as JSON text, so writing to such a name would mean changing those commands or repeating their save logic in the CLI. I left that out.

The app opens such a file too. `file.open` takes its path as text, but it also accepts the file's bytes under a name, which is how dropped files already open. The app reads the file, opens its bytes under the lossy name, and puts the real path on the session, so Save writes back to that file. A file it can't read is logged and skipped, the way a file that fails to open already is. One gap: a password-protected file opened this way asks for the password, and that second open names the document by the lossy name, so Save then writes a new file. A `--control` port that isn't valid Unicode is an error, with exit 2.

Before (`upstream/main` 159b84f):

```
$ wordcraft-cli info $'caf\xe9.docx'
thread 'main' panicked at …/library/std/src/env.rs:878:51:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "caf\xE9.docx"
exit 101

ERROR [main] wordcraft::logging: panic at /rustc/…/library/std/src/env.rs:878:51: called `…` on an `…` value: "caf\xE9.docx"
exit 101
```

After (`t/caf\xe9.txt` holds "Bonjour"):

```
$ wordcraft-cli info $'caf\xe9.docx'     # the issue's repro; no such file here
wordcraft-cli: caf�.docx: No such file or directory (os error 2…

title: Markdown import: unclosed backtick runs no longer make code spans and links rescan the text (#1336)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1336

Markdown import found the run of backticks that closes a code span by scanning the rest of the text (`find_backticks`). A run that nothing closes cost a scan to the end of the text, and a text can hold many of them, one per length. The link bracket scan (`matching_bracket`) repeated those searches for every `[` over them, outside its look-ahead budget. Runs of 1, 2, … 2000 backticks (2 MB) took seconds:

| Input (2 MB, release build) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| runs of 1…2000 backticks, none closed | 2.4 s | 59 ms |
| the same inside 8 nested `[` … `]` | 17.8 s | 55 ms |
| the same after one unclosed `[` | 3.8 s | 35 ms |

**Change** (`crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`): `tokenize` indexes the text's backtick runs once (`Backticks`: where runs start, by run length), and both code spans and `matching_bracket` look the closing run up with a binary search instead of scanning. Every lookup starts right after a whole run, so the runs it can find are the same maximal runs the old scan stepped through: what reads as a code span or a link is unchanged. The bracket scan's budget now covers all of its work, since a backtick lookup no longer reads ahead.

**Tests** (`crates/formats/src/tests.rs`):
- `unmatched_backtick_runs_take_linear_time`: the three inputs above through `import("md", …)`, each under 5 s, every backtick kept as text. It fails on main (17.8 s for the bracket case even in a release build).
- `code_spans_and_links_around_backticks_read_as_before`: an escaped backtick before a span, a span holding a shorter run, a run nothing closes, a `]` inside a code span in link text, and link text with a backtick nothing closes. It passes before and after the change.

The existing Markdown tests (round trips, fuzzing, hostile input) pass unchanged. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (1924 tests).

title: Picture Format › Crop: crop handles on the canvas
author: dkhlapov
body:
Adds crop handles on the canvas (docs/ui-parity.md row "Rotation handle, crop handles on canvas…").

## What changed
- **Picture Format › Size › Crop** (`ui.crop`) turns crop mode on and off for the selected picture.
- In crop mode, black crop handles replace the resize handles: L-shaped at the corners, short bars on the edges. They are drawn in code, with no image assets.
- Dragging a handle trims that side, or two sides from a corner. The visible part keeps its scale and stays where it is on the page. Dragging back out restores the cropped-away area, but never past the original edge.
- While cropping, the cropped-away part stays visible under a dark grey dim.
- Esc, Enter, a click outside the picture and the Crop button all leave crop mode and **keep** the crop. Esc during a drag cancels only that drag.
- One drag is one undo step. `picture.crop` takes optional `width`/`height` (pt) in the same edit. For a floating picture, the same edit also moves the frame by the trimmed amount, so the visible part stays in place.
- Flipped pictures: each handle trims the side you can see under it. The crop maths, the dimmed preview and the floating-picture shift all mirror the flip.
- The crop maths is a pure, unit-tested function (`crates/ui-egui/src/crop.rs`).

How Word behaves here was checked by hand in Word for Mac 16.113.4: the handle shapes, the dark-grey cropped-away area, the size and position kept when you trim, and all four ways out of crop mode keeping the crop.

## Limitations
- A rotated picture doesn't enter crop mode. You get a status message instead.
- Floating pictures stay in place only if they're placed by distance. Pictures placed by alignment (e.g. centred) are placed again by that alignment after the crop.
- An inline picture reflows with the text when you crop its left or top.
- Out of scope: Crop to Shape, aspect-ratio presets, Fill/Fit, moving the picture inside the crop frame, and cropping shapes.

title: Home › Font: a collapsed caret no longer means the whole word, and the Font box follows the text's script
author: YhSteven
body:
Fixes #1418.

Two defects around Home › Font and a collapsed caret, both measured against Word 2019 (Windows)
through its own ribbon handler (`CommandBars.ExecuteMso`) and through the properties its controls
bind to (`Selection.Font.Name`, `.Bold`).

### The caret sets what is typed next, not the word it sits in

With the caret inside a word, Word reads and sets the formatting at the insertion point only:
the text typed next takes it, and the word is left alone. WordCraft expanded the caret to the
whole word, so a word holding more than one font, size or weight blanked the Font box, the size
box and the Bold button, and clicking Bold (or picking a font or a size) reformatted that word.

`target` is now the selection alone; a collapsed caret falls into `apply`'s existing
pending-format branch, and `resolved` — which the ribbon reads — follows the insertion point.

### The Font box follows the script at the caret

Word's Font box shows, and sets, the font of the *script* at the caret: `Selection.Font.Name`
reports the East Asian font (`w:eastAsia`) for a CJK character and the Latin one for a Latin
character. The ribbon only ever looked at `font`, so the box read the Latin font with the caret
in Chinese, Japanese or Korean text.

`format.state` now says which of the two applies, as `fontScript`, and the ribbon and the mini
toolbar show and set that one. Which characters use the East Asian font is the shaper's own
predicate, so `layout::para`'s private `east_asian` becomes the public `uses_east_asian_font`
and is shared: whichever font draws the character is the font the box shows.

### Behavior changes worth calling out

- Picking a font while the caret is in CJK text now sets the East Asian font, which is what the
  box just showed. With the caret in Latin text nothing about that changed.
- A selection spanning a mix still reads blank, as Word reports it. For `fontScript` a selection
  goes by its **first character**, so a Latin-then-CJK selection answers `latin` — th…

title: Embed mode: WordcraftEmbed, TextIndex, decorations, read-only (Memento PR A)
author: cialanjcampbell-coder
body:
PR A of Memento's embedding contract (`docs/wordcraft-embed.md` in Memento): WordCraft runs on a canvas inside another web app, which owns the file. WordCraft-side docs: [`docs/embed.md`](docs/embed.md).

## What's in it
- **`wordcraft-web` is also a library** with `WordcraftEmbed` (wasm-bindgen, typed `.d.ts`): `start`, `open`, `save`, `isDirty`, `text`, `selection`, `select`, `setDecorations`, `setTheme`, `setReadOnly`, `on`, `destroy`. The trunk binary is unchanged. The handle and the eframe shell share the `WordApp` through a `RefCell`; a call that finds it borrowed gets a JS error, never a panic. Events fire in a microtask after the frame, so a callback can call straight back in.
- **Embed mode** (`WordApp::embedded`, `crates/ui-egui/src/embed.rs`): only the ribbon (no File tab or Share button) and the pages. No title bar, status bar, side panes, Backstage, Start screen or AutoSave. Save fires `save-shortcut` instead of saving; New, Open and Close are refused.
- **`TextIndex`** (`crates/engine/src/text_index.rs`): the body text (`\n` between paragraphs, `\t` between cells, fields as their results, tracked deletions left out), with UTF-16 offsets mapped to `Pos` and back.
- **Decorations**: painted beside the Reading Highlight, never saved. They're kept as offsets and carried over each edit by a text diff (`remap_ranges`). When a deletion could be read more than one way, the reading that keeps the passage whole wins.
- **Read-only** (`Session::read_only`): `Session::run` refuses `mutates` commands. It also takes back any pure command that changes the document anyway (Undo, Redo, Undo Actions, `file.encrypt`), since checking `mutates` alone would let Undo through. Opening another document is still allowed. Buttons for refused commands are greyed out.

## Known limitation
`open()` reports every file as `lossy: true` until the docx reader counts what it drops (PR B). Under the contract, Memento opens every file read-only until then.

title: Canvas: a redrawn page goes to egui as rendered, without a round trip through straight alpha
author: spiritbearlabs
body:
## Problem

Every time the canvas redraws a page (each keystroke on it, a zoom step, a page scrolled into view), the raster took a detour on its way to the texture:

1. `Rendered::to_straight()` cloned the page and un-premultiplied it.
2. `ColorImage::from_rgba_unmultiplied` premultiplied it again, pixel by pixel.

`Rendered` is premultiplied RGBA8 and so is egui's `Color32`, so the two steps cancel out. On a 1632×2112 px page they cost about half of the redraw.

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: a small `page_image` helper hands the raster over with `ColorImage::from_rgba_premultiplied`. One call site changes, the page redraw in `canvas::show`.

**Platforms:** all; nothing here is platform-specific. Measured on macOS.

## Test

`page_image_keeps_every_pixel_the_straight_alpha_round_trip_gave` compares the new path with the old one:

- every premultiplied pixel value there is (each channel from 0 up to its alpha, for each alpha: 32,896 pixels), and
- every page of the sample document, rendered with the canvas's own options.

Both come out identical.

## Measurement

Apple Silicon MacBook Pro, macOS 27, 120 Hz display at 2×, 100% zoom (a 1632×2112 px page), release build. Typing into the sample document through the control channel (`ui.text`, one character every 250 ms), medians.

Stages of one keystroke's redraw on page 1, from temporary timing prints around each stage (18 keystrokes before, 19 after):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `render_page` | 8.1 ms | 8.2 ms |
| `to_straight` | 3.5 ms | gone |
| to `ColorImage` | 5.1 ms | 2.9 ms |
| Canvas redraw (`renderMs`) | 17.2 ms | 11.4 ms |
| Whole frame (`frameMs`) | 19.6 ms | 14.2 ms |

On page 2, which is mostly empty, `renderMs` from `ui.inspect` goes from 13.0 to 7.5 ms (19 keystrokes each).

These are times inside the app. I did not measure key-to-screen latency, and I did not measure other platforms.

title: Markdown import: brackets no longer turn later links in the paragraph into plain text (#1452)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1452

Builds on #1446 (its commit is the first one here; once it is merged, only the second one remains).

Markdown import caps how far the link and image bracket scans may look ahead in one text (`scan_budget` in `tokenize`, 8 × the text length + 8 KB), so hostile input stays linear. The budget was charged more than the scans read, so ordinary paragraphs ran out of it and every later link became plain text:

| Paragraph | Links kept, before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Intervals [0, 1) and [docs](http://x.org)` (a `[` nothing closes takes the whole budget) | 0 of 1 | 1 of 1 |
| `[1] [2] … [12]`, 20 KB of words, then a link (every bracket pair is charged the rest of the text) | 0 of 1 | 1 of 1 |
| 60 links through 7.4 KB (every link is charged the rest of the text) | 10 of 60 | 60 of 60 |

**Change** (`crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`):
- `matching_bracket` keeps a stack of open brackets instead of a depth, and records in `known` every pair it closes and every `[` still open at the end of the text. A scan from any of those brackets would take the same path (the scan's state is only its position), so `tokenize` looks them up instead of scanning again; a lookup needs no budget.
- A scan that finds nothing costs the rest of the text from its `[` (what it read), not the whole budget.
- A link destination is read, and paid for, only when `(` follows the `]`. One that parses costs its own length; one that does not still costs the rest of the text, as before.

What reads as a link is otherwise unchanged: a recorded pair is the one a fresh scan would find.

**Tests** (`crates/formats/src/tests.rs`): `brackets_do_not_turn_later_links_into_text` covers the three paragraphs above; it fails without this change (run on #1446's branch, whose budget code is main's; the "before" column comes from there). The hostile-input tests (`hostile_importer_input_takes_linear_time`, `unmatched_backtick_runs_take_linear_time`) and the other Markdown tests pass unchanged. `cargo xtask ci` …

title: Equations: bound parser tree depth, escape \text in LaTeX, merge runs everywhere (#1456)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1456

One commit per finding, all in `crates/doc` (`math.rs`, `math_linear.rs`, `math_latex.rs`, `math_symbols.rs`).

## Root cause and changes

1. **Depth.** `MAX_DEPTH` bounds the parser's recursion, not the tree it builds: `x^1^1…`, `a/a/…`, `\sum\sum…` wrap the previous node once per operator, so the tree grows left-nested to thousands of levels and `clean`/`Clone`/`PartialEq`/`Drop`/serde recurse over it. New iterative `too_deep(&MNode)` (explicit stack, early exit, all node kinds). Wrapping an existing node (script base, numerator, accent base, limit base, `apply` base) is skipped when it is already 32 levels deep (`WRAP_DEPTH = MAX_DEPTH / 2`, because serde_json refuses input nested deeper than 128 containers and a node costs two). Linear: the operator stays as text. LaTeX: the operator is dropped, its operand kept. `nary_operands` no longer nests once per `\sum` past that depth (it was itself recursive per operator). Cost of a check is at most the size of the node, which the 20,000-char/token input caps bound.
2. **`\text{…}`.** Normal-text runs were written verbatim. They now escape `\ { } % $ # & _ ~` (backslash as `\backslash{}`). `\backslash` was not in the symbol table (so it also did not round-trip outside `\text`); it is now, and `raw_arg` ignores the empty `{}` after a control word. A `#` in normal text no longer numbers the equation (`parse_latex`, `has_number_mark`), otherwise `\text{#1}` could not round-trip.
3. **`merge_runs`** now recurses through `map_args` for every node kind.

## Tests and commands run
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc` (131 pass), `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout math`, `-p wordcraft-docx math`, `-p wordcraft-engine math` (pass), `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-doc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p wordcraft-doc --check`.
- New tests in `math.rs`: `deeply_chained_input_stays_shallow` (linear `x^1^1…` x9999, `a/a/…` x9999, accents, `┬`, `(a b)^1…`; LaTeX `x^1^1…`, `\sum` x5000, `\sin x^1…`; each parsed, cloned, compa…

title: Metafile: WMF object table without scanning, in-place shape ops, cropped DIB decode (#1463)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1463

## Root cause
- `Canvas::add_object(None, ..)` (WMF handle table, `MAX_OBJECTS` = 4096) scanned the table from index 0 for the first free slot on every `CREATE*` record; on a full table that is 4096 comparisons per record and the record count is not capped.
- `Canvas::shape` mapped the caller's `Vec<Op>` into a second `Vec<Op>`; `dib::decode` decoded the whole bitmap and `clip_blit` then copied the crop out.

## What changed (only `crates/metafile`)
1. Object table: a `BTreeSet` of free indices below the table length. A create takes the lowest one (`pop_first`), so the slot chosen is exactly the old "first free slot"; a create on a full table is O(1)/no scan; delete inserts the index; explicit EMF slots keep the set in step.
2. `Canvas::shape` now takes the `Vec<Op>` by value and maps it in place (all callers already owned the vector; the slice variant is gone).
3. `dib::decode_clip` replaces `decode` + `clip_blit`: the clip is computed first (shared `clip_rect`), and only the clipped rows and columns are decoded. Validation of the whole bitmap (header, size cap, palette, bits length) is unchanged, so every input that returned `None` before still does. `Rgba::bottom_up` was only read by the old `clip_blit` and is removed.
4. ROADMAP.md progress-log row.

## Measured
- 16 MB WMF, 1,004,096 CREATEPENINDIRECT records, `parse` only, release build, this machine: **about 1.0 s before, 9 ms after** (3 runs each: 1023/1017/953 ms vs 9/9/9 ms). The issue's 1.68 s was measured earlier on a different build; my before-number on this run is 1.0 s.
- The peak-memory figures in the issue are by reading, not measured. Not measured here either: the 2,000,000-point polygon and the 40-megapixel bitmap.

lost them in the TOC.

A side effect: when a `TOC n` style reserves a left tab stop for the number, the entry's only tab
lands on that stop instead of the right-aligned page tab, so a short entry gets its page number
right after the text and no dot leader.

## Fix
`toc_entries` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs`) walks the body's list counters in document
order, including paragraphs inside tables so the counts stay right, and puts the label and the
level's separator (tab, space or nothing, from `w:suff`) before the entry text, as Word writes it.
Bullets and unnumbered levels add nothing.

## Result
Repro from #1462 (`pdftotext -layout`):

```
main                                   this PR
Introduction ......... 1               1 Introduction ......... 1
   Scope ............. 1                  1.1 Scope ........... 1
   Terms ............. 1                  1.2 Terms ........... 1
Design ............... 1               2 Design ............... 1
   Overview .......... 1                  2.1 Overview ........ 1
```

## Testing

title: PDF: draw horizontal and vertical lines inside groups
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** a horizontal or vertical line inside a group is missing from the exported PDF, although the screen shows it. Word's documents use this for dividers inside grouped boxes (for example a line between two text blocks in an info box), so the PDF loses them.

**Cause:** such a line keeps a zero height or width in the group (`a:ext cy="0"`). `shape_path` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` returned `None` for every shape with `w <= 0 || h <= 0`, so the PDF export skipped it. The raster renderer has no such check, so the screen drew it. A floating line on its own was not affected, because `float_rect` gives it a 1 pt frame; connector presets (`straightConnector1` and the others) were not affected either, because they are drawn as paths. The affected shape is `prst="line"`, which Word also writes for its straight connectors (with `wps:cNvCnPr`).

**Fix:** lines (and connectors, for the frame-based fallback) may now be flat on one axis. Closed shapes still need an area, and a line without length is still skipped.

Found while converting generated letters to PDF with `wordcraft-cli convert`.

Reproduction: [`lines.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/lines.docx) (hand-written from the spec, no Word output), then `wordcraft-cli convert lines.docx out.pdf`: the red divider inside the grey group is missing on `main`.

![Before: the grey group without its divider. After: the red divider is drawn](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/blob/pr-assets/pdf-group-lines-before-after.png?raw=true)

Both images: `wordcraft-cli convert lines.docx out.pdf`, then `pdftoppm -r 100`. `lines.docx` is a hand-written fixture: a group (`wpg:wgp`) holding a rounded rectangle and a `prst="line"` shape with `a:ext cy="0"`.

Note: the 1 pt minimum in `float_rect` still draws a standalone horizontal line as a 1 pt diagonal; left alone here.

title: Shapes: rounded rectangles keep their own corner radius
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** every rounded rectangle is drawn with the same, large corner (16% of its shorter side), whatever corner the document gives it. Word's address and info boxes often use small corners (`adj` 3565, about 3.6%), so they come out visibly rounder than in Word, on screen and in the PDF.

**Cause:** a `roundRect`'s corner is its adjust value (`a:avLst/a:gd name="adj"`: the radius in 100000ths of the shorter side, ECMA-376 §20.1.10.56). The DOCX reader ignored it, and the renderer and the PDF export used a fixed 16%.

**Fix:**
- `ShapeExtra::corner` keeps the value, capped at 50000 (half the shorter side). `connector::corner_radius` gives the radius in points. Without a value the corner stays at 16%, as before.
- DOCX: read for `prst="roundRect"` only (presets drawn as rounded rectangles, like `wedgeRoundRectCallout`, keep the default), and written back as `<a:gd name="adj" fmla="val N"/>`.
- The corner is used on screen (`render::shape_path`), in the PDF (`pdf::shape_path`, including shadow, glow and soft-edge silhouettes) and for Tight/Through wrap outlines (`wrap::shape_outline`). `Draw::Shape` carries it.

Found while converting generated letters to PDF with `wordcraft-cli convert`.

Reproduction: [`round-rect.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/round-rect.docx) (hand-written from the spec, no Word output), then `wordcraft-cli convert round-rect.docx out.pdf`: on `main` all four boxes have the same corners.

![Before: four identical corners. After: adj 0 (square), 3565 (small), no adj (16%), 50000 (round ends)](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/blob/pr-assets/rounded-corners-before-after.png?raw=true)

Top to bottom: `adj` 0, 3565, none, 50000. Both images: `wordcraft-cli convert round-rect.docx out.pdf`, then `pdftoppm -r 72`. `round-rect.docx` is a hand-written fixture.

Notes:

title: Fields: PAGEREF in headers and footers shows its bookmark's page
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** a `PAGEREF` field in a header or footer shows the result stored in the file instead of the page its bookmark is on. Mail-merged letters use it for "Page X of Y", where Y is a `PAGEREF` to a bookmark at the end of each letter (each letter a section restarting at page 1), so every page of every letter shows the same stale total.

**Cause:** only `PAGE`, `NUMPAGES`, `SECTIONPAGES` and `SECTION` are computed during layout; `PAGEREF` is only updated by `references.updateFields`, and only in the body.

**Fix:** headers and footers are laid out after the body is paginated, so `layout_pass` now maps each body bookmark to the page it is placed on (`bookmark_pages`: its number and that page's number format; with two of the same name, the first in the document) just before `headers_footers`, and `field_text` resolves `PAGEREF` from it:
- A `\* format` switch wins over the page's format. `\p` (above/below), an unknown bookmark, and the body and the text boxes anchored in it (laid out before the map exists) keep the stored result.
- The map is only built when a header, footer or text box has a `PAGEREF`. Its hash is part of the page key of the paragraph cache, so a moved bookmark lays the footer out again.
- Like the page totals in headers and footers, page references are filled in after pagination: they don't make the body lay out again, and headers and footers are measured with the stored result.

Found while converting generated letters to PDF with `wordcraft-cli convert`.

Reproduction: [`pageref-footer.docx`](https://github.com/cyril265/wordcraft/raw/pr-assets/fixtures/pageref-footer.docx) (hand-written from the spec, no Word output: two letters of 3 and 2 pages, the stored result is 9), then `wordcraft-cli convert pageref-footer.docx out.pdf`:

branch: Page 1 of 3 | Page 2 of 3 | Page 3 of 3 | Page 1 of 2 | Page 2 of 2
```

title: Layout: PAGE fields on the later pages of a paragraph show their own page (#1352)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1352

## What was wrong
A paragraph's PAGE fields were all computed once, for the page the paragraph starts on. When a paragraph runs onto later pages, either through a page break inside it or because it is long, every PAGE field after the first page still showed the first page's number.

## What changed
- `crates/layout/src/fields.rs`: the field context can carry a per-offset page map, "from text offset X on, the field is on page P", plus `page_at(off)`. `para.rs` resolves each PAGE field from its own offset.
- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, in the `place_para_in_flow` fragment loop: when a paragraph with PAGE fields reaches a page other than the one its remaining lines were laid out for, it records `(resume offset, page)` and lays the paragraph out again with the same width, exclusions and label. It then continues from the line that starts at the resume offset.
  - Fields before the resume point keep their numbers, so earlier lines break the same way.
  - Lines after it re-break for the new number's width, as in the 9 → 10 case.
  - If the resume line is missing anyway, the old layout is kept.
- The map is a local variable. It is lent to the field context only during the paragraph's own re-layouts, so footnotes, text boxes and headers laid out in between never see it. The field context's page is also set to the current page for each piece of the paragraph, so a footnote referenced from page 2 of a split paragraph shows 2.
- The layout-cache key includes the map when one is lent, so a cached page-1 layout isn't reused.
- Bounded: at most `MAX_PAGE_RELAYS = 64` extra layouts per paragraph. Paragraphs without PAGE fields never lay out again; NUMPAGES-only paragraphs skip this too.

## Tests (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`), all failing before the fix
- `page_field_after_intra_paragraph_break_shows_its_page`: "A{PAGE}{page break}B{PAGE}" shows 1, then 2. Before: `[["1"], ["1"]]`.
- `page_field_in_a_split_paragraph_tail_shows_its_page`: a long paragraph that splits n…

title: Tables: a page break inside a vertical merge takes the merged cell's text along (#1485)
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #1485.

## Problem
`layout_table` laid out the whole of a vertically merged cell in the first row of the merge. When the table broke across pages between rows of the merge, the merged cell's text stayed on the first page, ran over the footer and off the page, and the merged cell was empty in the table's continuation. Word and LibreOffice continue the text on the next page.

## Fix
`crates/layout/src/table.rs`, `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`:
- **Content goes with its row.** In the second pass of `layout_table`, each item of a merged cell goes to the row of the merge it falls in (`Bands::put`), measured from that row's top: paragraph lines by the row their bottom is in (a paragraph is cut into line ranges), shading cut at the row edges, anything else by its top. Rows are placed one after another, so with no page break everything is drawn exactly where it was; a page break between the rows now takes the text along.
- **A line on a row edge.** A line that crosses the edge between two rows goes with the lower row and reaches a little above its top (up to a line height). On the same page that's where it belongs. When that row starts a page (under the repeated header rows), it would poke into the row above. `RowLayout` now records how many leading items are such carried content (`carried`) and how far it reaches above where a cell's text starts (`lead`). `place_table` calls `table::at_page_top` only for a row that moved to a new page whole: the carried content moves down by `lead`, so it starts at the cell's top margin like the row's other cells, and the row's height, shading, cell areas and borders grow by as much. Rows that don't start a page are never touched, so this changes nothing without a page break. A row split by `split_row` already keeps its continuation clear of the top.
- Turned text in a merged cell still moves as a whole (unchanged).
- **A row of the merge that splits.** Since #1177 `split_row` works cell by cell (`RowLayout::cells`). The carried content …

title: Word 365 cover pages: page-relative positions and freeforms drawn back to their start (#743)
author: benandez
body:
Follow-up to #743 / #843. With the original file from Word, the cover page still rendered blank on `main`. Two causes are fixed here:

- **Positions relative to the page.** Word 365 writes cover-page shape positions as `wp14:pctPosVOffset` inside `mc:AlternateContent` within `wp:anchor`; the Fallback holds the same position as `wp:posOffset`. `anchor_float` skipped the wrapper, so the shapes landed at the top of the column. The Fallback's offset is now read.
- **Freeforms drawn back to their start.** The cover's large panel is a `custGeom` path that returns to its first point without `a:close`. It was read as an open line, so with no outline it wasn't drawn, and the white title inside it disappeared with it. A path that ends where it started is now closed (filled), as in Word.

Test: `cover_page_relative_position_and_freeform_drawn_back_to_its_start` (crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs, before and after a save). Hand-written XML; it fails without the fix.

Checked locally: `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass. `cargo xtask ci` stops at clippy on Rust 1.98.1 with `clippy::drop_non_drop` at `crates/engine/src/ribbon.rs:465`. That's existing code this PR doesn't touch; `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Not covered: gradient fills on shapes. The panel's fill is `a:fillRef idx="1003"` (the theme's `a:bgFillStyleLst` gradient). It's drawn with the gradient's base colour as a solid and saved as solid. I'm happy to take that on as a follow-up.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Fix Replace All bypassing content-control locks
author: MMexicann
body:
Replace All could change text in content controls locked against editing, or remove controls locked against deletion, when Track Changes was off. It now checks every match with the existing control-lock rules before applying replacements; a refused batch leaves the document, selection, and undo history unchanged.

The batch reads the story's control ranges once and skips per-match checks when there are no controls. Regression tests cover tracked and untracked refusal, deletion locks, permitted text edits, and one-step Undo. The progress and parity documents record the fix.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed all six gates (formatting, full-workspace Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, assets, layering, and WASM). 1,924 tests passed; two existing tests were ignored. CLI smoke checks also verified lock refusal without saving an output file and a permitted replacement surviving DOCX save/reopen.
