title: fix(proof): classify each whitespace token once when checking spelling (#1335)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #1335

## Summary

`spelling_issue` found the whitespace-delimited token around every word by scanning backward and forward for whitespace, then classified that token as a web/e-mail address. Punctuation splits one token into many words, and each of them redid the scan — so a long whitespace-free paragraph of punctuation-separated words cost quadratic scanning in every public proofing entry point.

The token classification is now computed once per token and shared by all the words the token contains. Behaviour is unchanged: the same token boundaries, the same `://` / `@` / `www.` classification, and the same per-word dictionary checks.

## Changes

- `crates/proof/src/lib.rs` — the per-word scan is factored into `enclosing_token`, and a new `spelling_issues` batch helper caches the enclosing token's classification across consecutive words of the same token. All three callers (`check_spelling_with`, `check_spelling_in`, `check_text_with`) go through the helper, so the single-language and multilingual APIs are fixed alike.
- Two regression tests: `address_token_covers_every_word_split_out_of_it` (one classification shared by every word punctuation splits out of an address token, with `ignore_internet` on and off) and `spelling_scales_over_one_long_token` (2,000 punctuation-separated misspellings inside one whitespace-free token, one issue each, through `check_spelling`, `check_spelling_in`, `check_spelling_with` and `check_text`).

## Tests

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-proof` — 103 passed, 0 failed, including both new tests.
- `cargo fmt -p wordcraft-proof -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-proof --all-targets` — no warnings.

title: Layout: long tables keep one layout per cell and relayout without re-measuring
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #1491.

## Problem
With one long table (synthetic repro in #1491: 20 000 rows x 6 columns, table style), layout is slow and memory-hungry, and a relayout after typing one character elsewhere still takes most of a second. Profiling found three per-cell costs:
1. Table autofit (`column_content`) lays every cell paragraph out at an unbounded width through `Ctx::para_labelled`, so the cache keeps a second `ParaLayout` per cell that is only ever read for two numbers, and each pass walks all of them again.
2. `Key::table` is `hash_of(&format!("{t:?}"))` of the cell's `CellText`, done twice per cell paragraph on every pass, hits included.
3. `update_generated` adds the hidden `ListEntry` style even when there is no bibliography/index/TOA, which changes `env_hash`; the first layout after Update Fields misses every paragraph.

## Fix
- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`: `Ctx::para_labelled` is split into `para_key` / `para_env`; the new `Ctx::para_measured` uses the same key but keeps only the measured `(narrowest, widest)` in `LayoutCache::measures` (cleared and evicted with the layouts). `Ctx::table_key` memoises the `CellText` hash per pass (a document's tables only have a few region formats).
- `crates/layout/src/table.rs`: `blocks_content` measures through `para_measured`.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs`: `ListEntry` is added only when a generated list is rebuilt.

Output is unchanged: same keys, same layouts, same widths.

## Result
Release build, macOS 26.2 (Apple silicon), Session flow `select.all`, `references.updateFields`, `caret.docStart`, `references.updateToc`, `layout()`, then 5 x (`text.insert` + `layout()`). Synthetic table, 20 000 rows x 6 columns, 1053 pages:

| | main (159b84f) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `references.updateFields` | 4.1 s | 3.0 s |
| `references.updateToc` | 1.5 s | 0.52 s |
| relayout after one typed character | 730-790 ms | 260-315 ms |
| process RSS after layout | ~1.9-2.0 GB | ~1.3 GB |

author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1433

## What was wrong
Only the fixed list of paper sizes in Layout › Size was reachable from the UI. The engine command `layout.size` already took a width and height, but nothing exposed it.

## What changed

title: Dark page: highlights are dimmed so the text on them stays readable (#1252)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1252

## What was wrong
On a dark page (View › Switch Modes), every colour has its lightness inverted. Saturated highlight colours such as yellow have middle lightness, so they stayed bright, while the text on them turned white or light. That left white text on bright yellow, which can't be read.

## What changed
- **Highlights are drawn dimmed on a dark page**, keeping their hue. Yellow becomes a dark olive (#4A4A10), close to what Word for Mac 16.113.4 shows in Dark Mode with a dark page colour (checked by hand). The highlight and character-shading fill is marked as a text background in the display list (`Draw::Fill { text_bg }`), and the renderer maps it with the new `RenderOptions::ink_bg`.
- **Text on a highlight always reads.** Glyphs, underlines and strikethroughs on a highlight carry its colour (`text_bg: Option<Rgb>`). On a dark page, `ink_text` draws them in the lighter of their colour and its inversion. If that still falls below WCAG 4.5:1 against the dimmed highlight, it uses white. Pure blue on yellow was 1.34:1 with plain inversion.

- **Screen only.** Light pages, PDF export, printing and saved images don't change. The PDF writer ignores the new fields, and `dark` is only set by the on-screen canvas and previews. Text off a highlight keeps the existing inversion.

title: Native macOS menu bar
author: RiccardoTancredi
body:
## Native macOS menu bar

### What
A real macOS menu bar (**WordCraft, File, Edit, View, Go, Insert, Format, Tools, Window, Help**), built with `muda`. Menu labels follow the interface language, with Italian fallbacks for the few bar-only strings the catalogues lacked.

### Why
Adds the system menu bar macOS users expect, alongside the existing in-window menu.

### How it stays safe
- Every item runs through the **same path as the ribbon and keyboard** (`WordApp::run`), so "Save changes?" prompts, input dialogs and clipboard handling all apply. Commands that need input (table, link, symbol, export…) open the ribbon's own **dialog or Backstage page** instead of running with empty params — this also fixed menu entries that previously did nothing.
- Items carry **no key equivalents**: the keyboard and keymap are unchanged, so a menu never takes a key from a text field or the document.
- macOS-only (`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`); no `unsafe`.

### Tests
- Every menu item is exercised on a sample document: no command fails for want of parameters, and every dialog/Backstage page it names exists. Plus a registry check that every named command exists.

### Notes for maintainers
- Branched from `159b84f`; happy to rebase.
- New dependency: `muda` (macOS target only), reusing the tree's `objc2`/`objc2-app-kit`.

author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1269

## What was wrong
Every glyph on screen and in `render_page` was drawn from its outline, and glyphs with an empty outline were skipped. Colour emoji fonts store pictures or colour layers instead of outlines, so emoji were shaped (font fallback found the emoji font) but drawn as blank space:
- Noto Color Emoji uses CBDT bitmaps;
- Apple Color Emoji uses `sbix` bitmaps;
- Segoe UI Emoji uses COLR layers.

The PDF was fine because krilla draws colour glyphs itself.

## What changed
- **`crates/fonts/src/color.rs`** (new):
  - `FontFace::has_color_glyphs()` and `FontFace::color_glyph(gid, ppem)`, through skrifa, which the project already depends on.
  - COLR v0/v1 paint graphs become a flat, balanced list of draw operations: transforms, clips, layers with composite modes, and solid, linear, radial and sweep fills. Palette 0 is used, and the 0xFFFF entry takes the text colour.
  - Bitmap strikes (CBDT/sbix) are picked for the pixel size and placed in font units.
- **`crates/render/src/color_glyph.rs`** (new):

  - Bitmaps are drawn into their glyph box, and COLR operations are played into vello_cpu.

author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1374

**Builds on #1481 (#1352).** This branch contains #1481's three commits: two for #1352, plus the shared equation-number fix. Please merge #1481 first; after that, this PR's own diff is the two `#1374` commits.

## What was wrong
A paragraph was broken into lines once, in the column where it starts. Lines that continued into the next column, or onto the next page, were reused as they were, so they ran straight through a shape there. They also kept wrapping around a shape from the previous page that reached past the bottom of that page.

## What changed (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)

  - A relay is only used if the new layout has a line starting exactly at the resume offset, at the same height. Otherwise the old lines are kept.

- Page 2's lines no longer wrap around a page-1 shape that runs past the bottom of page 1. A new page clears the wrap areas, and Word limits a shape's wrap to its own page.
- **Equation numbers** (separate commit, also in #1481): re-laying out a paragraph no longer advances the automatic equation counter. A relaid paragraph used to give its equations numbers like (2), (5), (6) instead of (1), (2), (3).

title: ODT import: keep each section’s page properties (#1379)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1379

## What was wrong
ODT import used only the first master page's layout, for the whole document. The reporter's four-section file (portrait, then landscape with a page-number restart, then two columns, then portrait) became one portrait A4 section with one column. The landscape part, the columns and the restart were lost.

## What changed (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`, `model.rs`)
Following ODF 1.3:
- A paragraph or table whose style names a master page (`style:master-page-name`) starts a new next-page section. The section takes that master page's layout: size, orientation, margins, and columns when there is more than one.
  - The name can be inherited through parent paragraph styles, as LibreOffice does. The chain walk is capped at 16 steps and stops on cycles.
  - An explicit empty name stops the lookup.
  - At the very start of the body, it replaces the opening section rather than adding an empty one.
- `style:page-number` on that paragraph or table style restarts page numbering at that section. ODF applies it only together with a master page.
- A `text:section` with more than one column becomes a continuous section, with breaks before and after it, carrying its columns: count, gap and separator line.
- Files with a single master page convert exactly as before.
- Hostile input is bounded:
  - sections, master pages and page layouts are capped at 10,000;
  - columns, gaps and page numbers are clamped.
- `model::Para.section` is the same field that #1495 (RTF sections) adds, so the two PRs merge cleanly or with a trivial conflict.
- Headers and footers from master pages stay with #873, which reads them. `Pages.masters` is where its per-master-page headers would attach.

The reporter's Word 365 `.doc` file had three problems:
- cell shading was lost, so white header text was invisible on white;
- an extra empty sixth column appeared;
- a merged legend row was split.

## What changed (`crates/docbin/src/table.rs`)
- **Cell shading is read from every SHD record Word writes**, per [MS-DOC] §2.6.3, checked against Microsoft's public spec:
  - `sprmTDefTableShd`/`2nd`/`3rd` (0xD612/0xD616/0xD60C);
  - `sprmTDefTableShdRaw`/`Raw2nd`/`Raw3rd` (0xD670/0xD671/0xD672);
  - the older `sprmTDefTableShd80` (0xD609);
  - `sprmTSetShd`.
  
  Rules:
  - Later records win.
  - An "auto" entry clears the fill.
  - A nil entry in the Raw records keeps the table-style colour, as the spec says.
  - Each range covers its own 22 cells.
  - A clear-pattern Shd80 fill now shows its background colour, which is how Word 97-style files store plain fills.
- **No extra column:** the row-end mark is no longer counted as a cell when the row has its boundaries. Each table now gets its own grid; before, a table reused the previous table's.
  - This code is written to match open PR #1123 exactly (`row_end_only`, `def_table_edges`), with one added guard line against zero-cell rows, so the two PRs merge trivially.

A first-row-only grid, which I tried first, broke that case. So here the reporter's legend row is one shaded cell in the 5-column grid, without `gridSpan`, and gets its span once #1123 lands. On main it was two cells.

title: PDF export: Hebrew and Arabic text extracts in reading order (#1383)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1383

## What was wrong
The issue's diagnosis was the reverse of what happens. WordCraft wrote each right-to-left run's glyphs in **reading** order. PDF viewers (PDFium in Chrome and Edge, pdf.js, poppler) expect RTL text stored **left to right as drawn** and reverse it themselves, so they flipped our text: `שלום` came out as `םולש`, and Arabic came out reversed and split. krilla expects visual order too: it marks strictly reversed runs with `/ReversedChars` (PDF 32000 §14.8.2.3.3).

I checked this with real PDFium (pypdfium2, run locally only). On main, it printed exactly the broken text the reporter got.

| Variant (PDFium) | Hebrew | Arabic |
|---|---|---|
| main (reading order) | םולש םלוע | حرم با ب ملاعلا |
| /ActualText on the run | still reversed | worse |
| **visual order (this PR)** | **שלום עולם** | **مرحبا بالعالم** |

## What changed (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`)
- A run whose glyph x positions go backwards is written left to right as drawn.
  - Glyphs that share a text range form a cluster: a letter with its marks, or a lam-alef. Clusters are kept whole and in shaping order, and sorted by their leftmost x.
  - Each glyph's advance is the distance to the next drawn glyph, so nothing moves on the page.
  - Left-to-right runs are byte-identical to before.
- When a letter and its vowel marks are separate glyphs, each glyph maps to its own character, through the font's cmap with one leftover glyph allowed. Otherwise the cluster keeps its shared text. A viewer that reverses the word then reads the letter followed by its mark.
- The synthetic-italic slant origin uses the baseline most of the run's glyphs share.
- `/ActualText` was measured and rejected: krilla writes it only inside tagged spans, and PDFium handles it badly.
- Docs: `docs/file-format-parity.md` PDF export row, `docs/gaps.md` gap 16, and a `ROADMAP.md` progress-log entry, each with its status line and revision history.

author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1473

## What was wrong
All Caps runs, and the lowercase letters of Small Caps runs, are drawn with capital glyphs, but the PDF's text layer got the *source* (lowercase) text. krilla builds one ToUnicode entry per glyph from the first text that glyph was drawn with. So the capital-P glyph, first drawn for the `p` of a capped "period", mapped to `p` everywhere, including a later plain paragraph's real "P". The reporter's output:
```
EmploymEnt pEriod. your EmploymEnt will bEgin on thE datE bElow.
dirEct caps on thE run: mixEd casE words.
plain text, no caps: Employment period.
```

## What changed (layout side; `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` is untouched)
- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`:

  - **List labels** in a caps paragraph, so "a." is drawn and read back as "A.".
  - **Field results**, mapped per character wherever the capital keeps the same byte length, so the stored ranges stay valid.

title: Web: New/Open waits for Save before discarding the document (#1315)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1315

**Builds on #1465 (#1445).** This branch contains #1465's two commits, which make a failed save from the Save Changes prompt keep the document and bring the prompt back with the reason. Please merge #1465 first; after that, this PR's own diff is the two `#1315` commits.

## What was wrong
In the web app, Save from the "save changes?" prompt before New/Open started the browser's save picker and write in the background, and returned straight away. The New/Open then replaced the document at once. If the user cancelled the picker, or the write or close failed, the document and its undo history were already gone. Marking the new document dirty afterwards couldn't bring it back.

## What changed
- **`crates/ui-egui`**:
  - A new `async_saves` module tracks each picker save as a ticket that ends as Saved, Cancelled or Failed.
  - The prompt's New/Open is **held back** (`AwaitingSave`) together with the document's id and revision. It runs only when **all** of these are true:
    - the save reports Saved;
    - the document is still the same one, clean, and at the same revision;
    - no other save of that document is still unconfirmed.
  - On cancel or failure, the document stays open with its text, undo and dirty flag, and the prompt comes back with the reason. This reuses #1465's `save_failed`/`prompt_again` path. A cancel says "Saving {name} was cancelled…" rather than "Couldn't save".
  - While New/Open waits, the status bar says "Waiting for the save to finish…".
  - A result arriving after the document was replaced never touches the new one.
  - Desktop is unchanged: `async_saves` is `None` there.
- **`apps/wordcraft-web`**: picker saves report through those tickets, and a failed close counts as a failure. The old separate `PickerSaves` tracking is removed. The browser's leave-page warning still fires while a save is pending.

author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1348

> **Escape discards** a comment draft, as Word does: Word for Mac 16.113.4 throws the typed text away (checked by hand).

## What was wrong
Comment drafts in the Comments pane and the balloons were egui temp data keyed only by the comment id, and `commit_comment` removed the draft *before* running `review.editComment` and ignored the result. So:
- a refused edit lost the typed text;
- a new or opened document reusing the same comment id picked up stale text;

  - **Escape discards** the draft.
  - The fields are **read-only** where comments can't change.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`**: pending drafts are written before the user-path Save, Save As, Save as Template, Export PDF/PNG, Print, Share, Close, New and Open, so they count in the save decision.
  - If a draft is refused, Save, export and print still go ahead with the stored text, and the refusal is shown.
  - Close, New and Open treat the refused draft as an unsaved change and show the Save Changes prompt, where Don't Save drops it. Before this fix round, a refused draft could make the window impossible to close.
- **`crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs`**: `review.editComment` and `review.reply` report disabled when the document is protected as `readOnly` or `forms`.

title: Track Changes and content controls: table delete, Change Case and Unlink Fields respect them (#1329)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1329

## What was wrong
Four operations changed text directly, bypassing Track Changes and the content-control locks:
- Delete Table, Rows, Columns and Cells removed the structure;
- Change Case rewrote the letters;
- Unlink Fields replaced the field with its result.

So locked controls could be changed, and with Track Changes on, Reject All couldn't bring the original back.

## What changed (`crates/engine/src/cmd/`)
- **Content controls:**
  - Table deletes run the same `controls::check_delete` that Delete and Backspace use. A control locked against deletion inside the table, rows or cells, or locked content partly hit, refuses the command with no change.
  - A new `controls::check_edit` makes Change Case and Unlink refuse inside content locked against editing. Delete-locked controls allow them, because those keep the control.
- **Track Changes on:**
  - **Table deletes** (`table.rs`) work like Word for Mac 16.113.4, checked by hand: the cell text is marked deleted, using the same machinery as Delete, and the table structure stays. Rows, columns and cells do the same; the model has no row-level revision yet.

title: Document Inspector: find hidden text outside the body and from styles (#1344)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1344

## What was wrong
Inspect Document's hidden-text check (`file.inspect`) looked only at **body** runs whose **own** formatting said hidden. It missed:
- hidden text in headers, footers, footnotes and endnotes, comments and text boxes;
- text hidden through a character style, a paragraph style or the document defaults.

Remove All then left that text in the file while reporting success. That matters when a document is cleaned before sharing.

## What changed (`crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs`)
- **Finding:** every story is walked: the body and every part, including table cells. "Hidden" is decided from **effective** formatting (`resolve_char`: defaults → paragraph style → character style → direct), so text a direct format shows again stays visible.
  - Neighbouring hidden runs are reported as one piece.
  - Pieces made only of markers don't count.
- **Result:**
  - `found.hidden` lists `{story, part?, text}`, capped at 1000 entries, with `hiddenCount` and `truncated`.
  - `found.unsupported` lists:
    - objects kept verbatim from the source whose XML hides text;
    - tables whose **table style** hides text. These aren't resolved yet, so they're listed rather than claimed clean.
  - After a removal, `residual` lists anything still there, so a partial removal never looks like a clean success.
- **Removing (one undo step):**
  - Pieces are deleted last-first, directly in their paragraph, so even thousands of pieces stay fast.
  - A paragraph whose text and mark are both hidden is removed entirely. It's kept emptied, with its mark still hidden, when it's the last block of a story or cell, holds a section break or content-control markers, or sits between two tables (so the tables don't merge on reopen).
  - A hidden footnote or endnote reference is removed together with its note, which is reported in `removedNotes`.
  - The deletion is direct even under Track Changes, as before.

title: RTF: read and write tracked changes (insertions, deletions, authors, times)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Gap 19 in `docs/gaps.md` (RTF depth): RTF files now keep their tracked changes.

## What was wrong
RTF import skipped the author table (`\revtbl`) and ignored the revision words, so tracked insertions became ordinary text. **Tracked deletions reappeared as ordinary text too**, quietly corrupting the document. RTF export wrote no revisions.

## What changed
**`crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`**, following the RTF 1.9.1 "Revision Marks" section:
- **Import:**
  - The author table is read (Unicode names included), with index 0 as "Unknown".
  - `\revised` / `\deleted` with `\revauth`/`\revauthdel` and `\revdttm`/`\revdttmdel` become tracked insertions and deletions with their author and date. A run can be both inserted and deleted.
  - `\plain` resets the marks, because they're character properties; `\pard` doesn't.
- **Export:** `{\*\revtbl …}` is written when the document has tracked changes, plus the marks on each tracked run, so WordCraft → RTF → WordCraft keeps them.
- **DTTM ↔ ISO 8601:** validated (days per month, leap years) and limited to years 1900–2411, with the weekday computed. DTTM has no time zone or seconds; times are read and written as `Z`.
- **Hostile input:** the author table is capped at 10,000 names of at most 256 bytes. Bad or negative author indices become "Unknown". Impossible dates give no date.

**`crates/formats/src/model.rs`:**
- The shared flow formatting gains `ins`/`del` marks. Revisions are deduplicated by (kind, author, date) as the DOCX reader does, and headers and footers reuse the body's revisions.
- `from_doc` is unchanged, so TXT, MD, HTML, ODT and LaTeX output stays the same; a test pins this. RTF export uses a new `from_doc_tracked`.

**`crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs`:**
- Pasted RTF now carries revisions, so `adopt` adds the source's revisions to the target and remaps every index: runs, paragraph marks, paragraph formatting and numbering changes, and table, row and cell formatting changes.
- Pasted deleted text is never turned into …

title: ODT: read and write tracked changes (text:tracked-changes)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Gap 19 in `docs/gaps.md` (ODT depth): ODT files now keep their tracked changes.

**Builds on #1516 (RTF tracked changes).** This branch contains #1516's two commits and uses the same revision model. Please merge #1516 first; after that, this PR's own diff is the ODT commits.

## What was wrong
ODT import skipped `text:tracked-changes`. The deleted text stored in each change region was lost, and inserted text became plain text. Export wrote no change tracking.

## What changed
**`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`**, following ODF 1.3 Part 3 §5.5:
- **Import:**
  - Each `text:changed-region` gives its author and date.
  - Text between `text:change-start` and `text:change-end` becomes a tracked insertion.
  - At each `text:change` point, the region's deleted content is put back as tracked-deleted text. Deleted whole paragraphs keep their deleted paragraph marks, so Accept All and Reject All give the right paragraphs.
  - An insertion nested inside a deletion gives text that is both inserted and deleted.
  - An open body insertion doesn't leak onto deleted paragraph marks.
- **Export:** the tracked-changes regions are written with change-start/end for insertions, and a `text:change` point plus the region for deletions. Text that is both inserted and deleted is written as one deletion region with a nested insertion range.
  - `dc:date` is always written; the save time is used when a revision has no date.
  - Change marks may sit directly in the body or in table cells, which §5.5.7 allows.
- **Hostile input is bounded:** at most 10,000 regions and 64 open insertions; author and date capped at 256 characters; the first of any duplicate ids wins; each deletion is placed once.

**Shared model (`crates/formats/src/model.rs`), on top of #1516's:**
- `RevMark.id` keeps separate ODT regions as separate revisions. RTF leaves it empty and keeps merging by kind, author and date.

title: Draw: Ink to Shape recognises arrows
author: dkhlapov
body:
Gap 12 in `docs/gaps.md` (Draw / ink): Ink to Shape recognises arrows.

**WordCraft's own design.** Word for Mac 16.113.4 has no Ink to Shape at all (checked by hand), so there was nothing to observe. This extends WordCraft's own recogniser (#395) with its own geometry.

## What changed
- **`crates/engine/src/cmd/ink_shape.rs`:** `recognise` now finds single-stroke arrows: a straight shaft, then two barbs at the tip, drawn shaft-first or head-first.
  - **Tip:** the first point near the farthest distance from the start, then walked forward while the distance keeps growing, with 0.5 pt of jitter allowed. It lands on the real tip even with dense pen sampling or when the pen overshoots on the way back from the first barb.
  - **Shaft:** checked against its chord with the same 6% tolerance as lines, so bowed and wobbly hand-drawn shafts count.
  - **Head:** exactly two barbs on opposite sides. Each points back at 15–75° and is 5–50% of the shaft long. They must be of similar size, and the pen must return close to the tip between them.
  - V, checkmark, L, hook, Y, k, zigzag and a line with a scribble all stay ink; the hook gives `None`.
- **`draw.rs`:** an arrow becomes a straight connector with flips and an end arrowhead. That's how Insert › Shapes arrows are stored, so it saves to DOCX (`a:tailEnd`), draws on screen and in PDF, and can be moved like any connector.
- Not done:
  - two-stroke arrows, because the convert path handles each stroke separately;
  - arrows with a closed triangle head.
  
  Both are noted in gap 12.
- Docs:

title: fix(math): preserve equation text color on save/load (#1467)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Fixes #1467

## Problem
Custom color on math formulas are not being saved. After reloading files, equations default to black.

**Root cause:** Word files have no color setting for a whole equation, only for each piece of text inside it. The reader ignored these per-piece colors, and the writer always wrote back the original XML unchanged, so user color changes were lost.

## Solution
- **On load:** If every piece of text in an equation has the same color, lift it to the equation level and clear it from the pieces
- **On save:** Push the equation's color to every piece that has none of its own
- **Preservation:** Original OMML XML is still written unchanged until the user actually changes the color (keeps formatting the model can't represent)

## Changes (7 files, +128/−10)
- `crates/docx/src/read/math.rs`, `read/story.rs`: Lift uniform run colors to equation `CharProps`
- `crates/docx/src/write/math.rs`, `write/story.rs`: Push equation color to colorless runs
- `crates/doc/src/math_edit.rs`: Helper `each_run_mut` with recursion depth limit
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/equation.rs`: Two regression tests
  - `colour_survives_save_and_reopen`: Color, save, reload, reset to automatic
  - `imported_colour_keeps_source_omml_until_recoloured`: OMML preservation

## Testing
- ✅ Both new tests **fail without the fix** (verified by reverting docx changes)
- ✅ Both tests **pass with the fix**
- ✅ `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine`: 423 tests passed, 0 failed
- ✅ `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx -p wordcraft-doc`: all passed
- ✅ `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean on engine/docx/doc crates

## Code Review (Opus)
**APPROVED** - Fixes the reported issue. Tests prove the fix. AGENTS.MD compliant (no unwrap/panic, depth-limited recursion). Edge cases handled (mixed colors, theme colors). Minimal for correctness.

**Known limitations:**
- Only RGB colors saved; theme colors on equations → automatic (black) as before
- Equations with mixed piece colors keep them as-is (not merge…

title: Windows: mirror native title-bar buttons for RTL interfaces
author: talmidhon
body:
## Purpose

Make native Windows caption controls follow the resolved interface direction using `DWMWA_NONCLIENT_RTL_LAYOUT`. Windows continues to draw and handle Close, Maximize/Restore and Minimize.

This is separate from client-area RTL layout in #1479. It does not set `WS_EX_LAYOUTRTL`, mirror a GPU surface, transform input coordinates, alter document direction, or introduce a custom title bar.

## Implementation

- A Windows-only desktop module synchronizes DWM after interface-language resolution, on startup and direction changes.
- Initial LTR windows keep native defaults. Switching back from RTL applies `FALSE`.
- No `unsafe` is added or enabled. A pinned MIT-licensed WinSafe dependency provides typed DWM attributes and BOOL payloads. Its OS enumeration supplies a typed HWND on the UI thread; the module matches only the exact borrowed handle from eframe and applies the attribute immediately. It neither chooses by title/foreground window nor retains an HWND.
- An unchanged desired state makes no further native calls. Failure logs a warning once for that state, preserves usability, and may be retried on a direction or window change.
- Add explicit `LangInfo.rtl` / `Lang::is_rtl()` metadata. All 19 current catalogs remain LTR; no catalog, translation, font or default language is added. The private test fixture uses English labels.

### Overlap with #1479

The small direction-metadata contract is also present in #1479. It is included here so this PR can be reviewed against `main` without carrying that PR's client-layout diff. The two should share one contract whichever lands first; I can resolve the overlapping metadata edits accordingly. This PR does not depend on selecting a particular client-area mirroring implementation.

- Unit regressions cover untouched initial LTR, RTL/LTR transitions, deduplicat…

title: Proofing: Vietnamese text under the default English language gets no marks
author: haisondb35-blip
body:
## What this changes

A document typed in Vietnamese under the default editing language (en-US) was covered in red underlines, because every Vietnamese word was checked as English.

- **Proofing (`crates/proof/src/vi.rs`):** a paragraph that reads as Vietnamese is now treated like any language without proofing tools: no spelling or grammar marks. Word's automatic language detection behaves the same way. A paragraph counts as Vietnamese when its words use letters only Vietnamese has: the breve and horn letters, `đ`, `ĩ ũ`, the tone-marked vowels of Latin Extended Additional, or stacked combining marks. A Vietnamese name inside English text (`Nguyễn`) is no longer flagged either. French and Portuguese, which share `â ê ô`, are unaffected.
- **Hyphenation (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`):** automatic hyphenation leaves Vietnamese paragraphs and words whole, because single syllables never take a hyphen. The English patterns don't happen to split these words today; the guard keeps it that way.

## How it was verified

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout -p wordcraft-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout -p wordcraft-proof`: 340 passed

New tests:

- `proof::vi::tests::vietnamese_words`
- `proof::vi::tests::paragraphs`
- `proof::vi::tests::vietnamese_paragraphs_under_english_get_no_marks`
- `proof::vi::tests::english_keeps_its_marks_and_skips_vietnamese_names`
- `layout::tests::automatic_hyphenation_leaves_vietnamese_whole`

## Notes

- No new `unwrap`/`panic!` outside tests and no `unsafe`; no dependencies, assets or UI strings added.
- This is detection, not Vietnamese proofing: the text is left unmarked rather than checked. Real Vietnamese spelling would need an openly licensed dictionary (gap #8 in `docs/gaps.md`).

title: ODT and .doc import: pictures are read once, within their byte budget (#1334)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1334

**ODT** (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`): the pictures frames point at now go through a small `Pictures` budget (256 MB, as before):
- each entry is inflated at most once, however many frames point at it; later frames get a copy;
- an entry is inflated only when the size it declares fits in what is left, so a picture that doesn't fit is refused without inflating and costs nothing;
- the bytes inflated are charged even when an entry turns out bigger than it declared (reading stops one byte past what is left, which uses the budget up), and so is every later copy; once the budget is used up nothing is inflated;
- missing, unreadable and over-budget entries are remembered and not looked up again.

Before, every frame inflated its entry again and the total was checked after inflating, so frames after the budget was used up, or on an entry that didn't fit, kept inflating (up to 256 MB each). While a file is parsed the budget keeps one copy of each entry it read, dropped when parsing ends.

**DOC** (`crates/docbin/src/media.rs`): inline pictures remember failures as well as successes (as the BLIP store lookup already did), raw picture bytes are copied only when they fit in what is left of the cap, an inline shape's BLIP is decoded against what is left instead of the whole cap, and nothing is read once the cap is used up.

The reader's `Body` and the type of its picture callback are unchanged, so the other open PRs editing `odt.rs` merge as before.

**Tests**
- `docbin`: `rejected_inline_pictures_are_not_read_again` — a picture over a small cap isn't read again at the same place (without the fix the second lookup reads it again and takes what it holds now), a rejected picture costs nothing, anchors sharing a picture share it, filling the cap exactly works and nothing new is read after.

title: macOS: ⌘ arrows go to line and document ends, ⌘⌫ and the ⌃ keys work as in Mac text views (#954)
author: kkilchrist
body:
Fixes #954. Part of #1555.

On macOS, `Mod` is ⌘, so WordCraft's Windows-style Ctrl+← (word left) became ⌘←. Every Mac text view uses ⌘← for line start instead. This PR maps the Mac text keys before the keymap, with the canvas focused, on macOS only:

title: Comments: deleting a comment leaves no dangling anchors or replies (#1345)
author: squaredcow
body:
## #1345: deleting a comment leaves no dangling anchors or replies

Fixes #1345. `review.deleteComment` had two gaps:
- It removed comment anchors from the body only. A comment in a header, footer, note or text box kept its `CommentStart`/`CommentEnd` after the comment was gone, and the text stayed tinted as commented.
- It deleted only direct replies. In a thread root → reply → reply to the reply, the last one survived with its parent gone. It stayed in the Comments pane and was written to `comments.xml` on save.

Now:
- Anchors are removed from every story: the body and every part (headers, footers, notes, text boxes).
- Delete takes the whole thread below the comment. The thread comes from a parent-to-replies map built once, with a seen set. A parent cycle from a hostile file ends the walk, and a long reply chain isn't quadratic: 50,000 replies took 11 s with a per-reply scan and take under 0.1 s now.
- Undo restores the comments, their text and their anchors.

**Before and after** (headless `ui_shot`, 1440×900; the same script run on `main` at 159b84f and on this branch):

| Scenario | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Type body text, Insert › Header "Header text", select it, New Comment, Delete it, move the caret | Pane empty, but **"Header text" stays tinted as commented** | Pane empty, header text plain |
| 2. Select "quick", New Comment, Reply, Reply to that reply, Delete the root, Save as .docx | `deleted: [0, 1]`; **"Reply to the reply" stays in the pane** and in `word/comments.xml` | `deleted: [0, 1, 2]`; pane empty; no comment parts in the .docx |
| 3. Cmd+Z after either delete | Thread restored | All comments and anchors restored |

The saved .docx for scenario 1 is clean on both builds: the writer already skips anchors without a comment, so the stale anchors only showed in the open document.

title: fix(formats): preserve leading whitespace in markdown escape_line_start
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary
In crates/formats/src/markdown.rs, escape_line_start previously shadowed s with let s = s.trim_start().to_string();. Because s was already trimmed, lead = s.len() - t.len() always evaluated to 0. This caused leading whitespace to be stripped from paragraphs and quotes during Markdown export.

### Fix
- Changed escape_line_start to bind let t = s.trim_start(); without shadowing s, so lead accurately measures leading indentation and preserves it when emitting markdown.
- Added regression test escape_line_start_preserves_indentation.
- Added contributor entry in contributors/people.toml per AGENTS.md guidelines.

title: fix(engine): handle multi-byte UTF-8 characters before em-dash in dash_autoformat
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary
In crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:189, dash_autoformat checked the character preceding -- using  efore.trim_end().get(i - 1..i).

When -- is preceded by a multi-byte UTF-8 character (e.g. café--word ), i - 1 falls into the middle of the preceding character byte sequence. Because i - 1 is not a UTF-8 character boundary, str::get(i - 1..i) returned None, causing em-dash conversion to silently fail.

### Fix
- Replaced the byte slice check with  efore.trim_end()[..i].chars().next_back().is_some_and(|c| c != ' '). Since i is the offset of ASCII --, ..i is guaranteed to be a valid UTF-8 boundary, and .chars().next_back() safely inspects the preceding Unicode character.
- Updated regression tests in crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs to verify em-dash autoformatting following multi-byte UTF-8 characters (café--g  -> café—g ).

title: fix(engine): trim arguments when parsing sample text formulas
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:418`, `sample_text` parsed formula parameters (e.g. `=rand(2, 4)` or `=lorem(3, 2)`) using `arg.parse::<usize>()` without trimming whitespace.

When spaces were present after the comma (standard in Word, e.g. `=rand(2, 4)`), `" 4".parse::<usize>()` failed, causing `counts` to be `None` and silently falling back to default counts `(5, 3)` instead of expanding the requested number of paragraphs and sentences.

### Fix
- Changed `arg.parse::<usize>()` to `arg.trim().parse::<usize>()` in `sample_text`.
- Added test cases with parameter whitespace to `sample_text_formulas_expand_on_enter` in `crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs`.

title: .doc import: notes, headers and text boxes read their text once (#1319)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1319

The legacy `.doc` reader turns each story range of a subdocument into a part of its own. Each range only had to run forwards, so a story table that steps back to an earlier CP after every story pointed many stories at the same text, and each one was walked and stored again: 2,000 footnote references over `[0, 10, 0, 10, …]` made 1,001 copies of the footnote subdocument. The header/footer (`Plcfhdd`) and text box (`PlcftxbxTxt`) story tables had the same shape, so they get the same rule.

**Fix**: the CPs of a well-formed PLC ascend, so its stories are disjoint. In each story table, a story that starts before the end of the last one kept is now dropped:
- footnotes and endnotes (`notes::parse_notes`): that reference gets no note;
- headers and footers (`sections::header_stories`): the slot is left empty, so it is linked to the previous section's header or footer, as an empty slot already was;
- text boxes (`drawing::textbox_stories`): the box keeps its shape, without text.

Each range is still clamped to its own subdocument, so every subdocument CP ends up in at most one story. All the stories together never hold more than the text the file stores, so the total is bounded by the file itself and needs no separate counter. Ranges in order, including adjacent ones and empty header slots, are read exactly as before.

`lib.rs` is not touched, so this merges cleanly with the open PRs that edit it. The document-wide character cap proposed in #1235 would still fit on top as a second limit.

**Tests** (public `.doc` import of synthetic files; each fails without the fix):
- `note_stories_pointing_at_the_same_text_are_read_once`: 2,000 footnote references over `[0, 10, 0, 10, …]` give one footnote part (before: 1,001).
- `note_stories_stepping_back_are_dropped_and_ordered_ones_kept`: `[0, 5, 10, 3, 10]` for footnotes and endnotes. The two stories in order are read (the control); the backwards and overlapping ones are dropped (before: two extra notes holding copies…

title: Layout: widow control moves a three-line paragraph whole

body:
With widow/orphan control on, a three-line paragraph that had room for two of its lines at the bottom of a page was split two and one, leaving a widow. Taking one more line along would leave an orphan, so Word moves the paragraph whole; this does the same. title: Flat OPC: reading bounded everywhere in the file, CDATA base64 read (#1353)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1353

The Word XML Document (Flat OPC) reader in `crates/docx/src/flat.rs` counted only what it kept. A repeated or nameless part, a child of `pkg:package` that isn't a part, and anything nested inside one were read without being counted. Nesting had no cap. A part's inline XML was copied before its size was checked. Separately, base64 in `pkg:binaryData` was taken only from plain text events, so CDATA and character references were dropped: a picture written that way silently lost bytes.

**Fix** (all in `flat.rs`):
- **Nesting**: at most `3 + xml::MAX_DEPTH + 1` levels. That is the package, part and data elements, then as deep as the XML tree reader takes a part's own XML: `MAX_DEPTH` open elements and an empty one inside the deepest. So a part the tree reader accepts is never refused here (a unit test checks both readers at the boundary). Deep nesting outside any part is now an error instead of being skipped.
- **Part count**: every child of the package counts against `MAX_ENTRIES`, whether it is a part or not and whether its name repeats or not. Before, only the unique parts that were stored counted.
- **Elements**: each child of the package holds at most `2 + xml::MAX_ELEMENTS` elements. That is the part, its data element and the tree reader's per-part limit, so parts that nothing reads are bounded too.
- **Sizes**: every part's data counts against `MAX_PART` and `MAX_TOTAL`, including a repeated or empty name (as a repeated zip entry does). A repeated part still isn't stored, and the first one still wins. Inline XML is checked against what is left before it is copied. Base64 text is checked before each piece of text is appended, against what is left of both limits, not only the per-part one.
- **Binary data**: CDATA is read like text, and a character reference stands for its character (`A` is `A`, `
` is whitespace and skipped). A named entity can't be base64, so in binary data it is now an "invalid base64 data" error instead of vanishing.

title: All Caps draws ß as SS, as Word does (#1581)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1581

## What was wrong
With All Caps or Small Caps on, the shaper turned each character into exactly one capital (`to_uppercase().next()`), so `ß` drew as a single `S`: "Straße" showed as **STRASE**. Word shows **STRASSE**. Other letters whose capital is longer were cut short too, such as `ǰ`, `ŉ` and `ΐ`.

## What changed (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`, `shape_with`)
- A caps or small-caps segment that holds a letter whose capital is several characters (`caps_expands`) is shaped from a display string with the **full** capital, so ß becomes SS. This reuses the existing numeral-substitution mapping (`mapped`, `map_starts`, `orig_of`).
- Cluster starts are cut back to document-character starts, so both S glyphs share one cluster covering the ß. The caret, selection, hit-testing, line breaking and hyphenation all still see one character: you can't put the caret, or break a line, between the two S.
- Small caps scales both glyphs.
- Runs in a symbol font never expand.
- Segments without such letters take the old path unchanged.
- No indexing; the display text grows by at most 3 characters per character.
- Docs: a new caps row in `docs/layout-parity.md` and a `ROADMAP.md` progress-log entry, each with its status line and revision history.

## Tests (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`)

title: Italian proofing: po', qual è, È and un/un' grammar rules; more elisions in spelling
author: lupant
body:
Follow-up to the Italian proofing in #1090: grammar rules for the most common Italian slips, and fewer false spelling marks on elided and truncated words.

## Grammar (`crates/proof/src/it/grammar.rs`): rules that work with no dictionary installed

| Wrong | Fix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `un pò`, `un po` | `un po'` | `Po` (the river) is left alone |
| `qual'è`, `Qual’era` | `qual è`, `Qual era` | a truncation, never elided |
| `E' vero` | `È vero` | a quoted letter (`'E'`) is left alone |
| `un'altro`, `un'anno` | `un altro`, `un anno` | feminine `auto`, `eco` excepted |
| `un altra`, `nessun amica` | `un'altra`, `nessun'amica` | also `ciascun`, `qualcun`, `alcun` |

Gender comes from the ending and the rules stay quiet when unsure. They skip masculine and common-gender words in `-a` (`-ista`, `-ita`, `-ota`, `-cida`, `-ma`, `-eta`, `atleta`, `acrobata`…) and capitalized names. More emphatic doubles are allowed too: `pian piano`, `poco poco`, `così così`, `zitto zitto`.

## Spelling (`crates/proof/src/it/mod.rs`)

- More elisions check the word after the apostrophe: `dov'è`, `cos'è`, `com'è`, `anch'io`, `senz'altro`, `tutt'uno`, `nessun'altra`, `n'ha`…
- Truncations `po'`, `mo'`, `be'` are accepted. `words()` trims the trailing apostrophe, so spelling only sees `po`; the grammar rule checks that the apostrophe is there.
- `pò` and `qual'è` are left to the grammar rules, which give a clearer message and the fix, so the word isn't marked twice.

## Tests

- New tests for every rule.
- Proptests on the Italian grammar (any text, Italian-like text) and on Italian suggestions.
- `ProofLang::It` added to the mixed-span proptest, which was missing it.
- `docs/localization-parity.md` updated, including the stale line "No Italian proofing yet".

Checked: `cargo test -p wordcraft-proof` passes (127 tests), `clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. The engine's Italian, Polish and Portuguese review-command tests and `hostile_params_never_panic` pass. I didn't run…

title: Respect the image byte limit during DOC DIB conversion
author: haranishi
body:
Apply the caller's image byte limit to the BMP header, decoder allocation limit, and PNG output when converting DIB images from Word 97–2003 `.doc` files. Previously, the DIB payload alone was compared with the limit, so the additional 14-byte BMP header and encoded PNG could exceed it.

PNG writes are bounded by the limit, with a fallback to BMP when that BMP fits. A one-pixel synthetic regression case checks rejection at 57 bytes, BMP preservation at 58 bytes, and normal PNG conversion at 512 bytes. The same test was confirmed to fail before the fix. Large-scale resource consumption was not measured.

Related: #1334 and #1554. Repeated image reads and failure caching are already covered by #1554, so this PR is limited to the internal DIB conversion budget. The scope was also compared with the metafile-side DIB changes in #1466.

This branch uses the existing CI regression fix in #1578 (`2ab578c`) as its base. That fix is not reimplemented. Its prerequisite changes appear in the comparison until #1578 lands on main.

Validation:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all six gates passed (fmt, Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, wasm). Linux with Liberation and craft-fonts: 2,022 passed, zero failed, two tests ignored by default.
- All 68 docbin tests passed, including the new 57/58/512-byte regression and existing DIB/metafile, placement, crop, and alternative-text cases.
- Independent agent diff and public-content reviews found no issues. Four ordinary image tests also passed in a separate isolated verification of the identical four-file fix.
- [Fork Printing CI](https://github.com/haranishi/wordcraft/actions/runs/38538038190) at `7ab83cd`: all three jobs passed (Linux, Windows, and macOS app/UI checks, plus the Linux wasm check).

title: Text boxes in tables nested deeper than 16 survive edits (#1339)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1339

The model's paragraph walk, `each_para` / `each_para_mut` in `crates/doc/src/edit.rs`, stopped 16 tables down. A .docx opens with tables nested up to 24 deep, and pasting can nest them further. Text box pruning (`Document::prune_text_boxes`, run after every successful edit) finds the boxes still shown with that walk, so a box shown only from deeper than 16 counted as shown nowhere: the next unrelated edit dropped its story, and saving lost its text. The same walk decides which boxes a copy takes along and which pasted shapes get stories of their own, and it serves reading order, the next drawing id, note conversion and the content-control check.

**Fix** (only `edit.rs`): the walk keeps its own stack instead of recursing, so it reaches every paragraph however deep tables nest, in the same document order, with no call stack to run out of. A walk that stops early can't decide what is unreachable, so the walk is complete rather than bounded-and-careful. A block that is a paragraph still goes straight to `f` without allocating. The signature is unchanged (`depth` is now unused, and the doc comment says so), so every caller builds as before.

Not changed here: `para_paths`, plain text, word count and style renaming keep their 16-level limit. They leave deeper content out of a list, a count or an export, but never delete anything.

**Tests** (each fails without the fix, checked against `main` with only the new tests):
- `engine/src/tests.rs::text_box_in_a_table_nested_seventeen_deep_survives_an_edit_and_a_save` (the test from the issue): a box shown only from a table nested 17 deep, written to and opened from a .docx, keeps its story, reference and text through an unrelated `text.insert` and another save and open. A box shown nowhere, added as a control, is still pruned.
- `doc/src/tests.rs::text_boxes_shown_from_deeply_nested_tables_are_kept`: boxes 17 and 40 tables down in the body, one 18 down inside another box and one 20 down in a header are all kept, a…

title: Paste without formatting: Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+V pastes plain text (#1544)
author: subasah
body:
Fixes #1544.

### Summary
Modern Microsoft Word (Microsoft 365) established `Ctrl+Shift+V` / `Cmd+Shift+V` as "Paste: Keep Text Only" (pasting clipboard contents as plain text without formatting).

This PR adds `Ctrl+Shift+V` (and `Cmd+Shift+V` on macOS) support to `edit.pasteText` ("Paste: Keep Text Only") without breaking existing functionality:
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`:
  - `edit.pasteText` key combo updated to `Mod+Shift+V / Mod+Shift+Alt+V`, allowing both standard `Ctrl+Shift+V` / `Cmd+Shift+V` and legacy `Mod+Shift+Alt+V`.
  - Format Painter (`edit.copyFormat` / `edit.pasteFormat`) updated to `Mod+Shift+C / Mod+Alt+C` and `Mod+Alt+Shift+V` to prevent collision.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs`:
  - `canvas_events` handles `Event::Paste` with Shift pressed to dispatch `edit.pasteText`.
  - Added `is_paste_text_release` to handle `Mod+Shift+V` releases when the clipboard holds no text (reporting that clipboard is empty).
  - In `canvas_events`, Shift suppresses treating pasted file paths as image insertions.
  - In `dispatch`, `app.canvas.pasted = true` is set when resolving paste commands from keys to prevent duplicate release handling.
  - Added unit and regression test `mod_shift_v_pastes_plain_text_without_formatting` verifying that `Mod+Shift+V` strips HTML formatting and inserts plain text across both paste events and keyboard events.
- Progress docs:
  - Updated `docs/typing-parity.md` and `ROADMAP.md` progress log.

### Validation
- `cargo fmt --check`: passed
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-engine -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine`: all 421 tests passed
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib keys::`: all 6 tests passed
- `cargo run -p xtask -- assets`: passed (all 53 assets attributed)
- `cargo run -p xtask -- layers`: passed (0 violations)

title: Layout: a table's percentage width past 100% is kept
author: finwarman
body:
A table's percentage width past 100% is kept, as Word keeps it.

- `w:tblW w:type="pct"` above 5000 was capped at the text column. A cover-page footer table at 131% with the left margin as a negative indent ended three-quarters of the way across the page instead of spanning it.
- Cap is now 10x the column, only to bound hostile input. The existing guard that shrinks autofit tables wider than 150% is unchanged.

Test: `a_percentage_width_past_the_text_column_is_kept`.


Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`, in its own commit.

title: Shapes: a right triangle keeps its right angle
author: finwarman
body:
`rtTriangle` gets its own shape kind, `ShapeKind::RightTriangle`, instead of being read as an isosceles triangle.

- Drawn with the right angle at the bottom left (ECMA-376 preset geometry), on screen and in PDF.
- Wrap contour and connection sites follow the same outline.
- Saved back as `rtTriangle`. The .doc reader maps msosptRightTriangle (6) to it.

Found on a report cover whose white corner cut-outs pointed up into a peak instead of cutting a V into the photo above them.

title: Shapes: a solid fill keeps its transparency
author: finwarman
body:
A shape's solid fill keeps its `a:alpha` transparency.

- Read into `ShapeExtra::fill_transparency` (percent, 0 = opaque), so no shape constructors change.
- `Draw::Shape` carries the fill opacity; the rasteriser and the PDF writer use it.
- Written back as `a:alpha` on save.

Found on a report where a 31% white wash over a photo was drawn opaque and hid the photo.

Also updates `blend_backgrounds`, which assumed shape fills are opaque, to use the fill opacity.

Limit: solid fills only; gradient stop alpha is unchanged.

title: Layout: page numbers can restart at 0
author: finwarman
body:
Page numbers can restart at 0 (`w:pgNumType w:start="0"`).

- The reader kept 0, but layout set the counter to restart - 1 with a saturating subtract, so 0 laid out as 1. A report numbering its cover 0 read "Page 2" where Word reads "Page 1".
- The restart is now the next page's number itself (`PageBuilder::restart_at`).

Test: `page_numbers_can_restart_at_zero`.

Not changed: NUMPAGES. Measured in Word, it counts physical pages whatever the start.

title: Save Changes prompt takes the keyboard from the page (#1597)
author: alik654zx
body:
Fixes #1597.

The Save Changes prompt gave Save the focus only when nothing else had it (#861). In the app the page keeps the focus while you type and claims Tab and the arrow keys (set_focus_lock_filter in canvas.rs), so the prompt opened with no focused button and the arrows moved the caret behind it. The existing tests drew the dialog alone, where nothing else could hold the focus, so they passed.

Save now takes the focus whenever none of the prompt's buttons has it.

- Test: save_prompt_takes_focus_from_the_page draws the whole app with the page focused after typing, closes the document, and checks that Save has focus, that → moves to Don't Save without moving the caret, and that Enter answers. It fails on main and passes with the fix; arrow_keys_choose_the_save_prompt_answer and enter_answers_with_the_focused_button still pass.
- Docs: docs/ui-parity.md, ROADMAP.md

title: Escape selects a text box or WordArt, so Delete removes it (#1538)
author: Yasas-Sri
body:
Fixes #1538.

## Problem

Inserting WordArt leaves its text selected, so Delete erased only "Your text here" and left an empty, invisible box in the document. Escape couldn't help either: in a text box it put the caret in the body just after the box, so there was no keyboard way to select the box itself. Only Undo got rid of it. Plain text boxes had the same problem.

## Change

Escape while editing a text box or WordArt now selects the box (`select.range` over its anchor character), with or without a text selection, so Delete removes it. A second Escape goes back to a caret in the body. Delete while typing inside the box still only deletes text. This is what I understand Word does; I couldn't check it against Word on my machine, so please double-check.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs`: the Escape branch selects the box instead of moving the caret after it (`checked_sub` on the offset, no panic path).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: the regression test below.

## Tests

- New `escape_selects_a_wordart_box_and_delete_removes_it` (UI harness): insert WordArt, Escape selects the box, Delete removes it, Undo brings it back, two Escapes leave a caret in the body. It fails without the fix ("Escape selects the box") and passes with it.
- Checked by hand in the app on Linux: Insert › WordArt → Escape → Delete removes it.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt and clippy pass. 2020 tests pass; the two failures (`commands_do_not_touch_the_file_system_themselves`, `clicks_on_ribbon_and_status_bar_chrome_keep_typing_in_the_document`) also fail on current main without this change (#1569, fixed by #1578). Assets, layers and wasm (all 16 crates) pass.

title: Shape fills: gradients and transparency (#1500)
author: benandez
body:
Closes #1500.

Shape fills keep, draw, save and edit gradients and transparency, as Word does. Word 365 cover pages now show their theme gradient panel and translucent wave (the full #743 cover also needs #1487).

title: Layout: a page break followed by another page start makes one page
author: finwarman
body:
A paragraph of only a page break, followed by another page start, makes one page, not two.

- After #932 the break's mark stays on the old page, but its space after still went onto the new page. A following heading with page break before then wasn't at the top and broke again.
- A next-page section break carried by that paragraph also started a second page. The empty page the break started is now taken back first.

Found on a 60-page report: two blank pages Word doesn't have. Test: `a_page_break_then_a_new_page_makes_one_page` (both cases).

title: Layout: paragraph spacing adds up when HTML auto spacing is off
author: finwarman
body:
Paragraph spacing adds up when the document sets `w:doNotUseHTMLParagraphAutoSpacing`.

- #733 made the gap the larger of space after and space before, which is Word's default. Measured in Word with 12 pt before and after: 24 pt with the option, 12 pt without, the same in compatibility modes 14 and 15.
- The option is read into `Settings::sum_paragraph_spacing`, laid out in the body and in boxes, and written back in `w:compat`.

Found on a 60-page report whose cover came out about 60 pt short, so the next page's anchored pictures landed on the cover.

Tests: `space_between_paragraphs_is_their_sum_when_html_auto_spacing_is_off` (body and cell), `html_auto_spacing_off_is_read_and_kept`.

title: Fonts: a missing roman font is drawn in Cambria, as in Word
author: finwarman
body:
A font that isn't installed is drawn in Cambria when the font table classes it as roman, as Word does.

- Measured in Word with one missing font: `w:family` roman gives Cambria, swiss or auto gives Calibri. WordCraft picked by name only, so an unknown brand font always came out sans.
- Roman fonts are read from the font table into `Settings::roman_fonts`. Layout looks a missing one up as Cambria, which falls back to Caladea.
- Other classes keep the existing substitutes, which already start with Carlito.

Limit: only the paragraph text path uses it; equations and watermarks still resolve by name.

title: Layout: an empty section mark stays on a full page
author: finwarman
body:
An empty paragraph closing a section before a new page stays on a full page, instead of starting a blank page of its own.

- Measured in Word: 50 lines filling a page, then an empty paragraph carrying a next-page section break, then the next section gives 2 pages. WordCraft gave 3.
- Control, also measured: a plain empty paragraph in the same place moves to the next page in both.
- `PageBuilder::next_starts_page` is set per section; the line-fit check skips an empty mark that closes the section.

Found after a full landscape drawing page in a 60-page report.

Limit: only empty marks, and only before a new-page section. A continuous break, or a mark with text, behaves as before.

title: Layout: a bookmark after a page break takes no line
author: finwarman
body:
A bookmark after a paragraph's closing page break takes no line on the next page.

- Word writes the next heading's TOC bookmark start (`_Toc…`) into the paragraph that ends with a page break. The line after the break then held that marker, so it wasn't treated as the empty mark kept with the break (#932). It went onto the next page with the paragraph's spacing and pushed the heading 17 pt down.
- Lines holding only zero-width markers (`InlineObject::is_marker`: bookmarks, comment and permission ranges, field and control boundaries) now count as empty there.

Found on a 60-page report, where it cost a page in the calculations section. Test: `a_bookmark_after_a_page_break_takes_no_line`.

title: Layout: a numbered paragraph opening with a page break takes its number along
author: finwarman
body:
A numbered paragraph whose text opens with a page break draws its number on the next page, with the text.

- The label was always drawn on line 0. When line 0 holds only the opening page break (and zero-width markers), the number stood alone at the bottom of one page and the heading text started the next.
- `ParaLayout::label_line()` picks line 1 in that case; display draws the label there. The label's x is unchanged and lines up as in Word.

Found on three numbered headings in a 60-page report (5.2.3, 5.4, 5.4.3). Test: `a_numbered_heading_opening_with_a_page_break_takes_its_number_along`.

title: Tables: text running past an exact-height row is cut off
author: finwarman
body:
Text that doesn't fit an exact-height table row is cut off at the cell's edge, as Word does, instead of being drawn over the rows below.

- Table layout marks such a cell: `Placed::Cell` gets `clip`, set when the row is `hRule="exact"` and the cell's content is taller than the row.
- `page_display` draws lines inside a clipped cell within a `Draw::Clip` of the cell's area. The PDF writer draws item by item for tagging, so it passes the page's clipped cells along with each line.
- Hit testing and the caret are unchanged: the lines keep their layout positions.

Found on a welder qualification certificate whose identification block rendered as overlapping lines. Test: `text_overflowing_an_exact_row_is_clipped_to_it`.

Limit: only text lines are clipped; a picture overflowing an exact row still draws in full.

title: Tables: a row with less room than its minimum height moves on whole
author: finwarman
body:
A table row with an at-least height doesn't split where less than that height is left on the page; it starts the next page whole.

Measured in Word, with about 49 pt left on the page:

| Row | Word | WordCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| 8 lines, no height | splits after line 3 | same |
| 8 lines, at least 63.6 pt | moves whole | split |
| nested table of 6 rows, no height | splits after its row 3 | same |
| nested table of 6 rows, at least 63.6 pt | moves whole | split |
| 2 lines, at least 63.6 pt | moves whole | same |

`place_table` skips `split_row` for the first part of such a row. Found on a report whose title row (a logo beside a small nested table) started at the foot of its cover page, two pages off by the end. Test: `a_row_with_less_room_than_its_minimum_height_moves_on_whole`.

title: Fonts: a Bidi theme slot names the theme's complex-script font
author: finwarman
body:
`minorBidi`/`majorBidi` theme font slots name the theme's complex-script font (`a:cs`), not its Latin font.

Measured in Word, with a run set to `w:asciiTheme="minorBidi"`:

| Theme `a:cs` | Word | WordCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| Times New Roman | Times New Roman | Calibri (the Latin minor font) |
| empty, style sets Arial | Arial (inherited) | Calibri |

- `PropCtx` keeps the theme's major and minor `a:cs` faces. `theme_font` returns them for `…Bidi` slots, and nothing when they're empty, so the font beside it in `w:rFonts`, or the inherited one, applies. `w:cstheme` resolves the same way.

Found on a template whose title runs use `asciiTheme="minorBidi"` with an empty `a:cs`: Word draws them in the style's Arial, WordCraft drew Calibri. Test: `bidi_theme_slots_name_the_complex_script_font`.

Limit: with an empty `a:cs` and no explicit font anywhere in the style chain, Word draws Times New Roman; WordCraft keeps the theme-based default (the model doesn't record whether an inherited font came from the theme). East Asian slots are unchanged.

title: Layout: an inherited footer sizes its percentage tables by its own section
author: finwarman
body:
An inherited header or footer sizes its percentage-width tables by the section that defines it.

Measured in Word, with a 100%-wide footer table defined by a portrait section:

| Landscape section | Word | WordCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| inherits the footer | portrait width (451 pt), centred | landscape width |
| names the same footer itself | landscape width | landscape width |

Paragraph alignment in an inherited footer follows the landscape page in Word, as it already did here, so only table percentage widths change.

- `defining_width` finds the section that names an inherited part. `Ctx::pct_base` carries its text width while the part is measured (header and footer heights) and laid out. A top-level table takes its percentage share of that width.

Found on a 60-page report whose landscape calculation pages drew the footer table full width. Test: `an_inherited_footer_sizes_its_percentage_table_by_its_own_section`.

title: Equations: a multi-letter subscript stays whole after build-up
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1609.

The linear-format parser reads a script or limit as one letter or a number, as in Word (#347 grouped the gallery templates for the same reason). `to_linear` didn't follow that rule: a subscript holding `dd` was written bare as `V_dd`. Build-up re-reads the text before the caret on Space, a relation sign or a move, so a subscript typed in the subscript box came back as V_d followed by d. Scripts, n-ary limits and `┬`/`┴` limits now write a run of more than one character as a group, `V_(dd)`. Single characters and numbers stay bare (`x_i`, `x_10`, `x^2.5`), so other equations write the same linear text as before.

What this doesn't change, so I left the issue open for you to decide:
- Typing `V_dd` straight in still gives V_d then d. That's Word's rule; `V_(dd)` is the way to get a two-letter subscript.
- `{…}` stay visible braces, as in Word. `V_"dd"` (quoted normal text) isn't read as text yet. That's a separate parser feature, and I can do it in a follow-up if you'd like.

Validation:
- `math::tests::multi_letter_scripts_round_trip`: fails on main (`V_dd` reads back as V_d then d), passes here
- `math_edit::tests::build_up_keeps_a_multi_letter_subscript` (subscript box → `dd` → Right → build-up): fails on main (build-up rewrites the equation), passes here

title: DOCX: a picture's a:alphaModFix transparency is drawn
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

A picture faded with *Picture Format › Transparency* is written as `<a:alphaModFix amt="10000"/>` inside its `a:blip`. The DOCX reader dropped the element, so a letterhead's dotted pattern that Word draws at 10 % opacity came out at full strength on screen and in the PDF export.

## How

In `read_pic`, when the blip carries an `a:alphaModFix`, the picture's alpha is multiplied into its pixels and the result is kept as a PNG under its own media key (`image5_a10000.png`). This is the same approach the `picture.transparency` command already takes, so layout, screen and PDF need no new path and a save keeps the fade. Details:

- two uses of the same picture at the same fade share one faded copy;
- a picture that can't be decoded (a metafile, an unknown format, a side over 30 000 px) is kept as it is and a warning is logged;
- the original bytes stay under their key;
- `image` moves from dev-dependency to dependency of `wordcraft-docx` (it is already in the tree through `wordcraft-pdf`, with the same features).

## Tests

`alpha_mod_fix_fades_the_picture` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`: a 2×2 opaque PNG with `amt="25000"` reads back with alpha 64, two pictures share the faded copy, `amt="100000"` is a no-op, and undecodable bytes stay opaque. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx` pass.

Found while converting a customer's DOCX to PDF through the `docx` and `pdf` crates; the header now matches Word's and LibreOffice's output.

title: Tables without w:tblGrid take their grid from the cells, and widths wider than the page are squeezed like Word
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

Template libraries write tables with no `w:tblGrid` and cell widths (`w:tcW`) that don't fit the page: 6000 and 24000 twips on an A4 page is a common pattern. Word rebuilds the grid from the cells on opening and squeezes the table into the text area. WordCraft gave every column of a grid-less table a fixed inch, so such a table came out a third of the page wide, with its labels broken over two lines and its exact-height rows overlapping.

## How

Two changes, one per crate:

- **`wordcraft-docx`**, `grid_from_cells`: a table without `w:tblGrid` takes its grid from the cells' preferred widths, the way Word rebuilds it: the widest `w:tcW` among the cells that occupy a column alone, a spanning cell's width shared among the columns no cell sizes, an inch for a column nothing sizes.

- **`wordcraft-layout`**, `autofit`: an autofit table wider than its room is squeezed into it the way Word does it. Every column gets its longest word, and the room left is shared in proportion to how far each preferred width exceeds that. The squeeze applies only to a table whose width comes from its columns (no `w:tblW` of its own), from 2 % over the room; a table that sets its own width keeps it, past the margin and the page, as Word does (see the second commit).

The layout rule was derived from Word's own PDF export of the document that showed the problem. With a label column (preferred 300 pt) and a text column (preferred 1200 pt) on a 482 pt text area, the rule predicts 115.9 pt for the label column; Word draws 116.3 pt. A plain proportional split gives 96 pt and wraps the labels. On a second table in the same document the prediction is 141.9 pt against Word's 144.6 pt.

## Tests

- `a_table_without_a_grid_takes_its_columns_from_the_cells` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`): grid from cells, from a spanning cell, and the fallback.
- `preferred_widths_wider_than_the_page_are_squeezed_like_word` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): the table stays inside the margins, the label column…

title: Tabs left of the margin stay on a default stop they already sit on (Word)
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

Left of the left margin, Word's next default tab stop is the first multiple of the interval **at or after** the current position, not strictly after it (its arithmetic truncates toward zero). So a tab that already sits on a stop, a second tab in a row or a leading tab on a line that starts at −72 pt, doesn't advance. A tab preceded by text or a space, or a line starting between stops, moves to the next multiple as usual, and right of the margin nothing changes.

Letterheads that line a footer up with spaces and tabs under a negative indent rely on this. One had a registration number on its last footer line drawn 72 pt too far right, over a vertical rule; it now lands within 0.2 pt of Word.

## How

`next_tab` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: for a negative position the default stop is `ceil(x / d) · d` instead of `(floor(x / d) + 1) · d`. Explicit stops and the hanging-indent stop are untouched.

## Measurements

Synthetic documents exported to PDF by Word (Calibri 9 pt, default tab 36 pt, left margin 37 pt, about 40 positions in total):

| text | left indent | X in Word | old rule | new rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a\t\tX` | −60 | −36 | 0 | −36 |
| `\tX` | −72 | −72 | −36 | −72 |
| `\tX` | −60 | −36 | −36 | −36 |
| `\t \tX` | −60 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `a\t\t\t\tX` | −30 | 108 | 108 | 108 |
| `a\tb\tc\td` | −108 | b −72, c −36, d 0 | same | same |

Positions are relative to the margin.

## Tests

`tabs_left_of_the_margin_stay_on_a_default_stop` in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs` pins the five cases above that distinguish the rules. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` pass.

title: A floating object anchored after a page break stays on the page its paragraph starts on
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

Word's cover pages (Insert › Cover Page) are one paragraph holding a page break and then the page-anchored text box with the title and the approval table. Word draws a floating object on the page its anchor paragraph starts on. WordCraft drew it with the line holding the anchor, which after the break is the first line of page two: the cover came out blank and the title box sat over the body text of page two.

## How

`place_objects` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` places a paragraph's floating objects from the paragraph's first piece, whichever of its lines holds the anchor, and none from later pieces. Inline objects still go with their own line. The wrap areas were already registered from the paragraph's first page (`anchor_floats` runs there), so nothing changes for text flowing around the object.

## Tests

`a_float_anchored_after_a_page_break_stays_on_its_paragraph_s_first_page` in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`: a paragraph of a page break followed by a page-anchored shape lays out on two pages with the shape on the first one only, at its page offset. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` pass.

Found converting a 21-page customer document to PDF; its cover now matches Word's export.
