title: Update Field works in headers, footers, notes and text boxes; printing updates every field (#1706)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1706

## What was wrong
**References › Update Field** (`references.updateFields`) only ever refreshed fields in the main text. With the caret in a header, footer, footnote or text box, Update Field did nothing to the fields you were looking at, so a header's author name or word count kept its old value forever.

## Word behaviour (user-checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4)
- With an AUTHOR field in the header, selecting all in the body and pressing F9 does **not** change the header's field.
- With an AUTHOR field in the body, the same steps update the body's field.
- Fields can't be inserted into (modern) comments at all.

So Update Field works on the story you're editing: from the body it updates the body, and from inside a header it updates that header.

## What changed
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs`: `update_fields` now refreshes the non-locked fields of the caret's story (`DATE`/`TIME`/`CREATEDATE`/`SAVEDATE`/`PRINTDATE`, `REF`, `PAGEREF`, `TITLE`, `AUTHOR`, `NUMWORDS`).
  - `SEQ`/`STYLEREF` numbering, citations and the table of contents are body-wide, so they still run only when Update Field is used from the body.
  - It's still one undo step.
- New optional param `{"all": true}`: updates the body (with SEQ, citations and the TOC) **plus every** header, footer, note and text box, wherever the caret is. The default is the caret's story, and a junk value falls back to that default.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/printing.rs`: "Update fields before printing" now passes `{"all": true}`, so printing from inside a header still refreshes the whole document.

## Tests
All three failed before their fix:
- `update_fields_in_the_body_leaves_headers_alone`: from the body, header fields keep their old value (Word check C).
- `update_fields_in_a_header_updates_that_header`: from the header, its AUTHOR/NUMWORDS fields update.

title: Insert Date & Time and date fields use local time, not UTC (#1707)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1707

## What was wrong
Insert ▸ Date & Time, updated DATE/TIME (and CREATEDATE/SAVEDATE/PRINTDATE) fields, the date picker's "today" and the File ▸ Home greeting's time of day all used UTC. Anyone far from Greenwich could get the wrong time, or even the wrong day.

## What changed
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`: `local_offset_secs()` reads the system time zone's UTC offset; `local_civil(unix, offset)` turns a timestamp plus offset into the local date, time and weekday; `local_now()` combines the two.
  - Native: `chrono` (workspace dep, `features = ["clock"]` only, under its own `# time` heading), called inside `catch_unwind` so a broken time-zone setup falls back to UTC instead of crashing.
  - wasm: the offset comes from `js_sys::Date::get_timezone_offset` (js-sys is already a dependency). chrono is a native-only dependency, so the wasm build pulls in nothing new.
  - The offset is clamped to ±26 h; NaN and huge values fall back to 0.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`: `format_date` now formats the local time through the new `format_date_at(fmt, unix, offset)`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/content_controls.rs`: the date picker's "today" is the local date.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs`: the Home greeting uses the local hour.
- `now_iso` (document metadata timestamps) stays UTC on purpose, since OOXML stores those as UTC (`…Z`).

**Why chrono, not jiff:** both work. jiff bundles its own time-zone database, which adds binary size (and matters for wasm); chrono with only the `clock` feature reads the system zone and stays small.

## Word behaviour
User-checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4: Insert ▸ Date & Time shows the Mac's local time.

## Tests
- `local_civil_date_follows_the_utc_offset`: UTC+13, UTC−5, UTC and a pre-1970 negative offset give the right local date, time and weekday; hostile values (`u64::MAX`, `i64::MIN/MAX`) don't panic.
- `format_date_uses_the_local_offset`: the same instant formats as Saturday noon in New Zealand, and as Friday 23:00 at UT…

title: Lowercase list items no longer get a grammar underline (#1741)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1741

## What changed
The "double underline" on lower-case list items is the grammar squiggle from the "Capitalize the first word of a sentence" rule. It treated a list item's first word ("item one") as the start of a sentence. Now the first word of a numbered or bulleted paragraph is never flagged for a missing capital. A later sentence in the same item ("item one. then two") is still checked, and so are ordinary paragraphs.

- `crates/proof`: `check_text_with` takes a `list_item` flag. English, Polish, Croatian, Italian, Turkish and Portuguese each have the same first-word rule, and all of them honour the flag (`check_with(text, capital_first)`; the old `check` stays as before).
- `crates/layout`: `para::is_list_item` decides whether a paragraph is a list item from its own numbering, else its style's numbering; `num 0` means the numbering was removed. The squiggles drawn on the page and the engine's proofing panes (Editor, spelling pane, next issue) all use this same check, so they agree.

**Word behaviour** (user-checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4): Word's AutoCorrect capitalises a list item's first word as you type, and no grammar underline appears on list items. WordCraft's AutoCorrect already does the same capitalising (`docs/typing-parity.md`). This fix covers lower-case items that AutoCorrect didn't touch, such as undone corrections, pasted text and opened files, which no longer get a squiggle.

## Tests
- `wordcraft-proof list_item_first_word_needs_no_capital`: a table over all six languages. A list item is not flagged, a plain paragraph is, and a later sentence in a list item is still flagged at "then" or "sonra". It failed before the fix (`left: 1, right: 0`).
- `wordcraft-layout list_item_first_word_gets_no_capital_squiggle`: goes through `layout()`, the drawn squiggles, and covers a plain paragraph, direct numbering, numbering from the style, and `num 0`. It fails if the drawing path ignores the flag (`own numbering: left: 1, right: 0`).

author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1744

## What was wrong
- **Copy** of a selected table (Select Table, or a drag over all of it) kept only the cells' paragraphs. Pasting it outside the table gave loose paragraphs instead of a table.
- **Cut** of a selected table only cleared the cells' text. The empty table stayed in the document.

## What changed
Behaviour follows what the reporter checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4 (3×3 table, a word per cell):

| Selection | Copy, then Paste outside the table | Cut |
|---|---|---|
| Whole table | a full copy of the table, with its formatting | the table is removed, in one undo step |
| Whole rows | a table of just those rows | the rows' text is cleared; the rows stay |
| Cells (one row, or a block of cells) | a table of just those cells | their text is cleared; the cells stay |

- Copy now puts a table fragment on the clipboard. Merged cells are trimmed to the copied range, and a merge that is only partly selected is widened to cover the whole merged cell. The plain-text clipboard is tab and newline separated.
- Cut of a whole table reuses Delete Table. Cut of rows or cells reuses the existing clear-cells path. It refuses when a cell holds a locked content control.
- With Track Changes on, Cut keeps the existing tracked behaviour: the text is marked deleted. It doesn't create new kinds of table revisions.
- No new command ids: `edit.copy` and `edit.cut` gain the behaviour, so the ribbon, the shortcuts, the CLI and MCP all get it.
- ROADMAP progress log and revision history are updated.

## How it's tested
New tests in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`, written first and seen failing before the fix:
- `copy_whole_table_pastes_a_table`, `cut_whole_table_removes_it_and_undoes`
- `copy_rows_and_cells_pastes_a_table_of_them`, `cut_rows_and_cells_clears_their_text`
- `copy_and_cut_of_an_empty_table_or_cell`, `text_selection_of_a_whole_table_copies_the_table` (also nested tables)

title: engine: read_file reads only a bounded regular file, so a pipe or device path can't hang or exhaust memory
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`insert.picture`, `picture.change` and `mailings.recipients` read their path through `io::read_file`, which passes it straight to `std::fs::read`. A path that is not a regular file turns that into a hang or an unbounded allocation: opening a FIFO blocks until a writer appears, and a device like `/dev/zero` never reaches end of file, so the buffer grows until allocation fails — an abort that `Session::run`'s crash guard cannot intercept.

The repository already has the correct helpers: `read_file_capped` checks `is_file()` and the size before reading, and `LocalImages` documents exactly this hazard for HTML pictures, but `read_file` used neither. This routes `read_file` through `read_file_capped` with a new `MAX_READ_FILE` of 2 GB (the same ceiling `open_path_with` gives a document), so pipes and devices are refused and reads are bounded. The regression test `insert_picture_from_a_named_pipe_is_refused_without_blocking` creates a FIFO, calls `io::read_file` on a worker thread and asserts an error arrives within 10 s (the old code times out), and also pins `/dev/zero`; it mirrors the existing HTML-picture FIFO test that #98 introduced.

Partially addresses #1690 (finding 1, unbounded read_file). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: engine: review commands refuse a comment id past u32 instead of wrapping to another comment
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`review.deleteComment`, `review.reply` and `review.resolveComment` parse their `id` with `x as u32`, which wraps instead of failing: an id of 2^32 + n truncates to n, so a hostile or buggy caller mutates a different comment — deletes the first comment and its replies, resolves it, or attaches a reply to the wrong thread. `review.editComment` in the same file already does this correctly with `u32::try_from`, returning a `Params` error for anything past u32.

This applies the same conversion in all three places so out-of-range ids are refused before they touch the document. The regression test `comment_ids_are_refused_not_truncated` creates a comment, moves the caret away from it, and calls all three commands with `id + 2^32`, asserting each errors and the comment is untouched and unresolved — the old code deletes it on the first call.

Partially addresses #1690 (finding 3, comment id u32 truncation). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: formats: the Markdown code fence outgrows any backtick run in its content, so a round trip keeps it
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Markdown export caps its fenced-code delimiter at 64 backticks (`3.max(longest + 1).min(64)`), but the importer treats any line with at least as many backticks as the opener as the closing fence. A code block whose content contains a run of 64+ backticks — legal Markdown, reachable by opening or pasting such a file — is therefore written with a fence no longer than its own content: on re-import the content line closes the block early and the text after it is swallowed by a spurious new block, so the document corrupts itself on save and reopen. The reader's rule is that the fence must be strictly longer than anything inside it; only the writer's `.min(64)` cap violated it.

The fix drops the cap so the fence is always `3.max(longest + 1)`, growing at most to the input's own backtick count. The regression test `markdown_code_fence_outgrows_its_content` imports an indented line of 100 backticks, exports, asserts a 101-backtick fence, and re-imports to check the line survives — the old code fails both the fence assertion and the round trip.

Partially addresses #1690 (finding 4, Markdown fence round-trip loss). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: docx: documentProtection without w:enforcement is enforced, as in Word, and survives a save
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`w:documentProtection` in `word/settings.xml` is only kept when `w:enforcement` is present and truthy, so a protected file whose generator omits the attribute opens fully editable in WordCraft, and the next save permanently strips the restriction and its password hash. Word does the opposite of the standard's literal reading here: [MS-OI29500] §2.1.402 (c) states that Word enforces protection when `w:enforcement` is missing, and this project's contract is Word parity.

The fix makes an absent attribute mean enforced while an explicit `w:enforcement="0"`/`"false"`/`"off"` still means unprotected, so the restriction, `w:formatting` and the hash round-trip. The regression test `protection_without_enforcement_is_enforced_like_word` builds a synthetic package whose settings carry `w:edit="readOnly"` plus hash attributes and no `w:enforcement`, asserts the protection and hash survive read → write → read, and that an explicit `"0"` stays off.

Partially addresses #1690 (finding 5, documentProtection enforcement). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: docx: read Standard-encrypted packages (MS-OFFCRYPTO 2.3.4.9)
author: Bra1nZ
body:
## What

Read packages encrypted with **Standard Encryption** (MS-OFFCRYPTO §2.3.4.9) — the scheme Word 2007 and later write by default when you set a "password to open".

Today `decrypt_package` recognises that header and refuses. This adds the path.

## Scope

One file, `crates/docx/src/crypt.rs`, +236/−1. No new dependencies — AES and SHA-1 are already in the tree.

## How it works

- **Dispatch.** `EncryptionInfo` version `(2..=4, 2)` routes here. The existing agile and legacy paths are untouched.
- **Key.** The password goes through the §2.3.4.11 iterated hash, 50 000 spins, truncated to the key size the header asks for. Result is kept in `Zeroizing`.
- **Password check.** The 16-byte verifier is decrypted and hashed; the first bytes of that hash are compared against the decrypted verifier hash. Mismatch is `DocxError::WrongPassword`, so a wrong password reads as a wrong password rather than as a corrupt file.
- **Payload.** The first 8 bytes of the package are the plaintext length, then segments of 4096 bytes in ECB, last one zero-padded.

Three things in the spec are easy to get wrong and are worth stating:

- `EncryptedVerifierHash` is **32 bytes** (two AES blocks), not one `VerifierHashSize` block. Slicing it at `VerifierHashSize` truncates the comparison.
- `EncryptionInfo` carries an 8-byte wrapper — a flags copy and the real header size — before the header proper. Reading from offset 0 yields a plausible-looking, wrong salt.
- The PKCS#5 hash buffer is **XORed** into a 64-byte buffer, not appended to.

## Verification

Verified against a real Standard-encrypted file, not a self-round-trip: `protected_passtika.xlsx`, password `tika`, derived key `8d4d00143a5f2e4918af7e6e7410d46c`. The test vector is the salt, the expected key and the known verifier — a round trip would pass even if the spec were read wrong, so the key is asserted against the published value.

`ecb_decrypt` checks the length is a whole number of blocks **before** slicing. The length comes …

title: mcp: let open_document take a password
author: Bra1nZ
body:
## What

`open_document` can take a `password`.

The engine has read this since password support landed: `file.open` pulls `password` out of its parameters and hands it to `open_path_in` / `open_bytes_in` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:205`). The UI asks for one and retries. The CLI has `--password`. The MCP tool simply did not pass it on, so an agent driving a server or a desktop app through MCP could not open a protected document by any route.

Two lines of behaviour, plus tests.

## Scope

One file, `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs`, +62/−3. No new dependencies.

## The schema

`password` is advertised and stays **optional** — `required` remains `["path"]`. The description says what happens without it: the call fails and the engine asks for a password, the same as the UI.

## The detail that matters

Without a password the parameter is sent as `null`, not `""`.

`file.open` reads an empty string as "no password given" — so collapsing the two would silently open a protected document with an empty password rather than failing. There is a test pinning that.

## Tests

Three, in a new `mod tests`:

- `open_document_forwards_the_password_to_file_open` — the password reaches `file.open` inside the `engine.execute` envelope
- `open_document_without_a_password_passes_null` — no password stays `null`, never `""`
- `the_schema_advertises_the_password_as_optional` — the schema offers it and does not require it

The first of these is worth noting: I wrote it expecting `file.open` as the backend method name, and it failed. `exec` wraps every call as `engine.execute` with the command nested under `params`. The test was wrong about the code, not the reverse.

`cargo test -p wordcraft-mcp` green (13 lib + 5 integration), `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Note for review

This is the MCP half of a three-part fix. The CLI half is #1770; Standard-encrypted (Office 2007) packages are #1795. Together they cover what an agent can actually open.

title: Layout: paragraph borders take their room and same-bordered paragraphs join in one shaded box
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #1799.

## What

- A paragraph's top and bottom borders now take their distance plus width in the text flow (body and boxes/cells/headers), as in Word; the top and bottom rules lie beyond their distance from the text and the shading fills the room up to them.
- Neighbouring paragraphs with the same borders and indents make one box: the top border goes above the first only, the bottom below the last, and the shading and side borders reach up through the space between paragraphs, so the box is continuous.
- Paragraphs whose borders differ stay boxes of their own (checked against Word with synthetic documents: a first paragraph with a top border and a second without one are not joined).

## Not covered

- `w:between` borders inside a group are still not drawn.
- The bottom border's room is not checked against the page bottom when the last line is the one that just fits.

## Test

`layout::tests::paragraphs_with_the_same_borders_join_in_one_shaded_box` (fails before the change: the title's line starts at the top of its shading, and the shading of two same-bordered paragraphs has a gap).

title: Layout: a tab whose text doesn't fit goes to the next line with it (#1839)
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #1839.

## Problem
A TOC entry whose title just fits on a line showed its page number at the left of the next line, without the leader. Two cases ended the line after the tab and started the next one with the tab's text at the indent:
- the text after a right, centre or decimal tab didn't fit;
- the text ended past the last tab stop and the next default stop was past the right indent (the tab stayed at the end of the line with no width).

## Fix
`crates/layout/src/para.rs`, `break_lines`:
- When the line has to wrap and the break it would take is a pending right/centre/decimal tab, it breaks before the tab instead. The tab's leader entry on this line is dropped.
- A tab whose next stop is past the right indent no longer stays on the line with no width: the line wraps before it (as the old comment already said Word does).

In both cases the tab starts the next line and goes to the first stop there, so a TOC page number ends at its stop after a leader. A tab that is the first thing on its line keeps the old behaviour, so a line always makes progress.

## Result
Synthetic 175-page document with a generated TOC (right tab with dot leader at 9345 twips), `pdftotext -layout`:

| | TOC lines holding only a page number at the left |
|---|---|
| main | 12 |
| this PR | 0 |

Page count and every other TOC line are unchanged.

## Testing
- New test `right_tab_whose_text_does_not_fit_moves_to_the_next_line_with_it` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): `"abc " x m + "y" x r + "\t63"` for 80 lengths, with the right dot-leader stop at the margin (468 pt) and at 400 pt (default stops every 100 pt). The number must be on the tab's line, end at the stop (or past it inside the margin, when the text already reaches the stop) and have a leader. Without the first change it fails with `stop 468, 20 words + 0: number ends at 85.344`; without the second, `stop 400, 20 words + 0: number ends at 85.344`.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layo…

title: engine: reject malformed comment IDs before editing or caret fallback
author: MMexicann
body:
A fractional comment ID such as `0.5` targets comment 0, and an explicit `null`, negative number or wrong-type ID can make Delete/Resolve target the caret instead. A buggy CLI, MCP or control caller can therefore delete, resolve, edit or reply to a comment it did not identify.

Related to #1690 finding 3. **This complements #1787:** that PR handles oversized integer conversion; this PR handles malformed JSON values and omission versus explicit invalid input. It does not close the broader audit issue.

### Root cause and change

The general `p::u64` helper coerces floating-point numbers and treats unsupported values as absent. Comment IDs require stricter input semantics. A shared validation step now accepts only an omitted ID or a non-negative JSON integer, returning `CmdError::Params` for explicit malformed values before the four comment commands mutate state. Delete validates before its `all` branch too.

Existing integer conversion and comment allocation are unchanged, so #1787 can supply its separate range check. Omitted IDs still use the existing caret behavior for Delete/Resolve; Reply/Edit still require an ID. Registry parameter documentation now states the JSON integer requirement and Resolve's toggle behavior.

### Regression and fidelity coverage

Seven tests in `crates/engine/tests/comment_ids.rs` use documents created through WordCraft commands. With the main implementation restored, **five tests failed and two controls passed**: negative IDs deleted/resolved the caret comment, fractional IDs edited/replied to comment 0, and Delete All accepted an explicit null ID.

The tests cover negative and floating-point numbers (including `0.0`), strings, null and booleans, both inside a comment and away from it. Refusals preserve the document, selection, dirty flag, undo labels and an existing redo step. Controls cover valid IDs, the maximum model ID, omitted caret IDs, Delete All, one-step undo/redo and two DOCX write/read cycles preserving body text, comment tex…

title: CI: recovery pruning test retries a scan that a lock race skipped

body:
`recovery::desktop::tests::failed_pruning_cannot_push_a_record_beyond_the_discovery_limit` (from #586) failed once in a full `cargo test --workspace` run and passes on its own. The likely cause: `scan()` skips a record it can't lock, and the lock can be held for a moment by a child process that another test is spawning (it shares the descriptor until it execs). In that case `scan()` returns Ok and the assertion fails. The test now retries for up to about a second before it asserts. Product code is unchanged.

title: engine: Check spelling as you type is saved with the proofing options, so it survives a restart
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
File › Options › Proofing offered Check spelling as you type, but the checkbox was the session's live `view.proofing` flag only: nothing wrote it to `ui.json`, so every restart came back checked while the neighbouring proofing options were remembered. The setting now lives in `Prefs.check_spelling` (saved as `editing.checkSpelling`), both the checkbox and `review.proofing` keep it in step, and `apply_prefs` restores the live flag from the saved preference. The regression test sets the option, round-trips `ui.json` and asserts the box comes back unchecked.

Fixes #1792

title: engine: Update Field evaluates DOCPROPERTY against custom and built-in properties
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`references.updateFields` handled DATE/TIME, REF, TITLE, AUTHOR and NUMWORDS, but a `DOCPROPERTY <name>` field always kept its cached result, so fields showing corporate metadata froze at import time (a freshly inserted one stayed empty). Update Field now evaluates `DOCPROPERTY` against the custom properties first and the built-in ones by their English names, accepting quoted names and ignoring format switches such as `\* MERGEFORMAT`. The regression test covers a custom property behind a `MERGEFORMAT` switch and a built-in (`Title`).

Fixes #1798

title: .doc import: symbol runs read their font and character, and paragraph borders are read
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A Word 97–2003 symbol character (Insert › Symbol, e.g. Wingdings ❑) is stored as the placeholder `U+0028` plus `sprmCSymbol`, which carries the font-table index and the real character code — the .doc reader ignored it, so every symbol exported as "("; paragraph borders (`sprmPBrcTop…`) were not read at all, so a bordered block lost its box. The reader now applies `sprmCSymbol` (character + font) and maps both border storage forms (Brc80 and the newer BrcOperand with a full colour) onto the model's paragraph borders. Regression tests build both fixtures in code per the spec (no Word files committed).

Fixes #1767

title: UI: Cut publishes what it copied from the ribbon and the context menu, as Copy does
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Copy's ribbon button and context-menu item pushed the copied content to the system clipboard, but Cut's never did: the click ran `edit.cut` and dropped the result, so a paste still saw the previously copied/cut segment. Both Cut entry points now publish exactly like Copy (the keyboard's `Event::Cut` path already did), all through the same `put`/`put_result` helpers. The regression test clicks the ribbon's Cut with a selection and asserts the cut reaches the system clipboard sink.

Fixes #1710

title: Proofing: -ically adverbs such as "specifically" are no longer flagged (#1694)
author: benandez
body:
Closes #1694.

## Problem
"specifically" was flagged as misspelled, and the suggestions offered were "pacifically" and "unspecifically". English spelling recognises inflected forms through suffix rules, but its "-ly" rule only tries the stem as is (or with "-le" added), giving "specifical", which isn't a word. So any "-ically" adverb missing from the Moby word list was flagged, even though its "-ic" adjective is listed.

## Fix
`crates/proof/src/lib.rs`: one more suffix rule, "-ally" → stem (specifically → specific).

## Tests
- `proof::tests::ically_adverbs_are_known`: specifically, scientifically, automatically, dramatically and Specifically are accepted; specificaly, specifcally and zzzically are still flagged. It failed before the fix.
- Checked end to end with `wordcraft-cli run … --cmd review.issues`: no issues for "specifically", "scientifically" and "automatically".
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

## Docs
`docs/localization-parity.md`: status line and revision history.

title: proof: flag aliases, single-byte flags, ICONV, IGNORE and KEEPCASE in affix dictionaries (#735)
author: Skaywalker
body:
First step of the `affix.rs` extension offered in #735, so the Hungarian Hunspell dictionary
(`hu_HU`, Magyar Ispell) can load. The dictionary isn't bundled; WordCraft keeps reading the copy
installed on the system, as it does for Polish.

## What changes

**Reading the files** (`hunspell.rs`)
- `hu_HU.aff` says `SET UTF-8` but writes its affix flags and flag aliases as single bytes above
  0x7F, which aren't UTF-8. Hunspell reads flags byte by byte unless `FLAG UTF-8` is set, and
  the decoder now does the same: flag fields (`AF`, the flag of `PFX`/`SFX`, continuation classes,
  one-flag directives, `.dic` flags) become one char per byte, U+0000..U+00FF. Words, affixes and
  conditions are still UTF-8 and still rejected when they aren't.
- Descriptive lines (`NAME`, `HOME`, `VERSION`, `LANG`, `AM`) and trailing `# comments` are read
  leniently; `hu_HU`'s `NAME` line is ISO 8859-2.
- Dictionaries with `FLAG UTF-8` (pt_BR) and ISO 8859-2 dictionaries (pl_PL) take the same path
  as before.

**Affix engine** (`affix.rs`)
- `AF` flag aliases, in the `.dic` and in continuation classes. `AM` aliases and the
  morphological fields after a stem are skipped.
- `ICONV` (the ligatures `ﬁ`, `ﬂ`… read as their letters) and `IGNORE`.
- `KEEPCASE`: such a stem is a word only in its own letter case.
- `SUBSTANDARD` and `LEMMA_PRESENT` are accepted; they only matter for morphological generation
  and suggestions.
- Flag masks grow from 128 to 256 bits (`Mask`), enough for every single-byte flag:
  `hu_HU` uses 158 distinct flags.
- Fields split on spaces and tabs only, as in Hunspell, so a flag byte read as U+00A0 or U+0085
  isn't taken for a separator.

Compounding (`COMPOUNDFLAG`, `COMPOUNDRULE`, `ONLYINCOMPOUND`…) and `NEEDAFFIX` are still
rejected, so `hu_HU` doesn't load yet; that is the next step. With those directives removed by
hand, the dictionary loads (91,498 stems, 24,542 rules) and accepts inflected forms such as
`házakban`, `legszebb` and `olvasnánk`, and `ﬁnom` thr…

title: Formats: ODT table repeats expand, and malformed XML is an error (#1342)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
An ODT body table's `table:number-rows-repeated` and `table:number-columns-repeated` were
ignored on rows, cells and covered cells: a file where a populated row or cell is stored once
with a repeat count imported as a single row/cell, and repeated blanks shifted the cells after
them into the wrong columns. The reader now expands the counts, bounded by the document
table's own row and column limits (so hostile counts stay capped), and owes every copy of a
spanning cell its own covered columns. The ODT content pass and the spreadsheet (ODS/XLSX)
readers also ended on a malformed-XML error as if it were the end of the file, so a truncated
or corrupt part imported as a successful partial document or recipient list; they now fail the
import with a "not well-formed" error instead. Regression tests cover repeated rows, cells and
covered cells, excessive counts, and truncated XML for ODT, ODS and XLSX.
>
Fixes #1342

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Desktop update check and one-click update (Linux .deb, Windows MSI)
author: pattalkslaw-del
body:
Closes #201. Also covers the Windows and macOS side of storytold/gridcraft#859.

@vangel76 claimed #201 on Oct 10 with a notice-and-link plan. This includes that notice and adds a one-click install where the platform supports it. Happy to rework or hand off pieces if you already have work in progress.

**What it does**
- Checks for a newer release on startup (throttled, can be turned off in Options) and from File > Check for updates.
- Shows the version, release notes, and Update, Skip, Later.
- **Update** downloads the asset for the running install and verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS.txt`; it refuses on a missing or mismatched checksum.
  - Linux `.deb`: installs through `pkexec` and dpkg, then closes WordCraft; the next launch runs the new version.
  - Windows MSI: runs `msiexec` without restarting the computer, then closes WordCraft. If the installer needs a restart, WordCraft says so and waits for OK first.
  - macOS: opens the verified `.dmg`; the user drags WordCraft into Applications. No bundle replacement, no forced quit.
- Flatpak and AppImage keep their own updaters (#22). Portable, `.rpm`, and unidentified installs get the notice and a link to the release page.
- Unsaved work prompts before WordCraft closes.
- A processor with no release build (RISC-V, say) gets "no installer for this computer," never another processor's build.
- Network and install steps run off the UI thread with timeouts.

**Testing:** `cargo xtask ci` green. Offline tests cover install-kind detection, architecture matching, throttling, checksum refusal, and the installer handoffs. Docs: `docs/desktop-updates.md`.

title: Corpus: verify the PngSuite digest and unpack it without `tar` (#1357)
author: maxm11
body:
## Summary

`cargo xtask corpus --download` fetched PngSuite over plain HTTP and piped the result straight into `tar -xzf`. Nothing authenticated the download, and `tar` honors `../`, absolute paths and links in a hostile archive — so a tampered download or a compromised network could write anywhere (#1357).

This replaces that path:

- **The archive is authenticated by its published SHA-256** (`0294b244c95a8342c01b00010cf34abdcabc7c6a34fd0fe1bd963917537bfdc8`), checked before extraction; a mismatch is refused and nothing is unpacked.
- **Extraction no longer shells out to `tar`.** The archive is decompressed with `flate2` and unpacked by a small tar reader that keeps only regular files whose names are relative and stay inside the corpus directory. A member that traverses (`..`, absolute, `\`, `:`) or is not a regular file (symlink, hard link, directory) is refused before any file is written; a decompressed stream far larger than PngSuite is capped.

On HTTPS: the host serves no working TLS — every handshake, on both IPs and all TLS versions, is answered with `TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR` (checked with curl, OpenSSL, Python and Node). So the transport cannot authenticate this download, which is exactly why the digest does.

Also adds my own contributor credit entry to `contributors/people.toml` (real name and display name "Max Murphy", `sync_github_name`; only my own entry, `contributors.json` left to the maintainers' refresh).

## Tests

Unit tests in `xtask/src/corpus.rs` cover the pieces the issue asked for:

- digest mismatch / unsafe and non-regular archive members are refused (`refuses_a_traversing_member`, `a_traversing_archive_writes_nothing`, `skips_links_and_directories`, `member_paths_stay_inside_the_archive`);
- the pinned digest path is pinned by the known SHA-256 vectors (`hashes_match_the_known_sha256_vectors`);
- tar parsing and extraction, incl. GNU long names and gzip (`reads_the_regular_files_of_a_tar`, `takes_a_gnu_long_name`, `gunzips_a_gzip_stre…

title: Restrict Editing: exceptions don't open page setup or styles; tracked-changes protection keeps revisions
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #1880, refs #1327 (the section-properties part; table/row/cell properties are left for later).

## What

- **Read-only (or comments) with an editable exception.** `outside_unchanged` only compared text, run formatting and paragraph formatting outside the exceptions, so `layout.orientation`, `layout.margins`, `styles.modify` and the like ran and changed the whole document. It now also compares the last section's and every section-ending paragraph's `SectionProps`, the document defaults and the styles that existed before the command (a command may add a style, e.g. applying a built-in character style inside an exception).
- **Protected for tracked changes.** `review.accept`, `review.reject`, `review.acceptAll`, `review.rejectAll` and `review.trackChanges` are refused in `check_before`, as Word disables them while the document is protected for tracked changes. Without this, an edit could be tracked and then accepted, leaving no revision.

## Tests

Two new tests in `crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs`, both failing without the change:
- `read_only_exception_does_not_open_page_setup_or_styles`: orientation, margins and `styles.modify` are refused and the document is unchanged; a character style still applies inside the exception.
- `tracked_changes_protection_keeps_revisions`: Accept/Reject (single and all) and the Track Changes toggle are refused after a tracked insertion; the document is unchanged.

`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` pass.

CLI check with the repro files from the issue: before, the three commands write the file; after:

```
layout.orientation: only the editable regions of this protected document can change
styles.modify: only the editable regions of this protected document can change
review.acceptAll: changes to this document are tracked
```

title: Length fields show their unit in the interface language (#1734)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1734

## What changes

Length fields and length labels (Page Setup margins, Paragraph, Tabs, the ribbon's Layout fields, Table Layout cell size …) took their unit suffix straight from `Unit::suffix()`, so `cm`, `mm` and `pi` were never translated. `pt` was already translated through the catalog where it is written by hand (`tl!("pt")`, `пт` in Russian).

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a side pane in WordCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the pane says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside WordCraft and names this app's world — headings and paragraph styles, the navigation pane, lists and tables, find and replace, track changes, comments, page setup, docx and pdf — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (polish this text, summarise, check grammar and style, structure a document, change the tone) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent menu or style names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept, copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the Arabic interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.

title: Layout: floats in table cells are not pushed up by align center/bottom (#1887)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1887

Cause: inside a table cell `float_rect` has no `PageFrame`, so the vertical reference area fell back to `(y0, 0.0)`, a zero-height box. `align_in` then computed `start + (0 - h) / 2` (center) or `start - h` (bottom), pushing the object up by half its height or more.

Fix: without a frame, `float_rect` no longer applies a vertical alignment; the object starts at the anchor line (like `box_float_table_rect` does for floating tables in cells). Aligning within the cell box proper would need the cell height, which is not known at that point.

Test: `a_centred_float_in_a_cell_is_not_pushed_above_its_anchor_line` (1x1 table, square-wrapped 100x200 pt shape, positionV relativeFrom=margin, align center and bottom). Without the fix it fails (top at y = -2.65 pt); with it, it passes. `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout`, clippy and fmt are clean.

Note: open PR #1666 also edits `float_rect` (h_align handling and PageFrame); this diff is a three-line change at the end of the function and should merge with little conflict.

title: Add wordcraft-hub: the CraftHub client path (the v3 adapter, spec §3.6 phase C / §18.4 row 2)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

`wordcraft-hub` — the app-side binding that speaks the generalized collaboration core ([`craft-collab`](https://github.com/hasan-sdaif/crafthub), extracted from figcraft's proven `figcraft-collab` and proposed as `storytold/craft-libs#128`). Nothing here changes user-visible behavior. The session wiring (a v3 `NetLink` behind the app's `crafthub` feature flag, default off) lands as the pilot follow-up once this contract is reviewed.

## The honest map

WordCraft's real model is stories of blocks: a `body` plus secondary `parts` (headers, footers, notes, comments, text boxes), each holding paragraphs and tables. The adapter maps exactly that:

- **Stories** hang under the root, one object each; a part's `partKind` and `textBody` ride as properties.
- **Paragraphs and tables** are objects under their story, ordered by fractional sibling keys.
- A paragraph syncs `text` (**RGA**), `runs`, `props`, `mark`, `objects`, `section` — with the compile-time guard that a new saved field must decide how it syncs. `rev` is a process-local cache counter and never syncs.

- The style sheet syncs per entry with its order; the comments map per entry. `media` bytes never ride a batch (the asset channel owns them); `passthrough` parts stay local.

title: Draw EMF text records (EXTTEXTOUTW) in metafile pictures
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1764

## Cause
The EMF reader had no handler for the text records (EXTCREATEFONTINDIRECTW, SETTEXTALIGN, SETTEXTCOLOR, EXTTEXTOUTW). They fell through to the catch-all arm that skips unknown records without a warning. The picture model also had only path and bitmap items, so a metafile's text never reached the PDF writer or the rasteriser and only the lines were drawn.

## Fix
The metafile crate now tracks the selected font, text colour and alignment (including through SaveDC/RestoreDC) and turns EXTTEXTOUTW into a new `Item::Text`. The item carries the reference point, font height, angle and per-character dx advances, and a shared `Text::layout` places shaped glyphs from font metrics. The PDF writer draws these runs as embedded-font text, so they are in the text layer, and the rasteriser fills the glyph outlines.

## Verified
- Regression tests `metafile_text_records_are_drawn_as_text`, `metafile_text_records_are_painted`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-pdf -p wordcraft-render --lib metafile_text_records`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
EMF+ records inside EMR_COMMENT are still not parsed: EMF+ dual pictures are drawn from their GDI fallback records, whose EXTTEXTOUTW text is now drawn. Not handled: EXTTEXTOUTA, SMALLTEXTOUT, glyph-index strings (ETO_GLYPH_INDEX), WMF text records, the ETO_OPAQUE background fill and synthetic bold/italic.

_Requested by **Dima**_

## What was wrong
Review › Compare could produce a result that didn't resolve back to either document:

title: File open: check regular file and size before reading, on native and web (#1333)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1333, together with #1786.

## What was wrong
Some file-reading paths read a file before checking its size or type:
- **Native:** `open_path_in`, `read_file_capped` and `read_file_head` checked the size the file reported and then read with no bound and no check that it was a regular file. A named pipe or device could hang the app or stream forever. A file growing while it was read could go past the limit.
- **Web:** dropped and picked files were read whole before any size check. Stored fonts were all loaded into memory at once.

## What changed
- **Native:** one helper does all of these reads.
  - It requires a regular file, checking both the path and the opened handle.
  - It checks the size against the limit, then reads at most the limit plus one byte, so a file that grew is refused rather than truncated.
  - Errors name the file and the limit ("2 GB").
  - `io::read_file` is left to #1786 ("read_file reads only a bounded regular file"), which now also gets the bounded read through `read_file_capped`.
  - The 2 GB limit is a typed `MAX_OPEN_BYTES` constant, which supersedes #1259. #1786 will have a trivial conflict where both insert a constant; its `MAX_READ_FILE` can be merged into `MAX_OPEN_BYTES` then.
- **Web (`apps/wordcraft-web`):**
  - A file's `size` is checked before reading on the drop, picker and paste paths. Pictures get the picture limit, fonts the font limit and everything else the document limit, chosen by the last extension.
  - Dropped files are read one at a time.
  - Stored fonts load one per key.
  - The picker needs rfd's `file-handle-inner` feature for the size check.

author: dkhlapov
body:

_Requested by **Dima**_

## What was wrong

title: DOCX: embedded-object preservation reports dropped resources (#1343)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1343

## What was wrong
DOCX embedded objects (charts, diagrams, OLE objects and other kept parts) were preserved on a best-effort basis that didn't report what it dropped:
- The reader counted an object as kept once its root part survived. A missing descendant, a part over the budget, or relationships cut by the cap were only logged.
- The writer could leave out descendant relationships and still write the root.
- A successful open or save never told the caller that an object came through incomplete.

## What changed
- **Reader:** the kept-parts manifest records a note for each part that can't be kept, with a kind and a reason: the part is missing, over the part limit, cut by the relationship limit, has an unreadable name, or the root failed. title: Fonts: bounded family caches; math follows font changes (#1354)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1354

## What was wrong
Two caches in the fonts crate had problems:
- The text font-family cache (`word.rs`) kept every family name ever asked for, with no limit. A document, or many documents, naming thousands of missing fonts grew memory without bound.
- The math font cache (`math.rs` `resolve_math`) was never refreshed. If you installed or removed a font, equations kept using the font they had found before.

## What changed
- **Text family cache:** capped at 4096 entries, the same cap as the existing East Asian fallback cache, and cleared when full. A name longer than 256 bytes is still resolved but not cached. Normal documents never reach the cap; at worst, a huge one runs as if it had no cache.
- **Math resolution:** now keyed by the font database's generation, which goes up whenever a font is added or removed. Installing or removing a font makes equations look up their font again. The math cache is capped at 1024 entries.
- Caches keyed by face id are left as they are. Face ids come from a counter that only goes up, so they are never reused and can't go stale.
- Docs: ROADMAP.md progress log.

## Tests
- `wordcraft-fonts`: 3 new regression tests failed before the fix and pass now:
  - many distinct missing family names keep the cache within its cap;
  - over-long names aren't cached;
  - the math install/remove test, described next.
- The install/remove test does what a user would do: it resolves a math family, installs a font with that name (a renamed Source Sans 3 with a minimal test-only MATH table), checks equations now use it, removes it, and checks they stop. Without the generation check it fails ("DejaVu Math TeX Gyre" vs "Zz Math Gen 1").
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Clamp negative margins before checking they leave text room
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/page.rs:392 (margins) and :424 (margins_fit)` (no existing issue): layout.margins accepts a negative margin to hide an oversized one, leaving a page with no text room.

## Cause
`margins_fit` added up the raw margin values, including negative ones, and `layout.margins` only clamped each margin to 0 when storing it. A negative margin could cancel an oversized one in the sum (top 2000, bottom -2000), so the check passed and the section was saved with a top margin taller than the page.

## Fix
`margins_fit` now treats each margin and the gutter as at least 0 before it checks the sums, which matches how the values are stored. `layout.margins` and Page Setup both call `margins_fit`, so both now return the 'margins leave no room for text' error for these values.

## Verified
- Regression test `layout_margins_negative_cannot_hide_an_oversized_margin`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib layout_margins_negative_cannot_hide_an_oversized_margin`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Negative margins are still stored as 0 as before. `layout.size` and the Page Setup dialog code are unchanged.

title: Double-click switches between header and footer editing
author: Silvertree2010

The canvas only entered header/footer editing on a double-click in a margin band when the caret was in the body (`story == StoryRef::Body`). While a header was being edited, a double-click in the footer band (or the reverse) skipped both the enter and the leave branches. The press handler then selected a word in the header.

## Fix
A new `hf_enter` condition is true when the double-click lands in a header/footer band and the caret is either in the body or in the other kind of part (header vs footer). Several things are not changed. Double-clicking a band from inside a text box in the header or footer still does nothing. Switching parts doesn't remove a header or footer that was just created and left empty; that still happens only on closing. Two parts of the issue no longer reproduce on main and are not touched: entering a header/footer that doesn't exist yet, and reaching the footer from the body. title: Web: stored fonts are saved when the IndexedDB transaction completes (#1362)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1362

**Depends on #1926 (#1333).** This branch is stacked on it because both change `font_store.rs`. Until #1926 merges, this PR's diff also shows #1926's commits. Only the last commit, "Web: font saves count as stored only when the IndexedDB transaction completes", is this PR's change.

## What was wrong
The web app's stored-font `store`/`forget` returned as soon as the IndexedDB *request* succeeded. A transaction can still abort after that (quota, a version change, …), and then the font silently isn't stored and the caller's error log never fires.

## What changed
- **New `apps/wordcraft-web/src/write_gate.rs`**, built for wasm32 and for tests:
  - `WriteGate` turns IndexedDB events into one verdict. A request success alone is still pending. Only the transaction's `complete` means stored. Abort, a transaction error or a request error mean failed, even if `complete` follows. The first final verdict sticks.
  - `WriteQueue` runs one write at a time, in call order, so the last store/forget for a font wins.
- **`apps/wordcraft-web/src/web/font_store.rs`:**
  - `store`/`forget` queue a write. A single worker runs each one in its own readwrite transaction, with handlers on the request's success/error and the transaction's complete/abort/error.
  - A save resolves only when stored. Failures are logged as before, and the queue moves on.
  - The load path from #1926 is untouched. No new web-sys features.
- **Docs:** ROADMAP.md.

## Tests
- 8 native tests of the gate and queue the browser code uses:
  - request success then complete gives stored;
  - success then abort fails;
  - a transaction error fails;

title: Web: input-method rewrites erase before retyping, so non-Latin typing no longer repeats (part of #1480)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Part of #1480. This fixes the repeated text; letters can still come out reordered in Chrome (see "Not fixed" below).

## What was wrong
In the web build, eframe's hidden text field keeps its value between keystrokes. On each input it sends `ImeEvent::DeleteSurrounding { before_chars, after_chars }` for what changed, followed by the new text. WordCraft ignored `DeleteSurrounding` and only typed the new text, so typing `ab` then `мир` produced `abмиabмриabм`.

## What changed
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs`:** `DeleteSurrounding` is handled. It erases `before_chars` and `after_chars` characters (Unicode scalar values, eframe's unit) around the caret through `text.backspace`, the command Backspace uses, so Track Changes and protection apply. Then the following text is typed.
  - The erase stays within the paragraph, and huge or hostile counts can't panic, join paragraphs or remove list numbers.
  - It does nothing when there's a selection or inside an equation.
- **The rewritten text keeps its formatting:** a bold `helo` corrected to `hello` stays bold.
- **Undo:** the rewrite joins the typing undo group, which stays open, so one Undo takes back the typing and its corrections together (`Session::continue_typing`).
- **Overtype:** the replacement text never overtypes.
- **After AutoCorrect or AutoFormat changes the text** (`(c)`→`©`, lists, dashes), the web build asks eframe to empty its hidden field for one frame (`should_interrupt_composition`), and only when nothing is being composed. Later `DeleteSurrounding` counts then can't reach past the change.

- This should also make Backspace and keyboard corrections work on mobile browsers. That's untested.

title: DOCX: mixed Hebrew/Latin keeps its order in Word (runs split by direction, w:rtl and language) (#1543)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1543

## What was wrong
In a right-to-left paragraph with Hebrew plus embedded Latin, numbers, punctuation or an email address, WordCraft wrote each run with no `w:rtl`. WordCraft orders text with the Unicode bidi algorithm (UAX #9), whatever the run direction. Word orders each run by its `w:rtl` flag (ECMA-376 §17.3.2.30). So Word laid the Hebrew out left to right, and the groups on either side of the Latin text swapped places.

## What changed
- **`crates/docx/src/write/bidi.rs` (new):** in a paragraph with right-to-left characters, every run with no direction of its own is split wherever its UAX #9 level changes between even and odd. It uses the same bidi levels as layout. Right-to-left pieces get `w:rtl` and a `w:lang w:bidi` matching their script: he-IL for Hebrew, ar-SA for Arabic.
  - Runs that already have a direction or language are written unchanged, and paragraphs without right-to-left text are byte-identical.
  - A tracked formatting change gets the same direction and language on its "before" copy, so Word shows no false formatting revision.
- **Engine:** text that is typed or inserted no longer takes the caret run's `rtl`. Its direction comes from its own letters, which is how WordCraft already displays it. Without this, Latin typed into a reopened Hebrew document would be saved right-to-left.
  - Pasting with source formatting keeps the pasted run's explicit `rtl`.
  - Reveal Formatting still shows the caret run's direction.
- **Docs:** file-format-parity.md (bidi rows), typing-parity.md (Text direction note), ROADMAP.md.

## Checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4 (user's Mac, 2026-10-15)
- **Before this change:** paragraph 1 was laid out left to right, and lines 3 and 6 had their groups reversed.
- **After:** every line matches WordCraft's order. That covers line 3 (`עברית WordCraft 2026 ואחריה עוד עברית.`) and line 6 (`לפני (ABC 123) אחרי; דוא״ל test@example.c…

title: Equations: a script runs until a space or operator, as in Word (V_dd, x_2a) (#1609)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1609. #1623 already fixed the subscript-box case; this fixes typing the script directly.

## What was wrong
After `_` or `^`, the equation parser read a script as one letter or one number. Typing `V_dd` and then Space gave V with subscript d, followed by an ordinary "d". A code comment said this was Word's behaviour, but it isn't.

## What Word does
Checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4 on the user's Mac, 2026-10-15. A script continues until a space or an operator, and letters, digits and Greek letters all continue it:
- `V_dd` gives subscript "dd". `V_(dd)` gives the same result, and the parentheses vanish.
- `x^ab` gives superscript "ab".
- `x_2a` gives "2a", `x_a2` gives "a2", and `x_αβ` gives "αβ".
- `x_i y` gives subscript i, then y on the baseline. `a_i b_j` gives two separate scripts.
- `x_max` and `x_(max)` show an upright "max", because it is a function name.
- Word's Linear format writes these as `V_dd`, `x_i y` and so on.

## What changed
- `crates/doc/src/math_linear.rs`: a script or limit operand is the whole run of letters and digits (Greek included). A run that starts with digits continues into letters, so `x_2a` works; `x_10` and `x_2.5` still work. The run ends at a space or an operator.
- `crates/doc/src/math.rs` `to_linear`:
  - multi-letter scripts are written bare (`V_dd`), as Word does;
  - a space goes after a bare script or limit when a letter or digit follows (`x_i y`), so converting to linear text and back no longer pulls the next letter into the script; repeated round trips don't add spaces;
  - known function names in a script stay upright and are written bare, and other upright text keeps its parentheses.
- The misleading code comments are corrected.

title: DOCX: a field nested in another field code survives saving (#1671)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1671

## What was wrong
When a field's code contains another field (`{ IF { REF amount } = 0 "…" "…" }`, `{ = { REF amount } + 5 }`), the DOCX reader added the inner field's cached result to the outer field's code. Saving then wrote `IF 0 = 0 …` and `= 0 + 5`, and the nested field was silently gone.

## Design
@Hamza0101 laid out two options in the issue, and no maintainer has picked one. This PR takes the conservative one: keep the nesting for round trips without modelling nested fields.
- `InlineObject::Field` gains an additive `code_xml: String` (serde default, omitted when empty, like `form`). It holds the field code as WordprocessingML runs, with the nested fields complete. `instr` keeps the flattened string, so every existing reader of field codes is unchanged.
- The document model is saved only as JSON (serde), and `crates/docbin` is the .doc reader. The new field is backward compatible both ways.
- Nested fields are not evaluated:
  - Update Field keeps their cached result and their `w:dirty` flag.
  - Check Compatibility says so, in every story.
  - SEQ/STYLEREF with a nested code are still evaluated on the flattened code, so SEQ numbering counts them.

## What changed
- **Reader (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`):** when an inner field ends inside an outer field's code, the outer field's `code_xml` is built from the code so far plus the inner field's full markup. Nested fields keep their own `w:fldLock` and `w:dirty`. Nesting is kept only when every piece shares the field's own revision and has no tracked formatting change. Otherwise it falls back to the old flattened code, and the docs say so.
- **Writer (`crates/docx/src/write/story.rs`):**
  - `code_xml` is written in place of the instrText run, inside the field's own revision and run formatting, so bold and tracked insertion or deletion save correctly. Under a deletion, `w:t`→`w:delText` and `w:instrText`→`…

title: Picture brightness, contrast and transparency from DOCX: VML washout, a:lum, a:alphaModFix (#1711, #1766)
author: mmazzieri
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @mmazzieri._

Fixes #1711. Fixes #1766.

Pictures keep the colour corrections their file gives them, instead of being drawn at full colour.

## What changes
- **Model:** `InlineObject::Image` gains `fx: PicFx { bright, contrast, transparency }`. The values are in OOXML units and clamped. The field is skipped in JSON when it is the identity, so existing documents are unchanged.
- **DOCX read:**
  - `a:lum` (`bright`/`contrast`) and `a:alphaModFix` inside `a:blip`.
  - VML `v:imagedata gain`/`blacklevel`, as used by Word's picture watermark "Washout". These are 16.16 fixed point (`19661f`) or decimals.
  - Word 2003 XML too.
- **Draw:**
  - On screen, the correction is applied to the straight RGBA pixels, and the pixmap cache key includes it.
  - In PDF, a picture whose pixels change is decoded, adjusted and embedded with Flate, once per media and fx; the JPEG passthrough is kept when only transparency is set.
  - Transparency is folded into the draw opacity, so it reaches the PDF as an ExtGState `ca`.
- **Save:**
  - DOCX writes `a:alphaModFix` and `a:lum` in `a:blip`. VML pictures are saved as DrawingML.
  - Word 2003 XML writes `gain`/`blacklevel`. Transparency can't be expressed there and is dropped; the docs say so.
- **Picture commands:** Corrections, Transparency and Color › Washout replace the file's values instead of stacking on them. The other Color modes leave the file's values alone. Reset Picture discards all corrections, as Word does.

## How the curve was measured
The curve comes from Word's own PDF export of a synthetic grey and colour ramp: 20 `a:lum` cases and 6 VML cases, exported through COM. Nothing produced by Word is committed. Per channel:

`y = s·(x − 127.5) + 127.5 + 127.5·b·(1 + s)`, with `s = 1 + c` for c ≤ 0 and `1/(1 − c)` for c > 0.

VML `gain` is `s` and `blacklevel` is `b/2`, so Washout (`gain 0.30`, `blacklevel 0.35`) is `a:lum 70000/−70000`.

title: Italian grammar: c'è, ha/ho/hanno and miei/mie rules, q/c suggestions, and review fixes to #1585
author: fabiodalez-dev
body:
Follow-up to #1585 (Italian grammar rules by @lupant), with the follow-ups @D13GOOOO listed in their review there and a native speaker's review fixes. I'm a native Italian speaker.

## New rules (`crates/proof/src/it/grammar.rs`), all working with no dictionary installed

| Wrong | Fix | Left alone |
|---|---|---|
| `ce un problema`, `Ce una soluzione`, `non ce nessuno` | `c'è` | `ce lo`, `ce la`, `ce ne`, `ce l'ho` |
| `lui a detto`, `chi a vinto`, `non a capito` | `ha` | `vado a Roma`, `non a caso`, `lui a piedi`, `a detta di tutti` |
| `io o mangiato` | `ho` | `uno o due`, `io o te` |
| `loro anno finito` | `hanno` | `l'anno passato`, `ogni anno fatto di…` |
| `i mie amici`, `dei tue libri` | `miei`, `tuoi` | `i miei`, `sono mie` |
| `le tuoi cose`, `nelle suoi parole` | `tue`, `sue` | `le mie`, `le sue` |

They stay conservative, as #1585's rules do. `ce` → `c'è` only fires before an article or an indefinite pronoun. `a`/`o`/`anno` → `ha`/`ho`/`hanno` only between a subject or clitic pronoun and a past participle (`-ato`/`-uto`/`-ito` and the common irregular ones: `detto`, `fatto`, `scritto`, `preso`…). The possessive rules only fire right after an article.

## Suggestions (`crates/proof/src/it/suggest.rs`)

The `it_IT` dictionary's `REP` table lacks the `q`/`c` slips, so `squola` got `scuola` third, after `suola` and `stuola`. A small built-in table now ranks them as known confusions, ahead of one-letter typos: `squola` → `scuola`, `aqua` → `acqua`, `coscenza` → `coscienza`, `efficente` → `efficiente`.

## Review fixes to #1585's rules

- The `un`/`un'` messages say "parola" instead of "nome", as D13GOOOO suggested: in *un altro* and *un'altra*, *altro* is an adjective or pronoun, not a noun.
- `buon'anno` → `buon anno`: *buon* never takes an apostrophe before a masculine word, and this is one of the most common slips there is. Only the masculine direction: before a feminine word *buona* is the usual form, so `buon amica` is left alone.

title: macOS: Option+Shift+- types an em dash outside Outline view (#1933)
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
Fixes #1933.

## What happened

On macOS, Option+Shift+- types an em dash (—). WordCraft typed nothing.

Option is Alt to egui, so the key arrives as Alt+Shift+-. That combo is bound to `outline.collapse` (Word's Collapse), which only runs in Outline view. In any other view:

1. `keymap.resolve` finds `outline.collapse`; it doesn't check the command's `when` condition.
2. `Session::run` refuses it (`only in Outline view`), but `dispatch` still returns `true`.
3. `canvas_events` sets `swallow_text`, so the `—` that macOS sends next is dropped.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs`)

In `dispatch`, on macOS, when Option is held without ⌘ or Control and the bound command can't run right now (its `enabled` check returns a reason), the key isn't treated as a shortcut. The character macOS composed is typed instead.

In Outline view, Option+Shift+- still collapses and types nothing. Windows and Linux are unchanged: Alt doesn't type characters there, so a refused Alt shortcut still swallows the key.

This covers any Option shortcut whose command is limited to a view or context, not only this one.

## Tests

- `keys::tests::option_shift_dash_types_an_em_dash_outside_outline_view` (macOS, through `canvas_events`): Option+Shift+- with its `—` text types `—` in Print Layout, and types nothing in Outline view. It fails without the change (`left: ""`, `right: "—"`).
- `docs/typing-parity.md`: Outline keys row, status line, revision history.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.

## Checked in the app

I tested a release build on macOS (ABC layout), pressing the keys through the system's own keyboard events (Option down, Shift down, `-`, then releases):

| Build | View | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | Print Layout | 5 presses, nothing typed (plain `x` and `y` typed fine) |
| this branch | Print Layout | each press types `—` |
| this branch | Outline | 3 presses, nothing typed |

title: Fonts: the font scan leaves out faces with no outline or color bitmap tables
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

The system font scan (`file_face_names` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`) also catalogs faces with none of the tables skrifa reads glyph outlines from (`glyf`, `CFF `, `CFF2`, `VARC`) and none of the color bitmap tables the renderer draws (`sbix`, `CBDT`).

On macOS 27.0.1 the scan of `/System/Library/Fonts` catalogs "GB18030 Bitmap" (`Supplemental/NISC18030.ttf`), and the font list (`FontDb::families_in`, built from `FontDb::families()`) includes it. The face stores its glyphs as `bdat` bitmaps and maps 27,544 characters. `FontDb::outline` returns an empty path for each of them, and `has_color_glyphs()` is false. The renderer draws none of them (`crates/render/src/lib.rs:750-770`).

## Fix

`file_face_names` leaves out a face whose table directory has none of those six tables. It reuses `OUTLINE_TABLES` from the interface CJK fallback (#1250). With the check, the scan of `/System/Library/Fonts` on the same Mac catalogs 2,607 faces instead of 2,608, and "GB18030 Bitmap" is the one left out.

VectorCraft's font scan checks the four outline tables (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/781), and the open https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/443 adds the same check to DesignCraft. The check in WordCraft's `file_face_names` also accepts `sbix` and `CBDT`, which the renderer draws (#1504). Noto Color Emoji (`NotoColorEmoji.ttf` from googlefonts/noto-emoji), one of the `SYSTEM_FALLBACKS`, has `CBDT` and no outline table, and the scan lists it.

## Test

`faces_without_outlines_are_not_cataloged` (`crates/fonts/src/tests_sysfonts.rs`) renames the `glyf` table record of a copy of the bundled Source Sans 3 Bold to `hvgl` in memory. The copy still maps `A`, and skrifa reads no outline for it. The scan lists no face for the file and, in a collection with a Semibold, lists only the Semibold. Without the check the test fails at `assert!(file_face_names(&dir.join("Sub/Sysfont-Bold.TTF")).is_empty())`.

title: PDF tests read ActualText spans, so RTL extraction no longer depends on the installed Arabic font (#1773)
author: Sriram-PR
body:
Fixes #1773.

`right_to_left_text_extracts_in_logical_order` fails on Linux machines where Noto Naskh Arabic is the first Arabic font in `RTL_FALLBACKS`. The exported PDF is fine. The problem is in the test helper.

Noto Naskh draws a dotted letter as a dotless body plus a separate dot glyph, and other letters reuse the same body. ToUnicode can only map a glyph to one string, so when a cluster can't be spelled from its glyphs' entries, krilla wraps it in an ActualText span. `stream_glyphs` only looked at ToUnicode, so inside the span it took the body glyph's own entry as well as the cluster's text. On my machine that turned مَرْحَبًا into مَرْحَببًا. rabis7575 got السالم for السلام, which looks like the same thing with their Noto Naskh build. Vazirmatn draws these letters as single glyphs, so the span never came up where the test was written.

I checked the same PDF in other extractors. PDFium (pypdfium2), poppler (`pdftotext`) and mupdf all read the span and give ب once. pdf.js doesn't use ActualText, so it does show the doubled letter. It also outputs U+0003 for the dot glyph, which has no ToUnicode entry. That part is down to how krilla writes ToUnicode, so I've left it out of this PR.

Changes, all test-only in `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs`:
- `stream_glyphs` pre-scans each page's BMC/BDC operators for `/ActualText`. Inside a span, the first glyph gets the span's text and the rest get none, which is how PDFium and poppler read it.
- New `stream_glyphs_read_actual_text` test. It draws one bundled Source Sans 3 glyph twice with the texts "A" and "B", which makes krilla write an ActualText span, so it works whatever fonts are installed. It reads `["A", "A"]` without the change.

Testing: `cargo test -p wordcraft-pdf` passes (37 tests), including all four RTL tests, on Fedora 44 with Noto Naskh Arabic. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-pdf --all-targets -D warnings` are clean. I didn't run `cargo xtask wasm` because the change is test-only.

title: Escape block syntax after manual line breaks in Markdown export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:1222` (no existing issue): Markdown export: lines after a manual line break aren't escaped, so a paragraph comes back as a list or heading.

## Cause
Markdown export writes a manual line break as a trailing backslash plus newline, but `escape_line_start` only escaped block syntax at the start of the whole paragraph. A line after a break that started with `- `, `1. `, `# `, `---`, `==` or `--` was read back as a list item, heading, thematic break or setext underline, so the paragraph was split or lost text.

## Fix
A new `escape_lines` helper runs `escape_line_start` on every line after a manual break. Plain paragraphs, quotes and list items now use it. List items are escaped before the continuation indent is added. A line made only of hyphens (like `--`) is now also escaped because it would otherwise be read as a setext underline.

## Verified
- Regression tests `lines_after_line_break_stay_in_paragraph`, `lines_after_line_break_stay_in_list_item_and_quote`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib lines_after_line_break`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Title paragraphs still join their lines with spaces, and code spans in list items are unchanged.

title: Read ^0nnn character codes 128-159 as Windows-1252 characters
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/find_pattern.rs:97` (no existing issue): Find: ^0nnn character codes (e.g. ^0151 for an em dash) are searched as literal text instead of the character.

## Cause
`numeric_code` passed the decimal value of `^nnn`/`^0nnn` straight to `char::from_u32`. For 128–159 this gives C1 control characters (e.g. `^0151` became U+0097). The control filter rejected these, so the code was searched for, or inserted, as the literal text `^0151`.

## Fix
Added an `ansi` helper that maps codes 128–159 to their Windows-1252 characters (151 to U+2014 em dash, 128 to U+20AC € and so on). `numeric_code` uses it for `^nnn`/`^0nnn` codes, but not for `^unnnn` codes. This covers Find, wildcard Find and Replace with, since all three go through `numeric_code`.

## Verified
- Regression test `ansi_codes_128_to_159_are_windows_1252`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib ansi_codes_128_to_159_are_windows_1252`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`^unnnn` Unicode codes still use the Unicode value as is. The five undefined Windows-1252 slots (129, 141, 143, 144, 157) and every code outside 128–159 behave as before.

title: Tables: a header's or footer's tables resize with the mouse (#1930)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1930.

Tables in a header or footer couldn't be resized. The table mouse looked only at the cells the page draws in its body (`Page::items`), while the layout draws a header's and footer's tables in `Page::header` / `Page::footer`. So their column and row borders, the resize handle and double-click AutoFit didn't react, the rulers showed no table markers, and Table Layout › Cell Size found no drawn cell: it showed a 0 height for a row without a set height, which its box raised to its 0.02" minimum and wrote to the row as soon as the tab was shown.

**What changes**
- `cmd::table_resize::Layer` (`Body` / `HeaderFooter`) says which part of the page the mouse reaches: the header's and footer's tables while one of them is being edited, the rest of the page's otherwise, i.e. whatever isn't dimmed on screen. `Layer::editing` is the caret's layer (for a caret in a text box, the layer the box is in).
- `cell_boxes`, `tables_on`, `resize_target` and `table_under` take the layer. `table.resizeDrag` and `table.fitColumn` use `Layer::editing`, so they behave the same headless (MCP/CLI): put the caret in the header first (`insert.editHeader`). Their params docs say so.
- UI: the resize arrow, the drag and its preview, the handle and the ruler markers (`table_ruler::cells`) follow the same rule; Cell Size looks for the caret's cell in the header and footer too.

title: File › Close closes the document and keeps the window (#1712)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #1712. This replaces #1725, which @Silvertree2010 closed so this branch could go in. Thanks!

## What was wrong

File › Close (Mod+W, Mod+F4) quit the whole app. `file.close` pushed a `close` UI request, and `handle_request` turned every such request into `quit_requested = true`, which is the same thing the window's close button does. In Word, Close closes the document and the window stays.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, no engine change)

`WordApp::execute` now handles `file.close` itself (`close_document`):

- After the usual Save / Don't Save / Cancel, the document is replaced by the placeholder blank document that marks "no document open" (#1129), and the Backstage closes. The window then shows no page, the ribbon is greyed out but for Help, and File › New or Open goes on from there, as in Word after closing its last document.
- The window's close button (`close_requested`) passes `{"quit": true}`, so it still asks first and then quits. The parameter travels with the prompt's pending command, so a Cancel leaves no state behind.
- With no document open, Close has nothing to close and does nothing. The window's close button still quits from there.
- The engine's `file.close` is untouched. That keeps this PR clear of #1391's `force` guard, which is now on `main`. That guard still applies: a programmatic close of unsaved work needs `force`, and then closes the document rather than the app.

## Tests

- `tests::close_asks_then_closes_the_document_and_keeps_the_window`: Cancel keeps the document. Don't Save closes it and the window stays. Closing the empty window asks nothing, a second Close does nothing, and File › New goes on.
- `tests::window_close_asks_first`, unchanged: the close button still asks, then quits.
- The tests that read `quit_requested` as "Close went through" now check that the document closed and the window stayed: the Backstage Close tests, the save prompt's Enter, arrow and focus tests, Save As then continue, and #1391's two progra…

title: Rendering and PDF check image limits before allocating (#1321)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1321

## What changed
- **New `geom::pixels`** (shared by render and pdf): `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` (512 MiB), `MAX_RASTER_PIXELS` (100M), checked `rgba_bytes`, `decode_fits` and `fit_pixels`.

title: Zotero bridge edits respect protection and tracked changes (#1323)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1323.

Before: the Zotero bridge edited the document model directly. Inserting, refreshing, converting or removing citations, bibliographies and Zotero preferences skipped Restrict Editing, content-control locks and Track Changes. So Zotero could change a read-only document, and its edits never became revisions that Reject could undo.

After: every Zotero call that changes the document runs through a new engine entry, `Session::guarded_edit`. It applies the same rules as normal commands and is one transaction: a refused call puts back the document, the selection, undo and the bridge's field ids.
- **Read-only and comments-only documents:** Zotero edits are refused, except inside the editable regions the user may change.
- **Forms protection:** edits are allowed only inside fillable content controls.
- **Locked content controls:** edits there are refused.
- **Track Changes, or the "tracked changes" protection:** Zotero's inserts and deletions are recorded as revisions, so Reject All restores the original text and Accept All keeps Zotero's text.

**Tests** (`crates/zotero/src/tests.rs`, real bridge calls; all 8 failed before the fix): `read_only_protection_refuses_every_zotero_edit`, `comments_protection_refuses_every_zotero_edit`, `read_only_exception_takes_a_citation_but_the_rest_refuses_one`, `forms_protection_refuses_zotero_edits_outside_fillable_controls`, `locked_content_controls_refuse_zotero_edits`, `track_changes_records_zotero_edits_as_revisions`, `tracked_changes_protection_records_zotero_edits_as_revisions`, `tracked_inserted_text_never_takes_a_deletion_mark`. `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed.
