title: fix(formats): support borderless and bordered tables in LaTeX import and export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In LaTeX export (`crates/formats/src/latex.rs`), `Writer::table` hardcoded vertical rules `|` in column specs and horizontal lines `\hline` between all rows, forcing visible borders even when tables were explicitly borderless (`t.borderless == true`).
In LaTeX import, `table()` hardcoded `borderless: false` for all tables regardless of whether the `tabular` spec or body contained any vertical rules (`|`) or horizontal rules (`\hline`, `\cline`, `\toprule`, etc.), causing borderless LaTeX tables to be assigned a grid style upon import.

### Solution
1. In `Writer::table` (export):
   - Check `t.borderless`: if true, generate column spec without `|` separators (e.g. `p{88pt} p{188pt}`) and omit `\hline` between rows and around multicolumn spans.
   - If false, retain the bordered tabular layout (`|p{...}|` and `\hline`).
2. In `table()` (import):
   - Inspect the column spec and row commands for any rule indicators (`|`, `\hline`, `\cline`, `\toprule`, `\midrule`, `\bottomrule`).
   - If no rules are found, set `borderless: true` on the parsed `FTable`.
3. Added unit tests verifying:
   - Exported borderless tables omit `\hline` and column-spec `|` rules.
   - Borderless and bordered tables round-trip through LaTeX while maintaining their respective borderless/bordered styles.

title: fix(docx): support preset/system colors, tint/shade modifiers, and default outline width in WordArt
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In DOCX WordArt text effects reader (`crates/docx/src/read/wordart.rs`):
1. `color()` only matched `w14:srgbClr` and `w14:schemeClr`. When effects used `w14:prstClr` (preset color) or `w14:sysClr` (system color), `color()` returned `None`, dropping the fill, glow, shadow, or outline.
2. `w14:tint` and `w14:shade` color modifiers were ignored, failing to adjust the base color towards white or black.
3. In `w14:textOutline`, if the optional width attribute `w14:w` was omitted, the reader returned `0.0` pt width instead of the default 0.75 pt, preventing the outline from rendering.

### Solution
1. In `crates/docx/src/read/wordart.rs`:
   - Updated `color()` to recognize `w14:prstClr` and `w14:sysClr`, resolving them via `super::drawing_color::preset_color`.
   - Handled `w14:tint` and `w14:shade` modifiers using `super::drawing_color::mix`.
   - Added `emu_or` helper so `w14:textOutline` defaults `w14:w` to 0.75 pt when omitted.
   - Handled `w14:alpha` whether placed directly as a modifier on the color element or on the parent effect.
2. In `crates/docx/src/read/drawing_color.rs`:
   - Exposed `pub(crate) fn mix` for sharing color tint/shade calculations.
3. Added unit tests for:
   - Default 0.75 pt outline width when `w14:w` is omitted.
   - Preset color resolution in fills and glow effects.
   - Tint and shade modifier calculations on WordArt colors.

title: RTF import: heading and code formatting compared with the file's own stylesheet (gap 19 follow-up)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Follow-up to #2088 (gap 19, RTF formatting revisions), now merged; this branch is rebased onto main and has two commits.

## What changed
On RTF import, WordCraft used to clear every direct size and bold on heading and Title text, and the font, size and bold on Code text, so the paragraph style would decide. That threw away sizes and bold the user had set by hand. It also meant that rejecting a tracked formatting change in such a paragraph couldn't restore them.

The reader now records each `\stylesheet` entry's `\b`, `\i`, `\fs` and `\f`, following `\sbasedon` (at most 16 hops, loops skipped). A run's property is dropped only when it equals the value from the file's own style:
- If a style's chain sets any character formatting, it counts as a full description: a missing `\b` or `\i` means off, a missing `\fs` means RTF's 12 pt. So Word 365's non-bold headings keep bold set by hand, and tracked bold changes in them still work.
- WordCraft's own style values are used only when the chain has no character words at all, e.g. `{\s2 heading 2;}`. The font falls back on its own, because WordCraft's writer puts the code font on the paragraph rather than in the Code style.
- A stylesheet entry without `\sN` is Normal and no longer overwrites the entry before it.

Applies to the run's formatting and to the old formatting of a tracked change. The writer is unchanged. Word evidence: Word writes resolved values in RTF, and `\oldcprops` holds only the changed properties.

## Tests (crates/formats/src/rtf.rs; each new test failed before the fix)
`heading_runs_are_compared_with_the_files_heading_style`, `style_formatting_is_resolved_through_sbasedon` (LibreOffice-style chain), `code_runs_in_the_files_code_font_have_no_direct_font`, `hostile_sbasedon_chains_are_harmless`, `a_style_chain_without_a_size_has_rtfs_default_size`, `a_code_paragraph_round_trips_without_a_direct_code_font`, `a_stylesheet_entry_without_a_number_is_normal`, `a_heading_size_set_by_hand_survives_in_the_old_form…

title: Layout: text above a float's anchor wraps around it (#2048)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #2048.

## Problem
Layout adds a floating object's wrap area to the page only when it reaches the object's anchor paragraph. A picture anchored in a later paragraph but placed higher up the page (fixed on the page / margin, or with a negative offset from its paragraph) was wrapped by its own paragraph and the ones after it, while the paragraphs above the anchor on that page ran behind it.

## Change (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)
- `anchor_floats` records each body float placed above its anchor paragraph's top while text was already placed before it on the page (page index, block, object index, wrap area).
- At the end of a pass, if those floats differ from the ones the pass started with, `layout_pass` returns `Pass::Rewrap` and the layout runs again. In the new pass each page starts with those wrap areas (`PageBuilder::new_page`), so the earlier paragraphs wrap around the float. This is the same kind of loop that page totals already use. When layout reaches the anchor, the seeded area is updated in place and not added a second time.
- At most 3 extra passes (`MAX_REWRAP_PASSES`). Documents without such floats never take an extra pass.

## Tests
- `layout::tests::a_float_placed_above_its_anchor_wraps_the_paragraphs_before_it`: covers a page-relative float and a paragraph-relative float with a negative offset, both anchored in the 5th paragraph. It checks that every line beside the picture starts to its right. It fails with the fix turned off and passes with it.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.
- Rendered a repro doc built through CLI commands with `wordcraft-cli render` and checked the PNG: all three paragraphs above the anchor now wrap to the right of the picture.

## Not verified
- Not compared side by side with Word on this machine (Word's behaviour is from the issue screenshot).
- Text in an *earlier column* beside a float anchored in a later column is still not wrapped (#1158) unless the float is also above its anchor.
- A paragraph-relative float that keeps movi…

title: fix(engine): support none in wordart reflection and outline color
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR addresses inconsistencies in WordArt / text effect parameter parsing in `crates/engine/src/cmd/wordart.rs`:
1. In `parse_reflection`, passing `{"reflection": "none"}` previously returned a parameter error (`CmdError::Params`) because only `null` and boolean `false` were accepted to clear reflection, unlike `parse_fill`, `parse_outline`, `parse_shadow`, and `parse_glow` which all accept `"none"`.
2. In `parse_outline`, passing `{"color": "none"}` within an object parameter (e.g. from `wordArt.textOutline` or `format.textEffects`) previously failed `Rgb::parse` and fell back to `d.color` (`Some(Rgb::BLACK)`), producing a black outline instead of no outline line.
3. Case-insensitivity (`eq_ignore_ascii_case("none")`) is now handled across `parse_outline`, `parse_shadow`, `parse_glow`, and `parse_reflection`.

### Testing

- Verified all tests in `wordcraft-engine` pass cleanly via `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine -- tests_wordart`.

title: fix(formats): support CDATA sections in HTML import
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
In HTML/XHTML import (`crates/formats/src/html.rs`), `<![CDATA[...]]>` sections were previously matched by the generic declaration scanner `if rest.starts_with("<!")` and skipped with `self.skip_past(">")`. This led to two issues:
1. The entire content of the CDATA section was discarded as empty text instead of being extracted as unescaped character data.
2. If the CDATA section contained a `>` character (e.g. `<![CDATA[a > b]]>`), `skip_past(">")` stopped prematurely at the first `>`, dropping the preceding content and leaking trailing CDATA content and the closing `]]>` delimiter into the document as plain text.

This PR adds CDATA handling in `Lexer::next` before generic `<!` declaration skipping, extracting the literal text between `<![CDATA[` and `]]>`.

### Testing
- Added unit test `cdata_sections_are_preserved_as_text` in `crates/formats/src/html.rs`.
- Verified all tests in `wordcraft-formats` pass cleanly via `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats -- html`.

title: fix(docx): support hyperlink sub-locations and normalize anchor hashes
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
In DOCX documents (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs` and `crates/docx/src/write/story.rs`):
1. In `read_inline`, reading `w:hyperlink` previously concatenated `format!("{u}#{a}")` without stripping any existing `#` from the base URL or leading `#` from `w:anchor`. If `w:anchor` contained a leading `#` (e.g. `<w:hyperlink w:anchor="#bookmark">`), it produced `##bookmark` instead of `#bookmark`. Furthermore, if the relationship target URL already contained a fragment or trailing `#`, combining them produced invalid URLs like `https://example.org/page#old#sec` or `https://example.org/page##sec`.
2. In `Writer::paragraph`, writing `w:hyperlink` for an external URL with a sub-location/fragment (e.g. `https://example.org/doc#section`) previously placed the entire string in the relationship Target and omitted `w:anchor`. In ECMA-376 / Word, external hyperlinks with sub-locations specify the base URL in `r:id` and the location in `w:anchor`.

### Testing
- Added unit test `hyperlink_sublocation_and_hash_normalization` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`.
- Verified all tests pass cleanly via `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx -- hyperlink`.

title: fix(docx, doc): support VML wrap side and case-insensitive float anchors
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. When parsing VML legacy shapes in DOCX (`read_vml` / `vml_float`), `w10:wrap` side attribute (`side="both" | "left" | "right" | "largest"`) was ignored, causing `wrap_text` to always fall back to the default `BothSides`.
2. In `wordcraft_doc::para::WrapText::from_ooxml`, `"both"` was not recognized (only `"bothSides"`), and comparisons were case-sensitive. In VML (`urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:word`), ST_WrapSide values include `both`, `left`, `right`, and `largest`.
3. Wrap types and CSS float relative anchors (`mso-position-horizontal-relative` and `mso-position-vertical-relative`) used case-sensitive string matching against lowercase strings. Values in Word XML/VML can be formatted with PascalCase or uppercase (e.g. `Square`, `Page`, `Margin`), causing them to fall back to the default column/paragraph anchors instead of honoring the specified page/margin coordinates.
4. Boolean attributes such as `filled` and `stroked` checked against lowercase `"false"` / `"f"`, failing to handle `"False"`, `"FALSE"`, or `"F"`.

### Solution
- Updated `wordcraft_doc::para::WrapText::from_ooxml` to support `"both"` alongside `"bothSides"` with case-insensitive matching.
- Updated `vml_float` to extract `w10:wrap/@side` and map to `wrap_text`.
- Made wrap types, relative anchor parsing, and boolean attribute parsing in `vml_float` and `read_vml` case-insensitive.
- Added comprehensive unit test in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs` verifying wrap side, anchor case-insensitivity, and boolean flag parsing on VML shapes.

title: fix(formats): support self-closing and flexible anchor tags in markdown
author: divyanshu2074
body: ### Problem When importing Markdown, HTML anchor tags (`` / ``) are used to establish cross-reference targets and bookmarks. However: 1. Self-closing anchor tags (``, ``, ``), which are widely used in markdown documentation, were not supported because the inline tokenizer required an immediately adjacent trailing ``. 2. Unquoted attribute values in self-closing tags (``) had their value parsed as `"foo/"` because `tag_attr` only checked for whitespace and `>` as delimiters. 3. Minor whitespace differences inside paired anchor tags (e.g., `` or tabs after ``) and paired anchor tags (`` / ``). - Updated `tag_attr` to terminate unquoted attribute values at `/` in addition to whitespace and `>`. - Added unit test `markdown_anchor_variants` covering self-closing tags, spaced self-closing tags, `name` attributes, paired tags with internal whitespace, and unquoted values.

title: fix(docx): fall back to default theme colors and support phClr in schemeClr
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. In `wordcraft_docx::read::drawing_color::color`, `a:schemeClr` directly indexed the provided `theme` slice (`*theme.get(scheme_slot(...)?)?`). When parsing documents that do not define an explicit theme part (where `theme` is empty or has fewer than 12 colors), `a:schemeClr` returned `None`, losing shape fills, line colors, and text colors. This contradicted the module helper `slot()`, which was designed to fall back to `wordcraft_doc::THEME_COLORS`.
2. `scheme_slot` did not recognize DrawingML's standard `phClr` (placeholder color), which in style evaluation maps to the primary/style text color slot (0, `tx1`/`dk1`).
3. `scheme_slot` performed case-sensitive string matches, failing on scheme color identifiers formatted in varying casing.

### Solution
- Updated `color()` in `drawing_color.rs` to call `scheme(c.attr("val")?, theme)?` rather than directly indexing the `theme` slice, ensuring reliable fallback to `THEME_COLORS`.
- Updated `scheme_slot` to support `phClr` (mapped to slot 0) and handle case-insensitive string matching.
- Added unit test `scheme_color_falls_back_to_default_theme_and_supports_phclr` verifying `a:schemeClr` fallback when `theme` is empty, support for `phClr`, and override with custom themes.

title: fix(formats): support 4/8-digit hex, space-separated rgb and hsl in parse_color
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
`wordcraft_formats::model::parse_color` parses CSS / HTML colors for HTML, LaTeX, and ODT imports. However:
1. 4-digit hex (`#rgba`) and 8-digit hex (`#rrggbbaa`) colors (standard in CSS Color Module Level 4) failed to parse because they were passed to `Rgb::parse` which strictly requires 6 hex digits.
2. Modern CSS Color Level 4 space-separated syntax (`rgb(r g b)` or `rgb(r g b / a)`) failed to parse because `rgb(...)` only split on commas.
3. `hsl(...)` / `hsla(...)` colors were completely unsupported.

### Solution
- Extended `parse_color` to parse 4-digit hex (`#rgba`) and 8-digit hex (`#rrggbbaa`) strings.
- Added support for space-separated `rgb(...)` / `rgba(...)` syntax, ignoring optional alpha channels.
- Added support for `hsl(...)` / `hsla(...)` syntax with angles (`deg`, `rad`, `turn`) and percentage saturations/luminances.
- Added unit tests in `model::tests::colors` covering 4/8-digit hex, space-separated `rgb()`, and `hsl()`/`hsla()`.

title: fix(formats): support backslash space, soft breaks and zero-width spaces in RTF
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When importing RTF documents:
1. In the RTF 1.9.1 specification, `\ ` (a backslash followed by an ASCII space) is a standard control symbol representing a required non-breaking space (equivalent to `\~`). In `wordcraft_formats::rtf::parse_full`, `\ ` was unhandled in the control symbol `match n`, falling through to `_ => i += 2` which consumed and discarded the space entirely.
2. Standard RTF break control words `\softline` (soft line break) and `\softpage` (soft page break) were ignored.
3. Special Unicode word opportunity characters `\zwbo` (zero-width break opportunity, U+200B) and `\zwnbo` (zero-width non-break opportunity, U+2060) were not recognized.

### Solution
- Added `b' '` alongside `b'~'` in the control symbol handler in `parse_full` to emit U+00A0 (non-breaking space).
- Added `\softline` and `\softpage` to `Reader::word` alongside `\line` and `\page`.
- Added `\zwbo` (U+200B) and `\zwnbo` (U+2060) to `Reader::word`.
- Added unit test `rtf_backslash_space_and_special_breaks` verifying that `\ `, `\~`, `\zwbo`, `\softline`, and `\softpage` are correctly imported.

title: Preserve header/footer content when adding page numbers (#2201)
author: MMexicann
body:
Fixes #2201.

Adding a top/bottom page number replaced the entire header/footer story, discarding existing text, formatting and tables. This change appends numbering on a separate paragraph and preserves existing PAGE fields rather than adding duplicates, including fields in anchored text boxes and deeply nested tables.

### Root cause and implementation

`insert.pageNumber` called `set_story` with only the generated paragraph. It now retains the existing block list and appends to it. Only a paragraph exactly equal to the untouched Header/Footer placeholder is reused; customized empty paragraphs are preserved too.

Before insertion, the command checks simple and range PAGE fields. Matching ignores case and preserves field switches, content and formatting. PAGEREF and NUMPAGES remain distinct fields. The current-position inline path and central command/Session execution path are retained.

PAGE fields can live in separate text-box stories or below the ordinary paragraph traversal's table-depth limit. The guard uses an iterative block walk, follows only TextBox parts anchored from the selected header/footer (including group members), and visits each story once. It descends nested tables without recursion and terminates on cyclic text-box references. PAGE fields in unrelated body text boxes do not suppress header/footer numbering.

### Regression and fidelity coverage

`crates/engine/tests/page_number_preservation.rs` contains nine regression tests: the original five (with the table case expanded to depths 1 and 17), plus four text-box/control tests. The public Session path creates the header/footer and first text box; inline synthetic model fixtures represent imported nested and grouped text boxes.

Coverage includes header/footer text and table preservation, paragraph alignment and cell bold formatting, unchanged selection, insertion undo/redo, repeated insertion without duplicate fields, existing PAGE fields with switches, locked/dirty range fields, unrelated fields…

title: fix(docx): trim marker id, bound bookmarks map, and support bookmarkEnd name fallback
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. In `wordcraft_docx::read::story::Reader::marker`, `w:id` attributes were not trimmed of surrounding whitespace. When `w:bookmarkStart` or other range markers have whitespace in their IDs (e.g. `w:id=" 42 "`), string lookups against unpadded `w:bookmarkEnd` IDs failed, dropping the bookmark end object.
2. `w:bookmarkEnd` elements can carry a `w:name` attribute (e.g. `<w:bookmarkEnd w:id="0" w:name="bookmark_name"/>`). If the bookmark was opened in a different story part or if ID matching failed, `BookmarkEnd` was dropped instead of utilizing the explicit `w:name`.
3. `self.bookmarks` map lacked an upper-bound cap, in contrast to `self.perms` which guards against adversarial XML files with unbounded unique IDs.

### Solution
- Trimmed `w:id` and `w:name` attributes in `marker()`.
- Added fallback in `w:bookmarkEnd` handling to extract `w:name` when `self.bookmarks.get(&id)` is not found.
- Added a 100,000 entry cap on `self.bookmarks` to prevent unbounded memory growth.
- Added unit test `bookmark_end_name_and_id_trim` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`.

title: fix(docx): inspect textbox style for v-text-anchor and handle case-insensitivity
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
In WordprocessingML / VML reading (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`):
- `v-text-anchor` was only checked on the outer shape's style attribute, ignoring `v-text-anchor` declared directly on `<v:textbox style="...">`.
- `mso-fit-shape-to-text` was only checked on `<v:textbox style="...">`, ignoring it if placed on the shape's style attribute.
- `v-text-anchor` matching was case-sensitive (`a.starts_with("middle")`), which failed for capitalized or upper-case values (e.g. `Middle`) commonly produced by Word/Office tools, and did not recognize `center`.

This PR:
1. Checks both `tb.attr("style")` and `shape.attr("style")` for both `v-text-anchor` and `mso-fit-shape-to-text`.
2. Trims and case-normalizes `v-text-anchor` values, supporting `middle`, `center`, and `bottom` regardless of casing.
3. Adds automated unit test `vml_textbox_style_anchor_and_fit` verifying `v-text-anchor` and `mso-fit-shape-to-text` parsing from `<v:textbox>`.

title: fix(docx): handle case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed ST_OnOff boolean values
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
In ECMA-376 (WordprocessingML / Office Open XML §22.9.2.11 `ST_OnOff`), boolean logic simple type values (`0`, `false`, `off`, `f`) represent "off" / false.

Across several reading modules (`crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`, `crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs`, `crates/docx/src/read/sdt.rs`, `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`, `crates/docx/src/read/math.rs`, and `crates/docx/src/units.rs`):
- Several attribute parsers used `!matches!(v, "0" | "false" | "off")`.
- When an attribute was serialized with capital or mixed case (e.g. `Off`, `OFF`, `False`, `FALSE`) or surrounding whitespace (e.g. `" 0 "`, `" off "`), `matches!(...)` failed, causing `!matches!(...)` to evaluate to `true`.
- As a result, attributes like `w:enforcement="False"`, `w:firstRow="False"`, `w:lastRow="Off"`, `w:b w:val="Off"`, `w:fldLock="False"`, `w:sep="False"`, and `rotWithShape="False"` were erroneously treated as enabled (`true`).

This PR:
1. Adds `units::is_off` and `units::on_off_attr` to normalize casing and whitespace when checking for off/false (`"0"`, `"false"`, `"off"`, `"f"`).
2. Uses `is_off` and `on_off_attr` uniformly across `props.rs`, `sdt.rs`, `story.rs`, `mod.rs`, `math.rs`, and `units.rs`.
3. Adds automated unit tests `st_on_off_case_insensitivity` and `test_is_off` verifying case-insensitive and whitespace-tolerant boolean parsing.

title: fix(formats): enforce tag boundary when skipping raw text elements in HTML
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
In HTML parsing (`crates/formats/src/html.rs`):
- When skipping raw text / script elements (`script`, `style`, `noscript`, `template`, `textarea`), the lexer called `lx.skip_past(&format!("</{name}"));` followed by `lx.skip_past(">");`.
- `skip_past` searched for `</{name}` anywhere as a substring. If the script or style contained occurrences like `</scripted>`, `</scripts>`, or `</styles>` in string literals or comments, `skip_past` falsely matched the substring `</script` or `</style` inside those other tag names and stopped at the next `>`.
- As a result, the remainder of the `<script>` or `<style>` content leaked into the document body as visible text and elements.

This PR:
1. Implements `Lexer::skip_past_end_tag` to verify that `</{tag}` is followed by a valid HTML tag boundary (whitespace, `>`, `/`, or end of input), avoiding false matches on words like `</scripted>` or `</styles>`.
2. Uses `skip_past_end_tag` when skipping `script`, `style`, `noscript`, `template`, and `textarea` elements.
3. Adds automated unit test `raw_text_elements_skip_only_matching_end_tag` verifying that scripts and styles containing substrings like `</scripted>` and `</styles>` do not leak their content into the document.

title: fix(formats): support case-insensitive and spaced !important in HTML CSS
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
In HTML CSS declaration parsing (`crates/formats/src/html.rs`):
- `apply_style` stripped `!important` using `v.trim().trim_end_matches("!important").trim()`.
- This was strictly case-sensitive and required no spaces between `!` and `important`.
- According to CSS specifications, `!important` is case-insensitive (e.g. `!IMPORTANT`, `!Important`) and permits whitespace between `!` and `important` (e.g. `! important`).
- Consequently, values using `!IMPORTANT` or `! important` (such as `color: #ff0000 !IMPORTANT`, `font-size: 14pt !important`, `font-weight: 700 !Important`, and `text-align: center !IMPORTANT`) failed to match/parse and were ignored.

This PR:
1. Implements `strip_important` to detect and strip `!` followed by `important` case-insensitively and regardless of internal whitespace.

title: fix(formats): support fin and gutter in RTF import and export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. In RTF paragraph formatting, RTF 1.5+ specifications standardize `\fin<N>` as first-line indent (alongside `\lin<N>` and `\rin<N>`). Wordcraft supported `\li` / `\lin` and `\ri` / `\rin`, but only supported `\fi`, ignoring `\fin`.
2. RTF page gutter margins (`\gutter` document-level and `\guttersxn` section-level) were completely unsupported in `PageGeom`, `SecFmt`, and RTF export, causing document/section gutters to be lost on import and export.

### Solution
1. Support `\fin` alongside `\fi` in `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`.
2. Parse `\gutter` and `\guttersxn` into `PageGeom`, include `gutter` in `SecFmt::props`, and emit `\gutter` when exporting RTF.
3. Added automated unit tests verifying both `\fin` parsing and gutter margin import/export roundtrip.

title: Update page numbers only: repeated headings match in order, tracked changes stay out of the number (#1197)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Update Table, F9 and Update Field on a table of contents now ask: update page numbers only, or the entire table.

In Word, updating a table of contents opens Update Table of Contents with two choices: Update page numbers only (the default) and Update entire table. The first leaves the entries alone, text edited by hand included, and only refreshes the numbers; the second rebuilds the table from the headings. This PR adds that dialog for References › Update Table, for F9 with the table selected (Ctrl+A, F9, or the caret in it) and for Update Field in the context menu (#1203). The page-numbers-only path is new in the engine: each entry finds its heading through the `PAGEREF` field Word writes for the number, its link, or else its text (headings with the same text in order), and gets that heading's page; an entry whose heading can't be found keeps its number. The new number is plain text, without the tracked changes of the one it replaces. Both paths are one undo step. `references.updateToc` and `references.updateFields` take `pageNumbersOnly`; without it scripts and agents still get the whole rebuild, as before (happy to switch the default). F9 away from the table updates the other fields without asking, as before. With Ctrl+A, F9 the choice only applies to the table: page numbers only still updates every other field, and Cancel updates none of them. A Word table of contents the engine keeps as a range field (imported with content it can't reproduce) doesn't show the dialog and is rebuilt whole, as before.

Closes #1197

Validation:
- `tests::toc_update_page_numbers_only_keeps_the_entries`, `toc_page_numbers_only_without_links_matches_entries_by_text`, `toc_page_numbers_only_updates_pageref_fields`, `toc_page_numbers_only_matches_repeated_headings_in_order`, `toc_page_numbers_only_drops_revisions_in_the_number`: fail on main (the whole table is rebuilt: the edited entry goes back to the heading text, a heading added since is listed, the `PAGEREF` field is gone), pass …

title: fix(formats): parse and export left alignment in Markdown table delimiters
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In Markdown GFM table support (`crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`):
1. In `delimiter_row`, table column alignment parsing matched `(true, true)` for `Align::Center` (`:---:`) and `(false, true)` for `Align::Right` (`---:`), but matched `_ => None` for `(true, false)` (`:---`). This caused explicit left-aligned columns to lose their alignment setting and be treated as unaligned / default.
2. In `table_md`, table delimiter serialization formatted `Align::Center` as `:---:` and `Align::Right` as `---:`, but mapped `Some(Align::Left)` to default `---` rather than `:---`, losing left alignment on export.

### Solution
1. In `delimiter_row`, map `(true, false)` to `Some(Align::Left)`.
2. In `table_md`, map `Some(Align::Left)` to `":---"`.
3. Add automated unit test verifying import and export of all delimiter alignment variants (`:---`, `:---:`, `---:`, `---`).

title: Make three-column header/footer presets editable tables (#2197)
author: MMexicann
body:
Fixes #2197.

The Three columns header/footer preset currently inserts three `[Type here]` strings separated by tabs. They are ordinary text in one paragraph, so the three areas cannot be edited as separate cells. The preset now creates a borderless table with one row and three independently editable cells.

### Root cause and implementation

The `blankThree` branch of the existing `insert.header` / `insert.footer` commands generated tabbed placeholder text. It now uses the document model's bounded table constructor with a constant one-row, three-column shape. Equal cell widths span the caret section's text width. Cell paragraphs keep the Header/Footer style and use left, center and right alignment. Explicit nil borders override inherited table-style borders, and a trailing paragraph lets the story also be edited after the table.

The existing command path still sets the caret, now in the first cell; ordinary typing and Tab navigation use the existing editing commands. Explicit `text` keeps its precedence over a preset.

The canvas shows screen-only cell guides for the active header/footer story. It leaves the document's borders and View Gridlines flag untouched. Closing header/footer editing removes the automatic guides; explicit View Gridlines still outlines all stories. Automatic guides scan header/footer placements without scanning the body placement list.

### Regression and fidelity coverage

`crates/engine/tests/three_column_headers.rs` reproduced the defect on unmodified upstream main: the three-cell-table test failed, while the explicit-text-precedence control passed. The tests cover both fresh and existing header/footer stories (including restoring replaced content on undo), custom section width, equal cells, nil borders, paragraph styles/alignment, first-cell selection, Tab navigation and independent middle-cell bold formatting. They also check preset and text undo/redo and two DOCX save/reopen cycles preserving body text, cell text, geometry, formatting …

title: fix(docx): correctly parse emu and case-insensitive units in measure
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In `crates/docx/src/units.rs`:
1. `measure` used `t.find(|c: char| !(c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.' || c == '-' || c == '+' || c == 'e' || c == 'E'))` to separate the numeric value from the unit suffix. Because `'e'` and `'E'` were unconditionally treated as part of the number, any measure with an `emu` or `EMU` unit (e.g., `"12700emu"`) had its `'e'` consumed into the numeric string (`"12700e"`), causing float parsing to fail with an invalid float error and returning `None`. Consequently, `emu` units in `measure` could never be parsed.
2. Unit suffixes (`pt`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pc`, `pi`, `px`, `emu`) were matched in a case-sensitive manner, causing uppercase or mixed-case units (e.g. `1IN`, `12PT`, `25.4MM`, `25400EMU`) to return `None`.

### Solution
1. In `measure`, verify that `'e'` or `'E'` is actually part of an exponent (followed by an optional sign and an ASCII digit) before treating it as part of the numeric prefix; otherwise, treat it as the start of the unit suffix.
2. Match unit suffixes case-insensitively using `to_ascii_lowercase()`.
3. Add automated unit test assertions verifying `emu` / `EMU` parsing as well as uppercase unit suffixes (`1IN`, `12PT`, `2.54CM`, `25.4MM`, `10PX`, `1e2pt`).

title: fix(formats): parse case-insensitive and pica units in ODT lengths
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In ODT import (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`), `length` parses XML attribute lengths (used for `fo:page-width`, `fo:page-height`, `fo:margin-*`, `fo:font-size`, `svg:width`, `svg:height`, and `fo:column-gap`):
1. Unit suffixes (`pt`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pc`, `px`) were checked via `strip_suffix` in a strictly case-sensitive manner without converting to lowercase first (unlike HTML's `css_len_pt`), causing uppercase or mixed-case lengths (such as `1IN`, `12PT`, `2.54CM`, `25.4MM`, `10PX`) to fail parsing and return `None`.
2. Standard pica measure `pi` was unsupported (only `pc` was handled).

### Solution
1. Convert `v` to lowercase via `v.trim().to_ascii_lowercase()` in `length`.
2. Support `pi` alongside `pc` for picas.
3. Added automated unit test assertions verifying uppercase units and `pi` parsing in `lengths()`.

title: fix(formats): parse leading plus and case-insensitive units in LaTeX lengths
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In LaTeX import (`crates/formats/src/latex.rs`), `length_pt` parses TeX dimension lengths (used for tabular column widths `p{...}`, `m{...}`, `b{...}`, and `\fontsize{...}{...}`):
1. Unit suffixes (`pt`, `bp`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `em`, `ex`, `pc`, `\linewidth`, `\textwidth`, etc.) were matched case-sensitively, so dimensions specified with uppercase units (such as `12PT`, `1IN`, `3CM`, `10MM`, `\TEXTWIDTH`) failed to match and returned `None`.
2. Dimensions with a leading positive sign (such as `+12pt` or `+2cm`) failed because `+` was not treated as part of the numeric prefix, causing `split` to be 0 and the numeric string to be separated improperly as `"+12pt"`.

### Solution
1. Strip leading `+` from the input string in `length_pt`.
2. Convert the unit suffix to lowercase via `to_ascii_lowercase()` before matching against known TeX units and dimension macros.
3. Add automated unit tests verifying `length_pt` with uppercase units, leading `+`, and macros.

title: fix(formats): support pc, !important, and flexible dimensions in HTML css_len_pt
author: divyanshu2074
body: ### Problem In HTML import (`crates/formats/src/html.rs`): 1. `css_len_pt` did not support `pc` (picas, 1pc = 12pt), which is a standard absolute CSS unit. 2. `css_len_pt` did not strip `!important` before parsing dimension units. When CSS properties such as `width`, `height`, or `font-size` specified `!important` (e.g. `width: 200px !important`), `css_len_pt` failed to strip the suffix and returned `None`. 3. In `` dimension parsing, `dim` relied on `trim_end_matches("px")`, which is case-sensitive (failing on `width="100PX"`) and failed on valid dimensions with non-px units (such as `2in`). ### Solution 1. Strip `!important` declarations (case-insensitively and respecting whitespace) in `css_len_pt`. 2. Support `pc` in `css_len_pt` mapped to `12.0` pt. 3. Use `css_len_pt` in `` dimension parsing to robustly handle numeric attributes, case-insensitive units (`PX`), other CSS units (`in`, `pt`), and style attributes with `!important`. 4. Add automated unit test verifying `pc`, `!important`, and `` attribute and style dimensions.

title: fix(formats): support mathvariant and case-insensitive display mode in MathML
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### What problem does this PR solve?
In the MathML reader (`crates/formats/src/mathml.rs`):
1. `<math>` display mode checking for the `mode` attribute only checked case-sensitive exact match `d == "display"`, ignoring case variations like `mode="DISPLAY"` or `mode="Display"` as well as surrounding whitespace.
2. The `mathvariant` attribute on `<mi>`, `<mn>`, `<mo>`, and `<ms>` was completely ignored for all values except `mathvariant="normal"` on single characters. Standard MathML variants including `bold`, `italic`, `bold-italic`, `double-struck`, `script`, `bold-script`, `fraktur`, `bold-fraktur`, `sans-serif`, `bold-sans-serif`, `sans-serif-italic`, `sans-serif-bold-italic`, and `monospace` were discarded rather than mapped to their corresponding `MSty` / `MScr` styles and mathematical alphanumeric Unicode codepoints via `math_alnum`.

### What changes are included in this PR?
- Updated `<math>` attribute inspection to trim and check `mode` case-insensitively for `"display"`, matching standard MathML specification behavior.
- Supported standard MathML `mathvariant` attribute values on token elements (`mi`, `mn`, `mo`, `ms`), assigning the proper `MScr` and `MSty` styles and converting alphanumeric characters to their mathematical alphanumeric Unicode representations.
- Added automated unit tests verifying `mode="DISPLAY"` and `mathvariant` parsing (`bold`, `double-struck`, `fraktur`).

title: Web host bridge: lock and unlock editing from the host page (readonly)
author: jyviko
body:
Closes #2229.

**Stacked on the `?host=parent` bridge.** This branch carries #405's commit (rebased onto current `main`), so the diff shows it too; only the last commit, d0fab24, is new here. I'll rebase onto whichever bridge PR (#405 or #1655) merges and take this out of draft then.

## What
- `Session::editing_locked`: while set, every command that changes the document is refused (mutating commands, plus Undo, Undo Actions and Redo, which restore history without being `mutates`). Reading, selecting, copying, saving and opening still work.
- It lives on the session, not the document: never saved, and Stop Protection can't lift it (unlike `review.restrict`).
- `Session::disabled_reason` / `command_enabled` fold the lock into the enabled state the ribbon (`widgets.rs`) and control channel (`ui.commands`) report, so edit buttons grey out.
- Web bridge:
  - `wordcraft:readonly` `{ readonly }` from the parent locks/unlocks; echoed back once applied.
  - `?readonly=1` starts locked (never editable before the first message).
  - `wordcraft:ready` now carries `{ readonly }`.

## Why
Hosts with a follow mode (one person or agent holds the pen, others watch) need to stop local edits without reloading the document. It's also groundwork for #1589.

## Tests
- `host_editing_lock_refuses_edits_only`: edits, formatting, Undo refused; select, copy, save, open allowed; the lock isn't saved with the file.
- `host_editing_lock_leaves_the_document_unchanged`: runs every command under the lock and checks the document is unchanged (fails if Undo is dropped from the lock).
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.

Not yet tested in a real host iframe. File › Open stays available while locked, since the host's `wordcraft:open` uses the same command.

title: fix(formats): support asian/complex scripts and underline/strike types in ODT
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### What problem does this PR solve?
In the ODT format reader (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`):
1. Font weight and style only inspected `fo:font-weight` and `fo:font-style`, completely ignoring `style:font-weight-asian`, `style:font-weight-complex`, `style:font-style-asian`, and `style:font-style-complex`, which are standard ODF 1.3 (§20.378, §20.379) attributes commonly produced by LibreOffice and OpenOffice for CJK and complex-script formatting.
2. Underline and strikethrough only inspected `style:text-underline-style` and `style:text-line-through-style`, ignoring `style:text-underline-type` (ODF 1.3 §20.388) and `style:text-line-through-type` (ODF 1.3 §20.381) values such as `"single"` and `"double"`.
3. Attributes such as `fo:font-weight="BOLD"`, `fo:font-style="ITALIC"`, `fo:text-align="CENTER"`, `fo:break-before="PAGE"`, `style:text-position="SUPER"`, and `style:font-pitch="FIXED"` were compared with case-sensitive exact string matches, failing on case variations and un-trimmed values.

### What changes are included in this PR?
- Extended `text-properties` parsing in `crates/formats/src/odt.rs` to inspect `style:font-weight-asian`, `style:font-weight-complex`, `style:font-style-asian`, and `style:font-style-complex`.
- Supported `style:text-underline-type` and `style:text-line-through-type` alongside underline/line-through styles.
- Made string value comparisons case-insensitive and whitespace-tolerant across font weight, font style, underline, strikethrough, vertical alignment, font pitch, break-before, and paragraph text alignment.
- Added automated unit test `test_asian_complex_and_extended_text_properties` verifying all cases.

title: fix(docx): standardize ST_OnOff boolean parsing across elements and attributes
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### What problem does this PR solve?
Across `crates/docx` (in `units.rs`, `props.rs`, `mod.rs`, `math.rs`, `sdt.rs`, and `story.rs`), `ST_OnOff` (ECMA-376 Part 1 §22.9.2.7) attribute values were parsed inconsistently with ad-hoc `matches!` expressions:
1. `on_off(e)` and `on_off_attr(e)` only checked exact literal matches like `matches!(v, "0" | "false" | "off")` or `matches!(v.trim(), "0" | "false" | "off" | "False" | "FALSE")`. Case variations like `"Off"` or `"OFF"` and values with whitespace were treated as `true` instead of `false`.
2. In document protection (`read_protection` in `read/mod.rs`), `w:enforcement="False"` and `w:formatting="False"` were treated as enforced/active due to case-sensitive matching against `"false"`.
3. In `read/props.rs`, `w:beforeAutospacing` and `w:afterAutospacing` checked `matches!(v.trim(), "1" | "true" | "on")`, failing on capitalized booleans like `"True"` or `"On"`.
4. Column separator and equal width attributes (`w:sep`, `w:equalWidth`), table look attributes in `w:tblLook` (`w:firstRow`, `w:lastRow`, `w:firstColumn`, `w:lastColumn`, `w:noHBand`, `w:noVBand`), and content control properties (`w:multiLine`) similarly lacked trimming and case-insensitive handling for standard off/false values.

### What changes are included in this PR?
- Introduced `pub fn is_on(s: &str) -> bool` in `crates/docx/src/units.rs` to trim and case-insensitively check standard off values (`"0"`, `"false"`, `"off"`).
- Updated `on_off` in `units.rs`, `math.rs`, `sdt.rs`, `story.rs`, `mod.rs`, and `props.rs` to use `is_on`.
- Added unit tests in `units.rs` verifying `is_on` and `on_off` against case variations, whitespace, and XML elements.

title: fix(formats): support xs:time, string-value, and case-insensitive cell types in spreadsheets
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR resolves several data extraction bugs in spreadsheet parsing across ODF Spreadsheets (ODS) and SpreadsheetML (XLSX):
1. **ODF `office:time-value` parsing:** Per ODF 1.3 §19.882, `office:time-value` specifies either an XML Schema `xs:duration` or an `xs:time` (e.g. `13:45:00`). `iso_time` previously only handled durations starting with `"PT"`, failing to parse standard `xs:time` strings and defaulting to 0.0 days.
2. **ODF `office:string-value` and numeric fallbacks:** Per ODF 1.3 §19.870, string cells can specify their string content via `office:string-value` rather than pre-rendered `<text:p>` children (common in programmatic document generators). Additionally, `percentage` and `currency` cells now fall back to `office:value` when formatted text is omitted. `office:value-type` comparisons are now also case-insensitive.
3. **SpreadsheetML case-insensitive cell types & `inlineStr` fallback:** Cell type attribute `t` (`c.kind`) matching is now case-insensitive (handling uppercase or lowercase variants per XML standards), and `inlineStr` gracefully falls back to `c.value` if `c.inline` is empty.

### Testing
- Added unit test `test_sheet_extended_value_parsing` covering `xs:time`, `office:string-value`, ODS percentage/currency value fallback, and SpreadsheetML case-insensitive cell types and `inlineStr` fallback.
- Ran test suite cleanly (`cargo test --lib sheet`).

title: fix(formats): handle column breaks, comment info destination, strikedl, and plain code page reset in RTF
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR addresses several control word and state management bugs in the RTF importer per the RTF 1.9.1 specification:
1. **`\comment` in `\info`:** RTF 1.9.1 specifies both `\comment` and `\doccomm` for comments/description in the document information group. Previously, `\comment` was only present in the catch-all skip list and was discarded instead of routed to `Dest::Info(5)` (`meta.description`).
2. **`\revtim` recognition:** The RTF specification defines `\revtim` for revision time, whereas the skip list only had `\revtime`. Added `\revtim` so it is properly recognized within the info group.
3. **`\column` break support:** RTF 1.9.1 defines `\column` as a column break. It is now handled by emitting `\u{000E}` (WordCraft's column break character).
4. **`\strikedl` (double strikethrough):** In RTF 1.9.1, `\strikedl` is the control word for double strikethrough. It is now parsed and sets `fmt.strike = true`.
5. **Additional underline styles:** Added recognition for `\ulhair`, `\ulthdash`, `\ulthdashd`, `\ulthdashdd`, `\ulthldash`, `\ululdbwave`, and `\ulwavy`.
6. **Code page reset on `\plain`:** When `\plain` resets character formatting to default, it now also resets `st.cp = None`. Previously, switching fonts with `\fN` having a custom code page (e.g. Cyrillic cp1251) followed by `\plain` would cause subsequent 8-bit characters to decode using the previous font's code page instead of the document default code page (e.g. cp1252), causing character corruption.

### Testing
- Added unit test `test_rtf_extended_control_words_and_state_reset` covering `\comment` in `\info`, `\column` break, `\strikedl`, extended underline styles, and code page reset on `\plain`.
- Ran full test suite cleanly (`cargo test --lib rtf`).

title: fix(formats): support robust !important, CSS pica units, tr bgcolor, small/big tags, and extended entities in HTML
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR resolves several formatting and parsing defects in the HTML reader:
1. **Case-insensitive & whitespace-tolerant `!important` stripping in CSS:** Previously, `apply_style` used `v.trim_end_matches("!important")`, which failed to strip `!important` if uppercase (`!IMPORTANT`, `!Important`) or if formatted with spaces (`! important`). This caused trailing text to corrupt values for `color`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, and `text-align`. It now safely strips `!important` case-insensitively and regardless of spacing.
2. **CSS `pc` (picas) unit support:** Added absolute length unit `pc` (1 pica = 12 points) to `css_len_pt`, standard in CSS Values and Units Level 3/4.
3. **`bgcolor` inheritance on enclosing elements:** In HTML 4/5 tables, `<tr bgcolor="...">` sets the background color for row cells. Previously only `<td bgcolor>` was handled directly. Now any enclosing element (like `tr`) sets `fmt.background`, allowing cells to properly inherit row background shading.
4. **`<small>` and `<big>` element sizing:** Added standard size scaling for `<small>` (0.833x) and `<big>` (1.2x) elements.
5. **Additional HTML entities:** Added entity decoding for `prime` (′), `Prime` (″), `radic` (√), `sum` (∑), `prod` (∏), `approx`/`asymp` (≈), `equiv` (≡), and `sdot` (⋅).

### Testing
- Added unit test `test_html_extended_css_and_attributes` covering `!important` stripping, `pc` units, `tr` bgcolor inheritance, `small`/`big` sizing, and extended entities.
- Ran full test suite cleanly (`cargo test --lib html`).

title: fix(docx): support extended NFC number formats and customStyle on/off normalization in WordML 2003
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR resolves number format and style attribute normalization bugs in the Word 2003 XML (WordprocessingML 2003) reader and writer:
1. **Office 2003 XML NFC number format code mapping:** In Word 2003 XML schemas, `w:nfc` specifies number format codes. Previously, codes like `50` (`numberInDash`), `51` (`russianLower`), `52` (`russianUpper`), `10` (`ideographDigital`), `11` (`japaneseCounting`), `12` (`aiueo`), `13` (`iroha`), `16` (`japaneseLegal`), `17` (`japaneseDigitalTenThousand`), `20`/`30` (`ideographTraditional`), `21` (`ideographZodiac`), `28` (`decimalEnclosedCircleChinese`), `29` (`ideographEnclosedCircle`), `38`–`41` (`hebrew`/`arabic`), and `42`–`49` (`hindi`/`thai`/`vietnamese`) were unhandled in `num_fmt` (defaulting to standard decimal) and dropped to `0` in `nfc()`. The mapping has been expanded in both `wordml2003.rs` and `wordml2003_write.rs` to support all these standard Office 2003 formats cleanly.
2. **`w:customStyle` on/off attribute normalization:** In Word 2003 XML, boolean attributes on `w:style` write `"on"` or `"off"`. Previously only `w:default="on"` was normalized to `"1"`, leaving `w:customStyle="on"` as `"on"`, which failed DOCX reader checks (`v == "1" || v == "true"`), causing custom styles to be marked as built-in styles. Normalization now covers both `w:default` and `w:customStyle` ("on" -> "1", "off" -> "0").

### Testing
- Added unit test `extended_nfc_and_custom_style_support` in `crates/docx/tests/wordml2003_write.rs` covering custom style attribute normalization and round-tripping of extended NFC number format codes.
- Ran tests cleanly (`cargo test --test wordml2003_write` and `cargo test --test word_xml`).

title: fix(formats): support tabs in list markers, odd backslash hard breaks, general URI autolinks, and self-closing anchors in Markdown
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

This PR fixes several CommonMark compliance and robustness defects in `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`:
1. **Tabs following list markers**: CommonMark 0.31.2 §5.2 permits list markers followed by a tab (`-\titem`, `1.\titem`), advancing to the next tab stop. Previously, `list_marker` only accepted space (`' '`), failing to recognize tab-separated list items.
2. **Hard line breaks with escaped backslashes**: CommonMark §6.7 specifies that any line ending with an odd number of backslashes represents literal escaped backslash(es) followed by a hard line break (`\n`). Checking `!l.ends_with("\\\\")` wrongly skipped line breaks when lines ended with 3 or more backslashes (`\\\`).
3. **General URI scheme autolinks**: CommonMark §6.4 permits absolute URI autolinks with schemes of 2–32 ASCII letters/digits/`+`/`.`/`-` followed by `:` (e.g. `<tel:+1234567890>`, `<geo:37.7749,-122.4194>`, `<urn:isbn:...>`). Previously, non-email autolinks required `://`, causing all other standard URI schemes without `://` to be ignored.
4. **HTML tag attribute parsing**: `tag_attr` previously calculated character offsets by subtracting from `tag.len()`, which miscalculated offsets whenever whitespace occurred around `=` or trailing attributes were present. It now calculates exact offsets and slices directly from `tag`.
5. **Self-closing and spaced anchor tags**: `<a id="..."/>` and tags with whitespace around `=` or before closing `>` are now correctly parsed into `Inline::Anchor`.
6. **Escaped quotes in link titles and escaped brackets in destinations**: Link title scanning now accounts for backslash-escaped quotes (`\"`), and `<...>` destination parsing allows escaped `\>`.

### Testing
Added comprehensive unit tests in `markdown::tests` covering odd-backslash hard breaks, list markers with tabs, URI autolink schemes, self-closing/spaced anchor tags, and escaped link titles/destinations. All 24 tests in `wordcraft-formats` pass.

title: Font dialog: Kerning for fonts and its Points and above size
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The Font dialog now has Kerning for fonts, with its Points and above size.

In Word, Kerning for fonts lives on the Font dialog's Advanced tab: a check box and a size in points; text at or above that size is kerned (`w:kern`). Turning the box on offers 12 pt, the value applies to the selection as one undo step, and when the selected text differs the box shows neither on nor off. #923 already reads, writes and lays out `w:kern`; this PR adds the UI on top of it. The box and the size sit under Spacing (pt), the size is greyed while the box is off, and OK sends `kern` only when the user changed it, like the other fields, so a mixed selection keeps each run's own value unless the box is clicked. Turning it off sets `kern` to 0, which Word lays out the same as no `w:kern` and which also overrides a style that kerns (Normal kerns from 1 pt in new documents). `format.state` now reports `kern` (null when mixed), which is what the dialog reads. Ligatures, number forms and stylistic sets stay out: they need the OpenType feature plumbing in layout first, and the dialog has no Advanced tab yet, so this keeps the field next to Spacing (happy to split the dialog into tabs if you'd rather).

Validation:
- `tests::format_state_reports_kerning_for_fonts`: fails on main (`kern` is missing from `format.state`), passes here
- `dialogs::tests::font_dialog_sets_kerning_for_fonts`: new (the dialog had no kerning fields): on, the size, one undo step, off, and a mixed selection shown neither on nor off and left alone

title: fix(formats): support multi-story comment anchors, case-insensitive HTML tags, and extension normalization in comments export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

This PR fixes multiple defects in `crates/formats/src/comments.rs` for document comments print-markup export:
1. **Multi-story comment anchor discovery**: Comments anchored outside the main body (e.g. in footnotes, endnotes, textboxes, headers, or footers) previously had their quoted anchor text missed completely because `notes()` only traversed `StoryRef::Body`. It now traverses all non-comment stories in the document (`StoryRef::Body` and non-comment `doc.parts`).
2. **Case-insensitive HTML tag matching**: `append()` previously used exact `s.rfind("</body>")`. If the HTML contained uppercase or mixed-case tags like `</BODY>` or `</Body>`, the closing body tag was missed, causing `<section class="comments">` to be placed after `</html>`. Additionally, if no body tag was found, it now searches for `</html>` before falling back to `s.len()`.
3. **Format extension normalization**: Callers passing extensions with leading dots (e.g. `".html"`, `".md"`, `".txt"`) or uppercase (e.g. `"HTML"`, `"TEXT"`) now have the extensions normalized cleanly via `ext.trim_start_matches('.').to_ascii_lowercase()`.
4. **Newline normalization**: When appending markdown or plain text comment notes to documents that already end in `\n`, `\n\n`, or `\r\n`, leading newlines/CRLF from the notes header are trimmed so excessive empty lines are not introduced.

### Testing
Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Notes extraction with nested replies
- Comment anchor discovery inside footnote parts
- Case-insensitive HTML tag insertion and extension handling
- Markdown and plain text newline normalization

title: fix(formats): support UTF-32 BOM decoding, preserve vertical tabs in text import, and handle colspan in table export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

This PR fixes text decoding and table export issues in `crates/formats/src/txt.rs`:
1. **UTF-32 LE/BE BOM support**:
   - `is_text` and `decode` previously did not check for UTF-32 BOMs (`0xFF, 0xFE, 0x00, 0x00` and `0x00, 0x00, 0xFE, 0xFF`). Because UTF-32 LE begins with `0xFF, 0xFE`, it was misidentified as UTF-16 LE, corrupting every character with alternating null bytes. UTF-32 BE was rejected as binary due to the leading zero bytes.
   - `decode_as` now supports explicit `"utf-32"`, `"utf-32le"`, and `"utf-32be"` labels.
2. **Preserve line/column breaks in plain text import**:
   - `import` previously filtered out `\u{000B}` (vertical tab / soft break) and `\u{000E}` (column break) via `!c.is_control()`. These characters are now retained.
3. **Table alignment and whitespace normalization in plain text export**:
   - `blocks_text` table export now respects `c.colspan` by padding empty tab-delimited cells and handles `c.covered` cells, ensuring every row aligns to the table's column count.
   - Multiline cell contents and internal tabs/newlines are normalized to single spaces so that TSV / tab-delimited table rows and columns are not split across unexpected lines.

### Testing
Added automated unit tests in `txt::tests`:
- `test_utf32_bom_decode_and_sniffing`: Tests UTF-32 LE and BE text detection and decoding.
- `test_import_preserves_soft_breaks`: Verifies `\u{000B}` and `\u{000E}` are preserved.
- `test_table_export_colspan_covered_and_newline_cleaning`: Verifies table column count alignment and newline sanitization.
All 138 tests in `wordcraft-formats` pass.

title: fix(formats): support CSS Color 4 hex/rgb/hsl syntax, extended colors, and RFC 2397 data URIs
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. `data_uri()` assumed `;base64` always occurs at the end of the data URI header (`head.ends_with(";base64")`). Under RFC 2397, media type parameters can appear after `;base64` (e.g. `data:text/plain;base64;charset=utf-8,...`), whitespace can surround parameters, the URI scheme `DATA:` can be uppercase, and base64 payloads may contain percent-encoded characters (`%2B`, `%2F`, `%3D`).
2. `parse_color()` failed on standard CSS Color Module Level 4 notations:
   - 4-digit `#rgba` and 8-digit `#rrggbbaa` hex colors
   - Modern space-separated and slash-alpha syntax: `rgb(r g b)`, `rgb(r g b / a)`
   - HSL colors: `hsl(h, s, l)` and `hsl(h s l / a)` with optional angle units (`deg`, `turn`, `rad`, `grad`)
   - Standard extended CSS color keywords (`pink`, `coral`, `gold`, `crimson`, `indigo`, `azure`, etc.).

### Solution
- Updated `data_uri()` to case-insensitively match the scheme, inspect all semicolon-separated header attributes for `base64`, and percent-decode base64 payloads before decoding.
- Extended `parse_color()` to support 4-digit and 8-digit hex colors, space-separated `rgb()` / `rgba()` syntax, `hsl()` / `hsla()` conversions, and the standard CSS named color keywords.
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering all supported data URI variations and color representations.

title: fix(formats): support none and dual scripts in mmultiscripts, mpadded phantoms, menclose borders, and mtable column align
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. In MathML generation (`to_mathml`), `<mmultiscripts>` omitted empty pre-subscripts or pre-superscripts using empty `<mrow></mrow>` tags instead of the standard `<none/>` empty element mandated by W3C MathML 3 §3.4.7.1.
2. In MathML parsing (`elem`):
   - `<mmultiscripts>` ignored post-scripts whenever `<mprescripts/>` was present (`p > 1`), losing all post-subscripts and post-superscripts.
   - `<mpadded>` was unhandled and fell through to bare children, discarding `width="0"`, `height="0"`, and `depth="0"` padding attributes used for zero-dimension phantom nodes.
   - `<menclose>` only recognized full `"box"` or `"roundedbox"`, ignoring partial side borders (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) and strikes (`horizontalstrike`, `verticalstrike`, etc.) written during export.
   - `<mtable>` ignored `columnalign` declared on the table or rows/cells, defaulting `col_jc` to empty.
   - `read()` only accepted lowercase `mode="display"`, missing uppercase/mixed-case HTML attribute values.

### Solution
- Emitted `<none/>` for empty subscripts/superscripts in `<mmultiscripts>` per MathML specification.
- Added support for preserving both pre-scripts and post-scripts in `<mmultiscripts>`.
- Handled `<mpadded>` with zero-size attributes to preserve zero-dimension phantom nodes.
- Reconstructed `hide` and `strike` configurations on `<menclose>` from individual border and strike notation attributes.
- Imported `columnalign` on `<mtable>` or first-row cells into matrix column alignments (`ColJc`).
- Matched `mode="display"` case-insensitively.
- Added comprehensive unit tests for all updated MathML constructs.

title: fix(formats): support borderless tables, typographic Unicode macros, and text symbols in LaTeX
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. When exporting tables to LaTeX (`Writer::table`), tables with `borderless: true` had hardcoded `|` column borders and `\hline` row dividers emitted on every column and row, forcing full grid borders on borderless tables.
2. During LaTeX table import (`table()`), `borderless` was hardcoded to `false`, failing to recognize tables defined without vertical bars (`|`) or horizontal rule commands (`\hline`, `\toprule`, etc.).
3. `escape_text()` emitted raw literal Unicode characters for common typographic glyphs (`…`, `—`, `–`, `•`, `©`, `®`, `™`, `§`, `¶`, `°`, `±`, `×`, `÷`, `†`, `‡`, `£`, `€`, `«`, `»`, `“`, `”`, `‘`, `’`), which triggers compilation errors under standard pdfLaTeX (`Unicode character ... not set up for use with LaTeX`).
4. `text_symbol()` lacked mappings for international quotation marks and symbols like `\quotesinglbase`, `\quotedblbase`, `\guilsinglleft`, `\guilsinglright`, `\textperthousand`, `\textminus`, `\textcelsius`, `\textinterrobang`, and `\textnumero`.

### Solution
- Updated `Writer::table` to omit vertical bars and `\hline` dividers when `t.borderless` is true.
- Detected `borderless: true` during LaTeX table parsing when no `|` occurs in the column spec and no rule commands are present.
- Mapped typographic Unicode characters to their standard LaTeX text-mode macros (`\ldots{}`, `\textbullet{}`, `\textemdash{}`, etc.) in `escape_text()`.
- Added mappings for international symbols and quotes in `text_symbol()`.
- Added automated unit tests verifying borderless table handling and typographic character round-tripping.

title: fix(formats): support rich strings and continue records in BIFF8 XLS strings
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In Excel 97–2003 (`.xls` BIFF8) sheet parsing (`crates/formats/src/sheet/xls.rs`):
1. `unicode_string` hardcoded characters starting at `at + 3`, ignoring `flags & 0x08` (rich text formatting run count `crun`) and `flags & 0x04` (phonetic extension length `cbExtRst`) as defined in [MS-XLS] §2.5.293 `XLUnicodeString`. Consequently:
   - For `RSTRING` records (which always carry formatting runs) and rich `LABEL` or `STRING` records, `unicode_string` misread the 2-byte formatting run count (or phonetic size) as character bytes, corrupting cell text or causing decoding errors.
2. In `sheet_rows`, `STRING` (formula string results) and `LABEL | RSTRING` records did not gather subsequent `CONTINUE` records when strings exceeded the record length boundary (8224 bytes).

### Solution
1. Updated `rich_string` in `Pieces` to robustly extract string text while safely skipping formatting runs and phonetic blocks.
2. Refactored `unicode_string` to delegate to `Pieces::rich_string()` so all `XLUnicodeString` variants with rich text and phonetic extensions are parsed correctly.
3. Updated `sheet_rows` to collect `CONTINUE` records for `STRING` and `LABEL | RSTRING` records into `Pieces` and parse them via `rich_string()`.
4. Added unit tests covering:
   - `unicode_string` with formatting runs (`flags & 0x08`) and phonetic data (`flags & 0x04`).
   - End-to-end BIFF8 workbook importing `RSTRING` records with formatting runs and `FORMULA` + `STRING` + `CONTINUE` multi-part records.

title: fix(docbin): handle default codepage, VT_I4, multiple property sets, and FILETIME dates
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary of Changes

According to [MS-OLEPS] §2.18.2 (Property 1: PID_CODEPAGE) and standard OLE Property Set stream layouts:
1. If `PID_CODEPAGE` (property ID 1) is not present in a property set, the default code page MUST default to `CP_ACP` (Windows-1252), rather than discarding the entire metadata stream with `property(1)?`.
2. `PID_CODEPAGE` can be stored as either `VT_I2` (0x0002) or `VT_I4` (0x0003). Previous parsing strictly required `VT_I2`.
3. An OLE Property Set stream can contain multiple property sets (`NumPropertySets >= 1`). The header check `u32_at(bytes, 24)? != 1` erroneously rejected streams containing both SummaryInformation and DocumentSummaryInformation property sets.
4. Extracted `PIDSI_CREATE_DTM` (property ID 12) and `PIDSI_LASTSAVE_DTM` (property ID 13) which are `VT_FILETIME` values (type 64) and formatted them as standard ISO 8601 UTC strings (`CoreProps::created` and `CoreProps::modified`).

### Testing
- Added unit tests for:
  - Missing `PID_CODEPAGE` falling back to CP-1252.
  - `PID_CODEPAGE` encoded with `VT_I4`.
  - Streams with `NumPropertySets > 1`.
  - Parsing of `PIDSI_CREATE_DTM` and `PIDSI_LASTSAVE_DTM` FILETIMEs into ISO 8601 timestamps.
- Verified all tests pass cleanly.

title: fix(formats): handle elapsed time formats, XMLSchema time, and ODS string/currency/percentage values
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary of Changes

1. **Custom Number Format Parsing (`custom_date`)**:
   - In ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.8.31, bracketed tokens `[h]`, `[hh]`, `[m]`, `[mm]`, `[s]`, and `[ss]` denote elapsed time (e.g. `[h]:mm` or `[m]:ss`). Previously, all bracketed sections were skipped unconditionally, causing formats like `[h]:mm` to miss the `h` token and erroneously be classified as `DateKind::Date` because of the remaining `:mm`. Bracketed elapsed time tokens are now recognized and correctly categorized as `DateKind::Time` or `DateKind::DateTime`.

2. **OpenDocument Time Values (`iso_time`)**:
   - OASIS ODF 1.3 §19.385 and §18.3.33 define `office:time-value` as either an XMLSchema `time` (`hh:mm:ss[.sss][Z|(+|-)hh:mm]`) or an ISO 8601 `duration` (`PT...`). Previously, `iso_time` strictly stripped `"PT"`, failing on standard XMLSchema time strings like `14:30:00` or `14:30:00Z`. Support for XMLSchema `time` has been added.

3. **OpenDocument Cell Value Fallbacks (`ods_read` & `ods_value`)**:
   - Per ODF 1.3 §19.383 and §19.385, string cells can specify `office:string-value`, and currency/percentage cells specify `office:value`. In programmatic ODS generators where `<text:p>` children are omitted, cells were previously dropped as blank. Now, `office:string-value` and numeric fallbacks for `office:value` on currency/percentage cells are properly extracted and preserved.

### Testing
- Added unit tests for:
  - `custom_date` with `[h]:mm`, `[hh]:mm:ss`, `[m]:ss`, and `yyyy-mm-dd [h]:mm`.
  - `iso_time` with XMLSchema time and timezone offsets.
  - ODS reading of `office:string-value`, `office:value-type="currency"` without `<text:p>`, and XMLSchema `office:time-value`.
- Verified all unit tests pass cleanly.

title: Copying a picture or shape replaces the clipboard's old text, so Paste duplicates it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2276.

A selected picture, drawing, shape or icon has no text, so Copy returns an empty `text` and `system_clipboard::put` returned early without touching the system clipboard. The text copied before stayed there, and Paste (which uses our own copy only while the system clipboard's text still matches it) saw different text and pasted that instead. Now a copy that took something but has no text empties the system clipboard's text, so on desktop the ribbon, context-menu and Ctrl+V Paste all fall back to the copied object and duplicate it, as in Word. An empty selection still leaves the clipboard alone.

Other programs get nothing from such a copy for now (before, they got the stale text). Putting the picture itself on the system clipboard would be nicer, but then Paste would prefer that bitmap over our copy and lose shape and drawing properties, so I left it out; happy to switch if you'd rather have it.

On the web build Ctrl+V still does nothing after copying an object (the ribbon Paste works): the key-release fallback in `keys.rs` only fires when `clipboard_picture` is set, which the web services don't provide. That was already the case before this change; I can look at it in a follow-up if useful.

Validation:
- `copying_a_picture_replaces_the_clipboards_old_text`: fails on main (the system clipboard keeps "My unsaved novel chapter" after copying the picture), passes here
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib` (clipboard, copy, cut and paste tests), `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(docx): case-insensitive OOXML enum parsing and theme-colored border resolution
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary of Changes

1. **Case-Insensitive OOXML Enum Parsing & Synonyms**:
   - `Highlight::from_ooxml`: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.40 `ST_HighlightColor` defines highlight values (`darkBlue`, `darkCyan`, `lightGray`, etc.). Third-party generators often produce lowercase variants like `darkblue`. Exact string matching previously dropped these values to `Highlight::None`. Matching is now case-insensitive, with support for common synonyms (`teal`, `turquoise`, `pink`, `violet`).
   - `Underline::from_ooxml`: Made case-insensitive (`dotdash`, `wavydouble`, `doublewave`, etc.) and added `nil` mapping to `Underline::None`.
   - `BorderStyle::from_ooxml`: Made case-insensitive and added support for `dashDotStroked` (mapping to `BorderStyle::DotDash`).

2. **Theme-Colored Border Resolution (`border_with` / `borders_with`)**:
   - ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.4 `CT_Border` specifies `w:themeColor`, `w:themeTint`, and `w:themeShade`.
   - Previously, `border` did not have access to `PropCtx`, so any border with `w:themeColor` (such as `w:themeColor="accent1"`) had its theme color and tint/shade ignored if `w:color="auto"` or missing.
   - Introduced `border_with` and `borders_with` accepting `Option<&PropCtx>`, plumbing theme color lookup across run borders (`w:bdr`), paragraph borders (`w:pBdr`), table borders (`w:tblBorders`), and cell borders (`w:tcBorders`).

### Testing
- Added unit tests verifying:
  - Case-insensitive parsing and aliases for `Underline`, `Highlight`, and `BorderStyle`.
  - Resolution of `w:themeColor="accent1"` on borders via `PropCtx::ppr`.
- Verified all unit tests across `wordcraft-doc` and `wordcraft-docx` pass cleanly.

title: fix(docx): fix emu unit parsing in measure and handle case-insensitive on_off
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary of Changes

1. **EMU and Universal Measure Parsing (`units::measure`)**:
   - In `units::measure`, splitting the number from the unit previously checked whether a character was part of a number using `!(c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.' || c == '-' || c == '+' || c == 'e' || c == 'E')`.
   - Because `'e'`/`'E'` was treated as part of the number for scientific notation without checking whether digits followed, parsing any value with unit `emu` (e.g. `"12700emu"`) erroneously split into number `"12700e"` and unit `"mu"`. Consequently, `f64::parse` failed on `"12700e"` and `measure` returned `None`, making the `"emu"` unit branch completely unreachable.
   - Refactored `measure` to cleanly match recognized unit suffixes (`emu`, `pt`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pc`, `pi`, `px`) case-insensitively, allowing both `"12700emu"` and uppercase units like `"12PT"` or `"1IN"` to parse correctly.

2. **Case-Insensitive `ST_OnOff` Evaluation (`units::on_off`)**:
   - ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.66 defines `ST_OnOff` values (`true`, `1`, `on`, `false`, `0`, `off`).
   - Previously, `on_off` matched against hardcoded variants `"0" | "false" | "off" | "False" | "FALSE"`, which failed to recognize `"Off"`, `"OFF"`, and other mixed-case forms as false.
   - Updated to use `eq_ignore_ascii_case` against `"false"` and `"off"`.

### Testing
- Added unit tests verifying:
  - `measure("12700emu", ...)` and `measure("12700EMU", ...)` parsing to `1.0` pt.
  - Case-insensitive units (`12PT`, `1IN`).
  - `on_off` correctly evaluating `"off"`, `"Off"`, `"OFF"`, `"false"`, `"FALSE"`, and `"0"` as false.
- Verified all unit tests pass cleanly.

title: fix(docbin): correct sprmTCellWidth operand parsing and handle percentage widths
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In `crates/docbin/src/table.rs`, `decode()` handled `T_CELL_WIDTH` (`sprmTCellWidth`, opcode `0xD635`) with:
```rust
if let [a, b, fts, w0, w1, ..] = prl.operand && *fts == 3 { ... }
```
According to [MS-DOC] §2.9.290, `sprmTCellWidth` has `spra = 6`, meaning its operand begins with a 1-byte count prefix `cb`. Because `[a, b, fts, w0, w1, ..]` did not discard the `cb` prefix, `a` took `cb`, `b` took `itcFirst`, and `fts` took `itcLim`. As a result:
1. `*fts == 3` failed whenever `itcLim != 3`.
2. Even if `itcLim == 3`, `a..b` evaluated to `cb..itcFirst`, which is an empty or corrupted range. `sprmTCellWidth` never worked to set any cell's preferred width.
3. Percentage cell width (`ftsWidth == 2`, expressed in 50ths of a percent per specification) was not supported and was ignored.

### Solution
1. Updated pattern matching to discard `cb`: `if let [_, a, b, fts, w0, w1, ..] = prl.operand`.
2. Supported both twips (`fts == 3`, twips / 20.0) and percentage widths (`fts == 2`, 50ths of a percent / 50.0).
3. Plumbed `width_pcts` into `RowInfo` and applied `width_pct` alongside `width` during `build_row` in `assemble()`.
4. Added unit tests verifying `sprmTCellWidth` twip and percentage parsing and end-to-end table cell properties.

title: fix(docx): handle ST_Merge none value and case-insensitive table attributes
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`, `tcpr` handled `w:hMerge` and `w:vMerge` as follows:
```rust
"w:hMerge" => hcont = k.attr("w:val") != Some("restart"),
"w:vMerge" => c.vmerge = if k.attr("w:val") == Some("restart") { VMerge::Restart } else { VMerge::Continue },
```
According to ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.21 (`hMerge`) and §17.4.84 (`vMerge`), the `w:val` attribute is of type `ST_Merge` with valid values `none`, `restart`, and `continue`:
1. When `<w:hMerge w:val="none"/>` was specified on a cell that is explicitly not horizontally merged, `k.attr("w:val") != Some("restart")` evaluated to `true`. In `read_table`, `hcont == true` merged the cell into the preceding cell and skipped it (`continue`), resulting in data loss.
2. When `<w:vMerge w:val="none"/>` was specified on a cell that is explicitly not vertically merged, `k.attr("w:val") == Some("restart")` evaluated to `false`, wrongly setting `c.vmerge = VMerge::Continue`.
3. Enum values and attribute types were compared case-sensitively, causing valid variations such as `w:val="None"`, `w:val="Restart"`, `w:type="DXA"`, `w:type="PCT"`, `w:vAlign w:val="Center"`, `w:tblLayout w:type="Fixed"`, and alignment/tab-stop values to fail or fall back to defaults.

### Solution
1. In `tcpr`:
   - Updated `w:hMerge` to check for `continue` (`v.eq_ignore_ascii_case("continue")`), so that `none` and `restart` correctly evaluate to `hcont = false`.
   - Updated `w:vMerge` to map `restart` to `VMerge::Restart`, `continue` to `VMerge::Continue`, and any other value (including `none`) to `VMerge::None`.
   - Made `w:tcW/@w:type`, `w:vAlign`, and `w:textDirection` case-insensitive.
2. In `tblpr`:
   - Made `w:tblW/@w:type`, `w:tblLayout/@w:type`, and `w:tblOverlap/@w:val` case-insensitive.
3. In `align` and `tab_stop`:
   - Made alignment values and tab stop alignments and leaders case-insensitive.
4. Added comprehensive unit tests in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` covering `hMerge`, `vMerge`, unit case-insensitivity, and …

title: Comments: shade every paragraph of a multi-paragraph comment
author: seif9116
body:
Closes #2314.
Closes #2324.
Closes #2325.
Closes #2326.

## What was wrong

A comment over several paragraphs was shaded only in its first paragraph and in the part of its
last paragraph before the end marker. The paragraphs between them were plain, so the comment
looked as if it covered only its first paragraph. The shade was worked out one paragraph at a time
from the markers inside that paragraph (`crates/layout/src/display.rs`, `lines`), and an end
marker with no start in its own paragraph shaded from the start of that paragraph.

A page wholly inside a range also stayed plain in the app: page pictures are cached by a
fingerprint of the page's paragraphs (`page_content_key` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`), and
adding a comment changes none of that page's paragraphs.

New Comment had two more problems with ranges over paragraphs (`crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs`,

title: Keep spaces that follow a tab in the ODT round trip
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/odt.rs:347 (writer, `plain_inlines`) and crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1550 (reader, `text`)` (no existing issue): ODT round trip drops a space that follows a tab ("a\t b" comes back as "a\tb").

## Cause
The ODT writer emitted `<text:tab/>` and then treated the next space as a literal one (`prev_space = false`). The reader's whitespace collapse treats text ending in a tab as preceding whitespace, so it dropped that literal space. A run of N spaces after a tab came back as N-1.

## Fix
After writing a tab, the writer now sets `prev_space = true`, as it already does after a line break. Spaces after a tab are therefore written as `<text:s text:c="N"/>`, which the reader keeps exactly.

## Verified
- Regression test `spaces_after_a_tab_survive_a_round_trip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib spaces_after_a_tab_survive_a_round_trip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The reader's whitespace collapse is unchanged, so ODT files from other producers are still read the same way.
